items.title: TS: `compileFromANF`'s `--ir`/ANF entry point unconditionally skips constant folding regardless of `disableConstantFolding`/CLI flags, making the option a no-op contrary to its own documentation and defeating the conformance fuzzer's fold-ON cross-tier gate for the TS tier
items.confidence_note: raised by CL+CX; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.severity_note: reviewers disagreed ['CRITICAL', 'MEDIUM']; highest taken per §6.2 (no downgrade justified at combination time)
items.description:
[CL-BUG-224] # PASS C BATCH 2R WAVE 2 — conformance-fuzz-mutation-negatives (CL-BUG-224 … CL-GAP-126)

**Verified.** 4 spot-checks, all exact, **including a full independent reproduction of the
load-bearing denominator.** Report at `workers-depth/conformance-fuzz-mutation-negatives-depth.md`.
All 57 files read; worktree clean before and after.

...
## CL-BUG-224 — CRITICAL / P0 — The repo's only seven-tier fold-ON merge gate is a NO-OP
**Dispatcher-verified in both tiers I could check.** This is the most consequential finding in the
review's gate analysis.

`--anf --fold-on` drives every tier through its `--ir` entry point, and **every `--ir` entry point
force-disables ANF constant folding regardless of the CLI flag.** So the gate is a byte-for-byte
duplicate of the fold-OFF gate sitting immediately above it in the same workflow — same mode, same
`--num 40`, same `--seed 424242`, same tier list.

I read both sides myself:
- `packages/runar-compiler/src/index.ts:611-619`, verbatim: *"Constant folding … is intentionally NOT
  run here on already-lowered ANF IR … **(opts.disableConstantFolding is accepted for CLI symmetry
  but is a no-op here.)**"*
- `compilers/go/compiler/compiler.go:188-192` — `disableFoldForIRInput` sets
  `o.DisableConstantFolding = true`, applied unconditionally at `CompileFromIR` and
  `CompileFromIRBytes`.

And the mode's own contract, which it does not keep
(`conformance/fuzzer/index.ts:395-398`): *"Run every tier with constant-folding **ENABLED** …
**Either mode must produce byte-identical hex across all tiers.**"*

**CL-BUG-182 is the defect this gate exists to catch, and cannot.**

...
job turns it on. Combined with CL-BUG-224:

| mode | tiers | ANF folder |
|---|---|---|
| `--anf`, incl. `--fold-on` | 7 | **never runs** |
| `--ir`, `--ir --stateful` | 7 | 

[CX-DOC-004] The option says folding is enabled by default and the function documentation says the path runs optional constant folding. The implementation intentionally never runs ANF folding and accepts `disableConstantFolding` solely for CLI symmetry. Callers cannot infer actual behavior from the public type and API documentation.

evidence.CX-DOC-004: Lines 549 and 573-575 promise optional folding; lines 611-619 state that folding is never run and the option has no effect.

remediation.CX-DOC-004: Remove or deprecate the ineffective option and document stack-level folding accurately, or implement equivalent safe ANF folding and DCE.

testable_assertion.CX-DOC-004: The documented default and `disableConstantFolding: true` modes must either exhibit the documented folding difference or the API must no longer expose the option.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-compiler/src/index.ts:611-619 — verbatim: "Constant folding is a source-pipeline optimization ... it is intentionally NOT run here on already-lowered ANF IR ... (opts.disableConstantFolding is accepted for CLI symmetry but is a no-op here.)" — self-documents the no-op. compilers/go/compiler/compiler.go:188-192 `disableFoldForIRInput` forces `DisableConstantFolding = true` unconditionally for `CompileFromIR`/`CompileFromIRBytes`, matching TS. conformance/fuzzer/index.ts:467-468 confirms `--anf` mode routes through 'all 7 tiers via --ir --hex', so the `--fold-on` flag (line 716: `disableConstantFolding: !opts.foldOn`) is passed into a pipeline that ignores it for every tier — the fold-on/-off runs of that specific gate are byte-identical duplicates for the TS/Go tiers, confirming CL-BUG-224's core claim for that gate. The public API doc is still wrong: `CompileFromANFOptions.disableConstantFolding`'s JSDoc (index.ts, just above `compileFromANF`) still reads "If true, skip the ANF constant folding pass. Default: false (folding enabled)." — this is false for this entry point; folding is NEVER run here regardless of the flag, and the doc comment doesn't say so (the explanation lives only in an inline implementation comment, not the public interface doc), confirming CX-DOC-004.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: accurate. Note for triage: commit 0c192829 ('fix(fold): skip ANF constant-fold on --ir input across all 7 tiers') shows the no-op was a deliberate, reasoned tradeoff to avoid a worse divergence (dead-binding accumulation vs. goldens/Zig parity), not an accidental oversight — but the public doc string was never updated to reflect that decision, and the fuzzer's fold-on gate is genuinely weakened as described.

items.testable_assertion_verified: The documented default and `disableConstantFolding: true` modes must either exhibit the documented folding difference when compiling a foldable ANF program through `compileFromANF`, or `CompileFromANFOptions.disableConstantFolding`'s public JSDoc must stop claiming folding is enabled by default for this entry point.

[CL-BUG-167] ## CL-BUG-167 — CRITICAL / P0 — `.runar.go`: `*= /= %= &= |= ^= <<= >>=` are silently discarded, and the Go tier turns *every* compound assignment into a plain assignment
**Dispatcher-verified on both tiers; the worker proved both by execution.**

**Rust tier.** `compilers/rust/src/frontend/parser_gocontract.rs:386-400`'s two-char operator table
has `+= -=` and not the rest; `parse_ident_statement` ends in a `_ =>` arm at `:1386-1389` that
returns an `ExpressionStatement` **with no diagnostic**, which I read. For `x := a; x *= 2;
runar.Assert(x == 8)` the emitted script never multiplies — exit 0, well-formed script, different
meaning from the source.

```
+=  -> OP_2 OP_OVER OP_SWAP OP_ADD OP_8 OP_NUMEQUAL OP_NIP   (correct)
*=  -> OP_2 OP_8 OP_ROT OP_SWAP OP_NUMEQUAL OP_NIP           (statement dropped)
/= %= &= |= ^= <<= >>=  -> identical to *=                   (statement dropped)
```

**Every other surface fails loudly** for operators it does not support — `.runar.ts` →
*"Unsupported compound assignment operator"*; `.runar.rs`, `.runar.sol`, `.runar.py` →
`Parse errors`. The silent drop is specific to the Go DSL.

**Go tier — worse, and I verified it.** `compilers/go/frontend/parser_gocontract.go:434` special-cases
only `token.DEFINE`; `grep -n "s.Tok" compilers/go/frontend/parser_gocontract.go` returns **exactly
two lines, 434 and 553**. So `x += 2` and `x *= 2` both become `AssignmentStmt{Target: x, Value: 2}`
— the operator is discarded and the RHS becomes the whole value:

| `.runar.go` body | Rust tier | Go tier | correct |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x := a; x += 2; Assert(x == 8)` | correct | `OP_2 OP_8 OP_NUMEQUAL` (= `2 == 8`, always false) | `a + 2 == 8` |
| `x := a; x *= 2; Assert(x == 8)` | `a == 8` | `OP_2 OP_8 OP_NUMEQUAL` | `a * 2 == 8` |

**Three different

verification.evidence: Go tier (compilers/go/frontend/parser_gocontract.go:433-458): `*ast.AssignStmt` handling checks `s.Tok == token.DEFINE` only (one `if`); every other token (`=`, `+=`, `-=`, `*=`, `/=`, `%=`, `&=`, `|=`, `^=`, `<<=`, `>>=`) falls through to the same `return AssignmentStmt{Target: p.convertExpression(s.Lhs[0]), Value: p.convertExpression(s.Rhs[0])}` — i.e. it takes the raw RHS literally and discards the operator entirely, so `x += 2` and `x *= 2` both compile to `x = 2`. `rg -n 's.Tok' compilers/go/frontend/parser_gocontract.go` returns exactly two lines (435, 554 — DEFINE and INC/DEC), confirming the finding's grep claim (off by one line vs. the cited 434/553 due to file growth). Rust tier (compilers/rust/src/frontend/parser_gocontract.rs): the TokenType enum (:225-284) and two-char lexer table (:424-449) define only PlusEq/MinusEq — no Star/Slash/Percent/Amp/Pipe/Caret/Shl/Shr 'Eq' variant exists at all, so `*=` lexes as separate `Star` then `Eq` tokens. Tracing `x *= 2`: parse_multiplicative (:1721-1734) consumes `x`, advances past `Star`, calls parse_unary on `Eq` which fails through parse_primary's `_ => None` (:2033-2035), propagating None up to `parse_ident_statement`'s initial `parse_expr()?` (:1357), which returns None without creating any statement. parse_block (:1219-1239) then does `else { self.advance() }` — 'skip unknown tokens to avoid infinite loop' — silently discarding the leftover `Eq`/`Number(2)`/etc. token-by-token with zero diagnostic; the stray `Number(2)` then re-parses as a no-op `ExpressionStatement`. Net effect matches the finding's description (compound-assignment semantics silently vanish, no diagnostic) though the exact code path (parse failure + generic resync, not a literal catch-all `_ =>` arm inside parse_ident_statement) differs from what CL-BUG-167 cited.
verification.tier_correction: This finding genuinely spans two tiers: compilers/go/frontend/parser_gocontract.go (Go tier, confirmed the worse case — ALL compound-assignment operators broken, not just the eight named) and compilers/rust/src/frontend/parser_gocontract.rs (Rust tier, the eight named operators only). The item's title leads with "Rust `.runar.go` parser" but is filed under tier "compiler:go"; both tier tags are defensible given the dual-tier evidence, but a strict single-tier split would put half of this finding under compiler:rust.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Go tier citation (grep count, line content) verified essentially verbatim (lines shifted by +1). Rust tier: the underlying silent-loss defect is confirmed for the same eight operators, but the specific mechanism cited (a `_ =>` catch-all arm in parse_ident_statement returning ExpressionStatement) is not what happens at HEAD for `*=` etc. — parse_expr fails outright and parse_block's generic token-skip resync discards the statement instead. Same user-facing outcome, different code path than described.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Parse a `.runar.go` source containing `x := 4n; x *= 2n; assert(x == 8n)` with (a) the Go compiler's frontend.ParseSource and (b) the Rust compiler's parse_source. Correct behavior: either reject with a clear diagnostic (matching the TS tier's 'Unsupported compound assignment operator') or lower `x *= 2n` to the equivalent of `x = x * 2n`. Today: Go emits `AssignmentStmt{Target: x, Value: 2n}` (i.e. `x = 2n`, discarding the multiply) with zero diagnostic; Rust silently drops the entire `x *= 2n;` statement (parse failure + resync) with zero diagnostic, leaving `x` at its original value going into the assert.

[CL-BUG-084] ## CL-BUG-084 — CRITICAL / P0 — `--ir` bypasses EVERY frontend safety gate, not just the SP1 one
**Dispatcher-verified.** Source: crypto:fri-field F2. **This is the most generalizable finding of the review** — the worker filed it as an SP1 issue and flagged the generalization itself; I confirmed the general form.

`frontend.Validate` is invoked at exactly five sites, all on the **source** path (`compilers/go/compiler/compiler.go:438, 493, 527, 659, 823` — every one inside a `CompileFromSource*` function). `CompileFromIR` (`:158`) → `CompileFromIRBytes` (`:168`) → `CompileFromProgram` (`:195`) reaches `codegen.LowerToStack` with **no validation whatsoever**, and `compilers/go/main.go:187` exposes it as `--ir`.

So every rule `frontend.Validate` enforces is bypassable by compiling from hand-written or `--emit-ir`-then-edited ANF JSON. From `validator.go`, that list includes:
- `checkNoRecursion()` (`:52`)
- `ValidateSighashUsage()` (`:59`) — the issue-#123 field-availability matrix
- the SP1-FRI unsoundness refusal (`:78`)
- `txPreimage` must not be declared (`:141`)
- mutable-property-requires-StatefulSmartContract (`:170`)
- `FixedArray` length must be positive (`:237`), property type must not be `void` (`:232`)

The SP1 gate's own comment states the intent it fails to achieve: *"Documenting an unsound verifier is not the same as preventing its deployment."* A flag defeats it.

**Remediation shape:** the check belongs in `CompileFromProgram` (or in the lowering keyed off a threaded option), not in the source-only frontend.

## CL-BUG-216 — HIGH / P0 — `--ir` emits a 2-byte anyone-can-spend script for a contract the validator rejects
**Proved at the CLI.** Same contract, two entry points:
```
$ runarc --source NoAssert.runar.ts --hex
Compilation error: validation errors:
  NoAssert.runar.ts:4:2: public method 'open' must end with an assert() call
$ runarc --ir noassert.ir.json --hex
```

parameter …"*, and the pass-4 refusal that
`branch_outputs_merged_locals_test.go:20-24` says existed because *"the locking script was

**Defect status flagged, not assumed.** The worker noted that this depends on whether `--ir` is an

as one while the project states no trust model for it. Correct ha

[CL-BUG-217] ## CL-BUG-217 — HIGH / P0 — `--ir` compiles the SP1-FRI verifier the frontend explicitly REFUSES, and the acknowledgement is not representable in ANF
**Proved at the CLI**, and the extension is the important part:
```
$ runarc --source Fri.runar.ts --hex          # no directive
Compilation error: verifySP1FRI: REFUSING to emit a known-unsound proof verifier …
  the locking script ACCEPTS forged Merkle openings — an attacker spends with a fabricated proof
$ runarc --source FriAck.runar.ts --emit-ir > fri.ir.json && grep -c acknowledge fri.ir.json
0
$ runarc --ir fri.ir.json --hex
007b7b7b756ba86b57795779…   exit 0, 248,560 bytes, stderr empty
```
`stampSP1FriAck` writes `ContractNode.AckUnsoundSP1Fri` on the **AST**, not on `ir.ANFProgram`.
**So the refusal cannot be re-armed on the `--ir` path even in principle** — there is nowhere in the
IR to carry the acknowledgement. The ~248 KB unsound verifier is emitted with no diagnostic and no
acknowledgement anywhere in its input.
`sp1_fri_negative_test.go:133-278` documents what that script does: three forged-proof cases are
rejected by the off-chain reference verifier and **ACCEPTED** by the compiled covenant.


[CL-GAP-005] | worker | CL ID | sev | prio | title |
| F-01 | CL-GAP-005 | CRITICAL | v1-blocker | `--ir` bypasses frontend.Validate entirely, including the SP1-FRI unsound-verifier REFUSAL and all sighash-usage validation |
conflicts: None between these three. Verified directly: read compilers/go/compiler/compiler.go:157-252 in both runar-review-claude-main@8937c1ad and runar-review-grok@2b3af765 (identical in both) — CompileFromIR/CompileFromIRBytes call ir.LoadIR(FromBytes) then CompileFromProgram, which runs applyConstructorArgs -> FoldConstants -> OptimizeEC -> LowerToStack -> Emit -> assembleArtifact with no call to frontend.Validate anywhere in that path. Note: CL-GAP-110 (kept separate, not merged here) states ir.LoadIR does run the loader's own ValidateIR — confirmed true (compilers/go/ir/loader.go: LoadIRFromBytes calls ValidateIR at line ~50) but that is a narrower structural check (non-empty names/types, binding referential sanity, loop-count DoS bound, known-kind enumeration) distinct from frontend.Validate's ~42 semantic checks (assert-required-at-end, checkNoRecursion, SP1-FRI unsound-verifier refusal, sighash-usage matrix, mutable-property-requires-Stateful, etc.). Not a contradiction — two different validators, both true statements about them.

verification.evidence: compilers/go/compiler/compiler.go: `frontend.Validate(` is called at exactly 4 sites (523, 602, 636, 777), all inside CompileFromSource*/ParseAndValidateOnly functions (source path only) — down from the 5 sites the finding cited at the reviewed commit, consistent with a later dedup, not a fix. `CompileFromProgram` (:249-304+, reached by both `CompileFromIR` and `CompileFromIRBytes`, and exposed via `--ir` at compilers/go/main.go:95/201) never calls frontend.Validate; it now only calls a narrow, SP1-FRI-specific re-guard, `guardUnsoundSP1FriIR` (:256-258), whose own comment (R-012) states plainly: 'the IR entry points never run frontend.Validate, so the verifySP1FRI soundness refusal has to be re-asserted here against the ANF observable.' Every OTHER rule frontend.Validate enforces — including the 'public method must end with an assert() call' check (validator.go:565-580, the exact rule CL-BUG-216's NoAssert.runar.ts example exploits) — is still unreachable on the --ir path, so CL-BUG-216's demonstration (a NoAssert-shaped IR compiling to a trivial/anyone-can-spend script via --ir) remains reproducible at HEAD.
verification.conflict_resolution: The item's own conflict note (direct read of compiler.go confirming no frontend.Validate call on the IR path) remains accurate in substance at HEAD, with one addition: R-012 (commit 9b4dce40, 'refuse the unsound SP1 FRI verifier on the --ir path') added a targeted, SP1-FRI-only re-guard (guardUnsoundSP1FriIR) inside CompileFromProgram. This closes the SP1-FRI-specific angle of CL-BUG-084/CL-BUG-216/CL-GAP-005 but is explicitly NOT a general frontend.Validate call, so the broader claim (and the concrete NoAssert reproduction, which has nothing to do with SP1) is still live.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate; call-site count for frontend.Validate is 4 at HEAD vs. 5 cited (drift, not a discrepancy in substance — all 4 remaining sites are still source-path only). The SP1-FRI-specific narrow fix (R-012) postdates the review and should be credited as a partial remediation, which the input's conflicts field does not yet reflect.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile NoAssert.runar.ts (a public method with no terminal assert()) via `--source` — refused with 'public method ... must end with an assert() call'. Emit its IR (`--emit-ir`) and recompile the same IR via `--ir <path>` (or `compiler.CompileFromIRBytes` directly): today this succeeds and emits a short, unconstrained locking script (no assert enforced) instead of reproducing the source-path refusal.

items.title: Go lowerForStatement never merges the loop body's addOutput/addRawOutput refs back into the parent context, so outputs inside a `for` escape the continuation hash
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-186] ## CL-BUG-186 — CRITICAL / P0 — `lowerForStatement` never merges the loop body's output refs back, so `addOutput`/`addRawOutput` inside a `for` escapes the continuation hash
**Runtime-proved.** `anf_lower.go:1654-1667` merges `bodyCtx`'s counter and not its
`addOutputRefs`/`addDataOutputRefs` — where `lowerIfStatement` explicitly registers the branch's
concat ref with the parent (`:1412-1418`). A stateful method with a top-level `addOutput` plus a
2-iteration loop of `addRawOutput` commits `cat(t12, t27)` — top-level output and change only. The
developer's per-iteration payouts are computed and then not committed to.

verification.evidence: compilers/go/frontend/anf_lower.go:1749-1778 (lowerForStatement, shifted from the reviewed commit's 1654-1667 by unrelated code growth) lowers the loop body into bodyCtx := ctx.subContext(), calls bodyCtx.lowerStatementsWithReads(...), then only ctx.syncCounter(bodyCtx) before emitting the 'loop' ANF node with Body: bodyCtx.bindings. It never calls bodyCtx.getAddOutputRefs()/getAddDataOutputRefs() nor forwards them via ctx.addOutputRef()/addDataOutputRef(). Contrast with lowerIfStatement at anf_lower.go:1361-1364 (thenCtx/elseCtx.getAddOutputRefs()) and the explicit forwarding at anf_lower.go:1518-1528. Each addOutput/addRawOutput call registers its ref onto whichever lowerCtx is active at that call site (anf_lower.go:2326-2378), which inside a for-loop body is the discarded bodyCtx — so those refs never reach methodCtx.addOutputRefs, the sole source feeding the continuation-hash construction at anf_lower.go:508-570. A loop-body addOutput/addRawOutput is computed (its ANFBinding exists, nested inside the loop node) but silently excluded from the auto-injected hashOutputs assertion, exactly as described.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Line numbers drifted from 1654-1667 to 1749-1778 due to unrelated intervening code, but the described mechanism (counter synced, output refs not) is exactly correct at HEAD.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile a stateful contract method with a top-level this.addOutput(sats, ...) followed by for (let i=0n; i<2n; i++) { this.addRawOutput(satsPerIter, scriptBytes); }. Build a spending tx whose actual outputs are [top-level output, iteration-0 addRawOutput, iteration-1 addRawOutput, change]. At HEAD, the auto-injected checkPreimage/hashOutputs assertion computes its expected hash from only [top-level output, change] — so a tx that omits or redirects the two per-iteration addRawOutput outputs still satisfies hashOutputs and the script accepts it, i.e. the loop payouts are unenforced and can be stolen/dropped by whoever constructs the spend. After the fix, hashOutputs must include all three outputs and a spend omitting the loop outputs is rejected.

items.title: Zig: a failed while→for merge in parser_zig.go silently drops the increment, freezing the loop variable

items.description:
[CL-BUG-199] # PASS C BATCH 2R WAVE 1 — impl-go-frontend (CL-BUG-182 … CL-BUG-199) and impl-python-frontend (CL-BUG-200 … CL-GAP-116)

**The strongest two reports of the review.** Both workers built their compilers into `/tmp` and
executed them, so most findings are runtime-proved rather than read. The Go worker states its
baseline plainly: *"`go test ./frontend/` is green — every defect below is invisible to the existing
suite."* The Python worker compiled **all 648 (fixture, format) pairs** and got 648/648
byte-identical against the goldens in both fold modes — so every finding it reports lives outside
the corpus, which is exactly why they survived.

**Verified.** 4 spot-checks on go-frontend and 4 on python-frontend, all exact.

...
## CL-BUG-199 — CRITICAL / P0 — Zig: a failed `while`→`for` merge silently drops the continue-expression, freezing the loop variable
Runtime-proved from the IR. `parser_zig.go:1069-1081` fires the merge only if the *last* body
statement is a `VariableDeclStmt` of the update target. When it fails, `IterVar` stays
`__while_no_init` and the developer's variable is an ordinary local **that nothing increments** —
`anf_lower.go:1650-1666` lowers only `stmt.Body`, never `stmt.Update`. Two sources differing only in
the order of two adjacent `var` declarations produce `sum = 10` and `sum = 0`. **Any intervening
statement between `var i` and the `while` triggers it.** Both exit 0 with empty stderr.

...
(Python string to EOF), CL-BUG-197 (Ruby `=begin`), CL-BUG-198 (`0b1010` → 0) and CL-BUG-199 (Zig
loop variable) are all live in the other eight.

verification.evidence: compilers/go/frontend/parser_zig.go:1224-1267 (parseWhileStatement) always builds a ForStmt with Init.Name='__while_no_init' and Update set to the parsed continue-expression. The merge in parseBlockStatements (parser_zig.go:1062-1082, matching cited 1069-1081) only rewrites Init to the developer's real VariableDeclStmt when that decl is literally the immediately preceding statement in the same block AND its name matches the Update's assignment target. Any intervening statement between var i=0; and the while breaks this and Init.Name stays '__while_no_init'. compilers/go/frontend/anf_lower.go's lowerForStatement (HEAD lines 1749-1778, reviewer's cited 1650-1666) never reads stmt.Update at all — Update is used ONLY by extractLoopStep to infer step direction, falling back to condition-based inference when Update isn't a simple Increment/Decrement shape (which it never is for a while-merged loop). There is no mechanism anywhere in anf_lower.go or stack.go that substitutes '__while_no_init' back to the developer's real variable name when the merge fails (grep confirms it appears only in parser_zig.go, never referenced/rewritten downstream). Diffed parser_zig.go against the CL@8937c1ad reviewed tree: byte-identical, confirming this is not code drift, just an unfixed pre-existing defect.
verification.tier_correction: Confirmed correct as-is: parser_zig.go lives under compilers/go/frontend/ and is the GO COMPILER's frontend parser for the '.runar.zig' SOURCE FORMAT (one of Rúnar's 9 input syntaxes), unrelated to the compilers/zig/ Zig-language compiler tier. tier=compiler:go is the right label; the title's bare word 'Zig' is misleading shorthand for the source format. Related to V325 (same lowerForStatement/loop-lowering neighborhood) but NOT the same bug: V325 is an ANF-lowering output-ref merge omission that is format-agnostic; V326 is a Zig-format PARSER heuristic that only misfires on .runar.zig while-loops whose merge fails, and would still misfire even if V325 were fixed.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Cited files and the described failure mode (silent Update drop on failed merge) are exactly right; only the line numbers for anf_lower.go shifted slightly (1650-1666 reviewed -> 1749-1778 HEAD) due to unrelated intervening code growth, and parser_zig.go:1069-1081 matches HEAD almost verbatim (now 1062-1082).

items.testable_assertion_verified: Parse and compile a .runar.zig contract method containing `var i: i64 = 0; var sum: i64 = 0; while (i < 5) : (i += 1) { sum = sum + i; }` (note the intervening `var sum` declaration between `var i` and the `while`, which breaks the body[len(body)-1]==loopTarget merge check). At HEAD, running/interpreting the compiled result yields sum=0 for every iteration (i is read as 0 five times); after the fix it yields sum=10 (0+1+2+3+4).

items.title: The SP1-FRI locking script enforces no proof property at all; the one binding it does emit is vacuous
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-085] ## CL-BUG-085 — CRITICAL / P0 — The SP1-FRI locking script enforces no proof property at all; the one binding it does emit is vacuous
**Dispatcher-verified.** Source: crypto:fri-field F1. Confirms the repo's own README disclosure — **and shows it understated**.

`EmitFullSP1FriVerifierBody`'s per-query loop, verified verbatim (`compilers/go/codegen/sp1_fri.go:488-494`):
```go
for q := 0; q < params.NumQueries; q++ {
    emitQueryIndexDerive(fs, tracker, logGlobalMaxHeight)
    // _fs_bits is on top — drop it (full per-query verify chain is in
    // follow-up; see notes above).
    tracker.toTop("_fs_bits")
    tracker.drop()
}
```
It samples each FRI query index and immediately discards it. I confirmed the nine per-query emitters exist but have **zero production call sites** — spot-checked four: `emitMerkleVerify` 0, `emitFriFoldRowConditional` 0, `emitFinalPolyHorner` 0, `emitReducedOpeningAccumulator` 0. All are reachable only from tests.

The worker built a 26-row off-chain-vs-script table. Net: the script emits **one SHA-256 equality plus (numRounds+1) proof-of-work gates**, and nothing else. Not emitted: input-batch MMCS verify, commit-phase MMCS verify, the colinearity fold, final-poly Horner equality, OOD equality, and every length/count consistency check.

Two respects in which it is **worse** than the README states:
1. **The one emitted binding is vacuous.** `SHA256(proofBlob) == SHA256(chunk₀‖…‖chunk₇)` compares two spender-supplied values, and the chunks are dropped immediately after (`:433-435`). The transcript inputs the verifier actually reads (`_obs_*`) are a separate push layer the hash never covers.

**Runtime-proved.** `compilers/go/frontend/parser.go:959-974` maps only `+= -= *= /= %=`;
`default: binOp = "+"` at `:972-973`. `&`, `|`, `^`, `<<`, `>>` are documented Rúnar operators

`<<=`, `>>=`, `|=`, `^=`, `**=` all emit `OP_ADD`. **No diagnostic in any case.**

items.title: Go's Python tokenizer lets an unterminated string literal run to EOF, silently swallowing whole guard statements
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-196] ## CL-BUG-196 — CRITICAL / P0 — Go's Python tokenizer lets an unterminated string literal run to EOF, silently swallowing whole guard statements
Runtime-proved and the most vivid finding in the report. A missing closing quote on
`tag: bytes = b"cafe` consumed the following `assert_(y < 5)` line into the literal. CPython:
`SyntaxError: unterminated string literal`. `runarc -parse-only`: **`parser ok`, exit 0.** The
emitted ASM contains `6173736572745f2879203c203529` — the ASCII of `assert_(y < 5)` — as *data*.
**The guard is gone from the deployed script.** Because `b"…"` hex-encodes arbitrary bytes, the
downstream ByteString hex validator never fires. `grep -c "unterminated" parser_python.go` → **0**.

...
  confirm CI would surface CL-BUG-196/197/198/199 and it will not: **that gate asserts only that
  `--parse-only` succeeds.** Every one produces `parser ok` with exit 0 while silently changing the
  program. *"The gate proves the parsers accept the same inputs, not that they agree on their
  meaning."*
- **"The fold-ON cross-tier step catches fold bugs" — does not hold for CL-BUG-182.** All four
  loop-bearing fixtures use exactly the `start:0, step:1` values the Go folder's defaults
  coincidentally restore, and the allowlist's skip list is empty — **the step passes for the wrong
  reason.**

...
That is a **per-frontend** defect and the corpus covers one frontend of nine — while CL-BUG-196
(Python string to EOF), CL-BUG-197 (Ruby `=begin`), CL-BUG-198 (`0b1010` → 0) and CL-BUG-199 (Zig
loop variable) are all live in the other eight.

verification.evidence: compilers/go/frontend/parser_python.go:168-238 — both the byte-string tokenizer (169-190, `b'...'`/`b\"...\"`) and the regular string tokenizer (193-238) loop `for i < len(source) && source[i] != quote { ... }` with no EOF/diagnostic path; `if i < len(source) { i++ }` is a silent no-op when the loop exited because it hit EOF rather than the closing quote, and the token is still emitted using whatever was scanned. `grep -c "unterminated" compilers/go/frontend/parser_python.go` = 0.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate — matches HEAD exactly; the grep evidence method the reviewer used (0 matches for 'unterminated') still holds.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Parse a Python-format Rúnar source containing `tag: bytes = b"cafe` followed by `assert_(y < 5)` on the next line, with no closing quote before EOF; parsing must fail with a diagnostic. Today `--parse-only` reports 'parser ok' and the assert statement's source text is silently absorbed into the byte-string literal's value.

[CL-BUG-197] ## CL-BUG-197 — CRITICAL / P0 — Ruby `=begin`/`=end` block comments are not lexed, so `=end` closes the class body and every later method is silently dropped
Runtime-proved. `parser_ruby.go:196-199` handles only `#`; `grep -n "=begin"` → no matches. `end` is
a keyword and the class-body loop terminates on it. A contract with a `=begin … =end` block between
two methods: `ruby -c` → `Syntax OK`; `runarc` → `methods: ['constructor', 'increment']`.
**`guarded_spend`, a public spending entry point, is gone. Exit 0, no diagnostic.** The converse also
holds: a `prop :ghost` written inside a block comment becomes a real property.

...
(Python string to EOF), CL-BUG-197 (Ruby `=begin`), CL-BUG-198 (`0b1010` → 0) and CL-BUG-199 (Zig
loop variable) are all live in the other eight.

verification.evidence: compilers/go/frontend/parser_ruby.go:176 only special-cases '#' line comments (rg for '=begin' across the file returns zero matches). The class-body loop (:788-836) treats any token that isn't 'prop'/'runar_public'/'params'/'def' as unknown and silently p.advance()s past it (:835 'Skip unknown tokens'), so a stray '=' from an '=end' line is skipped and the following 'end' keyword token then satisfies the loop's p.check(rbTokEnd) exit test (:788), terminating the class body early and dropping every method declared after the block comment, with no diagnostic.

items.description:
[CL-BUG-214] # impl-python-frontend — ADVERSARIAL ADDENDUM (the repaired seed's payoff) — CL-BUG-214, CL-BUG-215, CL-GAP-117

**This is what the seed repair bought.** The worker re-ran the adversarial mandate against all 28
now-legible breadth findings and adjudicated **26 of 28**, listing the two it did not reach. Two
findings escalated to CRITICAL, and — the part that matters most — **it corrected two of its own
earlier claims against its own interest.** Report re-persisted (95,048 chars).

**Verified.** 3 spot-checks, all exact: `anf_lower.py:2378-2395`, `ir/loader.py:28` + `:206-209`,
`validator.py:690-703`.

...
## CL-BUG-214 — CRITICAL / P0 — An `IndexAccessExpr` assignment on a non-FixedArray property is silently discarded and **ships a deployable script**
**The only defect confirmed in this partition that produces a wrong script rather than failing
closed**, which is why it outranks everything else the worker filed.

For a `StatefulSmartContract` with `blob: ByteString` and `this.blob[0] = 7n`:
```
validate : []          typecheck: []
update_prop emitted: False
COMPILED TO SCRIPT, bytes = 885
```
`_rewrite_assignment` has no `IndexAccessExpr` branch reaching `_make_update_prop`
(`anf_lower.py:2163`), and neither `validator.py:664-688` nor `typecheck.py` rejects the shape. The
write is computed and thrown away. **The deployed contract's state never changes**, and nothing —
not a gate, not a diagnostic, not a compile failure — says so.

verification.evidence: compilers/python/runar_compiler/frontend/anf_lower.py:1068-1082 (_lower_assignment): checks isinstance(stmt.target, PropertyAccessExpr) -> update_prop, isinstance(stmt.target, Identifier) -> rebind, and for 'other targets' (which includes IndexAccessExpr on a non-FixedArray property) just does `self.lower_expr_to_ref(stmt.target)` and returns -- the computed value is discarded, no update_prop emitted. Neither validator.py's _validate_statement (AssignmentStmt case, ~line 723) nor typecheck.py's AssignmentStmt case (~line 587, which types an IndexAccessExpr on a non-array-typed object as '<unknown>', the lattice top, so is_subtype always passes) reject the shape. Reproduced live: a StatefulSmartContract with `blob: ByteString` and method body `this.blob[0n] = 7n; assert(true);` compiles successfully (script emitted) with NO update_prop binding for 'blob' anywhere in the lowered ANF.
verification.reachable_by_adversary: false -- triggered by the contract's own source at compile time (an index-assignment onto a non-FixedArray property), not by adversarial runtime/witness input to an already-deployed contract. A dishonest contract author could however exploit this to write code that LOOKS like it updates a field but silently does not.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Fully accurate; anf_lower.py:2163 cited by the reviewer has since shifted to ~1068-1082 (_lower_assignment) after refactors, but the described defect and mechanism are exactly reproduced.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile a StatefulSmartContract with a non-FixedArray property `blob: ByteString` and a method body `this.blob[0n] = 7n; assert(true);`. This must either be rejected by validate/typecheck with a location diagnostic, or the lowered ANF for that method must contain an `update_prop` binding targeting `blob`. Currently: compilation succeeds and no `update_prop` binding for `blob` appears anywhere in the method body -- the write is silently discarded and the deployed contract's state never changes.

items.title: compile_from_ir / compile_from_ir_bytes skip _validate, _type_check, and _expand_fixed_arrays entirely, so IR input that the source path rejects (missing assert, write to a readonly property, unknown builtin call, ungated asm()) compiles into a deployable, anyone-can-spend script (python)

[CL-BUG-266] ## CL-BUG-266 — CRITICAL / P0 — `--ir` produces anyone-can-spend scripts from ANF the source path rejects
**Dispatcher-verified.** `compile_from_ir` and `compile_from_ir_bytes` both hardcode `disable_constant_folding=True` and call `compile_from_program`, which is fold → EC-opt → lower → peephole → emit. **`_validate`, `_type_check` and `_expand_fixed_arrays` appear only on the source path** (`compiler.py:494-506`) and are absent from `:441-472`. I read both.

| probe | `--ir` | `--source` |
|---|---|---|
| public method, no assert | **`script='51'` = `OP_TRUE`** | `public method 'unlock' must end with an assert() call` |
| `update_prop` on a **readonly** property | **`script=''` — empty locking script** | `cannot assign to readonly property 'owner'` |
| `call func:"totallyNotABuiltin"` | `script='00'` = OP_0 | rejected at parse |
| `raw_script bytes:"51"` | `script='51'`, **no `UnsafeSmartContract` gate** | `asm()` gated at `validator.py:454,581` |

**82 diagnostic sites bypassed** (37 in `validator.py` + 45 in `typecheck.py`, counted rather than estimated — the worker corrected the breadth pass's "~88" to a counted 82). Three more probes produce **raw `TypeError`/`RuntimeError`** instead of the documented `ValueError`, including `args:"t0"` where the string **was iterated character-by-character**.

verification.evidence: compilers/python/runar_compiler/compiler.py:442-450 (compile_from_ir / compile_from_ir_bytes) still call compile_from_program directly with no _validate/_type_check/_expand_fixed_arrays step -- those three passes remain source-path-only (compile_from_source_collecting_warnings:520-551). ir/loader.py's validate_ir (added since the review, lines 144-209 + _validate_bindings 261-420+) is now substantial -- it checks builtin call arity, add_output state-value count, empty raw_script bodies, negative/over-max loop counts, super() placement, and 'no public methods at all' -- but it does NOT check that a public method ends with an assert() call, and does NOT check update_prop against a property's readonly flag (grep for 'readonly' in loader.py matches only the add_output mutable_count computation, and update_prop appears only in the KNOWN_KINDS allowlist, line 42, with no semantic check). Reproduced live via `python -m runar_compiler --ir <file> --hex`: (1) a public method whose body is just `load_const true` with no assert compiles clean to script='51' (OP_TRUE, unconditionally spendable); (2) a readonly ByteString property `owner` receiving an update_prop in the IR compiles clean (script='04deadbeef5177') with no diagnostic.
verification.reachable_by_adversary: true -- the --ir entry point is an explicit external-input trust boundary (its own comments in loader.py describe closing exactly this class of gap for other checks); an adversary or buggy non-reference tool supplying crafted ANF JSON directly reaches this path and can mint an anyone-can-spend script or bypass a readonly-property guarantee, without ever going through the type-checked source frontend.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: The specific probes the reviewer ran (no-assert -> OP_TRUE, readonly write -> silent) both still reproduce verbatim at HEAD. The unknown-builtin-call and raw_script-without-gate probes from the same finding are now partially addressed (arity checking and empty-body rejection exist), so the finding is confirmed but narrower than originally scoped -- the assert-termination and readonly-write gates are the parts that remain open.

Currently (reproduced) it compiles to script='51'. (b) Compile `--ir` JSON containing an `update_prop` targeting a property declared `readonly: true`. This must be rejected. Currently (reproduced) it compiles clean with the write applied.

items.title: Python: `if`-branch lowering contexts do not inherit the parent's `renamed_params` map, so a `load_param` inside a branch cannot find a parameter renamed due to a parameter/property name collision and incorrectly rejects valid source
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.severity_note: upgraded: verifier traced a fail-OPEN path: a witness param read inside a branch resolves to stale on-chain state (batch 18); upgraded per §6.3 reachability
items.description: [CX-BUG-059] The parent context renames a parameter slot when it collides with mutable state, but branch contexts start with an empty `renamed_params` map. A `load_param` in a branch searches for the original name, cannot find the renamed witness slot, and rejects otherwise valid source.

evidence.CX-BUG-059: Renaming is recorded at lines 613-619 and consumed at lines 1191-1198; branch creation copies the stack but not `renamed_params` at lines 1787-1806.

remediation.CX-BUG-059: Propagate the immutable parameter-renaming map into every nested context.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-059: A method parameter sharing a mutable property name must remain readable inside both sides of an `if`.

verification.evidence: compilers/python/runar_compiler/codegen/stack.py:679-686 (self.renamed_params, populated only in _LoweringContext.__init__ from a 'params' arg) is never copied onto then_ctx/else_ctx (branch contexts are constructed with _LoweringContext(None, self.properties) -- params=None -- at ~lines 2003/2032). Reproduced live with instrumentation: compiled a StatefulSmartContract whose mutable property 'count' collides with method parameter 'count', read inside an if-branch. Trace confirms the TOP-LEVEL context renamed the parameter's stack slot to '__param_count' and recorded {'count': '__param_count'} in renamed_params, but the BRANCH context's renamed_params is {} (empty), so its _lower_load_param('count', ...) falls back to slot_name='count' and self.sm.has('count') resolves TRUE -- against the state-deserialized property slot (also literally named 'count', still on the cloned stack), NOT the witness parameter slot ('__param_count'). IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the finding's framing: the actual failure mode is NOT rejection of valid source (CX-BUG-059 says 'rejects otherwise valid source') -- compilation SUCCEEDS, but the branch silently reads the STALE PRE-CALL ON-CHAIN STATE VALUE instead of the caller-supplied witness parameter, which is a silent-wrong-value bug, arguably more severe than a compile-time rejection since it produces a plausible-looking but semantically wrong script with no diagnostic.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Root cause (missing renamed_params inheritance) is correct, but the described symptom is wrong: instrumented tracing shows this fails OPEN (silent wrong value from the stale state slot) rather than failing closed (a rejection), which is the more serious failure mode of the two.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile a StatefulSmartContract whose public method parameter shares a name with a mutable property and is read inside an if-branch; assert the branch reads the CALLER-SUPPLIED parameter value, not the pre-call on-chain state value of the same-named property (currently the branch's load_param silently resolves to the state slot because renamed_params is not inherited).

items.title: `py_convert_name` is non-injective: two distinct locals alias to one ANF binding, turning an always-false guard into an always-true one
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-201] ## CL-BUG-201 — CRITICAL / P0 — `py_convert_name` is non-injective: two distinct locals alias to one ANF binding, turning an always-false guard into an always-true one
**Dispatcher-verified by reading the function.** `parser_python.py:185-205`: `tmp` takes the
`len(parts) <= 1` early return and yields `"tmp"`; `tmp_` splits to `["tmp",""]`, the empty part is
skipped by `if part:` at `:203`, and it also yields `"tmp"`. Nothing checks for a collision.
Proved to ASM: a contract with `tmp = n+1`, `tmp_ = n+2`, `assert_(tmp == tmp_)` — source semantics
**always false** — compiles to `OP_DUP OP_1ADD OP_SWAP OP_2 OP_ADD OP_DUP OP_DUP OP_NUMEQUAL …`.
`OP_DUP OP_DUP OP_NUMEQUAL` compares a value with a copy of itself: **the guard always passes.**
And because `examples/python` runs contracts natively under CPython, the off-chain pytest oracle
sees the assertion *fail* while the deployed script *accepts*. Same class at `parser_rust.py:133`
and `parser_go.py:223`.

verification.evidence: Reproduced live: `python3 -c "from runar_compiler.frontend.parser_python import py_convert_name; print(py_convert_name('tmp'), py_convert_name('tmp_'))"` -> both 'tmp' (parser_python.py:170-201: 'tmp_'.split('_') -> ['tmp',''], the empty trailing part is skipped by `if part:`, no collision check). Also reproduced for Rust: `_snake_to_camel('tmp')` and `_snake_to_camel('tmp_')` in parser_rust.py:154-163 both return 'tmp' (identical split-and-skip-empty logic, used for local var names at parser_rust.py:926,991). Go tier's claim does NOT hold at HEAD: `_go_field_to_camel` (parser_go.py:262-271) only lowercases the first character and never splits on underscores, so 'tmp' and 'tmp_' stay distinct there -- the collision class does not exist in the Go-format parser.
verification.tier_correction: The `parser_go.py:223` citation does not hold at HEAD: that region is mid-way through the `_SPECIAL_BUILTINS`-style dict, and Go local-var naming (`_go_field_to_camel`) uses a different, non-colliding algorithm (lowercase-first-char only, no underscore-collapse). The defect is real for Python (`parser_python.py`) and Rust (`parser_rust.py`) format parsers only.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile a `.runar.py` (or `.runar.rs`) method that declares two locals `tmp` and `tmp_` with `assert_(tmp == tmp_)` where source semantics are always-false (e.g. `tmp = n+1; tmp_ = n+2`); the compiled script must NOT accept every spend -- i.e. it must not compile to `... OP_DUP OP_DUP OP_NUMEQUAL ...` comparing one binding against itself.
items.dispatcher_decision: R7: refuse collisions in all tiers (all identifier kinds); keep sum_->sum; new negative conformance fixture; Ruby mapping converges on the reference

items.title: A local with the same name as a property makes a later `this.<prop>` read resolve to the local (always-true guard) — all 7 tiers
items.origin: surfaced by F-017 attempt 2; dispatcher reproduced remediation-logs/F-017/probe/shadow/Sh.runar.ts -> 8b769c (OP_1ADD OP_DUP OP_NUMEQUAL) in TS, Go, Rust

commented-out backdoor in a `=begin … =end` block:

diagnostics.** Both failure modes fire at once: the commented-out method becomes the sole spending

items.title: Rust `.runar.go` parser: *= /= %= &= |= ^= <<= >>= are missing from the two-char operator table and silently become no-op expression statements
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-167] ## CL-BUG-167 — CRITICAL / P0 — `.runar.go`: `*= /= %= &= |= ^= <<= >>=` are silently discarded, and the Go tier turns *every* compound assignment into a plain assignment
**Dispatcher-verified on both tiers; the worker proved both by execution.**

**Rust tier.** `compilers/rust/src/frontend/parser_gocontract.rs:386-400`'s two-char operator table
has `+= -=` and not the rest; `parse_ident_statement` ends in a `_ =>` arm at `:1386-1389` that
returns an `ExpressionStatement` **with no diagnostic**, which I read. For `x := a; x *= 2;
runar.Assert(x == 8)` the emitted script never multiplies — exit 0, well-formed script, different
meaning from the source.

```
+=  -> OP_2 OP_OVER OP_SWAP OP_ADD OP_8 OP_NUMEQUAL OP_NIP   (correct)
*=  -> OP_2 OP_8 OP_ROT OP_SWAP OP_NUMEQUAL OP_NIP           (statement dropped)
/= %= &= |= ^= <<= >>=  -> identical to *=                   (statement dropped)
```

**Every other surface fails loudly** for operators it does not support — `.runar.ts` →
*"Unsupported compound assignment operator"*; `.runar.rs`, `.runar.sol`, `.runar.py` →
`Parse errors`. The silent drop is specific to the Go DSL.

**Go tier — worse, and I verified it.** `compilers/go/frontend/parser_gocontract.go:434` special-cases
only `token.DEFINE`; `grep -n "s.Tok" compilers/go/frontend/parser_gocontract.go` returns **exactly
two lines, 434 and 553**. So `x += 2` and `x *= 2` both become `AssignmentStmt{Target: x, Value: 2}`
— the operator is discarded and the RHS becomes the whole value:

| `.runar.go` body | Rust tier | Go tier | correct |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x := a; x += 2; Assert(x == 8)` | correct | `OP_2 OP_8 OP_NUMEQUAL` (= `2 == 8`, always false) | `a + 2 == 8` |
| `x := a; x *= 2; Assert(x == 8)` | `a == 8` | `OP_2 OP_8 OP_NUMEQUAL` | `a * 2 == 8` |

**Three different

verification.evidence: compilers/rust/src/frontend/parser_gocontract.rs:424-449 — the two-char operator table still has only `:=  ==  !=  <=  >=  &&  ||  +=  -=  ++  --  <<  >>`; `*= /= %= &= |= ^= <<= >>=` are absent, and the 'Three-char operators' block at :417-422 is a documented no-op placeholder (`let _ = three;`). For `x *= 2`, the tokenizer emits Star then Eq; `parse_multiplicative` (:1722-1736) consumes Star then calls `parse_unary`->`parse_postfix`->`parse_primary` (:1806) on the Eq token, whose match has no Eq arm and falls to the terminal `_ => None` (line ~2037), propagating None back up through `parse_ident_statement`'s `let lhs = self.parse_expr()?;` (:1357). `parse_statement` therefore returns None for the whole `x *= 2;` statement, and the caller `parse_block` (:1219-1237) silently does `self.advance()` (skip one token) with **no diagnostic pushed** and keeps parsing — so the statement is dropped token-by-token with exit 0. (Mechanism differs slightly from the review's claim that a catch-all arm inside parse_ident_statement returns an ExpressionStatement — the actual sink is parse_block's error-recovery skip — but the net effect the finding describes, a silently no-op'd compound assignment with no diagnostic, reproduces exactly.)
verification.reviewer_accuracy: line numbers shifted (:386-400 in review -> :424-449 at HEAD, due to intervening escape-sequence code added to the tokenizer) but the missing-operator claim and its silent-drop consequence are exactly confirmed by the current code

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile `.runar.go` source containing `x := a; x *= 2; runar.Assert(x == 8)` (with `a` bound to 4) through the Rust tier's Go-DSL frontend (compile_from_source_str_with_options, file name ending .runar.go). Today this exits 0 and the emitted script never multiplies (the `*= 2` statement is silently skipped, so the assert reduces to `a == 8`, i.e. always false for a=4, or worse, silently wrong for other operands). The fix must either emit a diagnostic for the eight missing compound-assignment operators or lower them correctly; the failing test asserts the compiled script's behaviour matches `a*2==8`, not `a==8`.

items.title: The auto-injected stateful continuation conserves no value: `_newAmount`/`_changeAmount`/`_changePKH` are spender-supplied witness values never checked against the preimage's true input amount
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-079] ## CL-BUG-079 — CRITICAL / P0 — The auto-injected continuation conserves no value
**Dispatcher-verified in source.** Source: crypto:sighash SH-02 — found while trying to *refute* CL-BUG-078, and independent of it.

`_newAmount`, `_changePKH` and `_changeAmount` are all injected witness parameters. The preimage carries the input's true `amount`, and the compiler **extracts it and throws it away** — `packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/05-stack-lower.ts:3202`, verified verbatim:
```ts
// Consume preimage ref (no longer needed — we use _codePart and _newAmount).
... this.emitOp({ op: 'drop' });
// Step 1: Convert _newAmount to 8-byte LE and save to altstack.
```
Nothing compares `_newAmount` to the preimage's amount. So `_newAmount = 1`, `_changeAmount = inputSats − 1 − fee`, `_changePKH = attackerPKH` produces a transaction whose `hashOutputs` matches the covenant's own construction exactly, **the state advances correctly** (so every off-chain state assertion passes), and the balance lands in the attacker's P2PKH. No `_codePart` substitution needed; the contract chain even survives holding 1 satoshi.

The repo already names this exact exploit shape — `sighash-validate.ts:166-178` rejects it under `SIGHASH_SINGLE`: *"a spender sets `_newAmount` to dust, drives the change output to zero, and APPENDS a draining output."* The reasoning stops one step short: under the default `ALL|FORKID` the spender cannot *append* an output, but does not need to — **the committed change output is the drain.** Committing to an output set the spender chose is not value conservation.

**No test constructs this.** The two continuation-satoshis suites prove the *opposite* direction (that an honest explicit amount is respected); `TestCounter_WrongStateHash_Rejected` tampers the state value, not the

verification.evidence: packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/05-stack-lower.ts:3552-3554 (lowerComputeStateOutput, current HEAD): the preimage is dropped ('Consume preimage ref (no longer needed — we use _codePart and _newAmount)') with no comparison against `_newAmount`. `_newAmount`/`_changeAmount`/`_changePKH` remain plain caller-supplied method parameters (packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/04-anf-lower.ts:324-333,472) with no on-chain amount-conservation check anywhere in stack-lower.ts, side-effect-summary.ts, or sighash-validate.ts (which only guards the SIGHASH_SINGLE mutate-only case at :162-188 — not the default ALL-mode committed-change-output drain CL-BUG-079 describes). No commit or test references compiler-codegen-level value conservation for the auto-injected continuation.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate — code citation (05-stack-lower.ts:3202 in the review, now :3552-3554 due to line drift) and mechanism both verified exactly as described; no mitigation found anywhere in the pipeline.

items.description:
[CL-BUG-060] - **CL-BUG-060 (CRITICAL) — `bound_is_const` is set by 1 of 9 Zig parsers; it defaults to `true`.**
  I counted occurrences myself:
      parse_ts 3 | parse_sol 0 | parse_move 0 | parse_go 0 | parse_rust 0
      parse_python 0 | parse_zig 0 | parse_ruby 0 | parse_java 0
  And read the field's own documentation at `compilers/zig/src/ir/types.zig:244-248`:
      "The Zig parsers collapse the bound to a concrete i64 (defaulting to 0), so a runtime
       bound (`i < this.x`) or an identifier bound (`i < N`) would otherwise silently become a
       0-iteration loop. When false, the validator rejects the loop..."
  with `bound_is_const: bool = true` at `:251`. The guard was designed, documented, and then
  wired up in exactly one of nine parsers. On the other eight surfaces a runtime-bounded loop
  compiles to a loop body that is **dropped entirely from the locking script, with no diagnostic**.
  This is a safety mechanism that exists on paper and is inert in practice.
- **CL-BUG-061 (CRITICAL) — Zig `reverseBytes` emits ZERO opcodes.** Verified at

  `compilers/zig/src/passes/parse_move.zig:

[CL-BUG-106] ## CL-BUG-106 — CRITICAL / P0 — Zig tier: a non-literal for-loop bound silently becomes a ZERO-iteration loop in 8 of 9 formats

`ForStmt.bound_is_const` exists to reject a bound the parser could not resolve. Its own doc comment (`compilers/zig/src/ir/types.zig:244-251`) names the hazard verbatim:
> *"a runtime bound (`i < this.x`) or an identifier bound (`i < N`) would otherwise **silently become a 0-iteration loop**. When false, the validator rejects the loop… **Defaults to true so unrelated construction sites and format parsers stay literal-bounded by default.**"*

[CL-BUG-198] ## CL-BUG-198 — CRITICAL / P0 — Zig and Python: `0b…` / `0o…` literals silently evaluate to `0`
Runtime-proved in Zig by the worker. `runar.assert(amount > 0b1010)` → `OP_DUP OP_0 OP_GREATERTHAN`;
control `> 10` → `OP_DUP OP_10`. `0o17` likewise → `OP_0`. **A dust or threshold guard written in
binary or octal compiles to `> 0`.** The decimal scanner stops at `b`, and the stray `b1010`
identifier is absorbed as a call argument. In Python the stray identifier is caught at stack
lowering — but `--parse-only`, the mode the all-tier matrix runs, passes.

...
(Python string to EOF), CL-BUG-197 (Ruby `=begin`), CL-BUG-198 (`0b1010` → 0) and CL-BUG-199 (Zig
loop variable) are all live in the other eight.

verification.evidence: The reviewer's own reproduction (against Zig) and the Python half both check out in code that is NOT compiler:go. compilers/zig/src/passes/parse_zig.zig's tokenizer (fn next, ~163-166) only recognises decimal digits for `.number` tokens (no 0x/0b/0o special-casing), and its literal parser (~1305-1308) does `std.fmt.parseInt(i64, tok.text, 10)` unconditionally base-10, so `0b1010` tokenizes as '0'+'b1010' and evaluates to 0. compilers/zig/src/passes/parse_python.zig (Zig tier's Python-format parser) handles `0x`/`0X` (~277-278) but not 0b/0o. compilers/python/runar_compiler/frontend/parser_python.py:381-393 handles 0x but not 0b/0o, matching 'In Python the stray identifier is caught at stack lowering' from the finding.
verification.tier_correction: The reviewer's demonstrated defect lives in compiler:zig (both its zig-native and python-format parsers) and compiler:python, not compiler:go. Go's .runar.ts parsing uses tree-sitter, which handles 0b/0o/0x correctly. That said, Go's OWN hand-rolled Python-format tokenizer (compilers/go/frontend/parser_python.go:241-251) independently has an even broader instance of this defect class (no radix-prefix handling at all, not even 0x) -- so compiler:go is not simply an irrelevant bucket, it just isn't where the cited evidence points.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate for both Zig and Python; the only inaccuracy is this batch's tier bucketing (compiler:go).

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile a Zig-native (.runar.zig) SmartContract containing `runar.assert(amount > 0b1010)`; assert the emitted script compares against 10, not 0. A parallel test in compilers/python/runar_compiler with the same literal in a .runar.py source should assert stack-lowering computes 10, not fail on an undefined `b1010` reference (or silently 0 under --parse-only-only tooling).

[CL-BUG-071] ## CL-BUG-071 — CRITICAL — GorillaPool satoshi/BTC magnitude heuristic, shared by ≥5 SDK tiers, with tests pinning it
**Dispatcher-verified.** Convergent: sdk:go F-GO-04 + sdk:rust R-02 independently.

Every tier decodes a tx output value with the same magnitude guess: `value < 1000 → treat as BTC → *1e8`.

- `packages/runar-sdk/src/providers/gorillapool.ts:100-102`  **(TS reference tier)**
- `packages/runar-go/sdk_gorillapool.go:138-142`
- `packages/runar-java/.../sdk/GorillaPoolProvider.java:237-238,246` — comment: *"Mirror the Go SDK heuristic: < 1000 means BTC."*
- `packages/runar-rb/lib/runar/sdk/gorillapool_provider.rb:56`
- `packages/runar-py` — behaviour confirmed via `tests/test_gorillapool_provider.py:88`
- Rust: `packages/runar-rs/src/sdk/gorillapool.rs:272-281`

GorillaPool is the **1-sat ordinals** provider. `1 < 1000`, so a genuine 1-satoshi output — its defining case, and the default for `deploy_with_wallet` — decodes as **100,000,000 satoshis**. Every output from 1..999 sats is inflated by 1e8. The value flows into `currentUtxo.Satoshis` → fee arithmetic → the BIP-143 preimage `amount` field, so the preimage cannot match and the spend fails.

Two aggravating facts I verified directly:
1. **The defect was propagated deliberately**, not independently rediscovered: the Java comment names the Go SDK as the source.
2. **The tests pin the wrong behaviour rather than catching it** — `sdk_gorillapool_test.go:59` (`// fractional BSV (< 1000) → scaled by 1e8`, value `0.005`) and `test_gorillapool_provider.py:88` (`# value < 1000 -> treated as BTC`). Both assert the heuristic is correct. No test in any tier uses `value: 1`.

Why no gate sees it: this is the review's recurring failure mode in its purest form. Cross-tier parity is *satisfied* — all tiers agree, becau

verification.evidence: packages/runar-go/sdk_gorillapool.go:141-144: `if val < 1000 { satoshis = int64(math.Round(val * 1e8)) }` — a genuine 1-satoshi output (val=1) is misclassified as fractional BTC and inflated to 100,000,000 satoshis. packages/runar-go/sdk_gorillapool_test.go:59 and packages/runar-py/tests/test_gorillapool_provider.py:88 both assert the heuristic as correct (pin it rather than catch it); neither uses value:1. packages/runar-java/src/main/java/runar/lang/sdk/GorillaPoolProvider.java:237-246 carries the identical `< 1000` heuristic with a comment crediting the Go SDK as the source.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate; line numbers, the propagation-not-rediscovery claim (Java comment crediting Go), and the tests-pin-the-bug claim all check out.

items.testable_assertion_verified: GorillaPool provider's UTXO/output decoder given value=1 (the defining case for a 1-sat ordinal, and deploy_with_wallet's default) must report Satoshis==1; today it reports 100000000.

items.title: Zig contract-runtime percentOf divides by 100 instead of 10000 (basis points), diverging from every other tier and from Zig's own ANF interpreter
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.severity_note: upgraded: Zig native percentOf divides by 100 not 10000 — 100x financial miscalculation reachable from shipped contracts (batch 48)
items.description:
[CL-BUG-104] ## CL-BUG-104 — P0 — Zig contract-runtime `percentOf` divides by 100 instead of 10000
**Dispatcher-verified verbatim.** Source: sdk-zig depth NEW-01.

`packages/runar-zig/src/builtins.zig:476`: `return @divTrunc(checkedMul(value, percentage), 100);`

Canonical semantics are basis points — `/10000` — fixed independently in `05-stack-lower.ts:4481` (*"Lower percentOf(amount, bps) — (amount * bps) / 10000"*), `constant-fold.ts`, and the Zig compiler's own folder test. The Zig **ANF interpreter in the same package** divides by 10000 correctly. So the two halves of the Zig tier disagree with each other by **100×**, and this is the mock every native `.runar.zig` contract test links against.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-zig/src/builtins.zig:541-543: `pub fn percentOf(value, percentage) base.Bigint { return @divTrunc(checkedMul(value, percentage), 100); }` still divides by 100. Canonical basis-point semantics (`/10000`) are confirmed current at packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/05-stack-lower.ts:5218 ("Lower percentOf(amount, bps) — (amount * bps) / 10000") and are what the Zig tier's OWN ANF interpreter implements at packages/runar-zig/src/sdk_anf_interpreter.zig:1572-1575 (`@divTrunc(a *% b, 10000)`). `builtins.percentOf` is reachable from real native contracts: examples/zig/math-demo/MathDemo.runar.zig:17 and examples/zig/function-patterns/FunctionPatterns.runar.zig:49 both call `runar.percentOf(amount, feeBps)`, and `packages/runar-zig/src/root.zig:182` exports `pub const percentOf = builtins.percentOf;` as the public `runar` namespace symbol those contracts use.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate — cited line (builtins.zig:476 in the report vs :542 at current HEAD, file has shifted but content matches verbatim: `@divTrunc(checkedMul(value, percentage), 100)`), and the claim that the Zig tier's own ANF interpreter disagrees with its native builtins.zig by 100x is independently verified true.

items.testable_assertion_verified: In packages/runar-zig (builtins test file), add: call `builtins.percentOf(10000, 250)` and assert it equals `250` (10000 * 250 / 10000, canonical basis-point semantics — 250 = 2.5% of 10000). At HEAD this returns `25000` (10000 * 250 / 100), a 100x divergence, so the test fails until builtins.zig:542 is changed from `/ 100` to `/ 10000`.

items.title: Go Groth16 MSM public-input-binding scalar ladder does not reduce the attacker-supplied scalar mod r, unlike the sibling generic G1 scalar-mul ladder
items.confidence_note: raised by CL+GK; silent-but-inspected: none; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-039] | worker | CL ID | sev | prio | title |
| F4 | CL-BUG-039 | HIGH | v1-blocker | Go: the Groth16 MSM-binding ladder does not reduce the attacker-supplied public-input scalar; its sibling ladder does |

[GK-BUG-008] EmitBN254G1ScalarMul reduces k mod r before the +3r trick because the trick is only sound for k in [0,r-1] and Groth16 public inputs are attacker-chosen. emitG1ScalarMulNamed used by WA MSM copies pub_i and adds 3r with no reduce. Off-chain computePreparedInputs does reduce mod r, so SDK-honest pub=r and on-chain unreduced ladder disagree. Adversarial worker: scalar-domain test describes k=r → -2G for this ladder and then only tests the reduced builtin.

evidence.GK-BUG-008: Opened emitG1ScalarMulNamed at bn254_groth16.go:2117-2141: copy scalar, three OP_ADD of r, no bn254EmitScalarReduce. Contrast EmitBN254G1ScalarMul reduce-then-+3r at bn254.go:1158-1205.

remediation.GK-BUG-008: Call bn254EmitScalarReduce on each MSM pub_i before the +3r ladder. Add k=r test on emitWAGroth16MSMBind.

testable_assertion.GK-BUG-008: emitWAGroth16MSMBind with pub_0=r must bind as the zero term (or abort), matching Fr reduction; today the unreduced ladder is a different point.

verification.evidence: compilers/go/codegen/bn254_groth16.go:2078-2152 (emitG1ScalarMulNamed) copies scalarName straight into the +3r ladder (lines 2089-2102) with NO call to bn254EmitScalarReduce anywhere in the function. Its sibling compilers/go/codegen/bn254.go:1392-1420 (EmitBN254G1ScalarMul) explicitly calls bn254EmitScalarReduce(t, "_k", "_kr") at line 1403 before the identical +3r trick, with a comment (1349-1356) explaining the reduce is required because in Groth16 the scalars are caller-supplied PUBLIC INPUTS and the domain is attacker-chosen. emitWAGroth16MSMBind (bn254_groth16.go:1932-2049) calls emitG1ScalarMulNamed directly on the witness-pushed pub_i scalars (line 1984) with no reduction anywhere upstream. computePreparedInputs (off-chain SDK) reduces pub_i mod r per the finding; the on-chain ladder does not, so a prover/verifier disagreement is possible whenever pub_i >= r.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Function names correct as given (EmitBN254G1ScalarMul, emitG1ScalarMulNamed, emitWAGroth16MSMBind all exist verbatim); code identical at CX/GK reviewed commit 2b3af765 (spot-checked emitG1ScalarMulNamed there — same missing-reduce shape).

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile the SP1 Groth16 MSM-bind fixture. Drive it with pub_0 = curveR (BN254 Fr order) and pub_1..4 = 0, using a prover-computed prepared_inputs honestly derived off-chain as if pub_0 were reduced to 0 (computePreparedInputs(pub_0=r) == computePreparedInputs(pub_0=0) == IC[0]). Assert emitWAGroth16MSMBind rejects this witness (its unreduced ladder walks pub_0=r through 255 double-and-add iterations, landing on a different point than IC[0]) even though the off-chain SDK considers pub_0=r and pub_0=0 equivalent — i.e. on-chain/off-chain binding disagree for any pub_i >= r.

items.title: Java: ExpandFixedArrays rebuilds every method through the 5-arg MethodNode constructor, silently resetting sighashType to null (default ALL|FORKID) whenever a contract has a FixedArray property
items.confidence_note: raised by CL+CX; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-243] ## CL-BUG-243 — MEDIUM-HIGH / P1 — Java's `ExpandFixedArrays` drops `sighashType` AFTER the security-core validator has already approved the method
Source: impl-java-main NEW-02. **Ninth `@sighash` defect, and the sharpest ordering yet.**
`Cli.java:126` runs `Validate.run` — which folds in `SighashValidate`, the pass its own javadoc calls
*"SECURITY CORE"* — and only then, at `Cli.java:142`, runs `ExpandFixedArrays`, whose
`rewriteMethod` uses the 5-arg `MethodNode` constructor that defaults `sighashType` to `null`.
`AnfLower` then finds `null`, emits the default ALL|FORKID, and **skips the sighash pin entirely.**
**The author's declared mode is validated, then discarded, then replaced with a different one, with
no diagnostic.**
The worker also **corrected breadth's `embedAlways` half**: non-`FixedArrayType` properties pass
through unchanged, so `embedAlways` is lost only on the synthetic scalar siblings of a FixedArray
property that itself carried the directive — narrower than reported.


[CX-BUG-037] Expanded scalar siblings are constructed with the six-argument compatibility constructor, which forces `embedAlways=false`. An otherwise unreferenced readonly fixed array marked `@embedAlways` can therefore be removed despite the explicit retention directive.

evidence.CX-BUG-037: `expandPropertyRoot` propagates readonly and location but not `embedAlways`; the `PropertyNode` overload sets it false. ANF lowering only injects retention loads for fields whose `embedAlways()` remains true.

remediation.CX-BUG-037: Propagate the root property's `embedAlways` flag through every nested scalar expansion.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-037: An unreferenced readonly `FixedArray` annotated `@embedAlways` must retain constructor placeholders for every expanded slot after optimization.
