items.title: --emit-ir's _IR_EXCLUDED_FIELDS drops synthetic_array_chain (and parent_class), so FixedArray state-field grouping and parentClass are lost across an --emit-ir -> --ir round trip even though the resulting script hex stays byte-identical
items.confidence_note: raised by CL+CX; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-268] ## CL-BUG-268 — HIGH / P1 — `--emit-ir` → `--ir` loses FixedArray grouping and `parentClass`, with byte-identical hex
**Dispatcher-verified.** `__main__.py:299-309` `_IR_EXCLUDED_FIELDS` drops **both** `synthetic_array_chain` and `parent_class` — and the code comments say it is deliberate, *"so it never affects cross-tier ANF parity."*
```
TicTacToe:  hex identical: True
  SRC stateFields: [playerO, board/FixedArray<bigint,9>, turn, status]
  IR  stateFields: [playerO, board__0 … board__8 (9 separate scalars), turn, status]
  SRC parentClass='StatefulSmartContract'   IR parentClass=''
```
**The locking script is byte-identical, so a hex-only conformance check can never see this.** The divergence is entirely in the state schema the SDK ingests. The worker found a **second, independent** break: even un-excluded, `_snake_key` has no mapping, so it would serialize as `synthetic_array_chain` while the loader reads `__syntheticArrayChain` — **the loader's read path is dead code today.**

This is the sharpest instance yet of a theme running through the whole review: **byte-identical hex is not the same as a correct artifact**, and the conformance gate only checks the hex.


[CX-BUG-070] `--emit-ir` intentionally removes `synthetic_array_chain`, but artifact assembly relies on that chain to regroup scalar leaves into FixedArray state fields. The IR decoder knows how to ingest `__syntheticArrayChain`, demonstrating that the round-trip carrier exists, yet the CLI never emits it.

evidence.CX-BUG-070: `_IR_EXCLUDED_FIELDS` contains `synthetic_array_chain`; artifact assembly reads it at `compiler.py:709`; the decoder accepts `__syntheticArrayChain` at `ir/types.py:421`.

remediation.CX-BUG-070: Define a canonical cross-tier FixedArray metadata field and preserve it across source-to-IR-to-artifact compilation, or reconstruct it losslessly from canonical type information.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-070: Compiling a stateful FixedArray contract directly and via `--emit-ir` followed by `--ir` must yield identical grouped `stateFields` and constructor ABI metadata.

conflicts: none — verified __main__.py:299-309 is byte-identical between the CL review tree and the GK/CX review tree: both synthetic_array_chain and parent_class are in _IR_EXCLUDED_FIELDS with comments confirming the exclusion is deliberate for cross-tier ANF parity.

verification.evidence: Of the two claims bundled in this finding, one is fixed and one remains open. FIXED: `synthetic_array_chain` is no longer unconditionally excluded from --emit-ir -- __main__.py:401-402 now skips it only when empty (omitempty-style, matching Go/Rust), and it round-trips correctly. Reproduced live: a stateful FixedArray<bigint,3> contract's `--source --hex` and `--source --emit-ir` -> `--ir --hex` scripts are byte-identical, AND `--output` artifact JSON's stateFields for both paths show the grouped name 'board' (not exploded board__0..board__2) on both the source and IR-round-trip artifacts. STILL BROKEN: `parent_class` remains in _IR_EXCLUDED_FIELDS (__main__.py:324-329, comment 'Excluded from --emit-ir so it never affects cross-tier ANF parity' -- unchanged). Reproduced live: same contract's source-path artifact has `parentClass: 'StatefulSmartContract'`, its --emit-ir->--ir round-trip artifact has `parentClass: None` -- the SDK-facing artifact loses which base class the contract extends, exactly as CL-BUG-268 described.
verification.fixed_by: 2c05685d "N-095: one spelling for syntheticArrayChain, and make every tier read it back" (fixed the FixedArray-grouping half only; parent_class exclusion is untouched)
verification.reachable_by_adversary: false -- a build-pipeline/tooling fidelity gap (an --emit-ir/--ir round trip silently drops which base class a contract extends), not an attacker-input security defect, though it could cause an SDK consuming the round-tripped artifact to misclassify a stateful contract as stateless.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate at the reviewed commit for both halves; at HEAD the FixedArray-grouping half is fixed but the parentClass half the finding also documented is unchanged, so the finding survives in narrowed form.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile a StatefulSmartContract with an inline-initialized FixedArray property directly (`--source --hex` / `--output`) and via the round trip (`--source --emit-ir` then `--ir --hex` / `--output`). Both paths must produce identical script hex (now true) AND identical `parentClass` in the artifact JSON. Currently (reproduced) parentClass is 'StatefulSmartContract' on the direct path and null/absent on the round-trip path.

sweep1.evidence: compilers/python/runar_compiler/__main__.py:324-329 _IR_EXCLUDED_FIELDS still contains "parent_class". Probe on examples/ts/tic-tac-toe/TicTacToe.runar.ts: direct `--source --output` vs `--source --emit-ir` then `--ir --output`: hex eq True, parentClass 'StatefulSmartContract' (direct) vs None (round-trip).

items.title: A malformed `@sighash` directive (e.g. missing whitespace, trailing punctuation) is silently treated as "no directive" and defaults to ALL|FORKID
items.confidence_note: raised by CL+CX; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.severity_note: reviewers disagreed ['HIGH', 'MEDIUM']; highest taken per §6.2 (no downgrade justified at combination time)
items.description:
[CL-BUG-174] | ID | tier | defect |
| CL-BUG-174 | Rust (TS surface) | a malformed directive (`@sighash:` / `@sighash=`) is silently ignored on `.runar.ts` while the same text is fail-closed rejected on the other eight surfaces — and a silently-dropped directive also skips the whole security-core pass |

[CX-BUG-086] The parser detects the `@sighash` marker, but the extractor returns `None` for malformed syntax such as missing whitespace or punctuation outside its restricted character class. `parse_sighash_on_method` treats that `None` as “no directive,” silently selecting the default mode. A contract author writing `@sighash SINGLE|FORKID!` can therefore deploy a materially different covenant without an error.

evidence.CX-BUG-086: `directive_present` returns true for the marker, while `extract_sighash_directive` returns `None` at lines 145-153; the caller maps `None => None` at lines 488-496. Searches found tests for unknown valid-token flags and missing FORKID, but none for malformed recognized markers.

remediation.CX-BUG-086: Once `directive_present` succeeds, require extraction to produce `Some`; otherwise issue a malformed-directive diagnostic.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-086: Parsing a public method annotated `/** @sighash SINGLE|FORKID! */` must return an error and no contract suitable for compilation.

verification.evidence: compilers/rust/src/frontend/sighash_directive.rs:117-152 `extract_sighash_directive` still returns `None` (not an error) both when the character immediately after `@sighash` is not whitespace (:139-141) and when the segment contains any character outside `[A-Za-z0-9_|\s]` (:142-147) — e.g. a trailing `!` as in `@sighash SINGLE|FORKID!`. compilers/rust/src/frontend/parser.rs:487-495 `parse_sighash_on_method` still has `None => None` (no error pushed) for exactly that return value, silently falling back to the default ALL|FORKID mode. `directive_present` (parser.rs:413-426), which gates entry into this path, only checks that the `@sighash` marker substring exists with a word boundary — it does not validate the rest of the directive.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: citations (parser.rs:409-497, sighash_directive.rs:119-155) closely match current parser.rs:413-495 and sighash_directive.rs:117-152; fully accurate, defect unchanged

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile a `.runar.ts` contract whose public method is annotated `/** @sighash SINGLE|FORKID! */` (trailing `!`, a deliberately malformed but human-plausible typo) through the Rust tier. Today this silently compiles with the default ALL|FORKID mode and no diagnostic — a materially weaker covenant than the author intended. The fix must make `parse_sighash_on_method` push an error when `directive_present` finds the marker but `extract_sighash_directive` fails to parse a well-formed flag list, instead of collapsing that case into 'no directive'.

items.title: WhatsOnChain provider's `getUtxos` returns an empty locking script (`script: ''`), which flows unchecked into BIP-143 `scriptCode` signing across six SDK tiers, producing signatures no real `OP_CHECKSIG` can accept
items.confidence_note: raised by CL+GK; silent-but-inspected: none; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-072] ## CL-BUG-072 — HIGH — WhatsOnChain `getUtxos` returns an empty locking script; signatures are computed over an empty scriptCode
**Dispatcher-verified.** Convergent: sdk:go F-GO-03 + sdk:rust R-01 independently.

Verified present in five tiers, each with the same explanatory comment:
- `packages/runar-sdk/src/providers/woc.ts:118-124` (TS reference)
- `packages/runar-go/sdk_woc_provider.go:184`
- `packages/runar-rs/src/sdk/woc_provider.rs:125`
- `packages/runar-py/runar/sdk/woc_provider.py:113`
- `packages/runar-rb/lib/runar/sdk/woc_provider.rb:103`

The empty string is passed unchecked into the signer as the BIP-143 `scriptCode` (Go: `sdk_contract.go:412`; Rust: `contract.rs:473-475`), producing a signature over a zero-length scriptCode that no P2PKH `OP_CHECKSIG` can accept. WhatsOnChain is the only shipped mainnet provider in several tiers.

Each tier also carries a `MAX_SCRIPT_BYTES` DoS guard immediately below that `continue`s on an empty script — so the guard is **unconditionally dead** (sdk:rust R-25). The author noticed the empty script without following through to the signing consequence.

NOT verified for Java: `WhatsOnChainProvider.java:136` is in `getTransaction`, which extracts `scriptPubKey.hex` properly. Java's `getUtxos` is un-inspected — do not extrapolate. → Pass E.


[GK-BUG-007] WhatsOnChainProvider.getUtxos maps WoC unspent entries to script:''. The comment says callers can look the script up if needed. Independent SDK workers for TS, Go, Python, Java, Zig, and Ruby all report deploy/call using that empty script as the BIP-143 subscript. TS was spot-checked. This makes production WoC funding signatures invalid unless another code path fills the script (not in getUtxos).

evidence.GK-BUG-007: Opened woc.ts:118-125 (script: '' with comment that WoC does not return locking script). Sibling SDK reports cite the same empty-script pattern; TS citation verified.

remediation.GK-BUG-007: Fetch the locking script (tx output or script-hash endpoint) before signing. Fail closed if script is empty. Add an integration test that a WoC-shaped UTXO cannot be signed with script:''.

testable_assertion.GK-BUG-007: Signing a funding input whose UTXO.script is '' must throw; today LocalSigner hashes the empty scriptCode.

conflicts: none — verified packages/runar-sdk/src/providers/woc.ts:110-135 (runar-review-claude-main, 8937c1ad): `script: ''` with the comment "WoC doesn't return the locking script in the UTXO list", and the MAX_SCRIPT_BYTES guard immediately below is gated on `if (u.script)`, so it is unconditionally dead for every WoC UTXO — confirming both findings' mechanism.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-go/sdk_woc_provider.go:184-195: GetUtxos still sets Script:"" unconditionally; the DoS guard immediately below (`if u.Script == "" { continue }`) is unconditionally skipped since Script is always empty. packages/runar-go/sdk_signer.go:88-102 LocalSigner.Sign takes `subscript` with no non-empty check, feeding it straight into `script.NewFromHex` -> `SetSourceTxOutput` -> `CalcInputSignatureHash`; sdk_contract.go:611,1346 call `fundingSigner.Sign(..., utxo.Script, ...)` passing the WoC-sourced empty script directly. packages/runar-sdk/src/providers/woc.ts:117-133 shows the identical pattern in the TS reference tier (still `script: ''`, guard gated on `if (u.script)`).
verification.conflict_resolution: The recorded 'conflict' text is a confirming cross-check between CL-BUG-072 and GK-BUG-007, not an actual disagreement — both describe the same mechanism and both hold at HEAD.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate; both sources' cited files/lines/mechanism match HEAD exactly, including the specific detail that the MAX_SCRIPT_BYTES guard is unconditionally dead.

items.testable_assertion_verified: LocalSigner.Sign(txHex, i, "" /* empty subscript from a WoC UTXO */, satoshis, nil) must return an error; today it succeeds, producing a signature computed over a zero-length scriptCode that no real P2PKH OP_CHECKSIG can accept.

items.title: Ruby WalletProvider#broadcast reports success for a rejected or unsent ARC transaction
items.confidence_note: raised by CL+GK; silent-but-inspected: none; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-158] ## CL-BUG-158 — HIGH / P1 — Ruby's `WalletProvider#broadcast` is the only one of that tier's four providers that reports success for a rejected or unsent transaction
Source: sdk-ruby NEW-04. Fail-open on the broadcast path, and inconsistent with its own three
siblings in the same tier — so the shape is a missed port, not a design choice. Same family as
CL-BUG-141 (TS `ensureFunding` swallowing the broadcast failure): two tiers, two providers, both
reporting success for a transaction the network never accepted.


[GK-BUG-029] Broadcast POSTs to ARC, then on HTTP/JSON/network failure rescue StandardError keeps a locally computed txid, caches it, and returns it. Non-success HTTP that does not raise also keeps the local txid (only HTTPSuccess replaces it). RunarContract#deploy/#finalize_call then set @current_utxo to an output that does not exist. TS WalletProvider throws on ARC error.

evidence.GK-BUG-029: Opened wallet.rb:174-202: local txid first, rescue StandardError empty, always cache and return txid. HTTPSuccess is the only path that overwrites from JSON.

remediation.GK-BUG-029: Raise on non-success HTTP and on rescue, matching TS. Optional allow_local_txid: opt-in for tests.

testable_assertion.GK-BUG-029: Stubbing ARC to 500/timeout makes broadcast raise; it must not return a 64-char hex as if the tx were accepted.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-rb/lib/runar/sdk/wallet.rb:192-220 (WalletProvider#broadcast): POSTs to ARC; on any StandardError (network/timeout) the rescue at :214-216 is a no-op comment ('ARC unreachable — use locally computed txid'), falling through to :218-219 which caches and returns the locally-computed txid unconditionally. Non-success HTTP is also silently skipped — the JSON txid replacement only happens `if resp.is_a?(Net::HTTPSuccess)` (:210-213) — so a 4xx/5xx ARC response likewise returns the fabricated local txid with no error raised.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Cited wallet.rb:174-202 is close (the actual broadcast method spans :192-220); the described mechanism is exact.

items.testable_assertion_verified: GK-BUG-029: Stubbing ARC to 500/timeout makes broadcast raise; it must not return a 64-char hex as if the tx were accepted. Verified reproducible against wallet.rb's current control flow.

items.title: Ruby build_p2pkh_script lacks the 66/130-char compressed/uncompressed pubkey branch Go/Python have, causing WalletProvider#get_utxos to raise
items.confidence_note: raised by CL+GK; silent-but-inspected: none; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.severity_note: reviewers disagreed ['HIGH', 'MEDIUM']; highest taken per §6.2 (no downgrade justified at combination time)
items.description:
[CL-BUG-157] ## CL-BUG-157 — MEDIUM / P2 — Ruby's `build_p2pkh_script` lacks the 66/130-char public-key branch Go and Python have, which is the root cause of `WalletProvider#get_utxos` raising on every call
Source: sdk-ruby NEW-03, which resolves seed RB-02's symptom to its cause. A per-tier divergence in a
helper, surfacing as a total failure of one provider method.


[GK-BUG-030] TS buildP2PKHScript accepts 40-char PKH, 66/130-char pubkey (HASH160), or Base58Check. Ruby build_p2pkh_script only accepts 40-char hex or Base58. WalletProvider#get_utxos copies the TS call shape and passes signer.get_public_key (66-char compressed). First character of a compressed key is 02/03; '0' is not in the Base58 alphabet, so BASE58_ALPHABET.index('0') is nil and num = num*58+nil raises TypeError before any UTXO is returned. address_to_pubkey_hash also never verifies the Base58Check checksum (takes bytes [1,20] after a 25-byte length check).

evidence.GK-BUG-030: Opened wallet.rb:211-212 (build_p2pkh_script(expected_pub_key)). Opened deployment.rb:155-163 (40-char hex or address_to_pubkey_hash). Opened 238-242 (no checksum).

remediation.GK-BUG-030: Port the TS 66/130-char HASH160 branch. After Base58 decode, SHA256d-check the last 4 bytes. Add a spec that get_utxos with a compressed pubkey returns without TypeError.

testable_assertion.GK-BUG-030: With a WalletSigner whose pubkey is 0279be667e…, WalletProvider#get_utxos returns without TypeError and keeps only outputs whose script equals HASH160 of that pubkey. Genesis address with last character flipped (still 25 decoded bytes) raises.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-rb/lib/runar/sdk/deployment.rb:155-164 (build_p2pkh_script): only branches on 40-char hex (address.length==40 && hex_string?), else falls to address_to_pubkey_hash -> base58_decode; no 66/130-char compressed/uncompressed pubkey branch. packages/runar-rb/lib/runar/sdk/wallet.rb:229-230 (WalletProvider#get_utxos) calls SDK.build_p2pkh_script(@signer.get_public_key), and get_public_key returns a 66-char compressed hex (e.g. '0279be667e...'). Reproduced directly (`ruby -e`): base58_decode('0279be667e...') raises TypeError ('nil can't be coerced into Integer') because BASE58_ALPHABET.index('0') is nil (Base58 excludes '0'). address_to_pubkey_hash (:238-243) also performs no Base58Check checksum verification, only a 25-byte length check before slicing bytes[1,20].
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Both cited files/line ranges match the described mechanism exactly.

items.testable_assertion_verified: GK-BUG-030: With a WalletSigner whose pubkey is 0279be667e..., WalletProvider#get_utxos must return without TypeError and keep only outputs whose script equals HASH160 of that pubkey; a Genesis address with its last character flipped (still 25 decoded bytes) must raise. Reproduced the TypeError branch directly.

[CL-BUG-137] ## CL-BUG-137 — HIGH (contained) / P2 — `TokenWallet.transfer`/`.merge` sign a throwaway transaction and broadcast a structurally different one
Source: sdk-ts NEW-06. `tokens.ts:106` signs a BIP-143 SIGHASH_ALL digest over a *locally* built
`prelimTx` (`:94-103`), then passes the result as a **concrete** arg to `contract.call` (`:108-110`),
so the SDK's two-pass auto-signing never runs and `prepareCall` builds a fresh transaction. Three
independent divergences invalidate the signature: the real DER sig is 70-72 bytes vs the fixed
72-byte placeholder (changing size → fee → change → `hashOutputs`); `prepareCall` filters the
contract's own UTXO out of funding candidates (`contract.ts:1321-1323`) while `tokens.ts:91` does
not (changing `hashPrevouts`); and `prepareCall` models contract-input and extra-output overheads
(`contract.ts:1431-1433`) that `tokens.ts` never does.
**Contained:** the worker established zero users in all seven tiers — every peer is
definition + barrel + self-test only, with no consumer outside its defining file in any tier, and
the Zig and Java peers do not even implement `transfer`/`merge`. Deleting `TokenWallet` from all
seven tiers is cheaper than fixing it. If kept, `docs/api-reference.md:540-545` documents it with a
working-looking usage example and must not ship until fixed.

...
- **CL-BUG-137 (`TokenWallet` signs a discarded transaction) — Ruby confirmed.** NEW-05 finds the
  identical defect in `packages/runar-rb`, with the Ruby-specific mechanism spelled out:
  `resolve_method_args` only auto-signs `nil` Sig slots, so the stale signature is embedded verbatim.
  Two tiers, same bug, neither with a consumer. Strengthens the "delete it in all seven" remediation.


[GK-BUG-024] transfer BIP-143-signs a preliminary tx (placeholder unlock, all wallet UTXOs as funding, no continuation) then passes that signature into contract.call([sig, to]). call/prepareCall rebuilds a different tx (selectUtxos, real unlock size). A non-null Sig skips auto-sign (contract.ts:855-858), so call will not re-sign. merge never passes additionalContractInputs — the second token UTXO is read for otherSupply/otherHolder and left unspent. getUtxos treats empty utxo.script as include-everything (tokens.ts:209-213), so a WoC-backed wallet (GK-BUG-007) would treat every P2PKH coin as a token UTXO. FungibleToken is a stateless SmartContract with readonly supply/holder; getBalance reads contract.state.supply. Tests only cover error throws.

evidence.GK-BUG-024: Opened tokens.ts:83-114 (prelim sign then call with stale sig), :184-190 (merge call without additionalContractInputs), :206-213 (empty script include-all). Opened contract.ts:855-858 (null Sig is the auto-sign gate). Opened tokens.test.ts:202-256 (no happy-path spend).

[CL-BUG-072] ## CL-BUG-072 — HIGH — WhatsOnChain `getUtxos` returns an empty locking script; signatures are computed over an empty scriptCode
**Dispatcher-verified.** Convergent: sdk:go F-GO-03 + sdk:rust R-01 independently.

Verified present in five tiers, each with the same explanatory comment:
- `packages/runar-sdk/src/providers/woc.ts:118-124` (TS reference)
- `packages/runar-go/sdk_woc_provider.go:184`
- `packages/runar-rs/src/sdk/woc_provider.rs:125`
- `packages/runar-py/runar/sdk/woc_provider.py:113`

items.title: Fold-ON conformance step reports a false PASS for single-tier fixtures because both parity checks trivially match and the golden comparison is skipped
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-088] ## CL-BUG-088 — HIGH / P1 — A single-tier fixture compares NOTHING in the fold-ON conformance step and is reported PASS
**Dispatcher-verified.** Source: conformance-harness depth NEW-01.

Two short-circuits stack. Verified verbatim in both comparison functions (`conformance/runner/runner.ts:2239` and `:2284`):
```ts
if (present.length < 2) {
  if (present.length === 0) return { ok: true }; // No compilers produced IR — not a mismatch
  if (expectedCount === 1) return { ok: true }; // Single-compiler fixture: trivial match
```
and both golden blocks are gated on `skipGoldenMf` (`:2937-2938`, `:2958`):
```ts
const skipGoldenMf = !constantFoldingDisabled();
if (!skipGoldenMf && existsSync(expectedIrFile))  { ... }
if (!skipGoldenMf && existsSync(expectedScriptFile)) { ... }
```
Under the CI step *"multi-format source conformance (fold ON)"*, `skipGoldenMf` is true. For a fixture whose `compilers` allowlist names one tier, `expectedCount === 1`, so **both parity comparisons return a trivial match AND both golden comparisons are skipped**. Nothing is compared. The only surviving check is that the compiler exited 0 — a compile-success check, not a conformance check. The row is reported `'pass'`.

[CL-BUG-089] ## CL-BUG-089 — HIGH / P1 — An unrecognised compiler id in `compilers[]` turns a fixture into a no-op PASS, and survives CI
**Dispatcher-verified.** Source: conformance-harness depth NEW-02.

`conformance/runner/runner.ts:2783-2784`, verified verbatim:
```ts
if (!config.compilers || !Array.isArray(config.compilers)) return null;
return new Set(config.compilers as CompilerId[]);
```
A bare cast. No runtime membership check. A typo (`"gp"`), a rename (`"golang"`), or a stale tier name makes `supportedCompilers` empty; every tier resolves to `undefined`; `compareIR`/`compareScript` take the `present.length === 0` arm and return `{ok:true}`; the golden blocks filter on `o.success` and iterate an empty array. Result: `errors: []`, `irMatch: true`, `scriptMatch: true` → **`'pass'`**.

**`assertAllCompilersAvailableInCi` does not close this** — it probes only that the six native binaries exist on disk and has no view of what any fixture's allowlist names. The vacuity survives `CI=true`. The governance layer does not close it either: the audit test types its approved allowlists as `Record<string, string[]>` and compares string sets, so a typo pinned in both files passes.

The worker grepped for a validating set across four naming conventions and found none anywhere in the partition.

verification.evidence: readFixtureCompilerAllowlist (runner.ts:2928-2940, functionally identical to the code the reviewer cited, just shifted a few lines) still does `new Set(config.compilers as CompilerId[])` -- a bare cast, no runtime membership check against the real CompilerId union. conformance/runner/__tests__/allowlist-audit.test.ts (the governance layer) only compares each fixture's `compilers` array against a hand-maintained APPROVED_ALLOWLISTS map via string-set equality (sameSet); it never validates that any string in either list is one of the 7 real compiler ids. A typo committed identically in BOTH places (source.json and APPROVED_ALLOWLISTS) would still pass the audit test while collapsing the runner's supported-tier Set to empty, taking the present.length===0 trivial-match arm in compareIR/compareScript.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: accurate -- code essentially unchanged, including the governance-layer gap

[CL-BUG-235] ## CL-BUG-235 — HIGH / P1 — The three strongest gates are dark on the repo's own primary commit path
**Dispatcher-verified.** The yardstick is the maintainers' own, at `ci.yml:173-177`: *"bd7ec284 — the
commit this gate exists for — is on main's FIRST-PARENT chain: pushed directly, never a PR (**only 5
of the last 100 commits reachable from main are PR merges**). A pull_request-only gate would have
watched it go straight past."*

Measured against that stated standard, I read the triggers myself:
- **`cross-compiler-bytewise.yml`** — the full 72-fixture × 7-tier byte-exact matrix plus the Lean
  verifier — is `pull_request` + `workflow_dispatch`. **No `push:`, no `merge_group:`.**
- **`differential.yml`** — the **only** oracle in the repo grading against an engine outside this
  codebase (`python-bitcoinlib`) — same trigger set.
- **`golden-provenance-gate`** — `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` (`ci.yml:97`).

**On ~95% of commits, the widest byte-exact matrix, the only external-reference oracle, and the
self-produced-golden gate all do not run.**

verification.evidence: .github/workflows/cross-compiler-bytewise.yml:23-27 still declares `on: pull_request (branches: [main, release/v*]) + workflow_dispatch` only — no `push:`, no `merge_group:` — despite its own header comment stating 'This workflow takes only pull_request and manual-dispatch triggers'. .github/workflows/differential.yml:21-24 is the same: `on: pull_request + workflow_dispatch` only. .github/workflows/ci.yml's golden-provenance-gate job still guards with `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` (line 106), even though ci.yml itself triggers on push/pull_request/merge_group (lines 2-11) — so on a direct push to main this job is skipped by its own `if`. All three gates remain dark on ~95% of commits exactly as described; only a FOURTH, textually adjacent gate (wire-format-must-move-golden, ci.yml:167-230) was given push+merge_group+pull_request triggers, addressing a different finding (TG-011/bd7ec284) rather than this one.

[CL-BUG-253] ## CL-BUG-253 — HIGH / P0 — Both webapp re-init handlers lack a phase guard: permanent fund loss
`webapp/main.go:111-150` and `webapp-blackjack/main.go:224-268` unconditionally overwrite the in-RAM
keypairs — `game.Alice`/`Bob`, `game.House`, `game.PlayerWallets`, `game.OracleKeys` — with **no
check of `game.Phase`**, though phase guards exist elsewhere in the same files
(`webapp/main.go:223`, `webapp-blackjack/main.go:352`). Fired mid-round, every live contract UTXO
becomes **permanently unspendable**: the blackjack locking script has the discarded `oraclePubKey`
baked in, and its only key-free escape, `cancel`, needs the discarded player and house keys.
Combined with the unauthenticated surface, **one request from a stranger.**

verification.evidence: examples/end2end-example/webapp/main.go: `handleInit` (lines 152-242) still unconditionally overwrites `game.Alice`, `game.Bob`, `game.AlicePubKey/BobPubKey`, `game.AliceAddr/BobAddr`, `game.History`, `game.Round`, resetting `game.Phase = "funding"` with NO check of the current `game.Phase` first — while sibling handlers in the same file DO guard on phase (`handleNewRound` at :273-274 `if game.Phase != "ready" && game.Phase != "complete"`, the reveal handler at :439 `if game.Phase != "deployed"`). examples/end2end-example/webapp-blackjack/main.go's init handler (lines 228-249) has the identical shape: no phase check, while `handleHit`-family handlers at :362, :525, :589, :897 do guard on phase. Calling /api/init mid-round (any Phase past "ready") still discards the live keypairs a deployed, unspent contract UTXO depends on, permanently bricking it.
verification.conflict_resolution: The item's 'unauthenticated surface, one request from a stranger' aggravating clause is now PARTIALLY mitigated, not fixed: `sessionFor` (examples/end2end-example/webapp/session.go:67-97), added under 'R-152: resolve this visitor's game. The package-level singleton is gone,' now scopes `game` to a per-visitor HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie rather than a shared package-level global — so a random unauthenticated stranger without the victim's session cookie can no longer brick a DIFFERENT visitor's game with one request. The core bug (no phase guard on re-init, so the SAME session/user can brick their own in-flight funds by re-initializing, e.g. an accidental double-click, a replayed request, or a same-session XSS) is unchanged.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate about the missing phase guard, which is unchanged and independently confirmed in both webapp/main.go and webapp-blackjack/main.go; the P0 severity's 'one request from a stranger' framing is now weaker than described, since R-152 added per-session cookie isolation after this finding was made.

items.testable_assertion_verified: POST /api/init a second time within the same session after reaching Phase=="deployed" (mid-round); assert the request is rejected (400, phase guard) rather than silently succeeding. It currently succeeds and overwrites game.Alice/game.Bob, after which the previously-deployed contract's UTXO can no longer be spent with the (now-replaced) in-memory keys.

sweep1.evidence: examples/end2end-example/webapp/main.go:152-194 handleInit locks the (now per-session, R-152) game and unconditionally replaces game.Alice/Bob and sets Phase='funding' with no game.Phase check; webapp-blackjack/main.go:224-249 handleNewGame likewise sets Phase='setup' etc. with no phase guard. Per-visitor sessions remove the 'stranger' vector but a same-session re-init mid-round (Phase=='deployed') still succeeds and discards the keys.

items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-082] ## CL-BUG-082 — HIGH / P1 — The shipped DSL `Groth16Verifier` contract performs no G2 on-curve or subgroup check
**Dispatcher-verified.** Source: crypto:bn254-groth16 F3.

`integration/go/contracts/Groth16Verifier.runar.go` checks **three G1 points** and **zero G2 points** before pairing, verified:
```
120:  runar.Assert(runar.Bn254G1OnCurveP(proofA))
121:  runar.Assert(runar.Bn254G1OnCurveP(proofC))
122:  runar.Assert(runar.Bn254G1OnCurveP(preparedInputs))
130:  runar.Assert(runar.Bn254MultiPairing4(proofA, proofBX0, proofBX1, proofBY0, proofBY1, ...
```
`proofBX0/X1/Y0/Y1` are spender-supplied method parameters fed straight into the pairing. Small-subgroup / off-curve G2 is the canonical Groth16 forgery vector. The witness-assisted path *does* emit all four checks (`bn254_groth16.go:1584-1587`) — this contract does not, and it is a template developers are invited to copy.

Aggravating: the contract is never executed by any test (`groth16_test.go` asserts only `scriptBytes >= 1000`), and the Go runtime mock it would run under returns `true` unconditionally — `packages/runar-go/bn254.go:277` `func Bn254MultiPairing4(...) bool { return true }`.

verification.evidence: integration/go/contracts/Groth16Verifier.runar.go:119-135: Verify() checks Bn254G1OnCurveP for proofA, proofC, and preparedInputs (all G1), then feeds spender-supplied proofBX0/X1/Y0/Y1 (the G2 point) straight into Bn254MultiPairing4 with no on-curve or subgroup check. No G2-validation builtin is even exposed to hand-written DSL contracts — the equivalent checks (emitWAG2OnCurveCheck at bn254_groth16.go:411, emitWAG2SubgroupCheck at :750, both invoked at :1547-1548/:1789-1790) exist only inside the compiler's own witness-assisted codegen path, unreachable from this contract. integration/go/groth16_test.go never calls Verify (frontend-parse-only test — verified: only TestGroth16Verifier_Parse, checking structure). packages/runar-go/bn254.go:277 Bn254MultiPairing4 mock unconditionally returns true.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate and precisely cited; verified against the actual assert sequence and the codegen's own (unreachable-from-DSL) G2 validation helpers.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Craft a proofB (G2 point) that fails the BN254 twist curve equation, or lies in a small-order subgroup, while the rest of the proof is validly formed; call Groth16Verifier.Verify with it and assert it rejects. Today it does not, because no G2 validation exists on the spender-supplied point before the pairing check — the canonical Groth16 forgery/small-subgroup-confinement vector.

items.title: The published decompiler silently loses ~95% of its capability and reports success
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-110] ## CL-BUG-110 — HIGH / P1 — The published decompiler silently loses ~95% of its capability and reports success
**Dispatcher-verified.** Source: pkg-decompiler depth NEW-4 (= F-03 × F-15 composed).

`tsconfig.json` has `rootDir:"."` with `main: "dist/src/index.js"`, so at runtime `__dirname` is `<pkg>/dist/src` and both data loaders resolve `'..'` to `<pkg>/dist/` — while `templates-data.json` (27 MB) and `fingerprints.json` (1.7 MB) live at `<pkg>/`. `"build": "tsc"` copies nothing. Independently, **`templates-data.json` is absent from `package.json` `files`**, so it is never published at all.

Both loaders fail **silently** (`templates.ts:47` returns an empty manifest; `fingerprints.ts:32-34` catches and returns an empty DB). Per `coverage.json`, 72 of 77 corpus recoveries come from the exact-hex manifest and 1 more from the fingerprint-assisted recogniser — and `symexec: 0`. So the shipped tool returns `raw_script` for ~95% of inputs where CI reports `byte-match`, **and prints `[round-trip OK]` with exit 0 while doing it**. No test can observe this: CI resolves `src/`.

verification.evidence: packages/decompiler/tsconfig.json: rootDir '.', outDir 'dist' — src/fingerprints.ts compiles to dist/src/fingerprints.js, whose `resolve(__dirname, '..', 'fingerprints.json')` resolves to dist/fingerprints.json. packages/decompiler/dist/ contains only __tests__/, scripts/, src/ subdirectories — zero .json files anywhere under dist/ (confirmed via find). package.json 'files': ['dist', 'fingerprints.json', 'coverage-baseline.json'] — templates-data.json is absent, so `npm publish` would never ship it even if the path were fixed. fingerprints.ts:29-36 and templates.ts:44-56 both silently degrade to emptyDB()/an empty Map on any read failure via try/catch. coverage.json confirms heavy reliance on the template/fingerprint paths (82 template + 1 assert-recognizer out of 87 byte-match, symexec: 0). CI's decompiler-roundtrip job runs `pnpm --filter runar-decompiler run test` (vitest), which resolves TS source files directly from their on-disk src/ path, so __dirname during tests is packages/decompiler/src (not dist/src) — CI structurally cannot observe the dist-path bug.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate and precisely verified — path resolution, files-array omission, silent-catch behavior, coverage numbers, and the CI blind spot all check out exactly as described.

items.testable_assertion_verified: After `pnpm --filter runar-decompiler run build`, invoke the compiled dist/src/index.js entry point to decompile a known template-manifest script (e.g. a plain P2PKH hex) and assert the recovery path is 'template', not 'raw_script'. This fails today because dist/fingerprints.json and dist/templates-data.json don't exist — only the package-root copies do — so the compiled loaders silently fall back to empty structures.

sweep1.evidence: packages/decompiler: package.json files=['dist','fingerprints.json','coverage-baseline.json'] (no templates-data.json); build='tsc'; templates.ts:46 resolve(__dirname,'..','templates-data.json') -> dist/templates-data.json which does not exist (no dist/*.json). Probe decompiling templates-data.json entries[0].hex: via dist/src/index.js -> recoveryPath 'raw_script', ok=true, loadFingerprints() entries 0; via src/index.ts (tsx) -> recoveryPath 'template', fingerprints 6.

items.title: Three Python negatives swallow their own failure signal; the BUG-001 malleability gate is guarded by nothing
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-233] ## CL-BUG-233 — HIGH / P1 — Three Python negatives swallow their own failure signal; the BUG-001 malleability gate is guarded by nothing
**Dispatcher-verified.** `examples/python/schnorr-zkp/test_schnorr_zkp.py:76-80`, which I read:
```python
    try:
        c.verify(r_point, EC_N)
        assert False, "expected assertion failure for s = n"
    except (AssertionError, Exception):
        pass
```
**The failure signal at `:78` is an `AssertionError`, caught by `:79`.** Identical at `:45-51` and
`:90-94`. If `verify` accepted `s = 0`, `s = n`, or a malleated `s`, all three stay green — and
**these are the only Python tests guarding the `within(s, 1, n)` gate.** The worker confirmed the
shape exists nowhere else in the 53 Python or 53 Ruby files.

verification.evidence: examples/python/schnorr-zkp/test_schnorr_zkp.py:76-84 (`test_rejects_s_at_n`), :86-97 (`test_rejects_s_zero`), and :39-51 (`test_schnorr_wrong_s`) all follow `c.verify(...); assert False, "..."` inside a `try` whose `except (AssertionError, Exception): pass` (or split `except AssertionError / except Exception`) catches the AssertionError the `assert False` line itself raises. If `verify()` silently accepted a malleated/boundary `s`, the injected `assert False` would fire and be swallowed the same way, so the test is green regardless of whether the contract's `within(s, 1, n)` gate actually rejects. Confirmed by direct read at HEAD; unchanged since it was introduced in commit 7101a5a9 (`BUG-001: adversarial s-bound tests`), the most recent commit touching this file.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate — line numbers and the swallow pattern match exactly (same shape recurs at three call sites, not just the cited one).

items.testable_assertion_verified: Monkeypatch/stub `SchnorrZKP.verify` (or construct a deliberately-broken build) so it returns normally for `s = EC_N` instead of raising, then call `test_rejects_s_at_n()` directly and assert it raises `AssertionError` (i.e. the test itself must fail when the gate is broken). Today it does not — the broken-gate scenario is swallowed and the test reports success. Fix: replace the try/except with `with pytest.raises(AssertionError): c.verify(r_point, EC_N)` (same for `s=0` and `wrong_s`).

sweep1.evidence: examples/python/schnorr-zkp/test_schnorr_zkp.py: test_schnorr_wrong_s :45-51 (`assert False` then `except AssertionError: pass` / `except Exception: pass`), test_rejects_s_at_n :76-80 and test_rejects_s_zero :90-94 (`assert False, ...` inside try, `except (AssertionError, Exception): pass`) — the failure signal is still swallowed; no pytest.raises.

[CL-BUG-053] 5. **CL-BUG-053 (six parsers silently turn a leading-zero decimal into 0).**
   I ran Python's own semantics: int('0123', 0) raises ValueError; five call sites swallow it
   and return 0, one (Zig) has no try at all. Rust and Java use base 10 and return 123.
   The same literal means two different numbers depending on the surface format.
6. **CL-GAP-071 (Go-DSL `x += 1` compiles to `x = 1`) is REAL but currently LATENT.**
   parser_gocontract.go:432-457 confirmed: only token.DEFINE is special-cased, every compound
   assignment falls to the plain-assignment arm. I then checked blast radius myself:
       grep for compound assignment in **/*.runar.go across examples/ + conformance/  -> 0 files
       grep for bitwise compound assignment in **/*.runar.ts                          -> 0 files
   So no shipped contract exercises it and conformance is legitimately green. It is a live trap
   for the next contributor, not an active miscompile. Severity stays HIGH; priority annotated
   "latent — zero current blast radius".

verification.evidence: compilers/python/runar_compiler/frontend/parser_move.py:1534-1538 (`_parse_move_number`) and parser_sol.py:1213-1219 (`_parse_sol_number`) both do `try: val = int(s, 0) \n except ValueError: val = 0` — Python's int(s,0) raises ValueError on a leading-zero decimal like '0123' (ambiguous with legacy octal), and both call sites swallow it and silently produce a BigIntLiteral(value=0). git blame shows both lines unchanged since 119f1d85a (2026-03-06), well before either review commit, and no later commit touches this logic.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate; no file:line was cited in this item, but the described mechanism (Python int(s,0) semantics, swallowed ValueError, silent 0) matches the live code exactly at two of the described five-to-six call sites checked.

items.testable_assertion_verified: In compilers/python (the Python-tier compiler that parses .runar.move/.runar.sol surfaces), compile a source string containing the literal `0123` as a property initializer and assert the resulting BigIntLiteral value equals 123 (matching Rust/Java's base-10 behavior). Today it silently compiles to 0 because `_parse_move_number`/`_parse_sol_number` catch int('0123', 0)'s ValueError and return 0 instead of propagating a parse error or falling back to base-10.

items.title: ArrayLiteralExpr is missing from four Go AST walkers (validator.go's recursion/hex-length checks, typecheck.go's type inference), so a call hidden inside an array literal defeats recursion detection, the type system, and the "only Rúnar built-ins" rule
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-190] ## CL-BUG-190 — HIGH / P1 — `ArrayLiteralExpr` is missing from four AST walkers, defeating recursion detection, hex validation, the type system and `asm` gating
Four walkers omit it — `validator.go:1155-1182`, `:1238-1272`, `:948-990` and
`typecheck.go:882-984` — **and all four are in the two *rejection* passes**, while five other
walkers have it. Four consequences, each proved by compiling a fixture:
1. **Compiler hang.** A self-call hidden in an array literal escapes `checkNoRecursion`; the
   compiler spins unboundedly (SIGQUIT dump shows the cycle, exit 124 at 30 s). Written directly,
   the same recursion is rejected.
2. **Type system bypassed.** `checkMultiSig([a: bigint, b: bigint], [1n, 2n, 3n])` compiles. The
   comment at `typecheck.go:1241-1244` claims the subtype loop stops this; **the loop is vacuous
   because both args type as `<unknown>`.**
3. **"Only Rúnar built-ins" bypassed.** `checkMultiSig([a], [p, totallyBogusFunction(1n)])` compiles
   cleanly and the IR keeps `{"func":"totallyBogusFunction","kind":"call"}`. Outside an array literal
   the same call is rejected.
4. Odd-length hex escapes the validator and surfaces as a stack-lowering error.
**The structural remedy the worker names is the right one:** the ANF layer is exhaustive by
construction (`UnknownANFKindError` panics); the AST layer has no such guard, *"which is why a node
added later was missed in exactly the passes that reject."*

verification.evidence: All four sub-claims verified live at HEAD. (1) Recursion: `collectMethodCallsInExpr` (validator.go, the helper `checkNoRecursion` at :1683 relies on, now ~1705-1738) switches on CallExpr/BinaryExpr/UnaryExpr/MemberExpr/TernaryExpr/IndexAccessExpr/IncrementExpr/DecrementExpr — no ArrayLiteralExpr case — so a self-call nested inside an array-literal element is never visited and escapes recursion detection. (2) Hex validation: `validateExpression` (validator.go, ~1345-1390) likewise has no ArrayLiteralExpr case (only BinaryExpr/UnaryExpr/CallExpr/MemberExpr/TernaryExpr/IndexAccessExpr/IncrementExpr/DecrementExpr/ByteStringLiteral), so a malformed odd-length/non-hex ByteStringLiteral nested in an array literal is never checked. (3) Type system: `typeChecker.inferExprType` (typecheck.go:1006-1170) has no ArrayLiteralExpr case, falling to the final `return "<unknown>"` (:1170-ish). `checkCallArgs`'s standard per-arg subtype loop (~1717-1723) does `argType := tc.inferExprType(args[i], env); if !isSubtype(argType, expectedType) && argType != "<unknown>" { addError }` — since an array-literal arg always types as `<unknown>`, the error condition is always false, so e.g. `checkMultiSig` never rejects a wrong-typed array argument. (4) Builtin-only rule: because inferExprType never recurses into ArrayLiteralExpr.Elements, a call nested inside an array-literal argument (e.g. `checkMultiSig([a],[p, totallyBogusFunction(1n)])`) never reaches `checkCallExpr`, so the 'unknown function ... only Rúnar built-in functions' error (typecheck.go:1467) never fires for it. Note: three OTHER helper walkers added since the review (`exprContainsCallTo` :678, `exprContainsAddDataOutput` :751, `walkExprForOutputSignals` :877) DO now handle ArrayLiteralExpr — the project has fixed the pattern in some places but not in the three rejection/inference walkers CL-BUG-190 actually names.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate in substance; old line numbers (948-990/1155-1182/1238-1272/882-984) have drifted with file growth (current: validateExpression ~1345-1390, collectMethodCallsInExpr ~1705-1738, inferExprType 1006-1170), but all four claimed omissions and their consequences are verified present at HEAD.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile a Go-format contract containing `checkMultiSig([validPubKeyArg], [pubKeyArg, totallyBogusFunction(1n)])` — an unknown function call nested inside the second array-literal argument. Today it typechecks with zero diagnostics and the IR keeps `{"func":"totallyBogusFunction","kind":"call"}`. A fix must reject it with the same 'unknown function ... only Rúnar built-in functions and contract methods are allowed' error checkCallExpr already emits for a non-nested call.

items.title: parseStatement's default case silently returns nil for syntactically valid but unrecognized TypeScript statement kinds (e.g. while, switch), and callers drop nil statements, so contract logic inside such a statement silently vanishes instead of failing to parse
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [CX-BUG-026] The syntax check rejects malformed trees, but syntactically valid unsupported statements reach `parseStatement`’s default and are silently discarded. Contract logic inside a `while`, `switch`, or another unrecognized TypeScript statement can therefore vanish while compilation proceeds.

evidence.CX-BUG-026: `parseStatement` recognizes only lexical declarations, expressions, `if`, `for`, and `return`; its default explicitly returns nil, and callers omit nil statements.

remediation.CX-BUG-026: Produce a source-located error for every unrecognized statement node, allowing only explicitly enumerated punctuation/comment nodes to return nil.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-026: A public method containing `while (condition) { assert(false) }` must fail parsing with an unsupported-statement diagnostic rather than compile with the loop removed.

verification.evidence: compilers/go/frontend/parser.go:783-805 parseStatement's switch has cases only for lexical_declaration, expression_statement, if_statement, for_statement, return_statement, and punctuation/comment token types; `default: // Skip unknown node types silently (e.g., punctuation) \n return nil`. Grepped parser.go for while_statement/switch_statement/do_statement — zero references anywhere, confirming these syntactically-valid tree-sitter node types fall through to the silent-nil default. parseStatements (parser.go:733-743) does `if stmt != nil { stmts = append(...) }`, so the dropped statement leaves no trace and compilation proceeds successfully. root.HasError() (checked earlier in Parse) does not catch this because `while (...) { ... }` is syntactically valid TypeScript that tree-sitter parses without an ERROR/MISSING node.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate — line numbers and mechanism (silent default-case nil) confirmed exactly as described; this dates to the initial commit, never patched.

items.testable_assertion_verified: A public method containing `while (condition) { assert(false) }` (or a `switch` statement) must fail parsing with an unsupported-statement diagnostic, not compile successfully with the loop/switch silently omitted from the emitted script.

items.title: ANFMethod.SigHashType is tagged json:"-", so a source-to-IR-to-artifact round-trip cannot reconstruct the ABI's sigHashType
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [CX-BUG-020] `ANFMethod.SigHashType` is explicitly excluded from JSON. A source-to-IR-to-artifact workflow can retain the per-node `sighashFlag` used by the script but cannot reconstruct the method-level value copied into the ABI, again creating an ABI/script signing mismatch.

evidence.CX-BUG-020: `SigHashType` is `json:"-"`, while `CompileFromIR` immediately assembles the artifact from the deserialized program.

remediation.CX-BUG-020: Put the method sighash type in the IR wire format or reconstruct it consistently from validated `check_preimage` nodes.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-020: Source compile and emitted-IR recompile of a non-default sighash method must produce the same ABI and script.

verification.evidence: compilers/go/ir/types.go:71 `SigHashType *int \`json:"-"\`` — deliberately excluded from JSON (comment lines 64-70: 'Carried in-memory only (json:"-") so it never appears in the emitted ANF IR JSON compared cross-tier ... The artifact assembler copies it to ABIMethod.SigHashType'). compiler.go:397-399 only sets ABIMethod.SigHashType when `method.SigHashType != nil`, which is always nil after a JSON load. The actual SCRIPT bytes stay correct after --ir because the separately-serialized per-node `SighashFlag int \`json:"sighashFlag,omitempty"\`` (ir/types.go:194) DOES survive the round-trip and drives codegen (stack.go:1416, 4299, 4331) — so this is specifically an ABI-metadata loss, not a script-correctness bug, exactly as the finding states. The project is aware of the same underlying constraint from two other angles (sp1_fri_ir_guard.go:20-26, constant_fold.go:606-611) but neither of those fixes the ABI round-trip gap itself.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate — exact json tag, exact mechanism, and the script-vs-ABI distinction confirmed.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile a `@sighash`-annotated method from source (assert ABI.sigHashType == 0x43); then `--emit-ir` that program and `--ir`-recompile the JSON; the recompiled artifact's ABI.sigHashType must still equal 0x43 (currently it is omitted/nil) while the script hex stays identical.

items.title: ANFProgram.ParentClass is tagged json:"-", so a source-to-IR-to-artifact round-trip loses the authoritative stateful/parent-class marker
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [CX-BUG-021] `ParentClass` is deliberately excluded from ANF JSON even though its comment calls it authoritative for stateful contracts with zero mutable fields. Recompiling emitted IR produces an artifact with an empty parent class and can omit stateful metadata derived during assembly.

evidence.CX-BUG-021: `ParentClass` is `json:"-"`; artifact assembly copies that now-empty field and separately infers ANF inclusion from mutable fields.

remediation.CX-BUG-021: Preserve parent class in the interoperable IR, or require it as explicit metadata when compiling IR.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-021: Source-to-IR-to-artifact round-trip of an all-readonly `StatefulSmartContract` must retain `parentClass` and artifact behavior.

conflicts: CX-BUG-021 treats this as a genuine Go-tier defect ('can omit stateful metadata derived during assembly'). CL-BUG-134 (elsewhere in this group) explicitly characterizes the same Go behavior (omitting parentClass from the IR path) as one of 'five tiers [that] degrade safely by omitting the key' — in contrast to Zig, which writes a positively wrong default. Verified at current HEAD: compiler.go:444 sets `ParentClass: program.ParentClass`, and program.ParentClass is `json:"-"` (ir/types.go:30) so it is empty string after an IR round-trip; the artifact field itself is `json:"parentClass,omitempty"` (compiler.go:136) so it is omitted from the artifact entirely, and the SDK's documented fallback (isStateful) is exercised safely in that case — supporting CL-BUG-134's 'safe' characterization for the SDK-trust question specifically. CX-BUG-021's separate concern, that Go's OWN artifact-assembly logic might derive other stateful metadata (e.g. the sighash subscript trim) from ParentClass during a --ir compile and get it wrong, was not resolved by this check and is a narrower, unverified claim. Kept as its own cluster because the two reports draw different conclusions about the same code, not because they duplicate each other.
dedup_uncertain: yes: real disagreement between reviewers on severity/safety of the identical Go behavior (see conflicts); the narrower question of whether Go's compile-time stateful-metadata derivation (as opposed to the SDK's runtime trust fallback) is affected was not independently verified here.

verification.evidence: Re-verified every citation in the item's pre-existing conflicts note at CURRENT HEAD: compiler.go:444 `ParentClass: program.ParentClass`, ir/types.go:30 `ParentClass string \`json:"-"\`` (comment: excluded solely so it 'never appears in the emitted ANF IR JSON that the conformance suite compares cross-tier'), and the ARTIFACT struct field compiler.go:136 `ParentClass string \`json:"parentClass,omitempty"\`` — so an empty string surviving a --ir round-trip is omitted from the artifact JSON entirely, exactly as previously noted; all three citations still accurate. Went further to resolve the note's OPEN question: grepped every use of `program.ParentClass` in compiler.go and stack.go — there is exactly ONE (compiler.go:444, the field copy). Go's own artifact-assembly logic derives isStateful from `len(stateFields)>0` (see V083), NOT from ParentClass; terminal-method marking (compiler.go:402) keys off isStateful+params, not ParentClass; computeUsesCodePart/emitCodePartAuthentication key off state-field/side-effect analysis, not ParentClass. So Go's OWN compile-time logic derives nothing else from ParentClass beyond that single artifact field.

items.title: Go: `check_preimage.sighashFlag` is a plain `int` from JSON with no range/validity check, letting a malformed flag (e.g. FORKID-bit-absent, negative, >255) reach an unspendable on-chain assert

[CL-BUG-218] ## CL-BUG-218 — MEDIUM-HIGH / P1 — `check_preimage.sighashFlag` is truncated to its low byte with no validation
**Dispatcher-verified at the source.** `ir/types.go:184` is `SighashFlag int \`json:"sighashFlag,omitempty"\`` —
a plain `int` straight from JSON — and `validateBindings` (`ir/loader.go:120-170`) has **no
`check_preimage` case at all.** The worker proved the consequence at the byte level:

| `sighashFlag` | emitted flag push | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `67` (0x43) | `01 43` | SINGLE\|FORKID — correct |
| `999999` | `01 3f` | 0x3F — **FORKID bit absent** |
| `-5` | `01 fb` | two's-complement low byte |
| `511` | `01 ff` | 0xFF |

All four exit 0, empty stderr. **A covenant demanding FORKID-clear cannot be satisfied on BSV: the
UTXO is permanently unspendable.** This is the Go analogue of CL-BUG-118 (Zig) — now two of six
tiers confirmed, four unchecked. **Ninth `@sighash` defect.**

verification.evidence: compilers/go/ir/types.go:194 SighashFlag int `json:"sighashFlag,omitempty"` is a plain int with no bounds; compilers/go/ir/loader.go's validateBindings (~156-303) has no check_preimage case — only kind=="loop" and kind=="raw_script" get value-level checks; compilers/go/codegen/oppushtx.go:74-90 checkPreimageBindingBytesWithFlag does fmt.Sprintf("01%02x", sighashFlag&0xff), confirming the low-byte truncation. Hand-computed the reviewer's four claimed encodings: 67(0x43)&0xff=0x43 (SINGLE|FORKID, correct); 999999(0xF423F)&0xff=0x3F (FORKID bit 0x40 absent — matches '01 3f'); -5 two's-complement low byte = 0xFB (matches '01 fb'); 511(0x1FF)&0xff=0xFF (matches '01 ff'). All four match exactly — reviewer's byte-level math is correct, not just plausible.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Fully accurate — cited paths/lines correct (types.go:184 is now :194 due to line drift but same field; loader.go range correct in substance), and the hex-encoding math checks out exactly.

DISPATCHER RE-SCOPE (2026-09-30): all 7 tiers incl. TS share the phantom sm.push after exit()'s OP_VERIFY (dispatcher-reproduced: ExitAssert4 TS hex 7c00a0697c519d7c55a0697c9177; honest spend rejected, crafted spend with y=999 accepted under strict Spend). items.title: Constant propagation retains stale values across same-name rebindings
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [CX-BUG-003] The constant environment supports setting and reading values but has no deletion/invalidation operation. When a name previously bound to a constant is rebound to a non-constant value, `foldBinding` leaves the old constant in the environment, allowing later expressions to fold against stale data.

evidence.CX-BUG-003: `foldBinding` updates the environment only when the new value is a constant at `constant_fold.go:367-372`; the environment API at `constant_fold.go:40-53` provides no invalidation path. No scoped test covers constant → runtime → use rebinding of the same name.

remediation.CX-BUG-003: Delete a name from the environment before processing or registering every new binding, then set it again only if the new value is constant.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-003: For bindings `x=5`, `x=load_param("p")`, `y=x+1`, folding leaves `y` as `bin_op` rather than replacing it with `6`.

verification.evidence: compilers/go/frontend/constant_fold.go: constEnv (:46-68) has exactly one call site for `.set()` — foldBinding at :388-391 — which only registers a name in the environment when the folded value's Kind is 'load_const'. When a name previously bound to a constant is rebound to a NON-constant value (e.g. a load_param alias), foldBinding does nothing to the environment, so the stale entry survives. Confirmed with the exact scenario: x=load_const(5) -> env['x']=5; x rebound via load_const('@ref:<param-derived-temp>') -> Kind is still 'load_const' but anfValueToConst (:401-416) explicitly excludes '@ref:'-prefixed strings, returning nil, so env.set is skipped and the stale env['x']=5 is never overwritten; a later y=bin_op(x,'+',1) (:448-458) calls env.get('x'), finds the stale 5, and incorrectly folds y to 6. NOTE: the identical pattern exists in the TS reference implementation (packages/runar-compiler/src/optimizer/constant-fold.ts:289-305), and 04-anf-lower.ts:1206-1208 documents that ANF genuinely reuses the same binding name for reassignment ('in ANF, this is just a new binding with the same name') — so this is not a Go-specific quirk of the IR, it is a real property of the shared ANF design that the Go port (and apparently the TS port) both fail to handle in constant folding.
verification.tier_correction: The bug is correctly located in compilers/go/frontend/constant_fold.go (compiler:go tier as scoped), but the identical invalidation gap appears to exist in packages/runar-compiler/src/optimizer/constant-fold.ts (the TS reference compiler) as well, suggesting this may not be Go-specific and is worth checking across the other 5 ports too.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate on the mechanism (single set() call site, no invalidation path); the finding did not note the same pattern is present in the TS reference compiler, which affects scope but not the correctness of the Go-tier claim.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Go unit test on foldBindings: bindings x=load_const(5), x=load_const('@ref:t')[t=load_param('p')], y=bin_op(x,'+',1); assert the folded y.Value.Kind is 'bin_op' (unfolded). At HEAD it is 'load_const' with value 6 — a miscompile.

items.title: Java: `_codePart` discovery (`methodUsesCodePart`) does not recurse into private helper methods that construct outputs

items.description: [CX-BUG-029] `methodUsesCheckPreimage` and variable-state discovery recurse through private methods, but `methodUsesCodePart` does not accept the private-method table and only scans nested `if`/loop bodies. A public method delegating `addOutput`/`addRawOutput`/`addDataOutput` to a private helper can therefore omit `_codePart`, after which the inlined output builder calls `bringToTop("_codePart", false)`.

evidence.CX-BUG-029: `_codePart` provisioning depends on `methodUsesCodePart` at lines 633-635; that scan has no `MethodCall` recursion at lines 697-709; `lowerAddOutput` requires `_codePart` at lines 3447-3448.

remediation.CX-BUG-029: Make code-part discovery recursively follow private-method calls with cycle protection, matching the adjacent preimage and variable-state scans.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-029: A stateful public method that calls a private helper containing `addOutput` must compile and provision `_codePart`.

verification.evidence: compilers/java/src/main/java/runar/compiler/passes/StackLower.java:999-1010 — `methodUsesCodePart(List<AnfBinding> body)` takes only a body list, recurses into If/Loop nested bindings, but has NO privateMethods/MethodCall case at all. Contrast with the sibling `methodUsesCheckPreimage` (:973-996), which takes `(body, privateMethods, seen)` and explicitly recurses through `MethodCall` targets (:986-993). The javadoc immediately above the neighboring `methodReadsVarLenState` (:1013-1029) even names this exact class of bug as 'Deep-review finding C18: private methods are INLINED into the caller's stack context, so the scan must recurse through private method_call targets exactly like the sibling methodUsesCheckPreimage' — but that fix was applied to methodReadsVarLenState, not to methodUsesCodePart, which still lacks it.

items.title: Java: ConstantFold's environment keeps a stale constant value after a same-name rebinding to a nonconstant value
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [CX-BUG-031] A binding updates the constant environment only when its new value is constant. Rebinding a name to a parameter, property, opaque call, or other nonconstant value leaves the old constant in the environment, so later operations can be folded using a stale value.

evidence.CX-BUG-031: Lines 102-108 perform `env.put` only for non-null constant slots and never remove `binding.name()` otherwise; later binops and calls trust `env.get` at lines 121-165.

remediation.CX-BUG-031: Remove the existing environment entry before evaluating or recording every rebinding, then add it back only when the replacement is proven constant.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-031: After `x=1; x=load_param("p"); y=x+1`, `y` must remain a `BinOp` rather than fold to `2`.

verification.evidence: compilers/java/src/main/java/runar/compiler/passes/ConstantFold.java:102-107 (foldBinding): `env.put(binding.name(), slot)` only executes inside `if (slot != null)` — when a name is rebound to a nonconstant value, the environment entry for that name is never removed or overwritten, leaving the prior constant visible to later lookups (foldValue's `env.get(bin.left())`/`env.get(bin.right())` at :122-123). No `env.remove(...)` call exists anywhere in the file (grepped).
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate, code-verified exactly as described.

items.testable_assertion_verified: ANF `t_x = 1; t_x = load_param("p"); t_y = t_x + 1` (same-name rebinding via the `emitNamed`/`@ref:` pattern AnfLower uses for reassignment) must fold `t_y` to a `BinOp` referencing the live load_param, not to the constant `2`.

items.title: Java: state pushdata encoder/decoder omit PUSHDATA4, so values >= 65536 bytes (which input limits otherwise allow) cannot be encoded/decoded correctly
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [CX-BUG-040] Values below 76 use a direct prefix, below 256 use PUSHDATA1, and every value at or above 256 is encoded as PUSHDATA2 with only two length bytes. The decoder likewise handles direct, PUSHDATA1, and PUSHDATA2 only, although accepted input limits allow payloads far larger than 65,535 bytes.

evidence.CX-BUG-040: The encoder's final branch unconditionally emits `4d` and a two-byte length; decoder branches on 77 and otherwise assumes 76. `rg -n "PUSHDATA4|0x4e|\"4e\"" StackLower.java` returned zero matches.

remediation.CX-BUG-040: Add PUSHDATA4 encode/decode branches and reject values beyond the supported script/state limit explicitly.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-040: A 65,536-byte mutable state value must serialize with `0x4e` plus a four-byte little-endian length and deserialize byte-identically.

verification.evidence: StackLower.java's on-chain state-value pushdata encoder, Ctx.emitPushDataEncode() (5108-5219), branches three ways on OP_SIZE: len<76 -> direct 1-byte prefix, len<256 -> 0x4c+1-byte (PUSHDATA1), and its final OP_ELSE (5189-5213) unconditionally treats EVERY remaining length (including >=65536) as 0x4d+2-byte-LE (PUSHDATA2) with no length check and no PUSHDATA4 branch. The matching decoder, emitPushDataDecode() (4313-4394), only discriminates fb<76 (direct), fb==77/0x4d (2-byte LE length), and falls through its final OP_ELSE (4375-4389) assuming fb==76/0x4c (1-byte length) for anything else — there is no fb==78/0x4e case, so a genuine PUSHDATA4-encoded value would be misdecoded as a 1-byte-length PUSHDATA1. packages/runar-ir-schema/src/input-limits.ts:75 sets MAX_STRING_BYTES to 4 MiB, far above the 65,535-byte boundary where PUSHDATA2 overflows, and IRInputLimits.MAX_IR_BYTES (16 MiB) / InputLimits.MAX_SOURCE_BYTES (4 MiB) impose no tighter cap on a mutable ByteString/Sig/SigHashPreimage field's length, so a value in the affected range is not rejected upstream.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate and precise — the cited StackLower.java region and the encoder/decoder asymmetry both hold exactly as described at HEAD; only the specific line numbers (3315-4161 span given) were a loose approximation of the true encoder (~5108-5219) / decoder (~4313-4394) locations.

items.testable_assertion_verified: A 65,536-byte mutable ByteString/Sig/SigHashPreimage state value must serialize through emitPushDataEncode with an 0x4e (PUSHDATA4) prefix followed by a 4-byte little-endian length, and emitPushDataDecode must decode that same encoding byte-identically; today the encoder instead writes 0x4d plus a 2-byte length that truncates/wraps for such a value, and the decoder has no fb==78 case at all.

items.title: Java: ANF loader silently converts missing or wrongly-typed required collections (properties/methods/params/body) into empty lists instead of failing
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [CX-BUG-046] Missing or non-list `properties`, `methods`, `params`, and `body` values silently become empty lists, while missing strings become null. The `--ir` path performs no schema validation afterward, and emitting a program with no public methods succeeds with an empty script.

evidence.CX-BUG-046: Each loader branch conditionally populates a newly-created empty list only when the value is already a list; helper list conversions behave identically. Emit explicitly returns `""` when public methods are absent.

remediation.CX-BUG-046: Validate all required fields and exact JSON types before constructing ANF records; reject null names and absent bodies.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-046: `--ir --hex` on `{"contractName":"X","properties":{},"methods":{}}` must fail with a schema error rather than succeed with empty hex.

verification.evidence: AnfLoader.toProgram (71-165) still silently treats a non-List/missing `properties` (74-77) or `methods` (78-82) as an empty list with no schema error, and toMethod (361-378) does the identical thing for a method's `params` (364-371) and `body` (372-376). HOWEVER the literal repro in this item's own testable_assertion — `{"contractName":"X","properties":{},"methods":{}}` — no longer demonstrates 'succeeds with empty hex': `methods` coerces to an empty list, which trips the unrelated N-113/R-081 no-public-methods guard added since review (107-116: 'contract X has no public methods... an empty locking script is anyone-can-spend'), so the call now throws. That guard is a coincidental catch, not schema validation, and it does not cover every malformed shape: a well-formed public method (valid `name`/`isPublic`) whose `body` field is present-but-wrong-typed (e.g. a JSON string, or simply omitted) still silently becomes an empty AnfBinding list at toMethod:372-376, sails through checkCallArity/checkAddOutputArity (both iterate zero bindings and find nothing to complain about), and reaches Emit with a public method whose ops list is empty — for the single-public-method case (Emit.java's runResultFull, ~266-321) that still yields a truncated/anyone-can-spend locking script from externally-supplied IR, silently.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Correctly identifies the absence of schema validation in the loader, which still holds at HEAD for nested fields (params/body) — but the specific top-level example given as the testable_assertion has since been overtaken by an unrelated guard (no-public-methods) and no longer demonstrates 'succeeds with empty hex.'

items.testable_assertion_verified: `--ir --hex` on a single-public-method contract whose method JSON has `"body": "not-an-array"` (or omits `body` entirely) instead of a binding array must fail with an explicit schema error identifying the malformed field, not silently compile to a non-empty artifact whose public method carries zero ops. (The finding's own literal example, empty-object `properties`/`methods`, now fails via the separate no-public-methods guard rather than schema validation, so it no longer isolates the defect.)

items.title: The tier-version drift gate cannot match the current version family
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-238] self-test for the gate CL-BUG-238 proves is blind** — and the end-to-end Solidity and Move examples,
so 2 of the 9 surface formats have no e2e coverage at all.

...
## CL-BUG-238 — HIGH / P1 — The tier-version drift gate cannot match the current version family
**Executed by the worker, regex behaviour shown.** `ci.yml:52` runs `bump-version.sh --check` and
`CHANGELOG.md:56-57` records it as the mechanism enforcing version coherence. Three defects:
1. `COMPILER_VERSION_FILES` (the six embedded per-compiler version strings) is **declared at line 45
   and referenced nowhere else in the file.**
2. `ZIG_ZON` and `RUBY_GEMSPEC` are referenced only inside `bump_version()`, never inside
   `check_versions()`.
3. The generic sweep — the **only** coverage for Java's `Version.java`, all 7 `build.gradle.kts`,
   the ordinals tests and the sdk-output fixtures — filters every line through
   `grep -E '0\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+'`. Executed: `1.0.0-rc.1` → no match. `1.0.0` → no match.
   `1.0.0-rc.0` → no match. `0.9.1` → **matches**.

**The gate sees only pre-1.0 leftovers.** `bump-version.sh --check` on the current tree prints
*"All versions consistent"* with Java, Zig, Ruby and all six embedded compiler strings never examined
— and its own self-test is one of the dark files in CL-GAP-129.

...
## CL-BUG-238 — CONFIRMED with an empirical detectability sweep, and it is BROADER than I recorded
The worker injected drift into `Version.java` + `build.gradle.kts` under `/tmp/fakeroot/` and swept:

| drifted value | gate |
|---|---|
| `7.7.7`, `2.0.0`, `1.0.1`, `1.0.0`, `1.0.0-rc.2`, `0.3.1`, `0.2.0`, `0.0.0` | **PASS (blind)** |
| `0.9.0`, `0.5.2`, `0.10.4` | FAIL (fires) |

**It is not an rc-suffix problem.** The filter matches only a `0.N.M` substring, so it detects drift
**only when the drift

BUT the third defect (the title's actual claim) is UNFIXED: the generic Java/gradle/fixture sweep at scripts/bump-version.sh:186 still filters through `grep -E '0\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+'` (present unchanged in the R-211 diff's context lines, i.e. predates R-211 and survives it), which requires a literal `0.N.M` substring to fire. The repo's current version family is `1.0.0-rc.1` (package.json:2) — neither that value nor a drifted same-family value like `1.0.1`, `2.0.0`, or `1.0.0-rc.2` contains a `0.N.M` substring, so the sweep is still blind to drift in Version.java/build.gradle.kts/etc. within the current 1.x version family, exactly as CL-BUG-238 titled it.

items.description:
[CX-BUG-071] The generic CLI serializer has no mapping from dataclass field `sighash_type` to canonical `sigHashType`, so non-default method policy is emitted as `sighash_type`. Note for that item: Python compiler.py:1134 already emits a method-level sigHashType the schema forbids while __main__.py excludes it - resolve both together. Option (b) (recover from check_preimage sighashFlag) cannot work for stateless contracts.

evidence.CX-BUG-071: `_SNAKE_TO_CAMEL` omits `sighash_type`, the generic loop emits unmapped names, and `_anf_method_from_dict` reads `d.get("sigHashType")` only.

remediation.CX-BUG-071: Add the canonical mapping and add a round-trip fixture for every non-default supported sighash combination.

Direct --source compile's artifact has abi.methods[0].sigHashType == 67 (0x43). The SAME source compiled via --emit-ir then reloaded via --ir loses it entirely (key absent from abi.methods[0]). Root cause: __main__.py's _IR_EXCLUDED_FIELDS (line ~338) excludes ANFMethod.sighash_type from the --emit-ir generic camelCase serializer by design (the mode is meant to ride on the check_preimage node's sighashFlag instead, per the comment there), but ir/types.py:508 (_anf_method_from_dict) still reads sighash_type=d.get('sigHashType') on reload -- a key that was never written -- so it silently becomes None. The underlying SCRIPT bytes round-trip correctly (test_n094_sighash_ir_wire_format.py already covers that, via the separately round-tripping sighashFlag field on the check_preimage node), but the ABI-level sigHashType the SDK reads to decide what preimage to sign does not -- a gap that test suite does not check.

items.title: Python `bn254G1Add` returns a silently different, still on-curve point for constructible ω-partner input pairs (Fermat-inverse of 0 in the denominator returns 0, not an error)
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-144] ## CL-BUG-144 — HIGH / P1 — `bn254G1Add` silently returns a *different on-curve point* for a constructible class of valid inputs
Source: impl-python-codegen NEW-03/U1, numerically constructed by the worker.
`bn254.py:568-570` computes `s_den = py + qy` and `:573` divides by it via `_bn254_field_inv`, which
is Fermat exponentiation `a^(p-2)` and therefore **returns 0 for input 0 with no error**
(`bn254.py:436-460`). The docstring at `bn254.py:546-554` claims *"The only input that still fails
is P == -Q"*. It is wrong on both counts:
- **The set is larger.** p ≡ 1 mod 3, so every P with px ≠ 0 has two further on-curve partners
  (ω·px, −py) and (ω²·px, −py) whose x-coordinates *differ* — exactly the pairs the docstring calls
  safe. Constructed witness: P = G1 = (1, 2), Q = (ω, p−2) with
  ω = `0x30644e72e131a0295e6dd9e7e0acccb0c28f069fbb966e3de4bd44e5607cfd48`.
- **It does not fail.** It returns a point, and for these ω-pairs that point is **itself on the
  curve** (the worker verified `ry² ≡ rx³ + 3 mod p`), so a downstream `bn254G1OnCurve` sanity check
  cannot detect it. The `P == −Q` case by contrast yields an *off*-curve point, which a check catches.

Silent wrong-but-valid output is the worst shape this can take. Same policy caveat as CL-BUG-142.


DISPATCHER RE-SCOPE (2026-10-04): the subagent proved (strict @bsv/sdk Spend) that the Go REFERENCE and every port emit byte-identical bytes that ACCEPT the wrong on-curve point (omega*px, -py) collision and REJECT the true sum. Fix option (b), fail-closed in the bn254G1Add builtin entry point only (not the shared bn254G1AffineAdd used by Groth16 MSM): Go first, then every port, byte-identical; add bn254G1Add to conformance/go-only-parity; correct the false 'keeps its fail-closed off-curve answer' comments.

verification.evidence: bn254.py:551-604 (_bn254_g1_infinity_flag/_bn254_g1_mask_infinity) added a P==-Q detector keyed on xeq AND NOT yeq (masks rx,ry to the all-zero infinity point only when px==qx), which fixes the narrow P==-Q case the old docstring claimed was the only failure. The ω-partner class the finding describes has px != qx (Q=(ω*px,-py)) while still having py+qy==0, so xeq is 0, notinf computes to 1, and _bn254_g1_mask_infinity (bn254.py:607-620) leaves the unified-formula result UNMASKED. _bn254_field_inv (bn254.py:435-459, Fermat a^(p-2)) still silently returns 0 for a 0 input with no error path, so the ω-partner witness's zero denominator still produces a wrong-but-finite, on-curve point that emit_bn254_g1_add returns unmasked.

items.testable_assertion_verified: bn254G1Add(P, Q) with P = G1 = (1,2) and Q = (ω*1 mod p, p-2), ω = 0x30644e72e131a0295e6dd9e7e0acccb0c28f069fbb966e3de4bd44e5607cfd48: the compiled script returns a different, wrong on-curve point than the true sum P+Q. A test comparing against an independently computed reference sum fails today.
