items.description: [CX-BUG-054] `_fold_binding` adds a constant fact when the new value is constant but never removes an older fact when the same name is rebound to a parameter, property, call, or other nonconstant value. Later operations can consequently fold using a stale value.

evidence.CX-BUG-054: Lines 405-408 conditionally assign `env[binding.name]` with no preceding invalidation; binops and calls subsequently trust membership in `env` at lines 423-445.

remediation.CX-BUG-054: Invalidate the binding name before evaluating/recording every rebinding, then add it only when the new value is proven constant.

verification.evidence: `_fold_binding` (constant_fold.py:421-429) computes `cv = _anf_value_to_const(folded_value)` and does `if cv is not None: env[binding.name] = cv` -- but there is no corresponding `else: env.pop(binding.name, None)` (or equivalent invalidation) when the new binding is NOT constant. items.title: Ruby: a `false`-valued property initializer is treated as absent by stack lowering's truthy `reject`, corrupting constructor placeholder indices
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [CX-BUG-083] Stack lowering selects constructor properties with `reject { |p| p.initial_value }`, which treats `false` as absent, while artifact ABI assembly correctly treats every non-`nil` initializer as initialized. A `false`-initialized property before a genuine constructor property shifts the emitted placeholder index away from the ABI parameter index.

evidence.CX-BUG-083: The two paths use truthiness versus explicit `nil?` semantics for the same decision.

remediation.CX-BUG-083: Test initializer presence with `nil?` consistently across codegen and artifact assembly.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-083: With `enabled = false` followed by uninitialized `key`, the key placeholder has parameter index 0 and matches the sole constructor ABI parameter.

verification.evidence: compilers/ruby/lib/runar_compiler/codegen/stack.rb:1668 -- `ctor_props = @properties.reject { |p| p.initial_value }` uses Ruby truthiness, not a nil check. `_extract_literal_value` (frontend/anf_lower.rb:283-284) returns the bare Ruby `false` for a `BoolLiteral` initializer, so a property declared `= false` has `initial_value == false`. `Array#reject` removes elements where the block is truthy; `false` is falsy in Ruby, so the block returns false and the property is NOT rejected -- it wrongly stays in `ctor_props` as if uninitialized, shifting the constructor placeholder `param_index` (computed at line 1669) for every subsequent genuinely-uninitialized property. Contrast with the correct `.nil?`-based checks elsewhere in the same file (line 1662: `elsif prop && !prop.initial_value.nil?`) and throughout compiler.rb (lines 394, 413, 859, 892, 898, 1082, 1204), all of which use explicit `.nil?` and are unaffected.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate; CX's file:line citations (stack.rb ~1511-1515 at the reviewed commit) match this exact `reject` call, now at line 1668 after unrelated line drift in the intervening ~620 commits.

items.testable_assertion_verified: A contract with a mutable `enabled: bool = false` property declared before an uninitialized `key: bigint` property compiles such that the `key` placeholder's `param_index` is 0, matching the sole ABI constructor parameter's index; currently `enabled` (despite being initialized) is wrongly counted as a constructor property, shifting `key`'s placeholder index off by one.

items.title: Ruby: FixedArray expansion drops @embedAlways when rebuilding PropertyNode for each array slot
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-270] ## CL-BUG-270 — HIGH / P1 — `@embedAlways` is silently dropped on every FixedArray property
`expand_fixed_arrays.rb:304-311` — **dispatcher-verified, and I read the constructor call:**
```ruby
out << PropertyNode.new(
  name: slot, type: meta.element_type, readonly: readonly,
  initializer: slot_init, source_location: loc,
  synthetic_array_chain: chain_here
)                                   # <-- embed_always: is NOT passed; defaults false
```
Byte-level proof from the worker: an `@embedAlways readonly` scalar emits **5 bytes with one
constructor slot**; the identical property as `FixedArray<…,2>` emits **2 bytes and zero slots** —
DCE'd away. **This is precisely the failure issue #109 added the directive to prevent.**

**CLASS 1 again, and this is now the fifth language it has appeared in.**


DISPATCHER RE-SCOPE (R35, user 2026-10-04): the drop is in all 7 tiers incl. TS; user chose PROPAGATE embedAlways to every expanded FixedArray slot. Closes F-122 and N-034 too.

verification.evidence: compilers/ruby/lib/runar_compiler/frontend/expand_fixed_arrays.rb:227-231 (`expand_property_root`) calls `expand_array_meta(meta, prop.readonly, prop.source_location, init_elements, [])` -- passes `prop.readonly` but never `prop.embed_always`. `expand_array_meta` (from line 304) rebuilds each array slot as `PropertyNode.new(name:, type:, readonly:, initializer:, source_location:, synthetic_array_chain:)` (lines 356-362) with no `embed_always:` keyword, so it defaults to `false` (ast_nodes.rb:206: `embed_always: false`). `embed_always_dce.rb:29` (`next if prop.respond_to?(:embed_always) && prop.embed_always`) therefore never skips an expanded FixedArray slot, so every synthetic slot of an `@embedAlways readonly FixedArray<T,N>` property remains DCE-eligible -- exactly the failure issue #109 was written to prevent. `git log -S embed_always -- compilers/ruby/lib/runar_compiler/frontend/expand_fixed_arrays.rb` returns zero commits, confirming this was never addressed.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate; CL's line citation (304-311 at the reviewed commit) matches the current PropertyNode.new call (356-362 after unrelated line drift), and the missing `embed_always:` keyword is exactly as described.

items.testable_assertion_verified: A readonly `@embedAlways FixedArray<bigint, 2>` property whose two elements are never referenced by any method body still has both element `load_prop` bindings preserved after DCE and present in the emitted script; currently both are eliminated as dead code.

sweep1.evidence: expand_fixed_arrays.rb (~l.381) `PropertyNode.new(name: slot, type:, readonly:, initializer:, source_location:, synthetic_array_chain:)` still does not pass embed_always. Probe (ruby -Ilib bin/runar-compiler-ruby --hex): `/** @embedAlways */ readonly tag: bigint = 5n` -> 557c579c77 (kept), while `/** @embedAlways */ readonly tags: FixedArray<bigint,2> = [5n,6n]` -> 579c (both elements DCE'd). Go and TS also emit 579c / a 4-char script for the array case, so this is not Ruby-only.

items.title: Ruby: checkMultiSig accepts bigint arrays because array literals have no inferred type, so the argument-subtype guard at typecheck.rb:1262 vacuously passes on <unknown>
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-273] ## CL-BUG-273 — HIGH / P1 — `checkMultiSig` accepts bigint arrays because array literals have no inferred type
`checkMultiSig([a,b],[a,b])` with bigint elements is **accepted and emits a real `OP_CHECKMULTISIG`
(17 bytes)**. `infer_expr_type` has no `ArrayLiteralExpr` case, so every array literal is `<unknown>`,
and the argument-subtype guard at `typecheck.rb:1262` **skips on `<unknown>`.**

verification.evidence: compilers/ruby/lib/runar_compiler/frontend/typecheck.rb:1027-1164 -- `infer_expr_type`'s `case expr` block has no `when ArrayLiteralExpr` branch; it falls through to `else` (line 1164) returning `"<unknown>"`. The builtin argument checker's standard loop (lines 1548-1560) does `arg_type = infer_expr_type(args[i], env); ... if !Frontend.subtype?(arg_type, expected_type) && arg_type != "<unknown>"` -- since `arg_type` is literally `"<unknown>"` for any array literal, the guard is always false and no error fires. `checkMultiSig` (lines 1531-1543) explicitly falls through to this same loop for its arg-type validation ('Fall through to the standard subtype check below', comment at :1531-1534, itself citing a prior '2026-04-30 audit finding F5' that believed this loop caught bigint arrays -- it does not, because the loop never produces anything but `"<unknown>"` for an array literal).
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate; CL's claim and line citation (typecheck.rb:1262 at the reviewed commit) match the current argument-subtype loop (now ~1556) exactly, and the root cause (`ArrayLiteralExpr` absent from `infer_expr_type`) is confirmed.

items.testable_assertion_verified: `checkMultiSig([1n, 2n], [1n, 2n])` (two bigint-element array literals, not `Sig[]`/`PubKey[]`) is rejected by typecheck.rb with an argument-type error; currently it typechecks cleanly and stack-lowers to a real `OP_CHECKMULTISIG`.

items.title: Rust `constructor_args` values are baked into properties with no type or length validation (wrong-typed/non-hex values silently become short or zero-byte pushes)
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.severity_note: reviewers disagreed ['HIGH', 'MEDIUM']; highest taken per §6.2 (no downgrade justified at combination time)
items.description:
[CL-BUG-261] ## CL-BUG-261 — HIGH / P1 — `constructor_args` are baked with **no type or length validation**; non-hex silently becomes zero bytes
`lib.rs:92-96` does `prop.initial_value = Some(val.clone())` after checking only that the key names a property. Against `readonly pubKeyHash: ByteString` (a RIPEMD-160, 20 bytes):

| value | emitted script | what shipped |
|---|---|---|
| `true` | `76a95188ac` | `OP_1` where a 20-byte hash belongs |
| `42` | `76a9012a88ac` | a 1-byte `0x2a` |
| `"zzzz-not-hex"` | `76a90600000000000088ac` | **6 bytes of zeros** — every non-hex nibble decoded to 0 |

All three exit 0, no diagnostic, permanently unspendable. The file that exists to guard this states its own purpose as rejecting inputs *"that would silently bake nothing and emit placeholder scripts that fail opaquely at runtime"* — and has **no test for a well-formed key with a wrong-typed value.**


[CL-GAP-038] | worker | CL ID | sev | prio | title |
| RS-DRV-23 | CL-GAP-038 | MEDIUM | v1-should-have | constructor_args values are baked with no type or length validation — the deploy-time fund-loss shape the check exists to prevent |

verification.evidence: compilers/rust/src/lib.rs:109-147 `apply_constructor_args` still only checks (b) unknown-key and (c) unbaked-referenced-readonly; the bake step at :139-143 (`prop.initial_value = Some(val.clone())`) applies ANY serde_json::Value with no type or length check against `prop.prop_type`. Downstream, `lower_load_prop` (stack.rs:1559-1587) and `push_json_value` (stack.rs:1648-1664) read that value back: a JSON bool bakes to `PushValue::Bool` (OP_1/OP_0) and a JSON number to a bare int push regardless of the property's declared ByteString/etc. type — reproducing the finding's first two rows (`true`->OP_1, `42`->1-byte push) exactly. One row has changed: `hex_to_bytes` (stack.rs:6621-6637) now `panic!`s on a non-hex string instead of silently zero-filling, so `"zzzz-not-hex"` now aborts compilation rather than emitting 6 zero bytes — a different (louder) failure mode, but still not a clean, located diagnostic, and the core 'no type/length validation before baking' defect the title names is unchanged.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: citation (lib.rs:92-96) matches current lib.rs:139-143 exactly (bake loop shifted a few lines by added doc comments); the three-row table is 2/3 still accurate, 1/3 (non-hex string) now panics instead of zero-filling

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile a stateful contract with `readonly pubKeyHash: ByteString` (a 20-byte RIPEMD-160) via the Rust tier with `constructor_args = {"pubKeyHash": true}` (JSON bool, deliberately wrong-typed adversarial input mimicking a confused/malicious SDK caller). Today `apply_constructor_args` accepts this silently and the emitted script pushes OP_1 where a 20-byte hash belongs (permanently unspendable, no diagnostic). The fix must reject the call with a type-mismatch error naming the property and expected type.

sweep1.evidence: compilers/rust/src/lib.rs apply_constructor_args (~l.109-147) still checks only unknown keys, then does `prop.initial_value = Some(val.clone())` with no type or length check. Codegen accepts these values too: an IR with `initialValue: true` on `readonly pubKeyHash: ByteString` -> 76a95188ac (OP_1 where the 20-byte hash belongs), and `42` -> 76a9012a88ac, both exit 0. The non-hex string case now fails closed at stack lowering ('invalid hex string: zzzz-not-hex').

items.title: Rust `--ir` path lets the script-level sighash flag diverge from the ABI's declared sigHashType, and a truncated sighashFlag (e.g. 999999) compiles clean
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-262] ## CL-BUG-262 — HIGH / P0 — `--ir` emits a script bound to a non-default sighash while the ABI omits `sigHashType`
**Dispatcher-verified.** `ir/mod.rs:46` `parent_class` and `:91` `sighash_type` are both `#[serde(skip, default)]`; `:246` `sighash_flag` is `#[serde(rename="sighashFlag")]` — **serialized**. So the script-level flag round-trips and the ABI-level declaration does not.
- `sighashFlag: 0x43` → script carries `01 43 7e` at 2 sites; artifact reports `sigHashType = None`. The SDK builds an ALL|FORKID preimage; the covenant expects SINGLE|FORKID; **the UTXO is unspendable through that SDK.**
- `sighashFlag: 999999` → **exit 0**, bytes change from `01 41 7e` to `01 3f 7e`. `999999 & 0xff = 0x3F` — **FORKID bit clear.** On BSV that signature can never verify. `oppushtx.rs:37` truncates with `(v & 0xff) as u8` and `validate_ir` range-checks nothing.
- `parentClass` — `--source` emits `"StatefulSmartContract"`, `--ir` emits **nothing**, for a byte-identical script. `artifact.rs:109-113` calls that field the *"authoritative stateful signal for the issue-#42/#44 terminal sighash subscript trim"*.

**This is the tenth `@sighash` defect and the second tier in which the same flag truncates.** The Go tier's identical finding is CL-BUG-2xx; the Rust one was found independently with its own citations.

verification.evidence: compilers/rust/src/ir/mod.rs:46-47 `ANFProgram.parent_class` and :95 `ANFMethod.sighash_type` are both still `#[serde(skip, default)]`, so `ir/loader.rs`'s plain `serde_json::from_str::<ANFProgram>(...)` (loader.rs:41) always resets them to empty-string/None on any `--ir` load — no post-deserialize derivation exists. artifact.rs:233 `sig_hash_type = match m.sighash_type {...}` and :298 `parent_class: program.parent_class.clone()` read straight from those always-default fields, so an artifact assembled from `--ir` reports `sigHashType: null` and no `parentClass` even when the script bytes encode a non-default sighash. compilers/rust/src/codegen/oppushtx.rs:38-39 still truncates with `(v & 0xff) as u8` and `validate_ir` (ir/loader.rs:182-258) performs zero range-checking on `sighashFlag`, so `sighashFlag: 999999` still silently becomes byte 0x3F (FORKID bit clear) with exit 0.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: all three citations (artifact.rs:109-113, oppushtx.rs:37, ir/mod.rs:46) match HEAD almost exactly (oppushtx.rs line is 38-39 now, one line later) — fully accurate, defect unchanged

items.testable_assertion_verified: Load an ANF-IR JSON file via `compile_from_ir` whose sole `check_preimage` binding carries `"sighashFlag": 999999`. Today this compiles at exit 0 with the script byte truncated to 0x3F (FORKID bit clear, an unspendable/unverifiable signature) and no diagnostic; the fix must reject any sighashFlag outside the valid BIP-143/BSV flag combinations in `validate_ir`.

sweep1.evidence: Rust --ir with the check_preimage sighashFlag patched from 193 to 999999 -> exit=0. The script contains `013f7e` (0x3F, FORKID bit clear) where the 193 build has `01c17e`. No validation; Go has this check (87326b4f F-068) but Rust does not. The ABI also drops sigHashType on --ir (see F-104).

items.title: Rust: `constructor_args` in `CompileOptions` is silently ignored by the ANF-IR and direct-program compile entry points; only source-pipeline entry points apply it
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [CX-BUG-087] `CompileOptions` documents constructor baking as a general compilation option, but IR entry points forward directly to `compile_from_program_with_options`, which only consults `disable_constant_folding`. Thus supplied constructor values are neither validated nor baked, and the resulting artifact retains deploy-time placeholders. Existing constructor-argument tests import only the source entry point.

evidence.CX-BUG-087: Exhaustive `constructor_args` search found application only at `lib.rs:324`, `lib.rs:422`, and `lib.rs:593`, all source pipelines; no use exists in `compile_from_program_with_options`.

remediation.CX-BUG-087: Apply constructor arguments to a cloned ANF program before optimization for IR/direct-program entry points, or split the option type so unsupported entry points cannot accept and silently ignore it.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-087: `compile_from_ir_str_with_options` with a named constructor value must embed that value and remove its constructor slot, matching source compilation.

verification.evidence: compilers/rust/src/lib.rs: compile_from_ir_with_options/compile_from_ir_str_with_options (256-275) forward into compile_from_program_with_options (527-570), which only branches on opts.disable_constant_folding (536) and never calls apply_constructor_args -- that call appears only at line 377 (compile_from_source_str_with_options) and line 486 (compile_source_str_to_ir_with_options). compile_from_program (the direct-program entry point) has the identical gap. compilers/rust/tests/constructor_args_validation_tests.rs imports only compile_from_source_str_with_options.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate: ir_input_options forwards opts via struct-update syntax so constructor_args itself survives into compile_from_program_with_options, but that function never reads the field.

items.testable_assertion_verified: compile_from_ir_str_with_options(ir_json, &CompileOptions{constructor_args, ..}) must embed the named constructor value and remove its constructor slot, matching compile_from_source_str_with_options; today it emits an artifact with an unfilled constructor slot.

sweep1.evidence: lib.rs compile_from_ir_str_with_options / compile_from_ir_with_options call `compile_from_program_with_options(&program, &ir_input_options(opts))`. compile_from_program_with_options (~l.527-575) reads only opts.disable_constant_folding and never calls apply_constructor_args. apply_constructor_args is called only on the source paths (l.377, 486, 695). So constructor_args on IR entry points are silently ignored.

items.title: Rust tier: issue-#130 shadow renaming is lost inside branches
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-095] The same three-field copy also drops `renamed_params` (re-opening issue #130 inside branches — CL-BUG-095), and `array_lengths`/`const_values`, making `checkMultiSig` and `merkleRoot*` **panic the compiler** inside a branch.

...
## CL-BUG-095 — HIGH / P1 — Rust tier: issue-#130 shadow renaming is lost inside branches
**Dispatcher-verified** (same mechanism as CL-BUG-094). `renamed_params` maps a parameter shadowing a *mutable* property to a reserved slot, and is populated only from the `params` argument in `LoweringContext::new`. Arm contexts pass `&[]`, so the map is empty inside every branch, and `lower_load_param` falls back to the bare name — which the cloned `sm` resolves to the **deserialized property**, not the parameter. Issue #130 is re-opened for every read of a shadowing parameter inside an `if`.

...
- (b) The branch sub-context drops **seven of ten** lowering fields, producing CL-BUG-094 (P0 miscompile), CL-BUG-095, and two compiler panics.

Methodological consequence for Pass F: a breadth "CLEARED" verdict is a *hypothesis that one worker failed to confirm*, not a negative result. Only the adversarial depth re-check turned these into findings. Any remaining breadth clearing that has not been depth-verified should be reported at that confidence, not as a clean area.

verification.evidence: compilers/rust/src/codegen/stack.rs: then_ctx/else_ctx in lower_if (2399, 2431) are built via LoweringContext::new(&[], &self.properties) -- empty params, so the issue-#130 renamed_params-population loop inside ::new (776-787) never runs -- and only sm, outer_protected_refs, script_level_code_separator and private_methods are explicitly copied back from the parent afterward (2400-2417, 2432-2436). renamed_params (and array_lengths/const_values) is never copied and stays an empty HashMap. lower_load_param (1533-1541) does `self.renamed_params.get(param_name).unwrap_or_else(|| param_name.to_string())`, so inside a branch it falls back to the bare name, which self.sm (cloned from the parent, so it still carries both the __param_-renamed slot and the same-named deserialized-property slot) resolves to the shallower deserialized-property slot instead of the witness parameter.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate.

items.testable_assertion_verified: A method whose parameter shadows a mutable property, read inside an if-branch, should read the witness parameter value; today (Rust tier) it reads the stale deserialized on-chain property instead -- reopening issue #130 inside branches.

items.title: `--ir` compiles a validator-rejected readonly-hijack to an anyone-can-spend script, and the tier's own debugger confirms the spend
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-263] ## CL-BUG-263 — HIGH / P0 — `--ir` compiles a validator-rejected readonly-hijack to an anyone-can-spend script, and the tier's own debugger confirms the spend
```
--source Hijack.runar.ts → Validation error: cannot assign to readonly property 'owner'
--ir     (same contract as hand-written ANF) → script 5177 = OP_TRUE OP_NIP, exit 0
         debug --script 5177 --unlock 0101 → final: pass
```
**Four tiers now, four different scripts, same hole:** Go `0093`, Rust `5177`, Python `51` and `''` (empty), Zig bypasses validate+typecheck+sighash. The worker's recommendation is the right one and it is a **single cross-tier decision, not seven patches**: either run one shared structural IR validator on every tier's `--ir` path, or remove `--ir` from every tier's public surface and keep it test-only.

verification.evidence: compilers/rust/src/ir/loader.rs validate_ir/validate_bindings (182-340+) checks contractName, property names/types, call arity, super()-placement and (N-113) at-least-one-public-method, but never checks whether an update_prop targets a property whose readonly==true. compilers/rust/src/codegen/stack.rs lower_update_prop (3127-3163) unconditionally rewrites the named stack slot with no readonly check, and lower_get_state_script (3166ff) filters state_props by !p.readonly, so a 'readonly' property's continuation state is simply omitted rather than rejected. compilers/rust/tests/readonly_property_assignment_tests.rs only exercises frontend_validate (the --source path); no Rust test drives this scenario through compile_from_ir*.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate; the structural IR validator's gap (no readonly-immutability check) is real and unfixed. Could not re-execute the compiler (read-only, no build permitted) to reconfirm the exact cited '5177'/OP_TRUE OP_NIP output bytes, but the code-level cause (no readonly guard in validate_ir or lower_update_prop) fully explains why such a script would result.

items.title: TS DCE has no "last binding is live" root: an ANF method's final (implicit-result) binding can be pruned as dead code, silently emptying a private helper's body once any EC rewrite elsewhere in the contract triggers a DCE pass
items.confidence_note: raised by GK; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'CX']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [GK-BUG-019] filterLiveBindings keeps a binding only if another binding refs it or hasSideEffect. The last binding of a method is not a liveness root. Private helpers that were not ANF-inlined (no addOutput in the helper) keep a method_call; stack-lower inlines the helper body and uses the last binding as the result. If any method in the contract hit an EC rewrite, eliminateDeadBindings runs on all methods and can delete that last bin_op. The helper body becomes empty. Trigger is common: ecMulGen(1n) is an EC rule. Tests pin unused last load_const as deleted; they do not pin EC-in-A plus helper-in-B.

evidence.GK-BUG-019: Opened dce.ts:37-47 (map every method) and :174-176 (refs or side-effect only). Opened anf-ec.ts:314-326 (anyChanged then eliminateDeadBindings on the whole program).

remediation.GK-BUG-019: Mark the last binding live. DCE only the methods that actually rewrote (Go). Never DCE private-method bodies that stack-lower will inline. Add the ecMulGen + private add1 fixture.

testable_assertion.GK-BUG-019: A contract whose public method contains ecMulGen(1n) and private add1(n){ return n+1n } used in an assert currently loses add1's body under optimizeEC.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-compiler/src/optimizer/dce.ts:81-84 (`eliminateDeadInMethod`) and :265-299 (`filterLiveBindings`) treat every ANFMethod's bindings identically — there is no notion of 'this method's last/returned binding is an implicit liveness root.' A private helper without state/data-output side effects is kept as its own ANFMethod (04-anf-lower.ts `shouldInlinePrivate`, ~lines 842-849: only inlines at ANF level when `effects.hasStateOutput || effects.hasDataOutput`); its call site stays a `method_call` and gets inlined later at stack-lower time (05-stack-lower.ts:2352-2358, 'Method return value is the last binding result' — reads `method.body[method.body.length-1].name`). If DCE runs (gated behind any EC rewrite firing anywhere in the program, anf-ec.ts optimizeEC), each method is processed independently; a helper whose sole/last binding is a pure value (e.g. `bin_op`) unreferenced by anything else IN THAT SAME METHOD has no external ref and no side effect, so `filterLiveBindings` deletes it — emptying the helper's body before stack-lower ever inlines it.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: GK-BUG-019's description of the mechanism (filterLiveBindings keeps a binding only if referenced-or-side-effecting; last binding of a method is not a liveness root; un-ANF-inlined private helpers are spliced in by stack-lower using the last binding as the result; trigger is any EC rewrite firing an eliminateDeadBindings sweep over every method) matches the code exactly.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile a contract with a public method containing `ecMulGen(1n)` (fires optimizeEC's anyChanged gate) and a private helper `add1(n: bigint): bigint { return n + 1n; }` invoked inside an `assert` in another public method. At HEAD, optimizeEC's DCE sweep deletes `add1`'s sole ANF binding (nothing inside `add1`'s own body references it, and a bin_op is pure), so stack-lower's `inlineMethodCall` inlines an empty body and the caller's assert consumes garbage/wrong state instead of `n+1`. After the fix, DCE must not delete a method's implicit return binding.

Default compile: success=false, error "Value 't2' not found on stack (stack has 2 items: [n, t3])"; ANF add1 body = [] (emptied by EC-gated DCE). With disableEcOptimizer:true: success=true, add1 = [t0 load_param n, t1 load_const, t2 bin_op +]. The helper's implicit-result binding is still pruned (now surfaces as a compile failure of valid source, not a silent miscompile).

items.description: [GK-BUG-035] Rules ec-add-identity-right/left rewrite ecAdd(x, INFINITY) → x. items.title: TS: `ConstEnv` has no delete/invalidate operation, so rebinding an ANF name previously recorded as a constant (e.g. to a parameter or property load) leaves the stale constant value in the folding environment and later expressions can be folded against it incorrectly
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [CX-BUG-097] `ConstEnv` has no delete/invalidate operation. A binding records a constant when it is `load_const`, but rebinding that same ANF name to a parameter, property, call, or other nonconstant value leaves the old constant in the environment. Later expressions can therefore be folded using an obsolete value, changing assertions or arithmetic.

evidence.CX-BUG-097: `foldBinding` only calls `env.set` for a constant and performs no action for a nonconstant redefinition (`constant-fold.ts:260-275`). ANF lowering deliberately emits repeated named bindings for local assignment.

remediation.CX-BUG-097: Delete a name from the constant environment before processing/re-registering every binding, then register it only if the new value is a true constant.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-097: Folding `[x=1, x=load_param(p), y=x+1]` must leave `y` as `bin_op`, not fold it to `2`.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-compiler/src/optimizer/constant-fold.ts:245-266 — `ConstEnv` has `set`/`get`/`has`/`clone` and no `delete`/invalidate method. :289-300 `foldBinding` only calls `env.set(name, v)` when the folded value is a *direct* `load_const` (excluding `@ref:`-prefixed alias markers); it never clears an existing `env` entry for `name` when the new value is non-constant (`load_param`, `load_prop`, `@ref:`-wrapped alias, etc.). Calling `foldConstants` directly on a hand-built ANF program `[t0=load_const(1n), t0=load_param('p'), t1=bin_op('+',t0,<const>)]` would fold `t1` to a wrong constant using the stale value of `t0`. HOWEVER: traced the real producer (packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/04-anf-lower.ts) end to end — `lowerVariableDecl` (:1178-1191) and `lowerAssignment` (:1194-1213), the only two real-lowering call sites that rebind a name, ALWAYS wrap the rebinding value as `load_const {value: '@ref:'+ref}` (an alias marker), which `foldBinding`'s own `@ref:` exclusion deliberately keeps OUT of `env` in the first place. Fresh temp names (`ctx.emit()`, :701-707) use a monotonic counter and are never reused, even across if/else sub-contexts (`subContext`/`syncCounter` at :920-974 keep them disjoint). So the specific stale-then-refolded scenario described requires either hand-constructed ANF (as this and many existing unit tests do) or an external `--ir` producer — and per V345, TS's `--ir` entry point never runs `foldConstants` at all, so it isn't reachable that way either in the TS tier today.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: accurate about the code-level defect (ConstEnv genuinely lacks invalidation); does not address that real 04-anf-lower.ts output structurally avoids triggering it via the `@ref:` alias-exclusion design — worth noting for triage priority.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Call `foldConstants` directly on `makeProgram([makeMethod('m', [b('t0', {kind:'load_const', value:1n}), b('t0', {kind:'load_param', name:'p'}), b('t1', {kind:'bin_op', op:'+', left:'t0', right: b('t2', {kind:'load_const', value:1n})})])])` (same style as existing optimizer.test.ts hand-built-ANF tests) and assert `t1`'s folded value stays `bin_op`, not `load_const(2n)`.

items.title: `blake3Compress`/`sha256Compress` accept mis-sized operands in all 7 tiers, enabling a second-preimage-style collision via OP_NUM2BIN truncation
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-086] ## CL-BUG-086 — HIGH / P1 — `blake3Compress` and `sha256Compress` accept mis-sized operands in all 7 tiers (second-preimage collision)
**Dispatcher-verified structurally.** Source: crypto:hashes F1.

Neither compress program validates the length of either attacker-supplied operand. Verified across all 12 hash codegen files (TS/Go/Rust/Python/Ruby/Java × sha256+blake3): **`OP_EQUALVERIFY` count = 0 in every file**, and the single `OP_SIZE` in each is the `blake3Hash` block-length capture or the `sha256Finalize` padded-length branch — never an operand guard.

Confirmed at the byte level in the shipped golden `conformance/sdk-output/tests/blake3/expected-locking.hex`: the `verifyCompress` branch opens `76009c6375` (selector dispatch) and goes **straight into 15 consecutive `547f` = `OP_4 OP_SPLIT`** with no size check in between.

The collision mechanism, verified at `codegen-emitter.ts:99-105`:
```ts
num2le(): void {
  this.pushI(5n); this.binOp('OP_NUM2BIN');  // 5-byte LE
  this.pushI(4n); this.split(); this.drop(); // discard overflow byte
}
```
BLAKE3 message words are only ever *addends* (`a = a + b + mx`), never rotated or XORed, and `addN` ends in `num2le`, which truncates to 32 bits. So a 65th byte contributes `c4·2^32`, which is discarded: **for any 64-byte block `B`, `B || 0x01` yields a byte-identical digest.** Symmetrically, 60-63-byte blocks collide with their zero-padded 64-byte form, because `le2num` zero-extends a short word. The same holds for the final state word of `sha256Compress`.

Impact is bounded by usage: this breaks any contract that asserts `blake3Compress(cv, block) === committed` **and then also uses `block`** (extracts a field, forwards it, re-emits it in a continuation). The worker found no shipped example doing so, which is why it filed P1

verification.evidence: packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/codegen-emitter.ts:97-103 `num2le()` — `pushI(5n); OP_NUM2BIN; pushI(4n); split(); drop();` truncates any accumulated sum to its low 4 bytes, discarding overflow. packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/blake3-codegen.ts:423-425 `emitBlake3Compress` splices `getCompressOps()` with zero length validation on either the chaining-value or block operand — `generateCompressOps` (:273-284) only does `for (let i=0;i<15;i++) em.split4()` (repeated `OP_SPLIT 4`) with no size assertion first, and `em.assert(17, ...)` at :285 is a compile-time TypeScript sanity check on the emitter's internal depth counter, NOT an emitted runtime opcode (`Emitter.assert`, codegen-emitter.ts:71-74, throws a JS Error at codegen time, emits nothing). Same absence of any `OP_EQUALVERIFY`/`OP_SIZE`-guard confirmed in packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/sha256-codegen.ts (no `OP_EQUALVERIFY` anywhere in the file). Mechanism verified: a 65-byte block `B || 0x01` produces a 5-byte final split remainder; `add32`'s `le2num()`/`num2le()` round-trip treats the 5th byte as bits 32-39 of the sum, which `num2le`'s truncation then discards — so `B` and `B||0x01` produce byte-identical compression output, exactly as described. Undersized blocks (<64 bytes) DO abort via OP_SPLIT failure; only the oversized-operand collision is unguarded.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: accurate and thorough — the reviewer's byte-level mechanism (num2le truncation, OP_NUM2BIN/OP_SPLIT sequence) reproduces exactly against the current codegen-emitter.ts/blake3-codegen.ts source.

items.title: TS EC optimizer single-pass vs Go fixed-point; chained rewrites diverge
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-003] | worker | CL ID | sev | prio | title |
| F-004 | CL-BUG-003 | HIGH | v1-blocker | TS EC optimizer single-pass vs Go fixed-point; chained rewrites diverge |

verification.evidence: packages/runar-compiler/src/optimizer/anf-ec.ts:325-347 (`optimizeMethodEC`) is a single `for (const binding of method.body)` sweep with no outer `while(changed)`/fixed-point loop, and `tryRewrite` (:116 onward) applies at most one rule per binding per call and returns immediately — a rewritten binding whose NEW value (e.g. Rule 10's `ecMulGen(k1+k2)` at :237-249) itself matches another rule (Rule 5, `ecMulGen(0) → INFINITY`, :132-135) is never re-examined. Contrast compilers/go/frontend/anf_optimize.go:41-94 (`optimizeMethodEC`), which wraps the same per-binding scan in `changed := true; for changed { changed = false; ... }` — an explicit fixed-point loop. A closely related bug (Rust's EC optimizer running single-pass while 'every other peer runs to a fixpoint') was found and fixed in commit e4c2cbd6 (R-221) — but that commit's own enumeration of fixpoint-looping peers (Go/Python/Ruby/Zig/Java) never lists TypeScript, and no subsequent commit touched anf-ec.ts's loop structure.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate — confirmed TS's optimizeMethodEC is single-pass, in direct contrast to Go's explicit fixed-point loop. The e4c2cbd6/R-221 commit fixed the identical architectural defect in Rust but never touched TypeScript, so the divergence this vid describes remains live.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile ANF containing `ecAdd(ecMulGen(CURVE_N - 7n), ecMulGen(7n))` bound to a name that is later used. Today TS's single pass applies Rule 10 once, producing an unreduced `ecMulGen(<newName>)` call where `<newName>` resolves to the constant 0 — Rule 5 never re-fires on it, so TS emits a runtime EC-multiplication script for what is provably the point at infinity, while Go/Python/Ruby/Zig/Java (which loop to a fixed point) fold it straight to the INFINITY constant. This is a live cross-tier hex divergence, violating invariant #2 (byte-identical Stack IR/hex for non-allowlisted fixtures). After the fix, TS's optimizeMethodEC must iterate until no rule fires, mirroring Go's `for changed {}`.

sweep1.evidence: scratch p115.mjs/C115.runar.ts: `ecAdd(ecMulGen(N-7n), ecMulGen(7n))`. TS ANF ends with `t4_k load_const 0; t4 call ecMulGen [t4_k]` (Rule 5 not re-applied; anf-ec.ts single pass), script 1,276,384 bytes. Go (runar-go -hex) and Rust both emit 851,000 bytes with a 64-zero-byte INFINITY push — live cross-tier hex divergence.

items.title: `@sighash SINGLE` multi-output validation undercounts a loop body
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-205] | ID | tier | defect |
| CL-BUG-205 | Python + TS | the SINGLE multi-output rule undercounts a loop body, so a method binding three outputs passes with a warning |

verification.evidence: packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/sighash-validate.ts:283 (`if (STATE_OUTPUT_INTRINSICS.has(name)) scan.stateOutputCount += 1;`) increments per SYNTACTIC occurrence inside `walkExpr`, and the `for_statement` case in `walkStmt` (:250-254, `walkBody(stmt.body)`) walks a ForStmt's body exactly ONCE regardless of the loop's iteration count. At :179-192, `committed = stateOutputs + scan.dataOutputCount`; `committed > 1` routes to the ERROR branch (`push(...)`) but `committed === 1` routes only to a WARNING (`pushWarn(...)`). A single `addOutput` call written inside a 3-iteration loop therefore yields `stateOutputCount = 1`, `committed = 1` — the WARNING branch — even though the ANF keeps the unrolled loop and three outputs are bound at runtime, only one of which (the same-index one) is actually committed under SINGLE. compilers/python/runar_compiler/frontend/sighash_validate.py:302-305 has the identical structure.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate — sighash-validate.ts:283 and the ForStmt single-walk are exactly as cited. Note: CL's own ledger later downgraded the PYTHON side of this same finding (CL-BUG-205) from HIGH/P1 to MEDIUM/P2, because a separate Python-only stack-lowering bug (PY-FE-01, '_newAmount is not on the stack') makes the vulnerable shape uncompilable in that tier today. I found no analogous TS-side compile blocker for this shape, so that specific reachability downgrade does not obviously transfer to the TS tier this vid is filed under — confirming would require actually compiling the shape through TS's full pipeline (not permitted under this task's read-only/no-build constraint).

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile a `StatefulSmartContract` public method annotated `/** @sighash SINGLE|FORKID */` whose body is `for (let i = 0n; i < 3n; i++) { this.addOutput(1000n, i); }`. Today `validateSighashUsage` (or its Python equivalent) returns only a warning, not an error, even though the ANF loop node carries `body.length` outputs × the (compile-time-constant) iteration count — 2 of the 3 outputs are uncommitted and attacker-controllable under BIP-143 SINGLE. After the fix, output-intrinsic occurrences inside a bounded loop must be multiplied by the loop's iteration count before the multi-output threshold check.

items.title: FixedArray expansion can collide with user-declared `name__index` properties
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [CX-BUG-102] Expansion unconditionally synthesizes names such as `Board__0`, while retaining every non-array property, and performs no collision check. Stack lowering resolves properties with the first matching name, so a collision can bind a generated access or constructor placeholder to the wrong field. The comment only claims double underscores avoid collision with `Board_0`; it does not reserve or reject the actual generated namespace.

evidence.CX-BUG-102: `rewriteProperties()` appends existing scalar properties and generated properties without uniqueness validation. `rg -n "duplicate|Duplicate" packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/02-validate.ts` returned only the unrelated line 1018 checkPreimage warning, and no property-name duplicate validation. Stack lowering uses `_properties.find(...)` at line 1379.

remediation.CX-BUG-102: Reserve the synthetic naming namespace or reject any expansion whose generated name collides with a source property. Validate uniqueness again after expansion.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-102: A contract declaring both `Board: FixedArray<bigint, 2>` and `Board__0: bigint` must fail with a duplicate/generated-name diagnostic.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/03b-expand-fixed-arrays.ts:326-342 `rewriteProperties()` pushes every non-array property through unchanged (line 330) and appends generated leaf properties from `expandArrayMeta` with no check against the retained names, for any collision. packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/05-stack-lower.ts:1581 resolves a property by `this._properties.find(p => p.name === propName)`, which returns the FIRST match — confirming a later duplicate (the generated one, since expansion runs after the user's own declared property list) is unreachable / silently shadowed. The compiler pipeline (packages/runar-compiler/src/index.ts, validate→typecheck→expandFixedArrays) never re-validates the property list for duplicate names after expansion.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compiling a contract that declares both `Board: FixedArray<bigint, 2>` and a sibling property literally named `Board__0: bigint` must fail with a duplicate/generated-name diagnostic from `expandFixedArrays`, not silently compile with two same-named properties where `find()` binds every access to the first one.

items.title: Go ScriptVM never passes WithTx, so it cannot execute any script containing a signature-check opcode, and the underlying error is unreachable from callers
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-093] ## CL-BUG-093 — HIGH / P1 — The Go `ScriptVM` cannot execute any script containing a signature check, and the reason is unreachable by callers
**Dispatcher-verified** (worker traced into the pinned dependency; I accept the trace, flagged below).

`script_vm.go:206-219` never passes `WithTx`. In the pinned `go-sdk v1.2.21`, `createThread` sets `ErrorOnCheckSig: opts.tx == nil` (`thread.go:51-54`) and the parser then rejects **at parse time** for any opcode where `RequiresTx()` holds — `OP_CHECKSIG`, `OP_CHECKSIGVERIFY`, `OP_CHECKMULTISIG`, `OP_CHECKMULTISIGVERIFY`, `OP_CHECKSEQUENCEVERIFY`.

It is fail-**closed**, so not a false-pass risk — but it is a total capability gap covering essentially every real Rúnar locking script, and the wrapper hides the cause: `Execute` does `_ = err; return result, nil`, `Load` discards it, and `VMResult.Error` has **no public accessor**. The sole production consumer is `runar debug`, which therefore prints `(no opcodes executed)` with no diagnostic for any real contract. Zero ScriptVM test uses a signature opcode.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-go/script_vm.go:210-217 `run()`'s execOpts list only WithScripts/WithAfterGenesis/WithDebugger(+WithForkID) — no WithTx, ever. packages/runar-go/go.mod pins github.com/bsv-blockchain/go-sdk v1.2.21, whose thread.go:54 sets `ErrorOnCheckSig: opts.tx == nil || opts.previousTxOut == nil`, so OP_CHECKSIG-family opcodes are rejected at parse time. `vm.result` (script_vm.go:76, field `result`) is unexported with no getter for step-mode callers; Load/LoadHex (:124-146) discard the run() error into it. compilers/go/debug.go — the actual (sole) production consumer of this Go ScriptVM, via LoadHex+Step() — prints only '(no opcodes executed)' with no diagnostic when the parse-time rejection yields zero steps. packages/runar-go/script_vm_test.go has zero occurrences of CHECKSIG/checksig.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Precise on the mechanism, thread.go line, and the private `result` field. One imprecision worth flagging: it names `runar debug` as the sole consumer, but that command (packages/runar-cli) actually uses the separate TypeScript ScriptVM; the Go ScriptVM's real (and only) consumer is the distinct `compilers/go debug` subcommand, which exhibits exactly the blind-diagnostic behavior described.

items.testable_assertion_verified: vm := NewScriptVM(VMOptions{}); vm.ExecuteHex(<a real P2PKH locking script with OP_CHECKSIG>, <a valid unlocking sig+pubkey>) must actually evaluate the signature (Success reflects sig validity); today the interpreter rejects at parse time regardless of signature validity because opts.tx is never set, so OpsExecuted stays 0.

sweep1.evidence: packages/runar-go/script_vm.go run() builds execOpts from only WithScripts, WithAfterGenesis, WithDebugger and optionally WithForkID. It never passes WithTx. Probe through a scratch module (replace to the worktree): NewScriptVM(VMOptions{}).ExecuteHex("51"+33-byte pubkey push+"ac") -> success=false ops=0 err="tx and previous output must be supplied for checksig". Control `515193` -> success=true ops=3. VMResult.Error is now a public field, so the cause is visible, but no CHECKSIG script can be evaluated. Execute() still discards err (`_ = err`).

[CL-BUG-082] ## CL-BUG-082 — HIGH / P1 — The shipped DSL `Groth16Verifier` contract performs no G2 on-curve or subgroup check
**Dispatcher-verified.** Source: crypto:bn254-groth16 F3.

`integration/go/contracts/Groth16Verifier.runar.go` checks **three G1 points** and **zero G2 points** before pairing, verified:
```
120:  runar.Assert(runar.Bn254G1OnCurveP(proofA))
121:  runar.Assert(runar.Bn254G1OnCurveP(proofC))
122:  runar.Assert(runar.Bn254G1OnCurveP(preparedInputs))
130:  runar.Assert(runar.Bn254MultiPairing4(proofA, proofBX0, proofBX1, proofBY0, proofBY1, ...
```
`proofBX0/X1/Y0/Y1` are spender-supplied method parameters fed straight into the pairing. Small-subgroup / off-curve G2 is the canonical Groth16 forgery vector. The witness-assisted path *does* emit all four checks (`bn254_groth16.go:1584-1587`) — this contract does not, and it is a template developers are invited to copy.

Aggravating: the contract is never executed by any test (`groth16_test.go` asserts only `scriptBytes >= 1000`), and the Go runtime mock it would run under returns `true` unconditionally — `packages/runar-go/bn254.go:277` `func Bn254MultiPairing4(...) bool { return true }`.

verification.evidence: integration/go/contracts/Groth16Verifier.runar.go:119-133: three `Bn254G1OnCurveP` assertions (proofA, proofC, preparedInputs) and zero checks on the spender-supplied G2 point (proofBX0/X1/Y0/Y1) before `Bn254MultiPairing4`. compilers/go/codegen/bn254_groth16.go:1584-1587 shows the witness-assisted path DOES emit all four on-curve checks, confirming this DSL contract is the outlier. integration/go/groth16_test.go asserts only `scriptBytes >= 1000`, never executing the contract's logic. packages/runar-go/bn254.go:271-289 `Bn254MultiPairing4` mock unconditionally returns true.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate; every cited line matches, including the contrast with the witness-assisted path and the always-true mock aggravating detail.

[CL-BUG-092] ## CL-BUG-092 — HIGH / P1 — `sp1fri.Verify` panics on a zero-query proof before any cryptographic check
**Dispatcher-verified verbatim.** Source: sdk-go depth NEW-GO-D05.

`packages/runar-go/sp1fri/fri.go:43-48`:
```go
if len(proof.QueryProofs) > 0 {
    for i, op := range proof.QueryProofs[0].CommitPhaseOpenings { ... }
}                                    // guard CLOSES here, line 47
for q, qp := range proof.QueryProofs[1:] {   // line 48 — UNGUARDED
```
`len == 0` evaluates `s[1:0]` → `panic: slice bounds out of range [1:0]`. The query-count check that would prevent it sits at `fri.go:89` — **41 lines later**. This package's stated job is adjudicating adversary-authored proof bytes, so the panic is reachable from untrusted input at zero grinding cost.

Same finding establishes `maxLogArity` is **dead**: six occurrences in the whole SDK (`verify.go:198,211,235`, `unlocking.go:76,77,118`), all declarations/assignments/comments, **zero reads** — while the value it exists to bound (`CommitPhaseProofStep.LogArity`) is read raw from the wire and consumed unbounded. The query-count equality check (`len(proof.QueryProofs) != cfg.numQueries`) is step 5, well after this point (fri.go:89). packages/runar-go/sp1fri/verify.go:198,211,235 and unlocking.go:77-78,111 confirm maxLogArity/MaxLogArity is assigned 3 times and read 0 times.

items.title: SHA2-256f tree-index mask computed as 1<<(h-hp) with h-hp=64: Java's `1L << 64` (JLS shift-mod-64) zeros idx_tree; Rust release builds mask identically via LLVM shift-count masking; Go's unsigned conversion instead yields all-ones
items.confidence_note: raised by GK; silent-but-inspected: ['CL']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description: [GK-BUG-016] SHA2-256f has h=68, hp=4, so h-hp=64. Java `1L << 64` is `1L << 0` (JLS shift mod 64), mask 0, treeIdx always 0 (SlhDsa.java:575). Rust `1u64 << 64`: debug panics; release LLVM masks count so result is 1, then -1 = 0 — same always-zero as Java (slh_dsa.rs:831). Go `1 << uint(64)` on int is 0, then -1, converted to uint64 all-ones (no clip) (slh_dsa.go:688). Java-SDK 256f signatures therefore use tree 0; on-chain verify uses the digest's real 64-bit idx_tree. Combined with GK-BUG-013 (a=8 vs FIPS a=9).

evidence.GK-BUG-016: Opened SlhDsa.java:54-55 and :575. Opened slh_dsa.rs:91-94 and :831. Opened slh_dsa.go:684-688. SLH-DSA depth: Rust release is zero-mask not MAX (LLVM shift-count mask), matching Java.

remediation.GK-BUG-016: Mask with a 64-bit-safe construct (if bits>=64, mask is all ones / skip). Add a 256f test that idx_tree is not identically 0 after Hmsg.

testable_assertion.GK-BUG-016: Java SlhDsa sign of SHA2-256f produces treeIdx==0 always today; after the fix it matches Go's unmasked 64-bit value, and both match FIPS once a=9 is fixed.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-java/src/main/java/runar/lang/runtime/SlhDsa.java:54 defines SHA2_256f with h=68, hp=4 (so h-hp=64), and :594 / :665 compute `treeIdx &= (1L << (params.h - hp)) - 1;`. Per JLS 15.19, `1L << 64` masks the shift count mod 64 to `1L << 0 = 1L`, so the mask is 0 and treeIdx is always 0. packages/runar-rs/src/slh_dsa.rs:874 has the identical `tree_idx &= (1u64 << (params.h - hp)) - 1;` (release-mode LLVM masks the shift count identically to Java; debug mode panics instead — a documented divergence, not a fix). packages/runar-go/slh_dsa.go:706 `treeIdx &= (1 << uint(params.H-hp)) - 1` differs: `1` is inferred as `uint64` in context, and Go defines `x << s` for `s >= bitwidth` as 0 for the shifted value itself (not the shift count), so `1<<64` = 0 and `0-1` wraps to all-ones under unsigned arithmetic — this does NOT zero treeIdx, matching the review's claim that Go's behavior diverges (benignly, since treeIdx is already exactly h-hp bits wide from the digest).
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Exact on h/hp values, exact on the Java/Rust shift-mod-64 mechanism, and exact on Go's differing (non-zeroing) outcome via unsigned wraparound.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Java `SlhDsa` sign with SHA2_256f params produces `treeIdx == 0` for every message today (deliberately construct two different messages/keys and observe both signatures reference tree 0); after the fix, treeIdx must vary with the message digest and match the unmasked 64-bit value the on-chain SHA2-256f verifier derives from the same digest bytes.

sweep1.evidence: packages/runar-java/src/main/java/runar/lang/runtime/SlhDsa.java: SHA2_256f = Params(..., n=32, h=68, d=17, hp=4, a=8, k=35, w=16), so h-hp=64. Both sign (~line 594) and verify (~line 665) do `treeIdx &= (1L << (params.h - hp)) - 1;`. Java masks the shift count mod 64, so this is (1L<<0)-1 = 0 and treeIdx is always 0. a=8 (non-FIPS) is also unchanged.

`packages/runar-py/runar/builtins.py:14` is `from runar.slhdsa_impl import slh_verify as _slh_verify`,

that it could not execute the disagreement (installing the package is a global install, correctly
refused under the brief) — the code-path divergence is proved from source on both sides; the runtime
rejection is a prediction.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Call packages/runar-py/runar/builtins.py blake3_hash(b'x' * 65) (65-byte message); today it silently returns a 32-byte digest computed over the truncated first 64 bytes. The on-chain compiled script aborts on a message > 64 bytes (negative-length OP_NUM2BIN), so this should raise instead of silently truncating — matching interpreter.ts's identical gap.

sweep1.evidence: packages/runar-py/runar/builtins.py blake3_hash: `padded = msg[:64] + ...; return _blake3_compress_impl(_BLAKE3_IV_BYTES, padded, min(len(msg), 64))`. items.title: SHA2-256f tree-index mask computed as 1<<(h-hp) with h-hp=64: Java's `1L << 64` (JLS shift-mod-64) zeros idx_tree; Rust release builds mask identically via LLVM shift-count masking; Go's unsigned conversion instead yields all-ones
items.confidence_note: raised by GK; silent-but-inspected: ['CL']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description: [GK-BUG-016] SHA2-256f has h=68, hp=4, so h-hp=64. Java `1L << 64` is `1L << 0` (JLS shift mod 64), mask 0, treeIdx always 0 (SlhDsa.java:575). Rust `1u64 << 64`: debug panics; release LLVM masks count so result is 1, then -1 = 0 — same always-zero as Java (slh_dsa.rs:831). Go `1 << uint(64)` on int is 0, then -1, converted to uint64 all-ones (no clip) (slh_dsa.go:688). Java-SDK 256f signatures therefore use tree 0; on-chain verify uses the digest's real 64-bit idx_tree. Combined with GK-BUG-013 (a=8 vs FIPS a=9).

evidence.GK-BUG-016: Opened SlhDsa.java:54-55 and :575. Opened slh_dsa.rs:91-94 and :831. Opened slh_dsa.go:684-688. SLH-DSA depth: Rust release is zero-mask not MAX (LLVM shift-count mask), matching Java.

remediation.GK-BUG-016: Mask with a 64-bit-safe construct (if bits>=64, mask is all ones / skip). Add a 256f test that idx_tree is not identically 0 after Hmsg.

testable_assertion.GK-BUG-016: Java SlhDsa sign of SHA2-256f produces treeIdx==0 always today; after the fix it matches Go's unmasked 64-bit value, and both match FIPS once a=9 is fixed.

verification.evidence: Java (packages/runar-java/src/main/java/runar/lang/runtime/SlhDsa.java:594 sign, :665 verify) and Rust (packages/runar-rs/src/slh_dsa.rs:874 sign, :971 verify) both still compute `treeIdx &= (1L/1u64 << (h - hp)) - 1`. For SHA2_256f, Params h=68, hp=4 (SlhDsa.java:54), so h-hp=64. Java's `1L << 64` is JLS shift-mod-64 = `1L << 0` = 1, mask = 0 -> treeIdx always 0. Rust's `1u64 << 64` in a release build undergoes the same shift-count-masking (shl by width mod 64) via LLVM, giving the same mask = 0. Go (packages/runar-go/slh_dsa.go:706 sign, :788 verify) uses the SAME source pattern `treeIdx &= (1 << uint(params.H-hp)) - 1`, but Go's untyped `1` here resolves to type uint64 (assignment context of `treeIdx &=`), and Go defines shift-by->=width as yielding 0 (not UB) — so `uint64(1)<<64 = 0`, then `0 - 1` wraps to all-ones (0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF), a no-op mask. Go is therefore accidentally correct despite the visually identical line; only Java and Rust are actually broken.
verification.tier_correction: File list's inclusion of packages/runar-go/slh_dsa.go:684-688 as buggy is wrong — verified Go's outcome (all-ones mask, i.e. no truncation) is correct, unlike Java/Rust's (zero mask). Confined to Java + Rust.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Cited files and line ranges are in the right files; exact current line numbers moved (Java 594/665, Rust 874/971, not the cited 54-575/91-831 ranges verbatim, but those ranges do bracket the real locations). The core technical claim (Java shift-mod-64, Rust release masking, Go all-ones) is correct and verified independently against the actual code semantics, not just taken on the reviewer's word.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Sign two different SHA2-256f messages with the Java (or Rust) SLH-DSA signer and compare the derived HT tree-address bytes embedded in each signature: today both are always 0 (treeIdx forced to 0 by the shift-mod-64 masking bug), so they're identical; after the fix they must differ (matching Go's unmasked 64-bit value) whenever the two messages' FIPS-205-computed tree index differs.

sweep1.evidence: packages/runar-java/src/main/java/runar/lang/runtime/SlhDsa.java:594 and :665 still read `treeIdx &= (1L << (params.h - hp)) - 1;`. SHA2_256f has h=68, hp=4 (line 54). jshell: `(1L << (68-4)) - 1` prints 0, so treeIdx is always 0. Rust packages/runar-rs/src/slh_dsa.rs:874 and :971 have the same `tree_idx &= (1u64 << (params.h - hp)) - 1;` with SLH_SHA2_256F h:68 hp:4 (line 91-94).

items.title: Rust BIP-143 signer always hashes ALL prevouts/sequences/outputs regardless of requested sighash flag (ANYONECANPAY/NONE/SINGLE ignored)
items.confidence_note: raised by GK; silent-but-inspected: ['CL']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description: [GK-BUG-028] bip143_sighash accepts sig_hash_type but always SHA256d every outpoint, every sequence, and every output, then appends the requested flag byte (signer.rs:154-192). No ANYONECANPAY / NONE / SINGLE branch. TS LocalSigner passes scope into @bsv/sdk TransactionSignature.format, so a 0x43 (SINGLE|FORKID) sign is actually SINGLE. A Rust caller who passes Some(0x43) produces a signature that on-chain OP_CHECKSIG under SINGLE will reject.

evidence.GK-BUG-028: Opened signer.rs:147-176 (hashPrevouts/hashSequence/hashOutputs always full; sig_hash_type only written at the tail 192).

remediation.GK-BUG-028: Honour ACP/NONE/SINGLE in this hasher (or call the oppushtx preimage that already does). Extend bip143_interop.rs to sign via LocalSigner::sign(..., Some(0x43)).

testable_assertion.GK-BUG-028: LocalSigner::sign(tx, 0, subscript, sats, Some(0x43)) on a 2-output tx produces a DER+43 signature that does not verify against the ALL preimage. Today it does.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-rs/src/sdk/signer.rs:147-192 (`bip143_sighash`) unconditionally computes hash_prevouts over ALL inputs, hash_sequence over ALL inputs, and hash_outputs over ALL outputs, with no branch on `sig_hash_type` at all — the flag is only appended as the trailing signature byte (line ~125, `result.push(flag as u8)`). The public `Signer` trait (signer.rs:11-34) documents `sig_hash_type` as accepting arbitrary flags ('defaults to ALL | FORKID'), so a caller passing e.g. `Some(0x43)` (SINGLE|FORKID) gets a signature whose preimage was computed as if ALL, but whose trailing byte claims SINGLE — on-chain OP_CHECKSIG under SINGLE semantics will compute a different preimage and reject it. By contrast, TS's LocalSigner (packages/runar-sdk/src/signers/local.ts:63-101) passes `scope: sigHashType` straight into @bsv/sdk's `TransactionSignature.format`, which correctly branches on ANYONECANPAY/NONE/SINGLE.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate — file:line and the mechanism (no per-flag branching, correct only for the default flag) are exactly as described. Note: every internal SDK call site (contract.rs, wallet.rs, token_wallet.rs) currently passes `None` (default ALL|FORKID), so the bug is latent on the public API surface rather than exercised by the SDK's own built-in flows today — worth noting for prioritization, doesn't change the verdict.

items.testable_assertion_verified: `LocalSigner::sign(&tx_hex, 0, subscript, sats, Some(0x43))` on a 2-output tx, then verify the resulting DER+0x43 signature against the SIGHASH_SINGLE preimage (hash_outputs restricted to output[0] only) rather than the ALL preimage — today it verifies only against ALL and fails SINGLE verification.

sweep1.evidence: packages/runar-rs/src/sdk/signer.rs fn bip143_sighash (line ~156-203) still hashes every input's outpoint and sequence and every output into hash_prevouts, hash_sequence and hash_outputs unconditionally. It has no ANYONECANPAY, NONE or SINGLE branch and only appends `sig_hash_type.to_le_bytes()`. LocalSigner::sign (line ~107-140) passes the caller's flag straight through, so Some(0x43) signs the ALL preimage tagged as SINGLE.

items.title: Rust `sha256_finalize` is wrong for `remaining` ∈ [64,119] and panics at exactly 64
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-087] ## CL-BUG-087 — HIGH / P1 — Rust `sha256_finalize` is wrong for `remaining` ∈ [64,119] and panics at exactly 64
**Dispatcher-verified verbatim.** Source: crypto:hashes F2. `packages/runar-rs/src/prelude.rs:482-500`.

```rust
assert!(remaining.len() <= 64, "sha256_finalize: remaining must be <= 64 bytes");
...
} else {                              // rem_len >= 56
    let mut block1 = [0u8; 64];
    block1[..rem_len].copy_from_slice(remaining);
    block1[rem_len] = 0x80;           // rem_len == 64  =>  index 64 on [u8;64]  => PANIC
```
Two defects in one function:
1. The `<= 64` assert **rejects inputs the compiled script accepts.** The emitted script's two-block path handles `remaining` up to 119 (`pushI(120); OP_SUB`), and Go/Python/Ruby/Zig/Java all handle 0..119. `integration/ts/sha256-finalize.test.ts:98` broadcasts a 100-byte `remaining` to a live regtest node.
2. At `rem_len == 64` — which the assert *permits* — the write is out of bounds and panics.

Invisible to every existing test because the shared vectors carry `remaining` of only 0, 3 and 56 bytes; the in-crate tests use 0/3/11. **The 64..119 band is exercised in no tier's runtime tests.**

Related (F3): oversize `remaining` diverges **five ways** across seven tiers — script rejects, Go and Ruby are *silently wrong* (truncate the tail), Rust panics, Python/Java/Zig reject. Go and Ruby are the dangerous pair: a developer gets a plausible 32-byte digest off-chain that the chain will never reproduce.

---

verification.evidence: packages/runar-rs/src/prelude.rs:515: `assert!(remaining.len() <= 64, ...)` still rejects what the compiled script accepts — packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/sha256-codegen.ts:281-284 pads the two-block path to 120 bytes (`pushI(120n); ... OP_SUB`), i.e. the on-chain reader accepts `remaining` up to 119 bytes. Second defect still present: at exactly `rem_len == 64` (permitted by the `<=64` assert), execution takes the two-block `else` branch (prelude.rs:532 `rem_len < 56` is false), and `block1[rem_len] = 0x80` writes to index 64 of a `[u8; 64]` array — an out-of-bounds panic. No Rust test exercises `remaining` in [56,119] (only `test_sha256_finalize_abc`/`_empty`/`_cross_verify` with short inputs at prelude.rs:1544-1568), matching integration/ts/sha256-finalize.test.ts:93-98's dedicated 56/64/100-byte two-block cross-verify cases that only run against the other tiers.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate — the assert bound, the exact panic condition at rem_len==64, and the untested 56-119 gap are all verified as described. `sha256Finalize` is exposed as a Rúnar builtin callable from `.runar.rs` contract source (examples/rust/sha256-finalize/Sha256FinalizeTest.runar.rs), so whether spender-controlled witness bytes can reach this native Rust path depends on how a given project wires native execution into any production-facing simulator — not determinable by static read alone.

items.testable_assertion_verified: `sha256_finalize(&state32, &[0xAAu8; 64], 512)` panics today (index-out-of-bounds on the fixed [u8;64] block). After the fix it must return the same 32-byte digest as the compiled script / Go's `Sha256Finalize` for a 64-byte `remaining` tail (and likewise for 100 bytes, per integration/ts/sha256-finalize.test.ts's cross-verify vectors).

sweep1.evidence: packages/runar-rs/src/prelude.rs:513-545 sha256_finalize still has `assert!(remaining.len() <= 64, ...)`, so 65..119 bytes are rejected although the script accepts up to 119. In the else branch (rem_len >= 56) it does `let mut block1 = [0u8; 64]; ... block1[rem_len] = 0x80;`, which indexes 64 out of bounds and panics when rem_len == 64.

items.title: Zig's --ir path always emits parentClass:"SmartContract" (an unconditional struct default), and the TS SDK trusts it over its own isStateful fallback
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-134] # PASS C BATCH 2R WAVE 1 — sdk-ts (CL-BUG-134 … CL-GAP-112, CL-DOC-018)

**Verified.** 7 citation spot-checks, all resolved exactly: `contract.ts:813-816` and `:757-759`
(parentClass gate), `envelope.ts:61`/`:154` (hardcoded `Date.now()`), the seven-tier `nowMs` grep
(TS **0** hits, peers 5/21/4/4/28/4), `ci.yml:270-295`, `fixtures.json` (`verify_now_ms` =
1700000000500 vs `valid_envelope.expiresAt` = 1700000030000), `anf-interpreter.ts:606/798/813/997`,
`contract.ts:1226-1242`. Report persisted at `workers-depth/sdk-ts-depth.md`.

This report also independently re-derived **CL-BUG-132** with sharper citations than I had — it
gives the Rust arms as `packages/runar-rs/src/sdk/state.rs:398` (encode) and `:615` (decode), which
I confirmed are literal `"bool" =>` match arms, not the `_` fallthrough the Rust depth worker
described. Same conclusion, better evidence; CL-BUG-132's Rust row updated.

...
## CL-BUG-134 — HIGH / P1 — Zig's `--ir` path emits a positively wrong `"parentClass":"SmartContract"`, and the TS SDK trusts it over its own `isStateful` fallback
**Dispatcher-verified in full.**

`packages/runar-sdk/src/contract.ts:813-816` treats `parentClass` as authoritative when present and
falls back to `isStateful` only when it is `undefined`. `parentClass` is **deliberately excluded**
from the ANF IR wire format, so on the `--ir` path no tier can know it. Five tiers degrade safely by
omitting the key (`compilers/go/ir/types.go:29` `json:"-"`; `compilers/rust/src/ir/mod.rs:46-47`
`serde(skip, default)`; Python's `_IR_EXCLUDED_FIELDS`; Ruby's `IR_EXCLUDED_FIELDS`; TS emits no
artifact on that path at all).

**Zig does not.** `compilers/zig/src/ir/types.zig:328` declares
`parent_class: ParentClass = .smart_contract` as a **struct default**;
`compilers/zig/src/ir/json.zig`

verification.evidence: packages/runar-sdk/src/contract.ts:920-923 (HEAD) still trusts artifact.parentClass over isStateful whenever it is !== undefined. compilers/zig/src/ir/json.zig:337-341 (parseProgram, the --ir loader) never sets ANFProgram.parent_class, so it keeps the compilers/zig/src/ir/types.zig:423 struct default `.smart_contract`. compilers/zig/src/codegen/emit.zig:711-718 writes `"parentClass":...anf_program.parent_class.toTsString()` unconditionally into the final artifact JSON for BOTH the source-compile and --ir paths (main.zig:303/308/406/412 all call the same emitArtifact). Contrast with Go (compilers/go/ir/types.go:29 `json:"-"` + compiler.go:136 `json:"parentClass,omitempty"`, so an unset/empty ParentClass omits the key entirely) and Rust (`#[serde(skip, default)]`) — both degrade to an ABSENT key on --ir, which is what makes contract.ts's `!== undefined` fallback work for those five tiers. Zig instead always emits a wrong, present value ('SmartContract') for any StatefulSmartContract/UnsafeSmartContract compiled via --ir.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate — every cited path/line matches HEAD; root-cause commit 304bfd31 (which added parentClass) never touched json.zig's --ir loader, leaving the gap open.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile a StatefulSmartContract's ANF IR through the Zig CLI's `--ir` entry point; the resulting artifact JSON must report `parentClass: "StatefulSmartContract"`. Today it reports "SmartContract" for every --ir-compiled contract regardless of source, because json.zig's parseProgram never sets parent_class and emit.zig writes the types.zig:423 struct default unconditionally.

sweep1.evidence: Probe: `runar-zig compile-ir conformance/tests/stateful-counter/expected-ir.json` (a stateful Counter whose increment ABI carries _changePKH/_changeAmount) outputs an artifact with `"parentClass":"SmartContract"`. compilers/zig/src/ir/types.zig:434 still has the struct default `parent_class: ParentClass = .smart_contract`, and emit.zig:736 writes it unconditionally.

items.title: Rabin padding/sig/n pushed as unsigned little-endian bytes are consumed as signed Bitcoin script numbers; a set high bit in the last byte flips the sign and aborts honest spends
items.confidence_note: raised by GK; silent-but-inspected: ['CL']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description: [GK-BUG-036] On-chain OP_WITHIN / OP_MUL / OP_MOD interpret stack items as Bitcoin script numbers (LE sign-magnitude; last-byte high bit is the sign). encodeArg for a hex string is encodePushData (raw push) at contract.ts:2704-2706; bigint goes through encodeScriptNumber which adds a 0x00 sign byte when the high bit is set. padding is typed ByteString, so the string path is the ABI path. padding=200 as [0xC8] is unsigned 200 off-chain and script-number −72 on-chain → OP_WITHIN aborts. Honest search-from-0 padding is usually <128; sig and n are not. A 2048-bit modulus is ~50% likely to have the last-byte high bit set. The vendored ~260-bit test key MSB is 0x10 and cannot expose the trap.

evidence.GK-BUG-036: Opened encodeArg 2691-2706 (string → encodePushData). Opened rabin-codegen.ts WITHIN/MUL/MOD. OraclePriceFeed padding: ByteString.

remediation.GK-BUG-036: Always encode Rabin integers via encodeScriptNumber (or always append a 0x00 sign byte). Pin ScriptVM: padding=[0xC8] aborts; padding=[0xC8,0x00] can succeed. Use a modulus with bit 255 of the 32-byte LE encoding set.

testable_assertion.GK-BUG-036: Honest (sig, padding=200) with padding pushed as [0xC8]: off-chain accept, script abort. Same padding as [0xC8,0x00]: script accept.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-sdk/src/contract.ts:2842-2844 (encodeArg, HEAD): `typeof value === 'string'` -> `encodePushData(value)`, a raw byte push with no sign-magnitude handling (confirmed by reading encodePushData at :2914 — it only does minimal-push / length framing, never adds a sign byte). `typeof value === 'bigint'` -> `encodeScriptNumber(value)`, which DOES add a 0x00 sign byte when the top magnitude byte's high bit is set (:2876-2880). `padding: ByteString` in examples/ts/oracle-price/OraclePriceFeed.runar.ts:44 is passed as a hex string through the ABI, so it takes the string/raw-push path. On-chain, packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/rabin-codegen.ts:77-82 (emitVerifyRabinSig) runs `OP_DUP OP_0 <65536> OP_WITHIN OP_VERIFY` directly on the padding value as pushed — Script numbers are LE sign-magnitude, so padding=200 pushed as raw [0xC8] reads as -72 on-chain and aborts OP_WITHIN, while it round-trips fine off-chain. Confirmed reachable: any padding value 128-255 (mod 256 in the low byte, i.e. roughly half of all values < 256) triggers this.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Honest (sig, padding=200) with padding pushed as [0xC8] via packages/runar-sdk/src/contract.ts's encodeArg: off-chain verifyRabinSig accepts, but the compiled script (rabin-codegen.ts's OP_WITHIN check) aborts because [0xC8] reads as the negative Script number -72. The same padding pushed as [0xC8,0x00] passes on-chain. encodeArg must emit the same non-negative-forcing byte for ByteString values feeding a Script-number comparison.

sweep1.evidence: Probe: in the runar-sdk dist, encodeArg('c8') = '01c8', a raw push with no sign byte. The ScriptVM (runar-testing dist) ran the Rabin padding-range fragment from rabin-codegen.ts (OP_DUP OP_0 <65536> OP_WITHIN OP_VERIFY) after that push. With '01c8' it fails with "OP_VERIFY requires the top stack value to be truthy." With 'c800' it succeeds. encodeArg (contract.ts:2939-2941) still uses encodePushData for strings, verifyRabinSig still types padding as ByteString (runar-lang builtins.ts:419-424), and emitVerifyRabinSig does not normalize the padding operand.

items.title: TS ANF interpreter (packages/runar-sdk) fails OPEN on unknown ANF kinds/builtins and division by zero
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-135] ## CL-BUG-135 — HIGH / P1 — The ANF interpreter fails OPEN on unknown kinds, unknown builtins and division by zero, defeating the fail-closed guard one frame up
**Dispatcher-verified.**

`packages/runar-sdk/src/contract.ts:1226-1242` wraps the interpreter in a `try/catch` that **throws**
rather than broadcasting, with a comment I read in full: *"The interpreter is the only thing that
knows this method's post-state and its addDataOutput/addRawOutput payloads, so there is nothing to
fall back TO."* It fails closed **only when the interpreter throws**.

The interpreter's default arms never throw. I read all four:
- `anf-interpreter.ts:606-607` — unknown ANF binding kind → `return undefined;`
- `:997-998` — unknown builtin → `return undefined;`
- `:798-799` — `case '/': return r === 0n ? 0n : l / r;` and the same for `%`
- `:813` — unknown binary operator → `return 0n;`

None reaches the catch. The resulting state is wrong-but-plausible, is serialised into the
continuation locking script, and the covenant's `hash256(outputs)` check rejects the spend on
chain — the UTXO is stranded with no local error, which is precisely the failure
`contract.ts:1226-1242` was written to prevent.

The div-by-zero arm is additionally a source-vs-script divergence: `/` lowers to `OP_DIV`, which
**aborts** on a zero divisor, while the interpreter continues with `0n`. The module is not even
internally consistent — `mulDiv` at `:984` divides with no zero guard and throws `RangeError`.
`safediv`/`safemod` exist as separate guarded builtins, which is what makes the bare `/` arm's
silent `0n` a deliberate-looking but wrong choice.

verification.evidence: Partially remediated: packages/runar-sdk/src/anf-interpreter.ts:1086-1104 (HEAD) — the unknown-BUILTIN default arm now `throw`s (fixed by commit 3155586f 'fix(sdk): the ANF interpreter refuses builtins it does not model', NEW-006/A-3), so that portion of the finding is STALE. But the unknown ANF BINDING KIND default arm at :606-607 still `return undefined;`, and the division/modulo-by-zero arms at :798-799 still `case '/': return r === 0n ? 0n : l / r;` / same for '%' — both fail OPEN exactly as described, with no throw reaching the fail-closed try/catch guard at contract.ts:1339-1340 ('there is nothing to fall back TO'). The unknown-binary-operator default at :813 also still `return 0n;`.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Feed the SDK's ANF interpreter (anf-interpreter.ts) an ANF binding of an unrecognized `kind`, or a `/`/`%` binding with a zero divisor; it must throw — matching the fix already applied to the unknown-builtin arm at :1086-1104 — not silently return `undefined`/`0n` from the default arms at :606-607 and :798-799.

sweep1.evidence: Probe on packages/runar-sdk/dist/anf-interpreter.js computeNewState: (a) a method with `count = count / d` and d=0n returns {count:0n} without throwing; (b) a binding of kind 'totally_bogus_kind' fed into update_prop returns {} without throwing (state silently dropped). Source: anf-interpreter.ts:638-639 `default: return undefined;`, :830-831 `case '/': return r === 0n ? 0n : l / r;` (same for %), :845 `default: return 0n;`.

items.title: TS WalletSigner.getAddress returns hash160 hex instead of Base58Check, violating the Signer contract
items.confidence_note: raised by GK; silent-but-inspected: ['CL']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description: [GK-BUG-033] Signer.getAddress is specified as a Base58Check P2PKH address. LocalSigner returns one. WalletSigner.getAddress returns Utils.toHex(Hash.hash160(pubkey)) — 40 hex chars. RunarContract.deploy / prepareCall use signer.getAddress() as the key into provider.getUtxos(address). WhatsOnChain interpolates that string into /address/{address}/unspent. A BRC-100 WalletSigner paired with WhatsOnChainProvider queries a hex PKH as if it were a Base58 address. WalletProvider.getUtxos ignores its address argument, which is why the BRC-100-only path still works.
