items.title: Off-chain blake3Hash silently truncates messages >64 bytes; on-chain script aborts (mock/script split)
items.confidence_note: raised by GK; silent-but-inspected: ['CL']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description: [GK-BUG-011] Interpreter blake3 path uses Math.min(msg.length, 64) as block_len / truncates. Hashes worker: Go/Python/Ruby SDK truncate; Zig/Java panic/throw; on-chain emitBlake3Hash aborts >64. TestContract can pass a >64 message the locking script would reject.

evidence.GK-BUG-011: Opened interpreter.ts:1277 Math.min(msg.length, 64). Worker inventory of SDK truncate vs abort.

remediation.GK-BUG-011: All off-chain blake3Hash implementations must reject length>64, matching script. Add a constructed >64 test that interpreter and script both fail.

testable_assertion.GK-BUG-011: TestContract calling blake3Hash of 65 bytes currently returns a 32-byte digest; it should throw, matching ScriptVM.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-testing/src/interpreter/interpreter.ts:1566-1572 (case 'blake3Hash'): `padded.set(msg.subarray(0, 64))` and `Math.min(msg.length, 64)` still silently truncate any message >64 bytes with no length check or throw. Compare packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/blake3-codegen.ts:459-460 (emitBlake3Hash): the on-chain script computes `64 - len` via OP_SUB then OP_NUM2BIN — for len>64 this underflows/produces a negative size argument to OP_NUM2BIN, which the interpreter for that opcode rejects, i.e. the compiled script aborts on real chains for >64-byte input (matches the codegen doc comment 'inputs longer than one 64-byte block are out of scope'). No guard exists anywhere between the AST/typecheck layer and the interpreter dispatch to reject >64-byte input before reaching this branch, and packages/runar-testing/src/__tests__/blake3.test.ts has no case exercising a >64-byte message, so the divergence is untested. This is the exact off-chain/on-chain split GK-BUG-011 describes: TestContract (interpreter) returns a plausible-looking 32-byte digest for a >64-byte message that the real locking script would abort on.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Correct in substance; line cited (interpreter.ts:1277) is stale (current location is 1566-1572, and the fold-ON constant-fold/other unrelated edits since GK's review commit shifted the file), but the code and behavior described match exactly.

items.testable_assertion_verified: TestContract.call() on a contract that does `assert(blake3Hash(msg) == expectedTruncatedHash)` with a deliberately 65-byte `msg` currently returns success (interpreter truncates and hashes the first 64 bytes); it should instead throw/refuse (matching ScriptVM, which aborts because emitBlake3Hash's OP_NUM2BIN receives a negative size for the on-chain equivalent input).

sweep1.evidence: Probe: TestContract.fromSource on a contract with `assert(blake3Hash(msg) == this.expected)`, where expected = blake3('01'*64) = 29c04cc4...2497. Calling check with a 65-byte msg ('01'*65) returns {success:true}, so the interpreter truncates to 64 bytes. Code at packages/runar-testing/src/interpreter/interpreter.ts:1576-1582: `padded.set(msg.subarray(0, 64)); ... Math.min(msg.length, 64)`.

items.title: Zig tier compiles a non-adjacent .runar.zig while-loop that every other tier refuses, and ignores the declared start value (silent miscompile)
items.origin: surfaced by the F-006 remediation subagent; dispatcher reproduced: compilers/zig runar-zig on remediation-logs/F-006/scratch/NonAdj3.runar.zig emits 5300775a937c9d00009c (sum folded to 10 with start 3; correct is 7) while go/ts refuse with the For-loop-condition diagnostic
items.description: When the `var i` declaration is not immediately before the `while (i < N) : (i += 1)`, the TS reference and Go/Rust/Python/Ruby/Java leave the loop iterator as the placeholder `__while_no_init` and the condition-iterator validator refuses the program. The Zig tier instead takes the iterator name from the condition and unrolls from 0, ignoring the declared start, so `var i = 3; var sum = 0; while (i < 5) : (i += 1) { sum += i; }` compiles to a script that accepts sum=10 and rejects the correct 7 under Spend.validate. Make the Zig tier refuse the same shape with the same diagnostic as the TS reference (frontend parity).
items.testable_assertion_verified: compilers/zig refuses remediation-logs/F-006/scratch/NonAdj3.runar.zig with the reference's For-loop-condition diagnostic; the adjacent shape (Start3) still compiles and computes 7.

sweep1.evidence: Probe: `runar-zig compile NonAdj3.runar.zig --hex` (copied from remediation-logs/F-006/scratch) exits 0 and emits 535a7b9d00009c77 (OP_10 = 0+1+2+3+4, ignoring the declared start i=3), both with and without --disable-constant-folding. Go on the same file refuses with "For loop condition must compare the loop variable '__while_no_init' ...". The adjacent Start3 compiles to 577c9d00009c (OP_7), which is correct.

items.title: No constructed small-order G2 test for Groth16/pairing; MapToCurve2 off-r-torsion is not small-order
items.confidence_note: raised by GK; silent-but-inspected: ['CL']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description: [GK-GAP-004] The review bar is a test that constructs a specific small-subgroup attack, not random tampering. The repo has MapToCurve2(1,3) off-r-torsion (good for Scott subgroup) and coordinate +1 off-curve tests. Adversarial grep found no constructed 2-torsion (Y=0 on the twist) or cofactor-torsion generator of named small order. Missing adversarial test is its own finding even if WA doubling would abort; generic pairing would not.

evidence.GK-GAP-004: Adversarial report: no torsion/small-order/Y=0 G2 fixture in *bn254*/*groth16* tests except comments. gate0-evaluation.md still asks for a crafted small-order G2 point.

remediation.GK-GAP-004: Check in a named-order G2 (2-torsion or order < 2^16) and run it through emitWAG2SubgroupCheck (must abort), EmitBN254MultiPairing4 (must abort after F1 fix), and Bn254MultiPairing4Big.

testable_assertion.GK-GAP-004: A checked-in G2 of named small order exists such that WA subgroup check aborts and generic MultiPairing4 currently does not.

verification.evidence: compilers/go/codegen/bn254_groth16_subgroup_test.go (full file read) and compilers/go/codegen/bn254_pairing_validation_test.go:98-113 (advOffSubgroupG2) both construct the SAME off-subgroup G2 point via `bn254.MapToCurve2(&seed)` with seed (A0=1,A1=3) — a point that is on-curve but NOT cofactor-cleared, sitting in a subgroup of order ~2^255 (the twist's huge cofactor), not a NAMED SMALL order (e.g. 2-torsion Y=0). No test anywhere in compilers/go/codegen constructs an explicit small-order point (grep for 'SetZero'/2-torsion construction/cofactor-torsion generator turns up only comments discussing the theoretical case, e.g. bn254_groth16.go:444-448,585-587, never an actual constructed vector). docs/gate0-evaluation.md:422-426 itself still says, present tense, 'A targeted test using a crafted small-order G2 point should be added alongside the check' — confirming the project's own docs still record this as an open gap.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate — correctly distinguishes 'off-r-torsion, huge non-small order' (what exists) from 'named small order' (what's missing), and cites the exact existing tests and the doc's own outstanding TODO.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Construct a genuine 2-torsion (or other named-small-order) BN254 G2 point (Y=0 on the twist, or a known cofactor-torsion generator), feed it to both emitWAG2SubgroupCheck (WA path) and bn254MultiPairing4 (generic path) via the existing harness patterns in bn254_groth16_subgroup_test.go / bn254_pairing_validation_test.go, and assert both reject it. Constructing the vector requires curve arithmetic but the test itself is one function; too_large is not required.

sweep1.evidence: Partial. b094c0b5 (F-058) added compilers/go/compiler/f058_groth16_dsl_g2_validation_test.go: f058SmallOrderB builds an order-10069 twist point, and TestF058_Groth16VerifierDSL_RejectsSmallOrderB covers the WA DSL path. The generic path still has no constructed small-order vector: compilers/go/codegen/bn254_pairing_validation_test.go TestBN254MultiPairing4_RejectsOffSubgroupG2 and TestBN254Pairing_RejectsOffSubgroupG2 use only advOffSubgroupG2 (MapToCurve2(1,3), off-r-torsion, not named small order). grep for SmallOrder/10069 under compilers/go *_test.go outside f058 finds nothing. The TAV requires both WA and bn254MultiPairing4 to be exercised. (A Y=0 2-torsion point does not exist, since the twist order h·r is odd, so 10069 is the right named order for the missing generic-path test.)

items.title: Public runar-lang verifyRabinSig omits the padding-range bound; sig=0, padding=SHA256(msg) is a universal forgery
items.confidence_note: raised by GK; silent-but-inspected: ['CL']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description: [GK-GAP-012] On-chain EmitVerifyRabinSig asserts 0 <= padding < 65536 via OP_WITHIN/OP_VERIFY. Six SDK verifiers and the TestContract interpreter enforce it. The public runar-lang/runtime export does not: pubkey<=0 then (sig²+pad)%n == hash%n. sig=0, padding=SHA256(msg) satisfies that for every message and every n — a universal forgery on the package's stated off-chain oracle. Java MockCrypto comments that it mirrors this TS function but Java has the bound. runtime.test.ts only checks a wrong sig and zero pubkey.

evidence.GK-GAP-012: Opened builtins.ts:358-366: no RABIN_PADDING_LIMIT. Contrast rabin.go:50-56 and MockCrypto.java:144. Construction: lhs = (0+SHA256)%n == SHA256%n = rhs.

remediation.GK-GAP-012: Add `if (padBN < 0n || padBN >= 65536n) return false` to runar-lang/runtime. Construct sig=0 padding=sha256(msg) as a must-reject test.

testable_assertion.GK-GAP-012: verifyRabinSig(msg, 0n, sha256(msg) as ByteString, RABIN_TEST_KEY.n) returns true today from runar-lang/runtime. It must return false. The same triple against runar-testing rabinVerify already returns false.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-lang/src/runtime/builtins.ts:357-367 (HEAD) `verifyRabinSig`: `if (pubkey <= 0n) return false;` then computes lhs/rhs with NO padding-range check. sig=0, padding=sha256(msg) (as the same hex bytes, LE-interpreted identically by rabinBytesToUnsignedLE both places) gives lhs = ((0+padBN)%n+n)%n = hashBN%n = rhs for any n>0 — universal forgery, exactly as described. Contrast: packages/runar-testing/src/crypto/rabin.ts:108-111 HAS `if (padBN >= RABIN_PADDING_LIMIT) return false;` with a comment describing this exact forgery; packages/runar-go/rabin.go:50-56 has the same bound; packages/runar-java/.../MockCrypto.java:127-144 has RABIN_PADDING_LIMIT=65536 and the same comment naming both TS and Go as mirrored (Java itself is NOT vulnerable). packages/runar-lang/src/__tests__/runtime.test.ts:311-317 only tests wrong-sig and zero-pubkey, never the forgery — confirmed by reading the file.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Fully accurate — every cited line and behavioral claim verified exactly against HEAD, including the Java-has-the-bound / TS-doesn't asymmetry.

items.testable_assertion_verified: verifyRabinSig(msg, 0n, sha256(msg) as ByteString, RABIN_TEST_KEY.n) returns true today from packages/runar-lang/src/runtime/builtins.ts. It must return false. The same triple against runar-testing's rabinVerify already returns false (RABIN_PADDING_LIMIT bound present there).

sweep1.evidence: packages/runar-lang/src/runtime/builtins.ts verifyRabinSig (around line 357) still has no padding bound: `if (pubkey <= 0n) return false; ... lhs=((sig*sig+padBN)%pubkey...; rhs=(hashBN%pubkey...); return lhs===rhs`. Probe against dist/runtime/builtins.js with msg='deadbeef', sig=0n, padding=sha256(msg), n=2^512-569 printed `sig=0 pad=sha256(msg) -> true`, so the universal forgery still works.

items.title: TS peephole `optimizeNestedIf` unconditionally rebuilds every `if` op as a bare `{op:'if', then, else}`, dropping `sourceLoc` even when no rule fired in either branch — every compiled `OP_IF` is mis-attributed to the preceding op's source location

items.description:
[CL-BUG-117] ## CL-BUG-117 — MEDIUM / P2 — `optimizeNestedIf` strips `sourceLoc` from every `if`-op unconditionally
**Source:** impl-ts-optimizers depth NEW-05. **Dispatcher-verified.**
`peephole.ts:527-538` returns a freshly built `{ op: 'if', then, else }` for every `if`-op — whether
or not any rule fired inside the branches — dropping `sourceLoc`. The lowerer attaches one to every
op (`05-stack-lower.ts:637-643`) and the emitter only overwrites its context loc when the op carries
one (`06-emit.ts:395-398`), so **every `OP_IF` in every compiled contract** is attributed to the
preceding op. Broader than the earlier source-map finding, and a one-line fix
(`return { ...op, then, else }`).


[CX-GAP-024] Stack lowering attaches source locations to emitted operations, but peephole replacement objects do not inherit them. Recursive `if` optimization reconstructs the outer `if` with only `op`, `then`, and `else`, unconditionally losing its location even when neither arm changes.

evidence.CX-GAP-024: `emitOp` attaches `currentSourceLoc` at `05-stack-lower.ts:637-642`; representative peephole replacements create fresh objects at `peephole.ts:134-148`. `optimizeNestedIf` reconstructs the node without spreading metadata at lines 527-535.

remediation.CX-GAP-024: Define location-merging rules for replacements and preserve all non-branch fields when rebuilding `if`.

items.title: Constant-fold's `===`/`!==` on ByteString literals compares hex source text case-sensitively instead of decoded bytes, so `'aa' === 'AA'` folds to `false` at compile time but the emitted `OP_EQUAL` (via case-insensitive `hexToBytes`) evaluates `true` on-chain
items.confidence_note: raised by CL+GK; silent-but-inspected: ['CX']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-004] | worker | CL ID | sev | prio | title |
| F-006 | CL-BUG-004 | MEDIUM | v1-should-have | Constant folding compares ByteString literals case-sensitively |

[GK-BUG-020] Fold's string arm uses JS left === right on the hex literal text. Parser keeps case. Stack-lower hexToBytes is case-insensitive and emits OP_EQUAL. So 'aa' === 'AA' is false at fold-time and true on-chain. Fold is on by default. A condition folded to const false takes the else arm in the deployed script.

evidence.GK-BUG-020: Opened constant-fold.ts:76-83 (=== is left === right on strings after hex charset check).

remediation.GK-BUG-020: Compare decoded bytes or lowercase both sides. Pin fold of 'aa' === 'AA' as true.

testable_assertion.GK-BUG-020: foldConstants of two load_const strings 'aa' and 'AA' with bin_op === currently yields load_const false.

conflicts: none — verified packages/runar-compiler/src/optimizer/constant-fold.ts:75-84 (runar-review-claude-main, 8937c1ad): the string arm's `===`/`!==` cases do plain `left === right` / `left !== right` on the raw hex text, confirming both findings.
items.tier_reason: ANF/stack/emit/EC-optimizer boundary and emitted bytes change (§5 floor: mid min, top if bytes move)

verification.evidence: packages/runar-compiler/src/optimizer/constant-fold.ts:90-99 — the ByteString `===`/`!==` cases do plain JS `left === right` / `left !== right` on the raw hex source-text strings (case-sensitive). packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/05-stack-lower.ts:6349-6370 `hexToBytes` uses `hexNibble` per-character decoding that (standard hex decode) accepts both cases, so `'aa'` and `'AA'` decode to identical bytes and are pushed identically, then compared with the case-insensitive `OP_EQUAL` at runtime. So `'aa' === 'AA'` folds to `load_const(false)` at compile time (fold is on by default) while the deployed script's `OP_EQUAL` evaluates `true` — a compile-time-vs-runtime semantic divergence that can flip which branch of an `if` gets compiled away.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: accurate — both CL and GK cite the identical mechanism and it verifies exactly at HEAD; no fix found in git log for constant-fold.ts.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Call `foldConstants` on `[t0=load_const('aa'), t1=load_const('AA'), t2=bin_op('===', t0, t1)]`; assert the folded `t2` is `load_const(true)` (matching on-chain `OP_EQUAL` over the `hexToBytes`-decoded, case-insensitive bytes) instead of today's `load_const(false)`.

sweep1.evidence: packages/runar-compiler/src/optimizer/constant-fold.ts ByteString arm still does `case '===': return left === right;` on the raw hex text. Probe against dist foldConstants with [t0=load_const('aa'), t1=load_const('AA'), t2=bin_op('===',t0,t1)] gave `{"name":"t2","value":{"kind":"load_const","value":false}}`. The expected result is true, matching OP_EQUAL on the decoded bytes.

items.title: The flagship end2end PriceBet webapp's settle path is provably unspendable and never exercised on-chain
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-255] ## CL-BUG-255 — MEDIUM / P1 — The flagship webapp deploys a script whose advertised settlement path is provably unspendable
`webapp/compiler.go:111` sets `oraclePubKey` to `float64(12345)`. `EmitVerifyRabinSig` checks
`(sig² + padding) mod n == SHA256(msg)`; with `n = 12345` the left side is always `< 12345` and the
right is ~256 bits, so **`settle` can never succeed.** The app always spends via `cancel`, and the
winner is chosen in Go with `math/rand`.
**The worker narrowed the breadth claim rather than inheriting it**: the contract *is* exercised
on-chain, via `cancel`. The accurate statement is that the webapp never exercises the
oracle-settlement path it advertises — and that path *is* covered by `ts/regtest-demo-settle.ts`,
which no workflow runs.
dedup_uncertain: yes: CL-BUG-074 also bundles facts that fixing the oraclePubKey value alone would not close — the unlock-script builder always selects the cancel branch (bitcoin.go:281-284), the strike/oracle price are unsigned math/rand values chosen server-side, and the webapp UI's 'all variants compile to identical script' claim is untested. Kept together because the ledger explicitly frames BUG-255 as a correction of BUG-074's own claim rather than an independent finding, but a stricter reading could split the selector/unsigned-price/UI-claim facts into separate defects.
items.origin: split: CL-BUG-255 closes only the settle-path facet (oraclePubKey=12345); CL-BUG-074 also carries a cancel-only selector, unsigned price/threshold and a false UI claim. One failing test cannot close both.
items.tier_reason: needs a crafted adversarial input (§5 floor)

verification.evidence: Same as V349: examples/end2end-example/webapp/compiler.go:121-122 still hard-codes `oraclePubKey = float64(12345)`, which makes verifyRabinSig's `(sig^2 + padding) mod 12345 == SHA256(msg)` unsatisfiable (mod-12345 residue can never equal a ~256-bit SHA-256 digest). The narrower, corrected claim ('the webapp never exercises the oracle-settlement path it advertises, though the underlying PriceBet contract IS exercised via cancel, and ts/regtest-demo-settle.ts DOES cover real settle') still holds: examples/end2end-example/ts/regtest-demo-settle.ts exists and drives a genuine `settle` call, and no CI workflow runs it (grep of .github/workflows/*.yml for 'regtest-demo-settle' returns nothing).
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate; this is presented as, and reads as, a narrowing correction of V349/CL-BUG-074 rather than an independent defect, and the narrowing holds up against current code.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile PriceBet with webapp/compiler.go's actual oraclePubKey value, construct a genuine Rabin signature for a sample oracle price, and call `settle`; assert acceptance. It fails: no signature satisfies verifyRabinSig under n=12345 for a real SHA-256 digest.

sweep1.evidence: examples/end2end-example/webapp/compiler.go:121-122 still patches `case "oraclePubKey": program.Properties[i].InitialValue = float64(12345)`. compilers/go/codegen/rabin.go EmitVerifyRabinSig computes `(sig^2+padding) OP_MOD pubKey`, a value below 12345, and compares it with OP_NUMEQUAL against the unreduced 256-bit num(SHA256(msg)). settle therefore cannot succeed for any real digest. PriceBet settle still calls verifyRabinSig (ts/PriceBet.runar.ts:30, webapp/PriceBet.runar.java:58). No .github workflow references regtest-demo-settle.

items.title: The golden-provenance CI gate resolves the base commit from the unpinned pull_request.base.sha, the exact hazard its sibling wire-format gate documents and avoids
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-091] ## CL-BUG-091 — MEDIUM / P2 — The golden-provenance gate uses the exact base SHA its sibling gate documents as unsound, in the same file
**Dispatcher-verified.** Source: conformance-harness depth F-09 (breadth finding, confirmed and sharpened).

`.github/workflows/ci.yml:113` — `GOLDEN_GATE_BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}`.
`.github/workflows/ci.yml:210` — the *wire-format* gate's own comment, ~100 lines below:
> *"A base REF, not a pinned SHA. `pull_request.base.sha` is the base tip as of the PR's last sync, while the checkout is refs/pull/N/merge against the CURRENT base — so diffing from that SHA sweeps in every golden other PRs merged in between, and one of THOSE satisfies this gate for a PR that moved nothing."*

The wire gate resolves `origin/$PR_BASE_REF` at run time to avoid this. The golden gate does not. Two gates in one file, one documenting the hazard the other walks into.

verification.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:122 still sets `GOLDEN_GATE_BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}` directly (a pinned SHA captured at PR-sync time), while the checkout step for the same job (lines 108-112, `fetch-depth: 0`, no `ref:` override) uses actions/checkout@v4's default pull_request behavior — the synthetic `refs/pull/N/merge` against the CURRENT tip of the base branch. The sibling wire-format-must-move-golden gate ~100 lines below (lines 215-226) explicitly documents why this is unsound and resolves `PR_BASE_REF`/`git merge-base` at run time instead of trusting `base.sha`. The golden-provenance-gate step's own new comment (lines 118-121, 'base.sha = tip of the branch this PR merges into... so an already-merged commit from another PR is never misattributed here') asserts the opposite is true, but does not change the mechanism: when `refs/pull/N/merge`'s base has moved past the PR's last-synced `base.sha` (because other PRs merged in the interim), `git diff <old base.sha>...<merge-ref>` includes those interim commits' golden changes as if this PR made them, which is exactly the mechanism the wire-format gate's comment warns against for the same repo.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate; the exact hazard and both cited line ranges are unchanged, and a new comment was added defending the current (still unsound) design rather than fixing it — worth flagging to a dispatcher as a case where the rationale comment itself may need correcting, not just the code.

items.testable_assertion_verified: In a fixture repo: open a PR that does not touch any golden, let another PR modify+merge an UNjustified golden change to main, then re-run the golden-provenance-gate job (without re-syncing the first PR) against the stale `base.sha`. It should fail (no golden changed by THIS PR) but currently passes, because the three-dot diff against the stale base.sha sweeps in the second PR's already-merged, unjustified golden change and satisfies the gate for a PR that touched nothing.

sweep1.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:122 still has `GOLDEN_GATE_BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}`. conformance/scripts/check-golden-provenance.mjs:376 diffs `${base}...HEAD` against it. The wire-format gate at ci.yml:219-238 still documents the stale-base.sha hazard and resolves `origin/${PR_BASE_REF}` instead. The two gates are still inconsistent in the same file.

items.title: `executeStrict` does not mock `check_preimage` despite PROTOCOL.md and two doc comments promising it does — so 12 of 15 strict goldens are "abort at binding t2" and strict mode is unusable for the stateful contracts that most need it

[CL-BUG-055] | CL ID | sev | prio | title |
| CL-BUG-055 | MEDIUM | v1-should-have | `executeStrict` does not mock `check_preimage` despite PROTOCOL.md and two doc comments promising it does — so 12 of 15 strict goldens are "abort at binding t2" and strict mode is unusable for the stateful contracts that most need it |

verification.evidence: PROTOCOL.md:104-107 and packages/runar-sdk/src/anf-interpreter.ts:169-175's doc comment both promise strict mode keeps checkPreimage mock-returning true. That IS true for the explicit `checkPreimage(...)` builtin call path (evalCall, line 874: `if (!realCrypto) return true`). But the compiler auto-injects a DIFFERENT ANF node kind, `check_preimage` (packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/04-anf-lower.ts:344-350), for every stateful method's entry preamble, immediately followed by an un-marked `assert` node (:350, no `isAutoInjectedStateCheck` flag — that marker is only used for the exit-time continuation-hash assert, anf-interpreter.ts:521-526). The interpreter's handling of the `check_preimage` ANF-node kind (anf-interpreter.ts:601) unconditionally `return undefined` — it does NOT go through evalCall's mock-true logic. `isTruthy(undefined)` (line 1197-1203) falls through to `false`. So in strict mode the un-marked assert right after check_preimage throws `AssertionFailureError` at that binding. Directly verified against the checked-in goldens: `grep -l AssertionFailureError conformance/anf-interpreter/expected-strict/*.json` returns exactly 12 of the 15 files, and every one of those 12 carries `"bindingName": "t2"` — matching the finding's '12 of 15 ... abort at binding t2' precisely.

Today `executeStrict` throws `AssertionFailureError` with `bindingName: 't2'` for this and 11 other stateful fixtures. Fix: make the `check_preimage` ANF-node case return `true` when `strict?.realCrypto` is absent (mirroring evalCall's `checkPreimage` builtin handling) instead of unconditional `undefined`.

items.description: [CL-BUG-099] - **CL-BUG-099** `blake3Hash`: the interpreter truncates a >64-byte message and returns a digest; the script computes `64 - OP_SIZE(msg)`, which is negative, and `OP_NUM2BIN` aborts.

For msg.length > 64 this silently truncates to the first 64 bytes and computes blockLen=64 with no error — there is no bounds check comparable to `checkSplitIndex`/`checkNum2BinWidth` used elsewhere in this same file. The emitted script (packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/blake3-codegen.ts:440-456, `emitBlake3Hash`) computes `64 - OP_SIZE(msg)` via OP_SUB then feeds it as the width to `OP_NUM2BIN`; for msg.length > 64 that width is negative, and `checkNum2BinWidth` in this same interpreter file (line 244-248) documents that a negative width aborts on the real `Spend` engine (NEW-011) — but blake3Hash's hand-rolled logic bypasses that shared guard entirely. The codegen file's own doc comment (line 267, 432-435) even states 'inputs longer than one 64-byte block are out of scope' without the interpreter enforcing that as a refusal.

items.title: Go peephole replacements and reconstructed nested `if` operations discard SourceLoc, corrupting source maps for optimized code
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CX-BUG-012] Stack lowering attaches `SourceLoc` to emitted operations, but every synthetic peephole replacement is constructed without a location. Recursive conditional optimization also reconstructs the parent `if` using only `Op`, `Then`, and `Else`, discarding the parent’s location. Source maps are therefore incomplete or shifted after normal optimization.

[CX-BUG-023] Stack lowering attaches source locations to emitted operations, but the optimizer reconstructs nested `if` operations and peephole replacements without copying a source location. Emission only records mappings for operations that still have one, so optimized opcodes and `OP_IF` sites disappear from or weaken source maps.

evidence.CX-BUG-012: `StackOp` carries `SourceLoc`; `emitOp` populates it before optimization. Replacement literals and `optimizeNestedIf` do not copy it. `rg -n 'SourceLoc'` across the scoped optimizer tests returned no matches.
evidence.CX-BUG-023: Replacement literals such as `StackOp{Op:"opcode", Code:"OP_1ADD"}` contain no `SourceLoc`; `optimizeNestedIf` also drops the outer operation’s location.

remediation.CX-BUG-012: Assign a deterministic source location to replacements and preserve all metadata on rebuilt conditional nodes.
remediation.CX-BUG-023: Define deterministic provenance rules and copy/merge source locations into every replacement and reconstructed operation.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-012: Compiling the same source with an applicable peephole rule preserves a source mapping for the replacement opcode at the original source line.
testable_assertion.CX-BUG-023: With `IncludeSourceMap`, a source expression optimized from push-one/add to `OP_1ADD` and an optimized conditional both retain mappings to their source lines.

items.tier_reason: ANF/stack/emit/EC-optimizer boundary and emitted bytes change (§5 floor: mid min, top if bytes move)

verification.evidence: compilers/go/codegen/optimizer.go:34-48 (optimizeNestedIf) reconstructs StackOp{Op: "if", Then: optimizedThen, Else: optimizedElse} with no SourceLoc field copied from the input op — confirmed byte-identical to the CX/GK-reviewed commit 2b3af765. matchWindow2/3/4 throughout optimizer.go build brand-new StackOp{...} replacement literals with SourceLoc left at Go's zero value (nil). compilers/go/codegen/stack.go:738-744 (ctx.emitOp) is the only place that stamps ctx.currentSourceLoc onto an op, and it runs ONCE during stack lowering, before OptimizeStackOps ever executes on the resulting []StackOp slice. compilers/go/codegen/emit.go:610-615 (emitStackOp) only calls ctx.setSourceLoc(op.SourceLoc) if op.SourceLoc != nil, and recordSourceMapping (~223-230) only appends a mapping entry if ctx.pendingSourceLoc != nil, each emitStackOp call also resetting pendingSourceLoc to nil at its end — so a SourceLoc-less op emits with no mapping entry at all (not a stale reused one). CX-BUG-012 and CX-BUG-023 are genuine near-duplicates — both describe the exact same two code paths, just emphasizing different downstream symptoms; treat as one finding.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Cited line numbers (emit.go:470-475, optimizer.go:34-166, stack.go:26-1169) drifted from their values at the reviewed commit due to ~620 intervening commits (spot-checked emit.go:470-475 at commit 2b3af765 and it does land on the emitStackOp SourceLoc-propagation block there, confirming the citation was accurate when written); at HEAD the equivalent code is at optimizer.go:34-46 plus matchWindow2/3/4 through ~292, emit.go:196-230+610-615, and stack.go:35-44+738-744. This is a tooling/debuggability defect (source-map fidelity for runar-cli debug), not a consensus/funds-affecting one — no attacker input triggers it, hence reachable_by_adversary=false.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile a fixture with IncludeSourceMap where stack lowering emits a PUSH(1) immediately followed by OP_ADD with a known SourceLoc (e.g. from an explicit `x + 1n` at a known line), and separately a conditional (if) with a known SourceLoc. After optimization collapses PUSH(1)+OP_ADD into OP_1ADD and optimizeNestedIf reconstructs the if-op, assert the emitted source map still contains an entry mapping the OP_1ADD opcode's index (and the if op's opcode index) back to that original source line. Today both come back with no source-map entry.

sweep1.evidence: compilers/go/codegen/optimizer.go has no SourceLoc reference. optimizeNestedIf returns `StackOp{Op: "if", Then: ..., Else: ...}` and the PUSH1+OP_ADD peephole returns `[]StackOp{{Op: "opcode", Code: "OP_1ADD"}}`. emit.go resets pendingSourceLoc to nil after each op. Probe: a contract with `const y = x + 1n;` on line 6 compiled with `runar-go --source Inc.runar.ts --disable-constant-folding --emit-source-map`. ASM is `OP_1ADD OP_0 OP_NUMEQUAL`, and the source map has entries only for opcodeIndex 1 and 2 (line 7). OP_1ADD (index 0, line 6) has no mapping.

items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [CX-BUG-033] EC-generated binding names come from a process-global `AtomicInteger` that is never reset per program. In daemon mode, compiling identical input twice can therefore produce different canonical ANF solely because an earlier request advanced the counter.

evidence.CX-BUG-033: The global counter is declared at lines 129-130 and incremented at lines 365-370; daemon requests repeatedly call the optimizer in the same process at `Cli.java:469-477`.

remediation.CX-BUG-033: Use a program-local deterministic allocator seeded from the current method/body, with collision checks against existing names.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-033: Two identical EC compilation requests in one daemon process must return byte-identical IR JSON.

verification.evidence: compilers/java/src/main/java/runar/compiler/passes/AnfOptimize.java:130 declares `private static final AtomicInteger FRESH_COUNTER = new AtomicInteger(0)` — a class-static field, initialized once per JVM process. Line 417 calls `FRESH_COUNTER.incrementAndGet()` to mint fresh EC-optimizer binding names. Cli.java's daemon mode (--daemon, line 83+) serves multiple compile requests from one long-lived process; grepped the whole passes/ and Cli.java for any reset of FRESH_COUNTER — none exists. Two identical daemon requests compiling an EC-containing contract will therefore mint different fresh names (t_fresh_N vs t_fresh_M) purely because the second request's counter starts where the first left off.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate, code-verified exactly as described.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Two identical --daemon JSON-RPC compile requests for the same EC-containing contract, issued back to back in one runar-java daemon process, must produce byte-identical canonical ANF JSON (--emit-ir); today the second request's EC-generated fresh names differ because FRESH_COUNTER is never reset between requests.

sweep1.evidence: Daemon probe with java -jar compilers/java/build/libs/runar-java-compiler-1.0.0-rc.1.jar --daemon. Two identical requests {source:EcOpt.runar.ts (ecAdd(ecMulGen(2n),ecMulGen(3n))), emitIr:true}, with fold on and with fold off. Response id1 has `__ec_opt_1` and id2 has `__ec_opt_2`, and `ir` equality is False. AnfOptimize.java:132 `private static final AtomicInteger FRESH_COUNTER` is never reset, and freshConstName (~l.458) increments it.

items.title: Java: recursive peephole optimization of nested `if`/`loop` reconstructs IfOp via location-dropping constructors, losing the enclosing branch's source location
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [CX-BUG-034] Nested branch optimization reconstructs every `IfOp` using constructors that omit `i.sourceLoc()`. The emitter relies on the enclosing `IfOp` location to map structural `OP_IF`; branch contents may retain locations, but the control boundary loses its source attribution.

evidence.CX-BUG-034: `optimizeNestedIf` creates `new IfOp(thenB)` or `new IfOp(thenB, elseB)` at lines 58-64, despite explicit location-preserving constructors being used elsewhere at lines 146-161.

remediation.CX-BUG-034: Reconstruct with the original `sourceLoc`, and add a source-map regression around optimized branches.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-034: Peephole optimization of an `IfOp` with a source location must preserve that exact location on the result and on emitted `OP_IF` mapping.

items.tier_reason: ANF/stack/emit/EC-optimizer boundary and emitted bytes change (§5 floor: mid min, top if bytes move)

verification.evidence: compilers/java/src/main/java/runar/compiler/passes/Peephole.java:59-64 (optimizeNestedIf): for `op instanceof IfOp i`, always reconstructs via `new IfOp(thenB)` (elseB==null) or `new IfOp(thenB, elseB)` — both are the 2-arg/1-arg IfOp constructors (IfOp.java:21-27) which hard-default `sourceLoc = null`, and `i.sourceLoc()` is never read or passed through. optimizeNestedIf runs unconditionally on EVERY StackOp at the top of `optimize()` (line 48: `for (StackOp op : ops) current.add(optimizeNestedIf(op))`), so any IfOp with nested contents loses its source location on every single optimize() call, not only when a peephole rule actually rewrites something inside.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate, code-verified exactly as described; the loss is broader than the finding states — it happens on every IfOp passed through optimizeNestedIf, not only ones a rewrite rule actually touches.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Peephole.optimize() applied to a StackProgram whose IfOp carries a non-null sourceLoc must preserve that exact sourceLoc on the returned IfOp (and Emit's OP_IF source-map entry must still point at it); today optimizeNestedIf always emits a fresh IfOp with sourceLoc=null.

sweep1.evidence: compilers/java/.../passes/Peephole.java optimizeNestedIf (~l.58-65): `if (elseB == null) return new IfOp(thenB); return new IfOp(thenB, elseB);`. ir/stack/IfOp.java: those constructors delegate to `this(thenBranch, elseBranch, null)`, so i.sourceLoc() is always dropped on every IfOp passed through Peephole.optimize. Code-level verdict: the code path is unconditional.

items.title: Java: Validate.run's returned warnings are discarded by both CLI and daemon compilation modes
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [CX-BUG-048] `Validate.run` returns collected warnings on success. Both normal compilation and daemon compilation ignore that return value, so warnings about unsafe sighash use, locktime guards, or stripped readonly properties never reach users.

evidence.CX-BUG-048: Both call sites invoke `Validate.run(contract);` as a statement and only handle thrown errors; neither serializes or prints its returned list.

remediation.CX-BUG-048: Emit warnings to stderr in CLI mode and include structured warnings in daemon responses, including parse-only responses.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-048: Compiling a contract known to trigger `warnStrippedReadonlyFields` must visibly report the warning in CLI and daemon modes.

verification.evidence: The normal CLI compilation path (Cli.java:129-144) is already fixed: `for (String w : Validate.run(contract)) err.println("warning: " + w);`, with a comment explicitly citing CL-BUG-104 ('this used to discard them'). But the daemon path is not: serveRequest (Cli.java:733-777) calls `Validate.run(contract);` at line 741 and discards the returned warning list entirely — no 'warnings' field appears anywhere in the JSON response construction (grep for "warning" in Cli.java finds only the CLI-path eprintln and an unrelated NULLFAIL comment), so a daemon client has no way to see e.g. warnStrippedReadonlyFields or the locktime-sequence-guard warning for a request it submits.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Right about the daemon path, which still discards warnings unchanged — but the 'both normal compilation and daemon compilation ignore that return value' claim is now half-stale: CL-BUG-104 fixed the normal CLI path already.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Sending a compile request to the Java daemon (serveRequest) for a contract known to trigger a Validate warning (e.g. warnStrippedReadonlyFields) must surface that warning in the JSON response (a "warnings" array, matching the CLI path's behavior) rather than silently returning `{"id":N,"ok":true,...}` with no trace of it.

sweep1.evidence: The CLI path is fixed: f703a6ac (R-061), Cli.java:137 `for (String w : Validate.run(contract))` prints `warning: ... readonly field 'unused' ... eliminated by DCE`. The daemon path is not: serveRequest (Cli.java ~l.757) calls `Validate.run(contract);` and discards the result. items.title: Java: AnfLower's branch-property-update lifting generates new bindings with sourceLoc uniformly null, dropping source-map entries for conditional state-update opcodes
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [CX-BUG-050] The branch-property-update normalization replaces a located `if` with newly generated bindings whose `sourceLoc` is uniformly null. Stack lowering can only stamp locations carried by bindings, and emission skips operations with no location, leaving transformed conditional state-update opcodes absent from source maps.

evidence.CX-BUG-050: Every `new AnfBinding` in the transformation at lines 2528-2625 passes null; the original binding's location is not propagated.

remediation.CX-BUG-050: Attach the original conditional location, or the closest source binding location, to every generated binding.

items.tier_reason: ANF/stack/emit/EC-optimizer boundary and emitted bytes change (§5 floor: mid min, top if bytes move)

verification.evidence: AnfLower.liftBranchUpdateProps (2943-3097), called unconditionally on every method body from AnfLower.run (163), constructs every synthesized AnfBinding with a literal `null` third (sourceLoc) argument: the condition-setup rebinds (2972), the negation/conjunction/disjunction temporaries (2992, 3000, 3006, 3035-3040), the terminal assert(false)-reintroduction (3039-3040), the old-property load (3048), the per-branch value rebinds (3055, 3077-3078), the else-arm keep-old value (3083-3084), the synthesized If (3087-3088), and the UpdateProp itself (3091-3092) — every single one passes `null`. items.testable_assertion_verified: Emitting a contract with a conditional property update (e.g. `if (cond) { this.x = a; } else { this.x = b; }`) and requesting a source map must produce mappings whose opcode indices trace back to the conditional's or its branches' source lines; today liftBranchUpdateProps drops every sourceLoc to null, so no such mapping exists for the opcodes it generates.

Probe: Cond.runar.ts (if (c>0n){this.x=a}else{this.x=b}) compiled with Java `--emit-source-map` gives 6 mappings only: opcode indices 102-105 (line 7, the comparison) and 138-139 (line 12). items.title: `.runar.java`'s unsuffixed `0xFFFFFFFF` parses as Java `int` -1, diverging from TS's `0xFFFFFFFFn` and silently satisfying the sequence-finality bound check
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-244] ## CL-BUG-244 — MEDIUM / P2 — `0xFFFFFFFF` in a `.runar.java` source is the bigint −1, and that silently satisfies the #131 sequence-finality heuristic
Source: impl-java-main NEW-07, **verified empirically by the worker with javac in a temp dir**:
`0xFFFFFFFF` → `Integer = -1` (JLS §3.10.1: an unsuffixed hex literal is an `int`);
`0xFFFFFFFFL` → `Long = 4294967295`.
`JavaParser.java:624-626` passes javac's value straight through. So `.runar.ts` `0xFFFFFFFFn` is
`4294967295n` and `.runar.java` `0xFFFFFFFF` is `-1n` — **same fixture, two ASTs.**
And the constant matters: `0xffffffff` is the nSequence finality sentinel, `Validate.isSequenceBound`
accepts any `BigIntLiteral <= 0xffffffff`, and `-1` passes — so a contract writing
`assert(extractSequence(p) < 0xFFFFFFFF)` gets a covenant comparing against −1 **and silences the
#131 locktime-without-sequence-guard warning.** Everything else about the Java surface's literal
handling is clean; this is the one wrap case.

verification.evidence: compilers/java/src/main/java/runar/compiler/frontend/JavaParser.java:637-639 `convertLiteral`: `if (value instanceof Integer i) { return new BigIntLiteral(BigInteger.valueOf(i)); }` passes javac's attributed literal value straight through with no range/overflow handling, so an unsuffixed `0xFFFFFFFF` (javac type `int`, JLS 3.10.1, value -1) becomes `BigIntLiteral(-1)`, diverging from `.runar.ts`'s `0xFFFFFFFFn` = `BigIntLiteral(4294967295)`. This literal-parsing divergence is real and unfixed. HOWEVER the specific claimed CONSEQUENCE — that this silently satisfies the #131 locktime-sequence-guard heuristic — is now STALE: packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/02-validate.ts:1698-1699 `strictBoundOk = (e) => e.kind === 'bigint_literal' && e.value > 0n && e.value <= SEQUENCE_FINAL` (added by commit 94f5f31f, 2026-09-17, after the CL review) rejects any non-positive bound including -1n, so `assert(extractSequence(p) < 0xFFFFFFFF)` misparsed as `< -1n` no longer counts as a recognized guard and the #131 warning still fires.
verification.fixed_by: 94f5f31f fix(validate): locktime sequence guard must be asserted (F7) — closes only the 'silently satisfies the guard check' half of the claim; the underlying 0xFFFFFFFF -> -1 literal-parsing divergence in JavaParser.java is unfixed.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: The literal-divergence mechanism is exactly right. The illustrative consequence (silencing the #131 warning) was true at the reviewed commit but has since been fixed by an unrelated F7 change (94f5f31f) that tightened the same bound check for a different reason (rejecting `< 0n`).

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile `const n: bigint = 0xFFFFFFFF;` (no `L` suffix) through the Java-format frontend: today it lowers to BigIntLiteral(-1). The equivalent `.runar.ts` `const n: bigint = 0xFFFFFFFFn;` lowers to BigIntLiteral(4294967295). Same fixture, two ASTs — cross-format AST parity is broken for any unsuffixed hex literal with the top bit set (0x80000000-0xFFFFFFFF).

sweep1.evidence: Probe: Lit.runar.java with `assertThat(x.eq(Bigint.of(0xFFFFFFFF)))`. Both the Java jar and Go compiler `--emit-ir` give load_const `"value": -1` (TS 0xFFFFFFFFn is 4294967295). F-026 (e4087cca) now pins this deliberately: conformance/negatives/int-literal-cases.json java row `["0xFFFFFFFF", -1]`, ts row 4294967295. The cross-format AST divergence therefore remains, by design decision R15. On the warning side, Validate.isStrictSequenceBound now requires signum()>0, so `< -1` no longer silences #131. isNonStrictSequenceBound (`<=`) still accepts -1.

items.title: A second, javac-invalid `PriceBet.runar.java` is the copy the playground serves
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-256] ## CL-BUG-256 — MEDIUM / P1 — A second, javac-invalid `PriceBet.runar.java` is the copy the playground serves
`webapp/PriceBet.runar.java:57` calls `num2bin(price, 8)` with an `int` literal that matches no
overload; `:60`/`:62` apply `>` to `runar.lang.types.Bigint`, a `final class`. The canonical copy
avoids exactly this with `price.gt(Bigint.of(0))`.
**It survives because `JavaParser.java:155` calls `task.parse()` only, never `analyze()`** — so the
Rúnar frontend accepts source javac's attribution phase rejects. It is served because
`compiler.go:45` lists `dirs: []string{".", "../java"}` with `"."` first, and the comment at
`:41-44` claiming *"no external PriceBet.runar.java yet"* is false.

verification.evidence: examples/end2end-example/webapp/PriceBet.runar.java:57 `num2bin(price, 8)` calls with a bare `int` literal `8`; packages/runar-java/src/main/java/runar/lang/Builtins.java:302,311,320 only overload num2bin for `(BigInteger,BigInteger)`, `(Bigint,Bigint)`, `(Bigint,BigInteger)` — none accepts primitive `int`, so real javac would report 'no suitable method'. Lines 60/62 of the same file apply `>` directly to `Bigint` operands (`price > strikePrice`), which is not valid Java syntax for a non-primitive final class. The canonical copy at examples/end2end-example/java/src/main/java/runar/end2end/PriceBet.runar.java:52,55,57 uses `num2bin(price.value(), java.math.BigInteger.valueOf(8))` and `price.gt(...)`, avoiding both issues. compilers/java/src/main/java/runar/compiler/frontend/JavaParser.java:145-155 `parseToTree` calls `task.parse()` only (never `task.analyze()`), so type/overload-resolution errors (which are caught during javac's Attr phase, not Parse) are never surfaced — confirmed no analyze() call exists anywhere in JavaParser.java. examples/end2end-example/webapp/compiler.go:46 `"java": {..., dirs: []string{".", "../java"}}` serves the webapp's own (broken) copy first; the adjacent comment ':41 "Java: no external PriceBet.runar.java yet"' is false — the canonical copy at ../java (examples/end2end-example/java/...) does exist.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate — every cited line and mechanism (overload set, `>` on Bigint, parse()-only, dirs ordering, false 'no external copy' comment) verified unchanged at HEAD.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Run real `javac` (attribution, not just parse) on examples/end2end-example/webapp/PriceBet.runar.java: it fails today with 'no suitable method found for num2bin(Bigint,int)' and 'bad operand types for binary operator >' errors. The Rúnar frontend (JavaParser.parseToTree, task.parse()-only) currently accepts it without error. Fix: either replace the webapp copy with the canonical one, or swap compiler.go's `dirs` order to prefer `../java`, and/or make JavaParser call `task.analyze()` so genuinely invalid Java is rejected.

sweep1.evidence: examples/end2end-example/webapp/PriceBet.runar.java still has `ByteString msg = num2bin(price, 8);`, `assertThat(price > 0);` and `if (price > strikePrice)`, applying `>` to Bigint. webapp/compiler.go still has `"java": {... dirs: []string{".", "../java"}}` with the stale 'no external PriceBet.runar.java yet' comment. compilers/java/.../frontend/JavaParser.java:155 is still `units = task.parse();`, and there is no analyze(). Code-level verdict: javac was not run.

items.title: Process-global _fresh_counter never resets between compilations, so optimized ANF for the same input differs depending on what else was compiled earlier in the same process
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [CX-BUG-053] `_fresh_counter` persists for the Python process and is never reset per program. Identical inputs compiled at different points in a daemon or test process can receive different binding names, breaking deterministic ANF and making collision behavior dependent on prior compilations.

evidence.CX-BUG-053: The module-global counter is incremented at lines 288-300; every public program compilation invokes the optimizer at `compiler.py:447-449`.

remediation.CX-BUG-053: Replace it with a deterministic method/program-local allocator initialized for every optimization invocation.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-053: Optimizing the same Rule 10 program twice in one process must return byte-identical serialized ANF.

dedup_uncertain: yes: same root object (_fresh_counter) as CX-BUG-052's collision bug — both stem from the counter not being scoped per-compilation — but the two failure modes (wrong-value-via-collision vs. cross-compilation non-determinism) are independently observable and CX filed them as two separate testable assertions, so kept separate.

verification.evidence: compilers/python/runar_compiler/frontend/anf_optimize.py:320 `_fresh_counter = 0` is still a bare module-level global with no reset hook anywhere in compiler.py or anf_optimize.py (grep for `_fresh_counter` in runar_compiler/ shows only the declaration and the increment site). Reproduced live: compiling the identical Rule-10 source (`ecAdd(ecMulGen(2n), ecMulGen(3n))`) twice via `compile_source_to_ir` + `optimize_ec` in one Python process yields `__ec_opt_1` on the first call and `__ec_opt_2` on the second -- non-deterministic ANF naming purely as a function of prior compiler activity in the process.
verification.reachable_by_adversary: false -- a process-lifetime determinism/reproducibility defect (affects CI/daemon reuse), not an attacker-input-driven vulnerability.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Fully accurate and independently reproduced exactly as described.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Optimize the same Rule-10 program (`ecAdd(ecMulGen(2n), ecMulGen(3n))`) twice in one Python process via `optimize_ec`. The two resulting serialized ANF programs must be byte-identical, including the generated `__ec_opt_N` binding name. Currently (reproduced) the second run names it `__ec_opt_2` instead of `__ec_opt_1`.

sweep1.evidence: Probe in one python3 process: runar_compiler.compiler.compile_source_to_ir(EcOpt.runar.ts with ecAdd(ecMulGen(2n),ecMulGen(3n))) called twice gives ['__ec_opt_1'] then ['__ec_opt_2'], and identical is False. frontend/anf_optimize.py:351 `_fresh_counter = 0` is module-global, incremented at ~l.373 and never reset.

items.title: is_stateful (and therefore is_terminal / artifact.anf) is derived from len(state_fields) instead of the documented-authoritative program.parent_class, so a zero-mutable-field StatefulSmartContract loses its terminal ABI flags and ANF state-tracking snapshot
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [CX-BUG-074] The IR comments say `parent_class` is authoritative even for a `StatefulSmartContract` with zero mutable fields, but artifact assembly sets `is_stateful` from `len(state_fields)`. Such a contract retains `parentClass` yet loses terminal ABI flags and the ANF snapshot that SDK state tracking expects.

remediation.CX-BUG-074: Derive stateful identity from `program.parent_class` and separately track whether mutable state fields exist.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-074: A zero-mutable-field `StatefulSmartContract` must retain terminal ABI metadata and its ANF state-tracking snapshot.

items.tier_reason: ANF/stack/emit/EC-optimizer boundary (§5 floor: mid min, top if bytes move)

verification.evidence: compilers/python/runar_compiler/compiler.py:824: 'is_stateful = len(state_fields) > 0' (unchanged by the parentClass fix). This gates is_terminal for ABI methods (line ~834) and 'if is_stateful: art.anf = program' (lines ~902-903). Reproduced live: compiled a StatefulSmartContract with a single readonly property and no mutable fields -- the artifact's abi.methods[0] has no isTerminal key at all, and the top-level artifact has no 'ir'/'anf' key, even though parentClass == 'StatefulSmartContract' is correctly present (from the separate 304bfd31 fix). This finding is about the compiler's OWN is_terminal/anf gating, which the parentClass fix did not touch and which remains wrong as described.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate and still open; correctly distinguishes parent_class as the documented-authoritative signal from the len(state_fields) heuristic actually used.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile a StatefulSmartContract with zero mutable properties (all readonly); assert the artifact's abi.methods[].isTerminal is set and the artifact carries an ir/anf ANF snapshot, instead of omitting both because is_stateful = len(state_fields) > 0 evaluates false.

items.title: Python: crypto op caches (`_get_compress_ops` in sha256.py/blake3.py) return the same shared `StackOp` list objects on every call, and `emit_op` mutates `source_loc` on them in place — a process-lifetime source-map corruption, not a consensus bug
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-147] ## CL-BUG-147 — MEDIUM / P2 — Python's crypto op caches are shared mutable objects that `emit_op` stamps in place — a genuine Python-only divergence
Source: impl-python-codegen NEW-05, **demonstrated by execution**, and the only Python-specific
defect in this report.
`_get_compress_ops()` (`sha256.py:452-459`) returns the *same list of the same 21,292 `StackOp`
objects* on every call; `blake3.py:595-602` does the same. `_LoweringContext.emit_op`
(`stack.py:663-667`) then **mutates** `op.source_loc` on the object it was handed. The first
`sha256Compress()` call site in a process stamps its location onto the cache permanently; every
later call site — same method, other method, other contract, other compilation in the same
process — emits ops still carrying the first location. Go is immune purely because
`compilers/go/codegen/stack.go:700-706` takes `StackOp` **by value**.
Emitted bytes are unaffected (source_loc is used only for source mapping), so this is a source-map
defect, not a consensus one — but it makes the Python tier's source-map output **order- and
process-dependent**, which is a latent flake in any cross-tier source-map comparison.

...
  (CL-BUG-147, the mutable op cache). `OP_NEGATE OP_NEGATE`, `_codePart`, `bn254G1OnCurve`
  canonicity, the WOTS+ length gate, `sqrt`, SLH-DSA `a=8` and the `merkle.py` rot-triple are all
  present identically in at least the Go tier, with citations given per finding. **That distinction
  is load-bearing for remediation: a single-tier fix to any of them breaks the hex-parity invariant.**

verification.evidence: compilers/python/runar_compiler/codegen/sha256.py:452-459 (_get_compress_ops) caches and returns the SAME list of the SAME StackOp objects on every call; compilers/python/runar_compiler/codegen/blake3.py:598-... does the same for blake3. compilers/python/runar_compiler/codegen/stack.py:693-696 (_LoweringContext.emit_op): 'if self.current_source_loc and op.source_loc is None: op.source_loc = self.current_source_loc' mutates the shared StackOp in place. Reproduced live and dramatically: in one Python process, compiled contract A (sha256Compress call at line 8) then contract B (sha256Compress call at line 11 of a DIFFERENT file /tmp/B.runar.ts). B's own artifact.source_map has 21,292 SourceMapping entries whose source_file is '/tmp/A.runar.ts' (contract A's file, stamped by the FIRST call in the process) and only 2 entries pointing to B's own file. items.title: Python: `emit_push_data_encode` has no `OP_PUSHDATA4` (0x4E) branch, silently truncating a ByteString state field's declared length modulo 65536 for fields ≥ 64 KiB
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-149] ## CL-BUG-149 — MEDIUM / P2 — `emit_push_data_encode` has no `0x4E` branch and silently truncates a ByteString state field's length modulo 65536
Source: impl-python-codegen NEW-10. The encoder handles `< 76`, `76-255` (`0x4C`) and `>= 256`
(`0x4D` + 2 bytes LE) and stops. For a ByteString state field ≥ 65,536 bytes,
`OP_NUM2BIN(4); OP_SPLIT(2); DROP` keeps only the low two bytes, producing a `0x4D` push declaring
`len mod 65536`. Used to build the state blob in both `_lower_get_state_script`
(`stack.py:2540-2541`) and `_lower_add_output` (`stack.py:3164-3166`), so the continuation output the
covenant commits to carries a corrupt push-data header.
**This is the same bug class the neighbouring `emit_varint_encoding` was explicitly fixed for** —
its comment at `stack.py:679-690` says *"We must support all four shapes … so we never silently
truncate"* and cites `integration/go/contracts/RollupBug.runar.go`. The same reasoning was applied a
third time in `_lower_deserialize_state`. The push-data encoder is the one place it was not carried
through.
items.tier_reason: ANF/stack/emit/EC-optimizer boundary and emitted bytes change (§5 floor: mid min, top if bytes move)

verification.evidence: compilers/python/runar_compiler/codegen/stack.py:816-911 (emit_push_data_encode): three branches only -- len<76 (1-byte length), 76<=len<256 (0x4C + 1-byte), and an unconditional ELSE for len>=256 that always does OP_NUM2BIN(2); OP_SPLIT(2) and pushes 0x4D + a 2-byte LE length. No 0x4E (OP_PUSHDATA4) branch and no bound on the ELSE case, so a value >= 65536 bytes truncates to 'len mod 65536' via OP_NUM2BIN(4)-then-2-byte-split semantics implied by the fixed 2-byte encode. Called from _lower_get_state_script (~line 2726-2730) and _lower_add_output (~line 3275-3280) to build the OP_RETURN state-continuation payload, so a covenant with a ByteString mutable state field >=64KiB commits to a corrupted push-data header on continuation. The neighbouring emit_varint_encoding (stack.py:697-...) DOES implement all four varint shapes (documented at line ~703-716, citing integration/go/contracts/RollupBug.runar.go for exactly this truncation bug class) -- confirming push-data encoding is the one place the same reasoning was not carried through, matching the finding's framing precisely. No length cap elsewhere in validator.py or typecheck.py prevents a ByteString state field from reaching this size.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate; the parallel to emit_varint_encoding's RollupBug precedent and the two call sites both check out at HEAD.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Directly lower a state binding whose ByteString mutable field length is >= 65536 through emit_push_data_encode; assert the emitted push-data header is a 0x4E (OP_PUSHDATA4) 4-byte-LE length equal to the true length, not a 0x4D 2-byte length truncated modulo 65536.

items.title: Python: `if`-branch lowering contexts do not inherit the parent's `const_values` map, so a Merkle builtin inside a branch rejects a depth literal declared immediately before the branch as a runtime value

items.description: [CX-BUG-060] `const_values` tracks literal depth arguments, but branch contexts do not inherit outer constants. Merkle builtins inside a branch therefore reject a depth literal declared immediately before the branch as a runtime value.

evidence.CX-BUG-060: `const_values` is initialized per context at line 596; branch construction never copies it; both Merkle lowering paths require lookup from this map at lines 4421-4428 and 4485-4492.

Reproduced live: compiled a contract with 'const depth = 4n;' declared before an if, calling merkleRootSha256(leaf, proof, index, depth) inside the if-body -- compilation fails with exactly 'merkleRootSha256: depth (4th argument) must be a compile-time constant integer literal. Got a runtime value for \'depth\'.', matching the finding precisely.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Fully accurate, exact error message reproduced verbatim.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile a contract that declares 'const depth = 4n;' before an if and calls merkleRootSha256(leaf, proof, index, depth) inside the if-body; compilation must succeed instead of raising 'depth (4th argument) must be a compile-time constant integer literal'.

sweep1.evidence: Probe with ANF IR from Python --emit-ir --disable-constant-folding, merkle depth arg patched to the top-level literal binding t0 (=4). Mk2 (call outside the if): Python --ir compiles (hex 5476557a...). Mk (same call inside the if-then branch): Python errors 'merkleRootSha256: depth (4th argument) must be a compile-time constant integer literal. Got a runtime value for 't0''. stack.py branch contexts (then_ctx/else_ctx ~l.2156/2200) copy sm, array_elements and similar but not const_values. Go behaves the same (Go-only family). The source-level `const depth = 4n` form fails even outside a branch, because the @ref alias is not tracked in const_values.

items.title: BabyBear field operations' documented non-negativity premise is not enforced; `bbFieldAdd(-1, 0)` returns −1
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-150] ## CL-BUG-150 — MEDIUM / P3 — BabyBear field operations' documented non-negativity premise is not enforced; `bbFieldAdd(-1, 0)` returns −1
Source: impl-python-codegen NEW-16. `_bb_field_add` (`babybear.py:192-204`) emits
`OP_ADD; push BB_P; OP_MOD` with the comment *"Sum of two values in [0, p-1] is always non-negative,
so simple OP_MOD suffices"*. Bitcoin's `OP_MOD` takes the sign of the **dividend**, so the shortcut
is correct only if the sum is non-negative — and both operands arrive from the witness as arbitrary
script numbers with no range check (absence-grep over `babybear.py` for `OP_LESSTHAN`, `OP_WITHIN`,
`canonic`, `range` returns nothing; I confirmed `OP_SIZE` count is 0 for that file). The value −1
then flows into every downstream field operation. `emit_bb_field_inv` likewise returns 0 for input 0
rather than aborting. `bn254.py:280-285` spells the same premise out as *"SAFETY: Only use when the
input is guaranteed non-negative"* — the premise is documented and unenforced.
**KoalaBear is an unverified lead, not a claim**: the worker's structural grep shows the same
absence but it did not read the file. Stated as a lead per the no-extrapolation rule.

verification.evidence:
BabyBear half is FIXED: `emit_bb_field_add` (babybear.py:324-332) now calls `_bb_emit_canon_verify(t, 'a', 'b')` (babybear.py:283-322, `OP_DUP/OP_PICK <0>

OP_WITHIN OP_VERIFY` per operand) BEFORE the internal `_bb_field_add`, at every public entry point (bbFieldAdd/Sub/Mul/Inv and all 8 ext4 entries) -- so `bbFieldAdd(-1, 0)` is now rejected rather than returning -1 (fixed by 8227afc9). BN254 half is STILL BROKEN: `emit_bn254_field_add`/`_sub`/`_mul` (bn254.py:967-998) call `_bn254_field_add`/`_sub`/`_mul` directly with NO canon-verify gate; `_bn254_field_add` (bn254.py:299-310) still reduces via the bare-OP_MOD `_bn254_field_mod_positive` (bn254.py:280-285, unchanged 'SAFETY: Only use when input is guaranteed non-negative' comment, no enforcement). Only bn254's EC-POINT builtins (bn254Add/Negate/Mul, via `_bn254_emit_coord_canon_verify`) got gated; the raw scalar-field builtins `bn254FieldAdd`/`bn254FieldSub`/`bn254FieldMul` (exported from packages/runar-lang/src/builtins.ts and dispatched via stack.py:1621/5058-5072 with no pre-dispatch gate) did not. So `bn254FieldAdd(-1, 0)` still returns -1 at HEAD.
verification.fixed_by: 8227afc9 -- BabyBear (and KoalaBear) only; bn254 raw scalar-field ops unfixed

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile and execute a contract calling `bn254FieldAdd(-1n, 0n)` with a witness -1: the deployed script must reject (or canonicalize to p-1), not accept a result of -1.

sweep1.evidence:
The BabyBear half is fixed by 8227afc9: Python bbFieldAdd asm now has `OP_0

OP_WITHIN OP_VERIFY` per operand, and ScriptVM gives a=-1,b=0,r=-1 -> false (OP_VERIFY). The TAV's bn254FieldAdd(-1n,0n) still reproduces. Python asm is `OP_ROT OP_ROT

OP_TOALTSTACK OP_ADD OP_FROMALTSTACK OP_DUP OP_TOALTSTACK OP_MOD ... OP_NUMEQUAL`, with no range gate. Executed via runar-testing ScriptVM (unlock 0181 00 0181 + locking): success=true, so the result -1 is accepted.

items.title: `parser_go.py` uses the C ladder, not Go's
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
CL-BUG-208 … CL-BUG-213
- **`parser_go.py` uses the C ladder, not Go's** (`:1397-1455`): `x&255 == 15` parses as
  `x & (255 == 15)` in the Python tier and `(x&255) === 15` in the Go reference, which uses
  `go/parser`. Three worked examples, both tiers executed. **The same defect CL-BUG-173 found from
  the Rust tier** — now confirmed in two tiers, with the Go tier the odd one out.
items.origin: decomposed from ledger range heading at line 3289 (bullet 1/11); the range IDs cannot be mapped 1:1 to bullets, so every bullet traces to all of them

verification.evidence: compilers/python/runar_compiler/frontend/parser_go.py:1450-1453: `_parse_bitwise_and` calls `_parse_equality()` for its operands (the C-precedence ladder, where `&` binds LOOSER than `==`), so `x&255 == 15` parses as `x & (255 == 15)`. Real Go (`go/parser`, and the project's Go tier reference) gives `&` the SAME precedence as multiplicative operators — strictly TIGHTER than `==` — so Go parses it as `(x&255) == 15`. Reproduced by direct code-path reading; no fixing commit found (`git log --grep` for CL-BUG-208..213 / precedence turns up nothing on this file).
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate; cited `:1397-1455` drifted to `:1419-1457` in current HEAD (file grew ~22 lines upstream) but the exact same ladder shape is confirmed.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile `x & 255 == 15` (as a Go-DSL .runar.go condition) through parser_go.py and assert the resulting AST is `BinaryExpr(&, x, BinaryExpr(==, 255, 15))`... i.e. that it does NOT equal the Go-precedence tree `BinaryExpr(==, BinaryExpr(&, x, 255), 15)` — cross-check against compilers/go's own parser output for the same source to prove divergence.

sweep1.evidence: Probe: Prec.runar.go with `runar.Assert(x&255 == 15)`. Python tier fails with 'right operand of '&' must be bigint or ByteString, got 'boolean'', which means it parsed x & (255==15). Go reference asm is `<ff00> OP_AND OP_15 OP_NUMEQUAL`, i.e. (x&255)==15. parser_go.py still has the C ladder (_parse_bitwise_or -> xor -> and -> _parse_equality, ~l.1471-1498). TS shows the same diagnostic.

items.title: Ruby: the EC alias resolver tests the wrong ANF kind (`load_param` instead of `load_const`+`@ref:`), so rules 7-11 silently no-op
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-274] same alias defect as Python's, independently found (CL-BUG-274).

**Remediation is the same three-line change in each tier**: return the value alongside the name and
splice a real binding into the body immediately before the rewritten one — or adopt the Java signature
(`freshConstName(value, vm, prelude)`) wholesale, since it is already written and correct.

**Method note.** This is what the no-extrapolation rule buys. Two workers found the same defect in two
tiers without either assuming it transferred; the dispatcher's sweep then established the true
denominator as **3 of 7, not 1, not 7.** Guessing either way would have been wrong.

---

...
## CL-BUG-274 — MEDIUM / P2 — The EC alias resolver tests the wrong ANF kind, so rules 7–11 silently no-op
`anf_optimize.rb:297,349` test `val.kind == "load_param"`, but ANF aliases are `load_const` with
`const_string = "@ref:…"` — emitted by `anf_lower.rb:1146` **and by this module's own `make_ref` at
`:364-369`.** So the `while changed` fixpoint at `:149-166` **cannot compose rules**:
`const a = ecMul(p,3n); const b = ecMul(a,5n)` → rule 9 never fires. **Same defect as Python's,
independently found.** And `anf_optimize.rb:136,152` are `body.any?`/`.each` — top level only — so an
`ecMul(x, 1n)` at top level is eliminated while the identical call inside an `if` survives.

verification.evidence: Executed reproduction (not just code reading): compiling `const a: Point = ecMul(this.p, 3n); const b: Point = ecMul(a, 5n);` through the Ruby frontend to optimize_ec shows ANF lowering binds `a` to `load_const(const_string: "@ref:t2")` pointing at the real call `t2 = ecMul(t0, 3)` — anf_lower.rb wraps EVERY `const x = expr` declaration in this alias indirection, not just property refs. anf_optimize.rb Rule 9 (:397-406) then calls resolve(args[0]='a', vm), which returns that @ref: load_const (kind=load_const), not the underlying call, so `inner.kind == "call"` is false and Rule 9 does not fire; the optimized output still contains two separate ecMul calls (t2 and t4) instead of one folded call.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate and reproduced by execution. R-263's comment (anf_optimize.rb:311-323) investigated a related dead branch in resolve()/canonical() and concluded — correctly, for that narrower claim — that TS's resolveArg is also a plain map lookup with no alias chase; but that conclusion doesn't refute this finding, since anf_lower wraps every const-binding in an @ref: alias, so a plain lookup genuinely fails to see through it for exactly the composition case CL-BUG-274 describes.

items.testable_assertion_verified: For ANF `t2=ecMul(t0,3); a=@ref:t2; t4=ecMul(a,5); b=@ref:t4`, ANFOptimize.optimize_ec should fold t4 into ecMul(t0, 15 mod N) via Rule 9. It currently does not — verified by direct execution.

sweep1.evidence: Ruby emit-IR for `const a = ecMul(p,3n); const b = ecMul(a,5n)` gives t2=ecMul(t0,t1), a=load_const '@ref:t2', t4=ecMul(a,t3). Compiled hex is 1,701,537 chars, two full ecMul expansions, so Rule 9 does not fold. In anf_optimize.rb, resolve(name, vm) is now just `vm[name]` and canonical returns name: R-263 (79b6909c) deleted the dead load_param chase and deliberately did not follow @ref: aliases. optimize_method and has_ec_calls? are still top-level-only. The TS reference anf-ec.ts resolveArg is also a plain map lookup and produces the same hex length, so a fix here is a cross-tier design decision, not a Ruby-only fix.

items.title: Rust tier's Java frontend has no hex-literal path; `0xFF` is a parse error where five other tiers accept it
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-169] ## CL-BUG-169 — MEDIUM / P2 — The Rust tier's Java frontend has no hex-literal path; `0xFF` is a parse error where five other tiers accept it
Source: impl-rust-frontend NEW-04, proved by execution. `parser_java.rs:359-367` consumes only
`is_ascii_digit()` and `_`, so `0xFF` becomes `Number(0)` then `Ident("xFF")`. Peers that handle it:
`packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/01-parse-java.ts:223-233`,
`compilers/go/frontend/parser_java.go:327-349`,
`compilers/python/runar_compiler/frontend/parser_java.py:403`,
`compilers/zig/src/passes/parse_java.zig:213`,
`compilers/ruby/lib/runar_compiler/frontend/parser_java.rb:1744`.
**A direct hit on invariant #1** — frontend parity across all seven compilers × nine formats, "no
exceptions", enforced by the `--parser-only` matrix. A `.runar.java` fixture with a hex literal
parses in five tiers and fails in Rust. Fails loudly, so a parity/coverage gap rather than a
miscompile — and it means the parser-only matrix has no fixture using a Java hex literal.

verification.evidence: compilers/rust/src/frontend/parser_java.rs:358-374 — the number-literal branch is gated purely on `ch.is_ascii_digit()` and consumes only digits/underscores plus an optional trailing L/l suffix; there is no `0x`/`0X` prefix check anywhere in the tokenizer. `0xFF` therefore still tokenizes as `Number(0)` (the leading '0') immediately followed by `Ident("xFF")` (since 'x' is alphabetic), which is not valid Rúnar-Java statement syntax — matching the finding's claim that Rust's Java frontend has no hex-literal path where five peer tiers (TS, Go, Python, Zig, Ruby, per the cited files) do.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: citation (parser_java.rs:359-367) matches current :358-374 almost exactly (shifted by ~1 line from intervening comment edits); fully accurate, defect unchanged

items.testable_assertion_verified: Parse a `.runar.java` fixture containing `Bigint.of(0xFF)` (or any hex-literal field default) through the Rust tier's Java frontend. Today this is a parse error (`0` then a stray `xFF` identifier); once fixed, the tokenizer must recognise `0x`/`0X`-prefixed hex literals the way parser_java.ts/.go/.py/.zig/.rb already do, and the all-tier parser-only matrix needs a fixture exercising a Java hex literal to catch regressions.

items.title: No nesting-depth bound in the Rust frontend: ~4-6 KB of deeply nested source SIGABRTs the compiler (stack overflow) on 7 of 9 surfaces
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-172] ## CL-BUG-172 — MEDIUM / P2 — No nesting-depth bound: a 4 KB source aborts the compiler with a stack overflow on 7 of 9 surfaces
Source: impl-rust-frontend NEW-07, proved by execution (release build, exit 134 = SIGABRT).
`compilers/rust/src/frontend/input_limits.rs:12` sets `MAX_SOURCE_BYTES = 4 MiB` and its docstring
calls this *the* DoS guard applied "BEFORE the tokenizer touches the input". The recursive-descent
chains have no depth counter. `n=1000` nested parens (2192 bytes) → rc 0; `n=2000` (4192 bytes) →
**SIGABRT**. At ~6 KB the same abort on `.runar.ts`, `.runar.sol`, `.runar.go`, `.runar.move`,
`.runar.rb`, `.runar.java`. `catch_refusal` cannot help — a stack overflow is an abort, not a
catchable unwind.
**The worker declined to rate it higher and said why, correctly:** whether this is a defect depends
on whether the compiler is ever fed untrusted source (a playground, a CI bot, an SDK `compile_check`
on user input), and the project states no frontend threat model. Recorded with the fact at full
strength and the severity bounded: **the module that exists to prevent exactly this does not cover
it**, and the byte bound is three orders of magnitude looser than the real limit.
Zig and the Rust DSL are unmeasured — the worker could not hand-write deep-expression fixtures those
grammars accept, and said so rather than extrapolating.
items.tier_reason: ANF/stack/emit/EC-optimizer boundary and emitted bytes change (§5 floor: mid min, top if bytes move)

verification.evidence: compilers/rust/src/frontend/input_limits.rs:12 still defines only `MAX_SOURCE_BYTES = 4 * 1024 * 1024` (a flat byte-size gate applied before the tokenizer runs); grepping the frontend recursive-descent parsers (parser.rs, parser_gocontract.rs, parser_java.rs, parser_move.rs, parser_python.rs, parser_ruby.rs, parser_sol.rs, parser_zig.rs, parser_rustmacro.rs) for any nesting/recursion-depth counter (nesting_depth, recursion_depth, MAX_NESTING, depth_guard) returns nothing — no depth bound has been added to any of the source-path parsers. The only nesting guard in the tree, `assert_ir_nesting_under_limit` (used at ir/loader.rs:33), gates the separate `--ir` JSON-loading path, not source parsing, so it does not cover the scenario the finding describes. Per HARD RULES this was verified by static reading, not by re-executing the reported SIGABRT.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: citation (input_limits.rs:12) matches HEAD exactly, same line and same constant; defect (no depth bound anywhere in the frontend) is structurally unchanged, though not re-executed in this pass

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile a `.runar.ts` (or `.runar.go`/`.runar.sol`/etc.) source string consisting of ~2000 nested parens (~4 KB, well under the 4 MiB MAX_SOURCE_BYTES gate) through the Rust tier's recursive-descent expression parser. Today this SIGABRTs (stack overflow, uncatchable by `catch_refusal`); the fix must add an explicit recursion-depth counter to the expression/statement parsers that returns a normal parse-error Diagnostic before the native call stack is exhausted.
