items.title: `.runar.go` reinterprets `& | ^ << >>` against Go's own operator precedence, silently, in a file the real Go toolchain also compiles
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-173] ## CL-BUG-173 — MEDIUM / P2 — `.runar.go` reinterprets `& | ^ << >>` against Go's own precedence, silently, in a file the Go toolchain also compiles
Source: impl-rust-frontend NEW-08 / U2, proved by execution.
Every non-TS Rust parser implements the C/TypeScript ladder. Go's own spec puts `* / % << >> & &^`
at the highest binary level and `+ - | ^` one below — so `&`, `<<`, `>>` bind **tighter** than `+`,
and `|`, `^` bind at the **same** level. `.runar.go` files are compiled twice, by Rúnar into Script
and by the real Go toolchain for the native tests CLAUDE.md prescribes, and for mixed
bitwise/arithmetic expressions the two disagree:

| source | Rúnar reading | Go reading |
|---|---|---|
| `runar.Assert((a & 3 + 1) == 0)` | `a & 4` | `(a & 3) + 1` |
| `runar.Assert((a << 1 + 2) == 0)` | `a << 3` | `(a << 1) + 2` |

items.description: [CX-BUG-092] Array-literal inference inspects only the first element, so `[sig, 1n]` is classified as `Sig[]` and can pass `checkMultiSig`’s standard subtype check. Stack lowering then includes every element in the actual `OP_CHECKMULTISIG` argument sequence. This permits malformed signer arrays to compile, usually producing an opaque runtime failure.

The checkMultiSig special case at :1638-1649 only special-cases arity (must be 2 args); its own comment (:1632-1634) says arg-type validation 'falls through to the standard subtype check below,' which calls infer_expr_type on the whole array-literal argument and gets back 'Sig[]' regardless of the second element's real type. The cited '2026-04-30 audit finding F5' comment addresses arity/subtype-check coverage, not per-element ArrayLiteral inference, so the heterogeneous literal still type-checks and compiles.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: accurate -- citations hold; the 'F5' comment's claim of closing the gap is itself the pitfall, since it fixed arity/subtype coverage but not per-element array-literal inference

sweep1.evidence: checkMultiSig([sig, 1n], [this.pk, this.pk]) probe: rust -> `Compilation error: Multi.runar.ts:1: Array element type mismatch: expected 'Sig', got 'bigint'` rc=1 (go gives the same error). Check is at compilers/rust/src/frontend/typecheck.rs:962.
sweep1.refuter: Only partly fixed. The bigint shape the testable assertion names is gone. At 3b5e7aad, Rust (typecheck.rs:949-967, from F-063) now type-checks every element of an array literal. My probes match: [sig, 1n], [sig, n:bigint], [sig, sig2, 1n] and a pubkey array [this.pk, 1n] are all rejected with 'Array element type mismatch', and [1n, sig] is rejected too. TS and Go give the same errors. Heterogeneous signer arrays still compile in the ByteString family, though. checkMultiSig([sig, this.pk], [this.pk, this.pk2]) (a PubKey in the signer array) and checkMultiSig([sig, b:ByteString], ...) both compile in Rust, giving hex 537a00000000547a547a52557a557a52ae777777 and 537a7b000000547a547a52557a557a52ae7777. The cause is that the element check uses is_subtype, which treats any two ByteString-family types as compatible (typecheck.rs:303-305). checkMultiSig then falls through to that same loose check (around :1680-1720). Rust's own checkSig special case (:1506-1534) enforces Sig exactly and rejects checkSig(this.pk, this.pk) with 'expected Sig, got PubKey', so Rust is inconsistent with itself: a PubKey is refused as a single signature but accepted inside a signer array. TS and Go also accept [sig, this.pk] and [sig, b]; TS accepts checkSig(pk, pk) too. items.title: Interpreter `checkSig` returns `false` where the script ABORTS; branching contracts diverge in the accepting direction
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-097] ## CL-BUG-097 — MEDIUM / P1 — Interpreter `checkSig` returns `false` where the script ABORTS; branching contracts diverge in the accepting direction
**Dispatcher-verified.** Source: pkg-testing depth NF-003.

`checkSig` lowers to a bare opcode with no encoding gate — `05-stack-lower.ts:94`: `checkSig: ['OP_CHECKSIG']`. On chain, `Spend`'s `checkSignatureEncoding` **aborts the entire script** on a malformed signature. The interpreter instead returns a boolean (`interpreter.ts:856-861`), because `verifyTestMessageSig` wraps everything in `catch { return false }` (`crypto/ecdsa.ts:86-88`).

For `assert(checkSig(...))` the two verdicts coincide, which is why this survived. For `if (checkSig(a,b)) {...} else {...}` — or `checkSig(a,b) || checkSig(c,d)`, the natural escrow/multi-path shape — the interpreter takes the alternate arm and can **accept a spend the chain aborts on**. The divergence is in the dangerous direction.

Two further divergences of the same shape found in the same pass, both interpreter-accepts / script-aborts:
- **CL-BUG-098** `merkleRootSha256`/`merkleRootHash256`: the interpreter uses `proof.subarray(i*32, (i+1)*32)`, which **clamps**, where the script's `OP_SPLIT` **aborts** on a short proof. This is exactly the NEW-010 bug class that `checkSplitIndex` was introduced to close for `substr`/`left`/`right`/`split` — it was never applied to the Merkle builtins.
- **CL-BUG-099** `blake3Hash`: the interpreter truncates a >64-byte message and returns a digest; the script computes `64 - OP_SIZE(msg)`, which is negative, and `OP_NUM2BIN` aborts.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-testing/src/crypto/ecdsa.ts:77-89 verifyTestMessageSig still wraps parse+verify in try/catch and returns false on any failure (including malformed DER encoding); packages/runar-testing/src/interpreter/interpreter.ts:1004-1008 checkSig case still returns that boolean verbatim; packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/05-stack-lower.ts:170 still maps checkSig to a bare 'OP_CHECKSIG' with no encoding gate. Real OP_CHECKSIG aborts the whole script on malformed signature encoding; the interpreter instead answers false and lets execution continue into the other arm of an if/else or ||, which is the accepting-direction divergence described.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate — cited files/lines still describe the exact mechanism (line numbers drifted slightly but the code shapes match).

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile `assert(checkSig(sigA, pubA) || checkSig(sigB, pubB))` with sigA a syntactically-malformed DER signature (e.g. wrong length byte) and sigB a valid signature. Run via TestContract: expect success=true (checkSig(sigA,..) returns false, checkSig(sigB,..) returns true). Run the compiled script via ScriptVM with the same inputs: the first OP_CHECKSIG's encoding check aborts the whole script before OP_BOOLOR ever evaluates the second checkSig, so ScriptVM must fail. Assert the two disagree.

sweep1.evidence: packages/runar-testing/src/crypto/ecdsa.ts verifyTestMessageSig: `try { ... if (!sig) return false; ... } catch { return false; }`, and interpreter.ts:1009 returns that boolean. Probe via TestContract on `if (checkSig(sig,this.pk)) { assert(false) } else { assert(true) }` with sig='30ff' (malformed DER) -> {"success":true}. The interpreter takes the else arm where on-chain OP_CHECKSIG strict-encoding would abort.

items.title: Zig CLI rejects source files above 1 MiB via a hardcoded `readFileAlloc` limit, despite the shared `input_limits.zig` / library API documenting and allowing 4 MiB

items.description: [CX-BUG-127] The public limit module and library API allow four MiB, but CLI input is read with a one-MiB hard limit before the shared guard runs. Inputs between those sizes therefore behave differently by entry point and surface as a generic file-read failure rather than the typed source-size diagnostic.

remediation.CX-BUG-127: Use the shared constant for the read bound and pass oversized input through one consistent diagnostic path.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-127: The CLI and library API must agree on acceptance/rejection and error type for files at 1 MiB + 1 and 4 MiB + 1.

verification.evidence: compilers/zig/src/main.zig:334 (`compileFromSource`, the CLI's `compile`/`--source` entry point) still hardcodes `.limited(1 * 1024 * 1024)` on the `readFileAlloc` call, while compilers/zig/src/frontend/input_limits.zig:12 defines `MAX_SOURCE_BYTES: usize = 4 * 1024 * 1024` and compiler_api.zig's shared `runPipeline` (Pass 0) enforces that 4 MiB limit via `assertSourceBytesUnderLimit`. A 1-4 MiB file therefore fails to even reach the shared guard from the CLI — it errors out of `readFileAlloc` itself (a generic Zig I/O error, not the typed `SourceSizeExceeded`) — while the same bytes handed to the library API (`compileSource`/`compileSourceWithOptions`, which take an in-memory `source` slice, not a path) would be accepted and correctly evaluated against the 4 MiB limit.

sweep1.evidence: compilers/zig/src/main.zig compileFromSource: `readFileAlloc(io, path, work_allocator, .limited(1 * 1024 * 1024))` while input_limits.zig MAX_SOURCE_BYTES = 4 * 1024 * 1024. The path is `packages/runar-go/slh_dsa.go:51`; content at that line is correct. Typo, not fabrication.

**Worker discipline worth recording.** The addendum states its own limits against its own interest:
*"Treat 'all seven tiers' in NEW-16 as 'five verified, two asserted'"* — it read the Ruby and Go
tables in full, single lines for TS/Java/codegen/Zig, and did not open Rust or Python. It also

## CL-BUG-165 — MEDIUM / P2 — `SLHDSA.verify` accepts trailing garbage: every length guard is a lower bound and the final offset is never compared to the signature length
**Dispatcher-verified.** I read `packages/runar-rb/lib/runar/slh_dsa.rb:755-776`. The three guards
are `sig.bytesize < n`, `< offset + fors_sig_len`, and `< offset + xmss_sig_len` inside the `d.times`

`current_msg == pk_root` (`:776`); `offset` is never compared to `sig.bytesize`. FIPS 20

verification.evidence: packages/runar-rb/lib/runar/slh_dsa.rb:757-775: the `d.times` loop's three guards (`sig.bytesize < n`, `< offset+fors_sig_len`, `< offset+xmss_sig_len`) are all lower bounds; :776 does `current_msg == pk_root` immediately after the loop with no `offset == sig.bytesize` check. packages/runar-go/slh_dsa.go:805-833 (SLHVerify) has the identical shape: the hypertree loop only checks `len(sig) < offset+xmssSigLen`, then falls straight into the pkRoot byte comparison — offset is never compared to len(sig). Trailing bytes appended to an otherwise-valid signature are silently accepted in both tiers.
verification.tier_correction: Ruby is an equal co-owner of this defect (already listed in files/title); no correction needed.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate — line numbers and the lower-bound-only guard pattern match exactly in both tiers.

items.title: A standalone `groth16-wa` UTXO is unsigned and its spend is replayable by any observer
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-083] ## CL-BUG-083 — MEDIUM / P2 — A standalone `groth16-wa` UTXO is unsigned and its spend is replayable by any observer
**Dispatcher-verified verbatim.** Source: crypto:bn254-groth16 F8.

`packages/runar-go/sdk_groth16.go:179` — `_ = signer // intentionally unused: Groth16 WA spends do not sign`; `:347` — *"The Groth16 WA verifier has no signature check in its locking script — the unlock is pure witness data — so the returned transaction is already fully formed and ready to broadcast."*

The locking script emits no `OP_CHECKSIG` and no preimage binding. Once the spend reaches the mempool the ~700 KB witness is public and replayable into a transaction paying anyone — fund loss by front-running for anyone deploying the standalone verifier with real satoshis. The Mode-3 stateful path is unaffected (it carries `checkPreimage`).

verification.evidence: packages/runar-go/sdk_groth16.go:179 `_ = signer // intentionally unused: Groth16 WA spends do not sign`; :347-350 documents 'The Groth16 WA verifier has no signature check in its locking script — the unlock is pure witness data — so the returned transaction is already fully formed and ready to broadcast.' [CL-BUG-178] ## CL-BUG-178 — MEDIUM / P2 — `SigAnalyzer` is defeated by one byte: `OP_CHECKSIG OP_2DROP` passes all three signature checks
Source: sdk-java. `CHECKSIG_RESULT_DROPPED` requires a literal `ops[i+1].opcode == OP_DROP`
(`SigAnalyzer.java:23-33`, which I read); `NO_SIG_CHECK` is suppressed by the mere presence of
`0xac` (`PathAnalyzer.java:337-351`); and `UNCONDITIONALLY_SUCCEEDS` is suppressed because
`OP_CHECKSIG ∈ VERIFY_OPS` (`PathAnalyzer.java:360`). Substituting `OP_2DROP` for `OP_DROP` evades
all three at once — a script that discards its signature result verifies clean.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-java/src/main/java/runar/lang/analyzer/SigAnalyzer.java:23-26 `CHECKSIG_RESULT_DROPPED` requires the literal next opcode to be `OP_DROP`. packages/runar-java/src/main/java/runar/lang/analyzer/PathAnalyzer.java:346-350 `hasCheckSig` fires on mere presence of `OP_CHECKSIG`/`OP_CHECKMULTISIG` anywhere in the path (suppressing `NO_SIG_CHECK`), and :353-363 `VERIFY_OPS` includes `OP_CHECKSIG`/`OP_CHECKMULTISIG` themselves, which the code around :369 uses to suppress `UNCONDITIONALLY_SUCCEEDS`. items.description:
[CL-BUG-180] ## CL-BUG-180 — MEDIUM / P2 — Two Java-only analyzer divergences against a byte-identical-JSON contract
Source: sdk-java, both relayed with citations I did not re-read.
- **Truncated PUSHDATA header:** `ScriptParser.java:69-73/96-100/121-125` return before reaching the
  `INEFFICIENT_PUSH` block; TS (`packages/runar-testing/src/analyzer/script-parser.ts:124-135` +
  `opcode-concerns.ts:48-59`) and Python emit a finding. Java is the outlier.
- **Ordering:** `INEFFICIENT_PUSH` is computed pre-collapse (`Analyzer.java:38-40`) and appended
  unconditionally (`:61-66`), where TS (`index.ts:107-110,127`) and Python run opcode-concern
  analysis on the *collapsed* list — so Java reports findings at offsets that no longer exist inside
  a `raw_script` span.

verification.evidence: Truncated-header divergence: packages/runar-java/src/main/java/runar/lang/analyzer/ScriptParser.java:66-72 (OP_PUSHDATA1 header itself truncated, `i + 1 >= byteLen`) returns immediately with no `INEFFICIENT_PUSH` finding, and packages/runar-java/src/main/java/runar/lang/analyzer/OpcodeConcerns.java:1-30 has NO INEFFICIENT_PUSH logic at all (only LARGE_SCRIPT/CODESEPARATOR_PRESENT) — in Java that finding lives inline in ScriptParser instead. TS's equivalent (packages/runar-testing/src/analyzer/script-parser.ts:123-134, header-truncated case) also breaks immediately but stamps `dataLength: 0` on the synthetic op, and packages/runar-testing/src/analyzer/opcode-concerns.ts:47-53 checks `dataLength !== undefined` (0 qualifies) and DOES emit `INEFFICIENT_PUSH` for it — Java is the outlier, confirmed. Ordering divergence: packages/runar-java/src/main/java/runar/lang/analyzer/Analyzer.java:38-39 parses and captures `parserFindings` BEFORE `collapseRawScriptSpans` runs (:42-44), then appends them unconditionally after `OpcodeConcerns.analyze` at :60-65 — so parser-emitted push findings carry pre-collapse offsets into a post-collapse findings list, unlike TS/Python which run opcode-concern analysis on the already-collapsed list.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Exact on the ordering claim; the truncated-header PUSHDATA1 claim is exact but I traced through *why* (Java's OpcodeConcerns.java has no INEFFICIENT_PUSH logic at all — it lives in the parser — whereas TS computes it in a separate opcode-concerns pass over the parsed op list, which is why the same 'header truncated, dataLength defaults to 0' case behaves differently in the two tiers).

items.testable_assertion_verified: Analyze a script whose final bytes are a bare `OP_PUSHDATA1` opcode with no length byte following (truncated header) embedded inside a `rawScriptSpans` region. Assert Java's finding list matches TS's for this input (an `INEFFICIENT_PUSH`-equivalent finding, or an explicit documented divergence) and that offsets in the parser-sourced findings correspond to the COLLAPSED op list's addressing, not the pre-collapse one. Today Java diverges on both counts.

sweep1.evidence: Truncated PUSHDATA1 `514c`: TS dist analyzeScript -> [UNCONDITIONALLY_SUCCEEDS, NO_SIG_CHECK, INEFFICIENT_PUSH@1], Java Analyzer.analyzeScript -> no INEFFICIENT_PUSH. Collapse ordering, `4c010151` with rawScriptSpan(offset 0, length 3): TS -> no INEFFICIENT_PUSH, Java -> INEFFICIENT_PUSH@0. Java Analyzer.java still does `all.addAll(parserFindings)` (pre-collapse parser findings) unconditionally after collapseRawScriptSpans.

[CL-BUG-125] ## CL-BUG-125 — MEDIUM / P2 — Python SDK: `_read_script_element` raises bare `ValueError` and silently truncates on provider-supplied scripts
**Source:** sdk-python depth NEW-03. **Dispatcher-verified.**
`script_utils.py:23` is `int(hex_str[offset:offset + 2], 16)` — when `offset >= len(hex_str)` the
slice is `''` and this raises an uncaught `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 16: ''`.
`from_txid(artifact, txid, vout, provider)` pointed at any output that is not this artifact crashes
here rather than returning a typed rejection; `matches_artifact` exists and is never called first.
The payload slices at `:29`/`:33` carry **no bounds check**, so a push running off the end yields a
silently short `data_hex` that `_interpret_script_element` hands back as a "recovered constructor
arg". `OP_PUSHDATA4` accepts a length up to 0xFFFFFFFF and folds it into `cumulative_shift`, so one
crafted push corrupts every later slot offset. **The correct pattern is two files away**:
`ordinals._read_push_data` (`ordinals.py:108-125`) bounds-checks and returns `None`.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-py/runar/sdk/script_utils.py:22 (`_read_script_element`) still `int(hex_str[offset:offset+2], 16)` uncaught — raises bare ValueError when offset is past the end. Payload slices at :29/:33/:37 still have no bounds check (Python silently short-slices past end-of-string). `matches_artifact` (script_utils.py:218) is defined but grep shows contract.py never calls it, confirming 'never called first' still holds — from_txid/from_utxo build a UTXO from provider data without first validating the script against the artifact.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate; script_utils.py:23 (finding) vs :22 (HEAD) is a one-line drift from an unrelated edit, mechanism unchanged.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Call extract_constructor_args (script_utils.py) against a script_hex with a push opcode whose declared length runs past the buffer end (adversarial/malformed provider-supplied script); today `_read_script_element` either raises an uncaught bare ValueError or silently returns a truncated data_hex with no error. sweep1.evidence: packages/runar-py/runar/sdk/script_utils.py _read_script_element is unchanged. verification.evidence: packages/runar-rb/lib/runar/ecdsa.rb:188-237 (parse_der_signature_bytes): the top-level length check only enforces bytes.length == declared_len+2 (or +3 with a stripped trailing sighash byte, :193-201); after parsing r and s the function never checks that the post-parse cursor idx equals bytes.length, so if r_len+s_len leave unconsumed bytes inside that declared total, they are silently dropped rather than rejected. verification.reviewer_accuracy: No files were cited in the input item; verified location and mechanism directly against HEAD.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Construct a DER signature whose outer SEQUENCE length includes N extra trailing bytes beyond r+s's actual encoded length (while keeping the top-level total-length check satisfied); parse_der_signature_bytes must reject it but today returns [r,s] identical to the un-padded signature. Separately: encode r or s with a leading byte >= 0x80 and no 0x00 prefix; parse_der_signature_bytes must reject it but today parses it to the same integer as the canonical 0x00-prefixed form.

sweep1.evidence: Ruby probe of Runar::ECDSA.parse_der_signature_bytes: canonical [30 06 02 01 01 02 01 02] -> [1,2]. So a Point whose x or y is >= EC_P but whose value mod EC_P happens to satisfy the curve equation returns true here while the compiled script's explicit range checks would reject it.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: No files were cited in the input item; verified location and mechanism directly against HEAD.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Construct a Point (x,y) where x = EC_P + x0 for a genuine curve point (x0,y0) (so x >= EC_P but x % EC_P == x0 keeps the curve equation satisfied), encode it, and call ec_on_curve: it returns true today; it must return false to match the on-chain range-checked script.

sweep1.evidence: Ruby probe: x0=1 is on the curve. A point with x = EC_P + 1 and the same y gives Runar::EC.ec_on_curve -> true. lib/runar/ec.rb ec_on_curve only computes `(y*y)%EC_P == (x*x*x+7)%EC_P`, and decode_point does no range check, even though the comment says the script checks x < p AND y < p.

items.title: Ruby's `truncate_div` routes through a Float, losing precision above 2^53 and raising `FloatDomainError` above `Float::MAX`
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-162] ## CL-BUG-162 — MEDIUM / P2 — Ruby's `truncate_div` routes through a Float, losing precision above 2^53 and raising `FloatDomainError` above `Float::MAX`
Source: sdk-ruby NEW-13. The helper written to *fix* the floor-vs-truncate divergence (CL-BUG-127)
introduces a precision bug of its own. Bitcoin script numbers routinely exceed 2^53 — every
`bigint` state field is 8 bytes — so this is inside the normal domain, not an edge case.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-rb/lib/runar/sdk/anf_interpreter.rb:811-817 (truncate_div): when signs of a,b differ and a%b != 0, routes through (a.to_f / b).truncate — a 64-bit Float division. Reproduced directly (`ruby -e`): truncate_div(-(2**60)-3, 7) returns -164703072086692416 vs the exact truncated value -164703072086692425 (off by 9), confirming precision loss above 2^53. Bitcoin Script bigint state fields are 8 bytes (up to ~2^63), squarely inside this domain.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: No files were cited in the input item; verified location and mechanism directly against HEAD, including a live reproduction of the precision loss.

items.testable_assertion_verified: truncate_div(-(2**60)-3, 7) must equal -164703072086692425 (exact truncation toward zero); today it returns -164703072086692416 due to Float rounding. A value near Float::MAX with an opposite-sign divisor must not raise FloatDomainError.

sweep1.evidence: lib/runar/sdk/anf_interpreter.rb truncate_div still uses `(a.to_f / b).truncate`. Probe: ANFInterpreter.truncate_div(-(2**60)-3, 7) = -164703072086692416 (expected -164703072086692425). truncate_div(-(2**1100), 3) -> FloatDomainError -Infinity.

[CL-BUG-139] ## CL-BUG-139 — MEDIUM / P3 — Generated wrappers pass intent-intrinsic witness params as call args, which `prepareCall` rejects by arity
Source: sdk-ts NEW-09. `codegen/common.ts:86-87` claims `getSdkArgParams` *"matches the SDK's
`userParams` filtering in `call()`/`prepareCall()`"*. It does not: the SDK drops
`_prevOutScript_<i>` and `_serialisedOutputs` (`contract.ts:828-839`), the codegen does not. Any
method using `extractPrevOutputScript` or `requireOutputP2PKH` gets a wrapper building an args array
too long, and `contract.ts:841-845` throws. Fails loudly, which caps severity, but those wrappers
are unusable. `multi-contract.ts:196-202` independently defines `isWitnessParam`, confirming the
category is first-class and the codegen ignores it.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-sdk/src/codegen/common.ts:89-92 (getSdkArgParams, HEAD): filters only SigHashPreimage/_changePKH/_changeAmount/_newAmount for stateful methods, no filter for `_prevOutScript_<i>` or `_serialisedOutputs`. packages/runar-sdk/src/contract.ts:931-944 (prepareCall's real `userParams`, HEAD): additionally strips both witness-param shapes via `isAutoInjectedWitnessParam`, for BOTH stateful and stateless methods, then throws at :946-949 if `userParams.length !== args.length`. So a generated wrapper for a method using extractPrevOutputScript/requireOutputP2PKH builds an args array longer than prepareCall expects and every call throws. multi-contract.ts:117-118 independently defines the identical `isWitnessParam` predicate, confirming codegen/common.ts's comment claiming parity with the SDK's filtering is simply wrong.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Generate a TS wrapper (packages/runar-sdk/src/codegen/gen-all.ts) for a method using extractPrevOutputScript/requireOutputP2PKH and call it with the codegen-documented arg list; RunarContract.prepareCall must accept the call. Today it throws 'expects N args, got N+k' because getSdkArgParams (codegen/common.ts:89-92) does not filter _prevOutScript_<i>/_serialisedOutputs the way prepareCall's own userParams filter (contract.ts:931-944) does.

sweep1.evidence: Probe (node, built dist): compiled examples/ts/intent-prev-output-script; ABI bind params = _changePKH,_changeAmount,_newAmount,txPreimage:SigHashPreimage,_prevOutScript_0:ByteString. codegen getSdkArgParams(...) returns ['_prevOutScript_0'] (1 arg), while prepareCall's userParams filter (contract.ts ~1003-1014, isAutoInjectedWitnessParam) yields 0, so the generated wrapper hits 'expects 0 args, got 1'. codegen/common.ts:89-93 getSdkArgParams still filters only SigHashPreimage/_changePKH/_changeAmount/_newAmount; no _prevOutScript_/_serialisedOutputs filter anywhere in packages/runar-sdk/src/codegen.

[CL-BUG-138] ## CL-BUG-138 — MEDIUM / P2 — `runar-sdk/codegen` is a published entry point whose Mustache templates are not in the published package
Source: sdk-ts NEW-08. `package.json` ships `"files": ["dist"]` and advertises
`"./codegen"` as an export, but `codegen/gen-all.ts:28-33` resolves templates via
`path.resolve(thisDir, '../../../../codegen/templates')` — four levels above
`node_modules/runar-sdk/dist/codegen` is the *consumer's* project root. The templates live at the
monorepo root, outside the package, so there is no packaged copy: `fs.readFileSync` throws `ENOENT`.

...
  the templates are found in-repo. Survives only as the packaging defect CL-BUG-138.
- **BUG-TS-05's impact is bounded by a default-on gate.** `assembleMultiContractCall` runs
  `dryRunMultiContractInput` on every input by default and throws before returning; the failure mode
  is a loud local rejection, not a broadcast invalid transaction.
- **GAP-TS-08 over-counts.** Three push-data encoders in `packages/runar-sdk/src`, not four, and the
  ordinals one sits inside a never-executed `OP_FALSE OP_IF … OP_ENDIF` envelope.
- **BUG-TS-14's practical impact via change scripts is nil.** `buildP2PKHScript` accepts a 40-char
  hex PKH as its first branch, so the change scripts are correct; the contract violation bites only
  where the string is used as an address (`provider.getUtxos`).
- **`dryRunMultiContractInput` is NOT a NEW-005 aliasing regression** — the transaction is freshly
  parsed inside the function, so the script objects are private to that invocation.

---

items.title: `finalizeCall` broadcasts a 72-byte all-zero placeholder when a declared `sigIndices` slot is left unfilled
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-136] ## CL-BUG-136 — MEDIUM / P2 — `finalizeCall` broadcasts a 72-byte all-zero placeholder when a declared `sigIndices` slot is left unfilled
Source: sdk-ts NEW-05. `contract.ts:1739-1743` substitutes only the indices present in `signatures`;
a missing one keeps the 72-zero-byte placeholder from `:874`, which `encodeArg` turns into a
well-formed `48 <72 bytes>` push. Nothing between `:1743` and the broadcast at `:1804` asserts that
`Object.keys(signatures)` covers `prepared.sigIndices`, and `dryRun` defaults OFF (`:1707`). A
2-of-3 multi-signer flow therefore builds, signs the funding inputs and broadcasts a transaction the
network rejects. No fund loss, but the one-shot consume guard at `:1727-1733` has already marked the
`PreparedCall` spent, so the caller must rebuild.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-sdk/src/contract.ts:1825-1908 (finalizeCall, HEAD): :1846-1850 only overwrites `resolvedArgs[idx]` for indices present in `signatures`; a missing sigIndex keeps the 72-zero-byte placeholder established during prepareCall (matches the `'00'.repeat(72)` placeholder pattern at :981). Nothing between assembling resolvedArgs (:1845) and the broadcast (:1911) asserts `Object.keys(signatures)` covers every `prepared.sigIndices` entry. The pre-broadcast dry-run only runs `if (prepared._dryRun)` (:1896), which is opt-in per CallOptions.dryRun, off by default. The one-shot consume guard at :1834-1840 marks the PreparedCall spent before any of this, so a caller who omits a signature still gets a broadcast attempt and must rebuild from scratch on rejection.

items.testable_assertion_verified: prepareCall a 2-of-3 multi-signer method, call finalizeCall with a `signatures` map missing one declared sigIndices entry, and no dryRun option. It must throw/refuse rather than broadcast. Today contract.ts:1846-1850 silently leaves the unfilled index at its 72-zero-byte placeholder and proceeds straight to provider.broadcast(finalTx) at :1911.

sweep1.evidence: contract.ts finalizeCall (line ~1915): `for (const idx of prepared.sigIndices) { if (signatures[idx] !== undefined) resolvedArgs[idx] = signatures[idx]; }` — no check that every sigIndices slot is filled; the only pre-broadcast guard is `if (prepared._dryRun)` (opt-in), then broadcast. Missing slot keeps the 72-zero-byte placeholder.

items.title: Go: `lowerBindings` panics on an empty public-method body
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-045] | worker | CL ID | sev | prio | title |
| F15 | CL-BUG-045 | LOW | post-v1 | Go: lowerBindings panics on an empty public-method body |
items.tier_reason: ANF/stack/emit/EC-optimizer boundary (§5 floor: mid min, top if bytes move)

verification.evidence: compilers/go/codegen/stack.go:1313-1344 lowerBindings: when terminalAssert=true (i.e. method.IsPublic), line 1333 unconditionally executes `lastBinding := bindings[len(bindings)-1]` BEFORE any length check — indexes bindings[-1] and panics (index out of range) if bindings is empty. Call sites at stack.go:6004 and 6045 (`ctx.lowerBindings(method.Body, method.IsPublic)`) have no empty-body guard before this call. validator.go only rejects an empty CONSTRUCTOR body (line 298: `if len(ctor.Body) == 0`); no equivalent rule exists for an ordinary method, so a stateless SmartContract public method with a syntactically empty body (`public foo(): void {}`) reaches stack.go:1333 with bindings=[] and panics. Note on blast radius: `CompileFromSourceStrWithResult` (compiler.go:850-859) wraps stack lowering in `defer recover()`, turning this into a diagnostic, not a crash — but `CompileFromProgram` (the `--ir` entry point, compiler.go:282-286) has NO such recover wrapper around `codegen.LowerToStack`, so hand-crafted --ir JSON with an empty public method body crashes the process outright.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Ledger row gave no file citation; independently located the exact panic site and confirmed the title's claim is accurate, and found the --ir path is unrecovered (worse than a source-only concern).

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile (a) a stateless SmartContract source with a public method whose body is empty, and (b) equivalent hand-written --ir JSON with an empty public-method `body: []`; both must return a clean 'method must have at least one statement' diagnostic, not an index-out-of-range panic (case (b) currently crashes the process since CompileFromProgram has no recover wrapper).

Source: impl-python-codegen NEW-17. Sites: `stack.py:1319-1320` (non-primitive property

(`_lower_load_const` fallback) and **`:1622-1627`** (`_lower_call`: an unrecognised function name
pops every argument off the stack map and pushes a literal zero). The last is the dangerous one —
an ANF `call` naming a function absent from `BUILTIN_OPCODES` compiles cleanly to a silently wrong
program. Reachable only via `compile_from_ir`, which skips typecheck (CL-GAP-113).

- **REFUTED as a Python defect: `emit_raw_bytes` dropping a zero-length raw span.**
  `compilers/go/codegen/emit.go:281-284` does the same, and the emitted bytes are empty either way —
  the defect, if any, is in accepting an ANF `raw_script` with empty bytes and non-zero arity.
- **REFUTED: "`sqrt` is wrong above ~2^32."** Far too generous and wrong about the failure mode.
  Smallest wrong input is n = 8; magnitude limit ~2²⁶. See the CL-BUG-114 sharpening above.
- **The no-extrapolation rule, applied by the worker against its own interest.** It set out to find
  Python-specific divergences and reports that of the seed's list, **exactly one** is Python-only
  (CL-BUG-147, the mutable op cache). `OP_NEGATE OP_NEGATE`, `_codePart`, `bn254G1OnCurve`
  canonicity, the WOTS+ length gate, `sqrt`, SLH-DSA `a=8` and the `merkle.py` rot-triple are all
  present identically in at least the Go tier, with citations given per finding. **That distinction
  is load-bearing for remediation: a single-tier fix to any of them breaks the hex-parity invariant.**

items.title: Python's `_lower_loop` does not set `current_source_loc` per unrolled binding
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-152] ## CL-BUG-152 — LOW / P4 — Python's `_lower_loop` does not set `current_source_loc` per unrolled binding
Source: impl-python-codegen NEW-13. `stack.py:2432-2433` iterates the loop body without setting
`current_source_loc`, unlike every other binding-iteration site (`_lower_bindings_protected` sets it
at `:1158-1160`). All opcodes emitted from a loop body collapse to the enclosing loop binding's
source position.
items.tier_reason: ANF/stack/emit/EC-optimizer boundary and emitted bytes change (§5 floor: mid min, top if bytes move)

verification.evidence: `_lower_loop` (stack.py:2519-2598) iterates the unrolled body with `for j, binding in enumerate(body): self._lower_binding(binding, j, last_uses)` (line ~2598) and never sets `self.current_source_loc`. Contrast `_lower_bindings_protected` (stack.py:1244-1255), which does `self.current_source_loc = binding.source_loc` before each binding and resets it after. `current_source_loc` is only ever set at stack.py:1228 and :1253 -- neither inside `_lower_loop`. So every opcode emitted from inside a loop body keeps whatever `current_source_loc` was set to by the enclosing (non-loop) binding iteration, i.e. the loop binding's own source position.

sweep1.evidence: compilers/python/runar_compiler/codegen/stack.py _lower_loop (~2744-2777): `for j, binding in enumerate(body): self._lower_binding(binding, j, last_uses)` with no current_source_loc assignment (only set at :1370/:1395 in the top-level binding loops). Probe: Python compile of a for-loop contract (`s = s + y` on line 8): sourceMap maps opcodes 1-20 all to line 7 (the loop), none to line 8. Note: the Python frontend also emits no sourceLoc on loop-body bindings (emit-ir shows sourceLoc None for t1/t2/s), so a fix needs both.

items.title: Two missed compile-time rejections in the Rust frontend: ByteString property initializers skip hex validation, and substr accepts a negative literal start
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-175] # PASS C BATCH 2R WAVE 1 — impl-rust-frontend (CL-BUG-166 … CL-BUG-175)

**Verified.** 6 citation spot-checks, all resolved exactly. Report at
`workers-depth/impl-rust-frontend-depth.md`. **This worker built and ran both the Rust and Go
compilers** (copies under `mktemp -d`, `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` and `GOCACHE` inside `/tmp`, worktree
unmodified), so most of its findings are proved by execution rather than by reading. That is within
the brief's allowance and it is why this is the strongest report of the wave.

**It also caught my seed bug** — see `coverage-ledger.md`. Its refutation duty is undischarged for 25
of 31 breadth findings and is re-queued against the repaired seed.

...
## CL-BUG-175 — LOW / P3 — Two missed compile-time rejections in the Rust frontend
Source: impl-rust-frontend NEW-10 and NEW-11, both proved by execution.
- `ByteString` **property initializers** skip the hex validator: `validator.rs:100-120` checks only
  "is this a literal?" and never calls `validate_expression`, so `readonly k: ByteString = 'zzz'`
  surfaces two passes later as `stack lowering: invalid hex string length: 3` with no source
  location — where the same literal in a method body gives the good message.
- `substr` with a **negative literal start** compiles: `assert(substr(a, -5n, 3n) === a)` emits
  `<85>` (minimal encoding of −5) into `OP_SPLIT`, which aborts at runtime. No literal-range
  constraint in `typecheck.rs:74` or the validator.
dedup_uncertain: yes: this one CL ID actually names two independent defects (ByteString initializer hex validation skip vs. substr negative-start literal). Not split here because nothing else in this batch matches either half; flagging in case a match surfaces in another batch.

verification.evidence: compilers/rust/src/frontend/validator.rs:100-118 validate_properties calls only is_literal_expression(init) for a ByteString initializer, never validate_expression, so the hex-format check at :1508-1520 (odd-length / non-hex) never runs on property initializers -- 'readonly k: ByteString = "zzz"' passes this pass and only fails two passes later in stack lowering with no source location. No literal-range constraint exists anywhere for substr's start parameter (typecheck.rs:96 FuncSig, validator.rs) -- a negative literal start still type-checks and compiles to a raw OP_SPLIT argument that aborts at runtime.

verification.evidence: compilers/rust/src/ir/mod.rs:379-411 `parse_const_value` still falls back to `BigInt::from(f as i128)` (line 395) for any JSON number that doesn't parse as an integer via `BigInt::from_str`, silently saturating/truncating a float constant. verification.evidence: compilers/rust/src/codegen/stack.rs:1671-1673 (`lower_load_const`) still does `if s.len() > 5 && &s[..5] == "@ref:"` / `let ref_name = &s[5..];` on an arbitrary `ConstValue::Str` pulled from a `load_const` value with no ASCII/char-boundary check. `.len()` counts bytes, not chars, so a string whose 5th byte falls inside a multi-byte UTF-8 character (e.g. `"abcdé!"`, where 'é' spans bytes 4-5) panics Rust's byte-slice indexing with 'byte index 5 is not a char boundary'. Nothing in loader.rs restricts a `load_const` string's charset to ASCII, so this is reachable from an external `--ir` file. A second, related unreported site (`hex_to_bytes`, stack.rs:6621-6637, `&hex_str[i..i+2]`) has the identical unchecked-UTF-8-slicing shape, though it is not the site this specific finding names.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate; code is unchanged (line numbers shifted from 1493-1495 at the reviewed commit to 1671-1673 at HEAD due to unrelated file growth, same statement).

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile an IR/source whose `load_const` value is the 7-byte string "abcd\u{e9}!" (byte offset 5 lands mid-character) through `compile_from_ir_str`/`compile_from_source_str` and assert a graceful `Err`, not a panic. Today `lower_load_const`'s `&s[..5]` slice panics with 'byte index 5 is not a char boundary'.

sweep1.evidence: compilers/rust/src/codegen/stack.rs L469, L667, L1825 still have `if s.len() > 5 && &s[..5] == "@ref:"`. Probe: I took the basic-p2pkh IR plus a load_const of "abcdé!" and ran `runar-compiler-rust --ir` -> `Compilation error: stack lowering: end byte index 5 is not a char boundary; it is inside 'é' (bytes 4..6 of string)`. The slice still panics. The panic only becomes an Err because the guarded_pass/catch_refusal boundary (refusal.rs) catches it, and the user sees the raw Rust panic payload rather than a diagnostic. Direct callers of stack lowering outside that guard would see an uncaught panic.

items.title: EC optimizer does not resolve through its own @ref: aliases; unchecked name minting
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-007] | worker | CL ID | sev | prio | title |
| F-013 | CL-BUG-007 | LOW | post-v1 | EC optimizer does not resolve through its own @ref: aliases; unchecked name minting |

verification.evidence: packages/runar-compiler/src/optimizer/anf-ec.ts:75-77 `resolveArg` is a plain `valueMap.get(argName)` with no dereferencing of `@ref:`-prefixed load_const values it or its sibling rules produce (e.g. lines 200/205/160/282 all emit `load_const{value:'@ref:X'}`), so a rule that consumes a previously-rewritten binding sees the alias wrapper, not the value X ultimately points to, and misses chained-optimization opportunities. Separately, lines 184-186/248-250/265-267 mint new binding names as `${binding.name}_k` with no check against existing names in valueMap/newBindings.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate — resolveArg has no @ref: chase, matching the claim.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Construct an ANF program where a first ecAdd(x, INFINITY) rewrite produces `y = @ref:x`, and a subsequent ecAdd(y, ecNegate(x)) should algebraically fold to INFINITY (since y aliases x) but does not, because resolveArg('y', valueMap) returns the load_const{'@ref:x'} wrapper instead of x's actual call value; assert the emitted script is not reduced to the INFINITY constant.

sweep1.evidence: packages/runar-compiler/src/optimizer/anf-ec.ts L75: `function resolveArg(argName, valueMap) { return valueMap.get(argName); }`. It does not follow `@ref:` aliases. The Rule 1 rewrite emits `{kind:'load_const', value:`@ref:${leftArg}`}`, and Rule 8 compares names (`rightVal.args[0] === leftArg`), so with y=@ref:x, ecAdd(y, ecNegate(x)) is not folded to INFINITY. The 'unchecked name minting' half was addressed by F-086 (collectUsedNames), but the alias-resolution defect remains.

[CL-BUG-181] # PASS C BATCH 2R WAVE 1 — sdk-java (CL-BUG-176 … CL-BUG-181)

**Verified, including a full independent reproduction.** Report at `workers-depth/sdk-java-depth.md`.
This worker delegated the analyzer package to a sub-agent and then **re-verified every relayed
citation itself before passing it on**, stating so explicitly — the same duty I owe it. It also
separated what it reproduced from what it relayed: it declined to assert the recomputed depth
figures because it did not model per-path opcode collection, and said so.

**My own reproduction.** I wrote an independent push-skipping walker, parsed the opcode set out of
`Opcodes.java`, and ran it over the fixture goldens. My numbers match the worker's **exactly**:

```
basic-p2pkh        ops=5        untabled={}
auction            ops=1288     untabled={0x8d: 2}
stateful-counter   ops=1351     untabled={0x8d: 2}
schnorr-zkp        ops=262004   untabled={0x8d: 1547, 0x8e: 2, 0xb7: 510}
ec-demo            ops=403869   untabled={0x8d: 2321, 0x8e: 3, 0xb7: 765}
```

...
## CL-BUG-181 — LOW / P3 — Two numeric/text normalisation divergences in the Java analyzer
Source: sdk-java. `jsToFixed1` uses `Math.rint` (half-to-even) where JS `toFixed(1)` rounds ties away
from zero (`OpcodeConcerns.java:38-55`): `(500992/1024).toFixed(1)` is `489.3` in node and `489.2` in
Java. Ties land at `scriptSizeBytes = 256·m` for odd m, and `LARGE_SCRIPT` is live on two fixtures.
Separately, `Analyzer.java:101-110` uses `Character.isWhitespace` where TS uses `/\s/g`:
U+00A0/U+2007/U+202F/U+FEFF are stripped by TS and rejected by Java, U+001C–U+001F the reverse.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-java/src/main/java/runar/lang/analyzer/OpcodeConcerns.java:38-51 `jsToFixed1` uses `Math.rint` (round-half-to-even) to emulate JS `toFixed(1)`, which for values landing exactly on a `.x5` boundary can disagree with JS's actual (round-half-away-from-zero-on-the-decimal-string) output. packages/runar-java/src/main/java/runar/lang/analyzer/Analyzer.java:101-108 `normalize()` uses `Character.isWhitespace(c)` where TS's normalize uses `/\s/g` — the two whitespace definitions differ at the Unicode-space and C0-control-character edges (U+00A0 etc. vs. U+001C-U+001F).
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Exact on both mechanisms; line numbers drifted slightly (Analyzer.java:101-110 cited vs. actual ~101-108) but point at the same code.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Analyze a script sized so `scriptSizeBytes/1024` lands on an exact tie for `toFixed(1)` (e.g. 500992 bytes -> 489.25... boundary cited by the reviewer). Assert the reported KB string matches the TS reference's `(500992/1024).toFixed(1)` output. Also feed a script whose hex string is padded with U+00A0 (non-breaking space); assert Java's normalize() strips it like TS's `/\s/g` does. Both currently diverge.

sweep1.evidence: packages/runar-java/src/main/java/runar/lang/analyzer/OpcodeConcerns.java jsToFixed1 L38-42 uses `Math.rint(value*10.0)` (half-to-even), so 500992/1024=489.25 -> rint(4892.5)=4892 -> '489.2', while node `(500992/1024).toFixed(1)` gives '489.3' (checked). Analyzer.java normalize() L101-109 still uses `Character.isWhitespace(c)`, where TS packages/runar-testing/src/analyzer/index.ts:81 uses `.replace(/\s/g,'')`, so U+00A0 etc. are handled differently.

items.title: Java's Cli.optimizeAnf never runs standalone DCE for non-EC programs, and the pipeline's 'DCE always on' comments are false
items.confidence_note: raised by CX+GK; silent-but-inspected: ['CL']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.severity_note: reviewers disagreed ['HIGH', 'MEDIUM', 'LOW']; highest taken per §6.2 (no downgrade justified at combination time)
items.description:
[CX-DOC-001] Comments describe “general cleanup” and “DCE + EC rewrite always ON,” but production wiring runs DCE only when the program contains an EC call. This can cause tests and reviewers to assume non-EC dead-binding behavior that the pipeline does not provide.

[CX-GAP-007] The production optimizer calls only `ConstantFold` and `AnfOptimize`. `AnfOptimize` returns immediately when no EC call exists, and DCE is invoked only after EC optimization, so ordinary non-EC programs receive no standalone DCE despite pipeline comments claiming general cleanup/DCE is always on.

[GK-GAP-003] hasSideEffect returns false for kind if and loop, so an unreferenced statement-if whose then-arm is assert can be deleted when DCE runs. compile() does not call eliminateDeadBindings as its own pass; optimizeEC calls it on EVERY method if ANY method's EC rewrite changed (anf-ec.ts:310-326). Java Dce.run has no Cli call sites. TS depth: merged-local if drops the if and keeps the stale pre-if binding; for-loops with only asserts vanish.

evidence.CX-DOC-001: `PipelineTestSupport` makes the explicit always-on claim at lines 12-14 and 37; `Cli.optimizeAnf` only invokes EC-gated `AnfOptimize` at lines 345-354.
evidence.CX-GAP-007: `Cli.optimizeAnf` never calls `Dce.run` at lines 345-354; the EC gate returns the original program at `AnfOptimize.java:84-98`; cleanup occurs only inside `optimizeEcMethod` at lines 175-176.
evidence.GK-GAP-003: Opened dce.ts:153-154 (if/loop return false). Opened anf-ec.ts:310-326 (DCE only if anyChanged). Opened Cli.java optimizeAnf via worker quote matching ConstantFold then AnfOptimize.run.

remediation.CX-DOC-001: Correct the comments if the behavior is intentional, or preferably wire standalone DCE and make the comments true.
remediation.CX-GAP-007: Wire `Dce.run` as an independent pipeline pass, with conformance approval for resulting byte changes.
remediation.GK-GAP-003: Mark if/loop as having side effects unless a nested walk proves purity. Invoke standalone DCE on every compile (or document that DCE is EC-only) and stamp goldens under that policy.

testable_assertion.CX-DOC-001: Documentation and a pipeline test must agree on whether a non-EC dead binding survives optimization.
testable_assertion.CX-GAP-007: An unused pure binding in a non-EC program must be removed by `Cli.optimizeAnf`.
testable_assertion.GK-GAP-003: An EC-containing method with a dead `if (false) { assert(false); }` currently has the assert DCE'd; after the fix the assert remains or DCE refuses to delete if-nodes with nested asserts.

conflicts: none — all three corroborate against current code.
dedup_uncertain: yes: CX-DOC-001 could instead be read as a narrower 'fix the stale comment only' request independent of the functional gap; merged because its own remediation text prefers wiring the real fix over just editing the comment.
items.tier_reason: reviewer conflict recorded (§5 floor: mid min)

verification.evidence: compilers/java/src/main/java/runar/compiler/passes/AnfOptimize.java:85-92 — AnfOptimize.run() returns `program` UNCHANGED (no DCE) when no method has an EC call; Cli.optimizeAnf (Cli.java:625-633) only calls ConstantFold + AnfOptimize.run, so a non-EC program gets zero standalone DCE. compilers/java/src/test/java/runar/compiler/passes/PipelineTestSupport.java:37 still carries the comment `// DCE + EC rewrite always ON`, which is false for non-EC programs — CX-DOC-001 and CX-GAP-007 both hold today. HOWEVER GK-GAP-003's specific mechanism claim is wrong: Dce.java:267-294 (hasSideEffect) already recurses into If/Loop bodies and returns true when a nested Assert exists, so 'an unreferenced statement-if whose then-arm is assert' is NOT deletable today — that part is REJECTED (reviewer misread, or described a pre-fix state). Also important: the TS analogue of this exact gate (optimizer/dce.ts, only reachable from optimizeEC after the anyChanged early-exit) was investigated and deliberately left AS-IS in commit c869f10a (R-194): forcing DCE to run on every program breaks 11/78 conformance fixtures outright (stack-lowering still needs bindings DCE removes), so 'wire DCE to run unconditionally' is not a safe drop-in fix — DCE itself would need repair first. Go's anf_optimize.go has the identical gate, so this is cross-tier architecture, not a Java-only defect.
verification.tier_correction: The core gap (non-EC programs get no standalone DCE) is cross-tier (TS, Go, Java at minimum share the same gated-invocation architecture), not Java-specific, though this batch only asked about Java.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: CX-DOC-001/CX-GAP-007 accurate for current code; GK-GAP-003's hasSideEffect(if/loop)-returns-false claim is inaccurate at HEAD (already recurses into nested asserts).

items.testable_assertion_verified: compilers/java/src/test/java/runar/compiler/passes/PipelineTestSupport.java's `// DCE + EC rewrite always ON` comment must be corrected to state the true invocation condition (mirroring TS's R-194 header fix in packages/runar-compiler/src/optimizer/dce.ts), and a test must show a non-EC program with an unused pure binding either (a) has it removed, or (b) the test documents that it is NOT removed and the doc says so. NOTE: per R-194's measurement, actually making DCE run unconditionally on non-EC programs will break TS's compilation of 11/78 conformance fixtures unless DCE's own defects are fixed first — a naive 'call Dce.eliminateDead always' patch is not safe without that groundwork.

sweep1.evidence: compilers/java/src/test/java/runar/compiler/passes/PipelineTestSupport.java:37 still reads `anf = Cli.optimizeAnf(anf, disableConstantFolding); // DCE + EC rewrite always ON`, and its header (line 12) says 'DCE + peephole ON'. The Cli.optimizeAnf javadoc still says 'constant folding + general cleanup'. AnfOptimize.run (AnfOptimize.java:86-94) returns the program unchanged when no method has EC calls (`if (!anyChanged) return program;`), so DCE (eliminateDead at line 212) never runs for non-EC programs.

items.title: conformance/ is outside the pnpm workspace, so 8 of its test suites (incl. wire-primitives.test.ts, subprocess-integrity.test.ts) run nowhere in CI
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-GAP-095] ## CL-GAP-095 — HIGH / P1 — `conformance/` is outside the pnpm workspace, so eight of its test suites run nowhere
**Dispatcher-verified (measurement).** Source: conformance-harness depth F-02/F-03/F-15, single shared root cause.

`pnpm-workspace.yaml` declares `packages/*` and `integration/ts` only. `conformance/` is not a member, so `turbo run test` cannot reach any `conformance/**/*.test.ts` — every such suite must be named explicitly in a workflow or it runs nowhere. Eight are not:
- `conformance/wire-primitives.test.ts` — the enforcing gate for the project's own standing requirement #4 ("every fund-critical wire primitive needs ≥1 assertion against the *other* implementation"). Zero workflow references; absent from `conformance:all`.
- 7 of 9 runner self-tests, including `subprocess-integrity.test.ts`, which pins the `code ?? 0` invariant whose regression previously produced fake cross-tier divergences.
conflicts: Verified against current HEAD: pnpm-workspace.yaml is unchanged (still packages/*+integration/ts only), and no workflow file references wire-primitives.test.ts or subprocess-integrity.test.ts — this gap looks still open, independently of CL-BUG-234's already-applied fix.
dedup_uncertain: yes: kept separate from CL-BUG-234 because the actual remediation applied for CL-BUG-234 (bypassing the pnpm filter in one workflow step) would not by itself make any job discover the 8 conformance suites this finding names — but both trace back to the same 'conformance/ is not a pnpm workspace member' root fact, so a dispatcher may still want to review them together.

verification.evidence: pnpm-workspace.yaml is unchanged (packages/* + integration/ts only; conformance/ still not a member). A NEW step was added to ci.yml, 'Conformance vitest suites not reached by any other step' (~line 949-979), whose own comment says 'These eight were named by nothing... a guard is only as real as the thing that runs it' and which runs `npx vitest run conformance/anf-scope.test.ts conformance/corpus-completeness.test.ts conformance/go-only-executing-coverage.test.ts conformance/fixture-count-doc.test.ts conformance/split-stack-desync.test.ts conformance/codepart-pin conformance/dce conformance/source-map conformance/subtype-parity conformance/sdk-vertical conformance/runner/__tests__ conformance/anf-interpreter/num2bin-engine-parity.test.ts conformance/analyzer/__tests__` — this DOES now reach `conformance/runner/__tests__/subprocess-integrity.test.ts` via the `conformance/runner/__tests__` directory glob, so that specific named file is fixed. But `conformance/wire-primitives.test.ts` is NOT in that list, is not in package.json's `conformance:all` (line 38, which omits `conformance:wire-primitives` even though the script itself exists at line 31), and a repo-wide grep of `.github/workflows/*.yml` for 'wire-primitives' returns zero hits. The item's own remediation-worthy example — 'the enforcing gate for the project's own standing requirement #4' — is still unreachable in CI.
verification.fixed_by: Partial: the 'conformance/runner/__tests__' portion (incl. subprocess-integrity.test.ts) is wired into ci.yml by the same remediation pass that added the codepart-pin/dce suites it references; wire-primitives.test.ts is NOT fixed.
verification.conflict_resolution: The item's own conflicts note ('no workflow file references... subprocess-integrity.test.ts') is now WRONG at HEAD — ci.yml's new step covers it via the `conformance/runner/__tests__` glob. The note's claim about wire-primitives.test.ts remains correct.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate at the reviewed commit; partially stale now — 7 of the 8 named-by-nothing suites (via conformance/runner/__tests__ and the other seven paths in the new step) are fixed, but wire-primitives.test.ts, the finding's headline example, is not.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Grep `.github/workflows/*.yml` for `wire-primitives.test.ts` or `conformance:wire-primitives`; today it returns zero matches, so the register test enforcing 'every fund-critical wire primitive needs >=1 assertion against another implementation' never runs in CI.

sweep1.evidence: pnpm-workspace.yaml still lists only packages/* and integration/ts. `grep -rln wire-primitives .github/workflows/` returns nothing, and conformance/wire-primitives.test.ts exists but no workflow runs it; package.json:31 defines a `conformance:wire-primitives` script that no workflow invokes, and it is absent from `conformance:all`. Partly fixed: commit 59fe9b16 added ci.yml:967-980, which runs conformance/runner/__tests__ (including subprocess-integrity), sdk-vertical, source-map and others.

items.title: 28 of 540 vitest-collectable files are unreachable from any workflow, including the gates for two of the project's own six standing requirements
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-GAP-129] ## CL-GAP-129 — HIGH / P1 — 28 of 540 vitest-collectable files are unreachable from any workflow, including the gates for two of the project's own six standing requirements
**Dispatcher-verified for the load-bearing case:** `grep -rn "wire-primitives" .github/workflows/`
returns **0**.

`CHANGELOG.md:19-20` calls the six testing-architecture items *"requirements, not preferences"*.
- **Requirement #4** — *"Round-trip tests are never sufficient… every fund-critical wire primitive
  needs ≥1 assertion against the *other* implementation of the format"* — names
  `conformance/wire-primitives.json` as its register. **The 347-line gate that machine-checks that
  register runs nowhere.** The per-tier files that do reference it are **round-trip** tests, which is
  precisely what the requirement declares insufficient.
- **Requirement #5** — parity must be vertical — is half-enforced: the CLI runner runs; the 728-line
  `vertical-pins.test.ts`, whose stated purpose is *"four deliberate corruptions, each proving a
  specific pin fires. A pin that has never been shown to fail is a pin that has never been tested"*,
  **never runs.**

Also dark: `source-map/independent-oracle.test.ts` (whose own header claims it is *"what makes the
independent oracle run in CI alongside the golden compare as a real gate"*),
`num2bin-engine-parity.test.ts` (the only non-self-referential num2bin oracle),
`subprocess-integrity.test.ts` (guards the runner's own exit-code handling, on which every parity
gate depends), and `spend-shapes.test.ts` (pins the constant `fuzzer-nightly.yml:775-784` instructs
maintainers to keep `--num 35` at or above).
Plus: all **6** repo-root `tests/*.test.ts` — including `version-consistency.test.ts`, **the
self-test for the gate CL-BUG-238 proves is blind** — and the end-to-

verification.evidence: Of the ~9 dark gates the finding named, all but one are now wired into CI by three intervening commits: 59fe9b16 ('ci: 22 conformance test files were executed by nothing') added a 'Conformance vitest suites not reached by any other step' job running conformance/source-map, conformance/sdk-vertical, conformance/runner/__tests__, and conformance/anf-interpreter/num2bin-engine-parity.test.ts directly — covering independent-oracle.test.ts, vertical-pins.test.ts, subprocess-integrity.test.ts, num2bin-engine-parity.test.ts. 202644a2 ('R-110 ci: run the repo-root tests/ directory') changed the repo-root step to `npx vitest run tests/` (whole directory), covering tests/version-consistency.test.ts and every other root test. 1ad1d761 wired conformance/fuzzer/__tests__/ (spend-shapes.test.ts) into fuzzer-nightly.yml. The ONE gate still genuinely dark: conformance/wire-primitives.test.ts (Requirement #4's own register gate) — `grep -rn wire-primitives .github/workflows/` returns 0 hits; the only reference anywhere is a DEAD package.json script `"conformance:wire-primitives": "npx vitest run conformance/wire-primitives.test.ts"` (added in the same commit, 32b9cb2a, that added the test and register) which no workflow ever invokes. items.title: Java TsParser silently drops a @sighash directive when the member shares a line with the preceding token, and wrongly honors a same-line trailing comment, diverging from ts-morph's comment-attachment window
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']

items.description:
[CL-GAP-140] ## CL-GAP-134 … CL-GAP-140 — the remaining wave-2 findings
- **A `@sighash` directive is silently dropped when the member shares a line with the preceding
  token, and a same-line trailing comment is wrongly honoured** (Java `TsParser`'s comment window
  differs from ts-morph's in both directions).
dedup_uncertain: yes: ID-to-bullet mapping within the shared 'CL-GAP-134…140' ledger entry is not stated; assignment here is by list order only.
yes: same positional-inference caveat as CL-GAP-134.

verification.evidence: compilers/java/src/main/java/runar/compiler/frontend/TsParser.java:531-540 (collectLeadingComments(afterLine, memberLine)) still selects comments purely by `c.line() > afterLine && c.line() <= memberLine`, with no column/position awareness, unchanged since the single commit that introduced it (d2ad8386, never revised). parseClassMember (lines 767-775) computes `afterLine = prevTokenLine` (the previous token's line) and `memberLine = location.line()` (this member's own first-token line) the same way. Two consequences, both still live: (1) when the previous member's last token and this member's first token share a line, afterLine==memberLine and the comment range collapses to empty -- any @sighash comment on that shared line is silently dropped; (2) a comment physically written AFTER this member's own tokens on its own declaration line (a genuine trailing comment) still satisfies `c.line() <= memberLine`, so it is wrongly captured as this member's own leading/directive comment. This diverges from ts-morph's position-aware (not merely line-based) leading-trivia attachment used by the TS reference tier.
verification.tier_correction: java
verification.reviewer_accuracy: accurate -- code matches the description exactly, confirmed by direct reading of both collectLeadingComments and its caller

items.testable_assertion_verified: Add a TsParserTest case where a property's closing `;` and the next method's `/** @sighash NONE */` comment + `public` keyword sit on the same source line (previous token's line == this member's first-token line); assert the parsed MethodNode.sighashType equals NONE. Today it is null because collectLeadingComments(afterLine, memberLine) yields an empty range when afterLine==memberLine.

sweep1.evidence: TsParser.collectLeadingComments(afterLine, memberLine) still uses the purely line-based window `c.line() > afterLine && c.line() <= memberLine`; the call site is parseClassMember with prevTokenLine = tokens[pos-1].line. Probe (scratch Sh2.runar.ts): a line reads `public a(sig: Sig) { assert(...); } // @sighash SINGLE|FORKID`. The Java artifact (--emit-artifact) gives a.sigHashType=67, so it honoured a same-line trailing comment. TS compile() gives sigHashType null for every method. A same-line `readonly pk: PubKey; /** @sighash NONE|FORKID */ public b(...)` gives null in Java. TS also gives null in that same-line case, so only the trailing-comment direction diverges. A divergence is still present.

items.title: Ruby `--ir` loader bounds each loop's iteration count individually but never the product across nested loops (compile-time DoS)
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-GAP-164] ## CL-GAP-164 — HIGH / P1 — `--ir` nested-loop product is unbounded in Ruby too
`ir/loader.rb:180-193` checks `MAX_LOOP_COUNT` **per binding, never the product across nesting.** A
**1,175-byte** payload (10 000 × 10 000) loads in 0.0 s, then `compile_from_ir` was killed at
**5 m 07 s / 3.7 GB RSS and still climbing.** `MAX_IR_BYTES` (16 MiB) and `MAX_IR_NESTING` (512) give
no protection. **Third tier with the identical per-binding-not-per-product hole** (Python, Rust, Ruby).
conflicts: none. Verified in compilers/ruby/lib/runar_compiler/ir/loader.rb (current HEAD, MAX_LOOP_COUNT = 10_000 at line 23, per-binding check at ~line 330): each loop binding's count is checked against MAX_LOOP_COUNT independently, including recursively for nested loop bodies, but the counts are never multiplied together, so two nested 10,000-count loops (100M actual iterations) each pass the per-binding check. Distinct from CX-BUG-080: this is the IR path specifically, where a bound already exists but is defeated by nesting; CX-BUG-080's claim is that the SOURCE path (validator.rb) has no bound at all on a single loop — a different file, a different code path, and a different fix.
items.tier_reason: reviewer conflict recorded (§5 floor: mid min)

verification.evidence: compilers/ruby/lib/runar_compiler/ir/loader.rb:324-337 -- the 'loop' kind check validates `count` against `MAX_LOOP_COUNT` (10_000, defined at line 23) per binding only, then recurses into `binding.value.body` via `_validate_bindings(binding.value.body, method_name, mutable_count)` at line 335 with no accumulator carrying the enclosing loop's trip count forward. Two nested loop bindings of 10,000 each (product 100,000,000 actual iterations) each independently pass the `count > MAX_LOOP_COUNT` check. No product/budget tracking exists anywhere else in the file -- MAX_IR_BYTES/MAX_IR_NESTING (referenced at :63-72) bound payload size and AST depth, not iteration count.
verification.conflict_resolution: The item's own conflicts note is correct and its distinction from CX-BUG-080 (source path, different file, different fix) is accurate.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate; CL's repro shape (per-binding-not-per-product check) matches the code exactly.

items.testable_assertion_verified: IR containing two nested `loop` bindings each with count: 10000 (product 100,000,000) is rejected by ir/loader.rb's validation with a bounded-total-iteration diagnostic before `compile_from_ir` proceeds to lowering; currently it passes validation silently and only blows up later during compilation.

sweep1.evidence: compilers/ruby/lib/runar_compiler/ir/loader.rb _validate_bindings only checks each loop on its own (`if count > MAX_LOOP_COUNT`, MAX_LOOP_COUNT=10_000) before recursing into the body. Nothing bounds the product across nested loops. Probe: an IR with two nested loops of count 10000 each (scratch nested.json), run with `ruby -Ilib bin/runar-compiler-ruby --ir nested.json --hex`, raised no diagnostic and was still burning CPU when `timeout 25` killed it (23.2s user). items.title: TS: verifyRabinSig's RabinPubKey parameter is unconstrained (may be a method parameter, not just a readonly property/literal), letting a spender supply an attacker-chosen modulus for universal forgery

items.description: [GK-GAP-014] verifyRabinSig(msg, sig, padding, pubKey) typechecks for any RabinPubKey expression, including a method parameter. Nothing requires the 4th argument to be a readonly property or a literal. With attacker-chosen n, pick padding=0 and n = sig² − H for any sig with sig² > 2·H. On-chain (sig²+0) mod n = H, RHS is unreduced H (GK-BUG-021), padding 0 is in-bounds. Universal forgery, no factoring. OraclePriceFeed bakes readonly oraclePubKey — convention, not enforcement. test_rabin.rb compiles a public verify(msg, sig, padding, pubKey) that is this shape.

evidence.GK-GAP-014: Opened 03-typecheck.ts:81 (four unconstrained types). OraclePriceFeed uses a readonly property. test_rabin.rb:78-80 is the spender-n shape.

remediation.GK-GAP-014: Validator rule: 4th arg must resolve to a readonly property or a constructor literal. Same class as requiring a committed PubKey hash for P2PKH.

testable_assertion.GK-GAP-014: A contract whose settle takes pubKey: RabinPubKey as a method argument currently typechecks; after the rule it is a type error. A ScriptVM spend with padding=0 and n = sig² − SHA256(msg) currently accepts.

Any expression whose static type is `RabinPubKey` — including an ordinary method parameter — typechecks. examples/ts/oracle-price/OraclePriceFeed.runar.ts:22-28 bakes `oraclePubKey` as `readonly` purely by contract-author convention, not compiler enforcement.

items.title: The TypeScript format guide documents the exact semantics that were a fund-loss defect
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-DOC-013] ## CL-DOC-013 — HIGH — The TypeScript format guide documents the exact semantics that were a fund-loss defect
**Dispatcher-verified.** Source: docs-spec DOC-02.

`docs/formats/typescript.md:126` tells readers:
> `| &&, \|\|, ! | Boolean logic | **Both branches evaluated; no short-circuit script-level.** |`

The compiler short-circuits, and `docs/language-reference.md:267` says so explicitly: *"**These short-circuit**, exactly as in TypeScript … `a && b` lowers as `a ? b : false` … which become real branches, so the skipped operand's opcodes never run."*

The eager behaviour the format guide describes is precisely the defect that was fixed. The fix-site comment (`04-anf-lower.ts:1876-1884`) records the consequence: `assert(d === 0n || (100n / d) > 1n)` *"compiled to a locking script the chain rejects for exactly the input the guard exists to protect."*

So the canonical guide for the primary source format instructs readers to write guards in the form that loses funds.

verification.evidence: docs/formats/typescript.md:126 still reads: `| \`&&\`, \`||\`, \`!\` | Boolean logic | Both branches evaluated; no short-circuit script-level. |`. This directly contradicts both the actual compiler (packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/04-anf-lower.ts:2030-2037: `if (expr.op === '&&' || expr.op === '||') { ... consequent: expr.op === '||' ? constant : expr.right, alternate: ... }` — lowers to a real ternary/OP_IF branch, not eager BOOLAND/BOOLOR) and docs/language-reference.md, which now states at line 361 (moved from :267 in the reviewed tree — :267 is now about FixedArray bounds, an unrelated topic): 'These short-circuit, exactly as in TypeScript: ... \`a && b\` lowers as \`a ? b : false\` and \`a || b\` as \`a ? true : b\`, which become real branches, so the skipped operand's opcodes never run.' Commit 49f50279 ('fix(codegen): make && and || short-circuit on-chain (NEW-014)') fixed the compiler and updated language-reference.md but never touched docs/formats/typescript.md.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate, though the cited language-reference.md line number has drifted (was :267 in the reviewed tree, is :361 at HEAD — the content at :267 today is unrelated FixedArray text). The substantive contradiction the reviewer flagged is unchanged and independently confirmed against the compiler's actual short-circuit lowering.

items.testable_assertion_verified: A docs-consistency check comparing docs/formats/typescript.md's operator table against docs/language-reference.md's Boolean-logic description and against 04-anf-lower.ts's actual lowering; today they disagree. (Note: the item's own `files` field cites an unrelated Ruby file -- ledger-scraping noise already flagged by dedup_uncertain -- the real evidence is in the Gradle wrapper files and ci.yml as above.)

crypto (**`checkSig` always true**, `checkPreimage` always true)."

`packages/runar-testing/src/interpreter/interpreter.ts:856-861`, which I read:

case 'checkSig': {

items.title: The 7-tier parity fuzzer has never compiled a countdown or closed-bound loop
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-GAP-096] ## CL-GAP-096 — MEDIUM / P2 — The 7-tier parity fuzzer has never compiled a countdown or closed-bound loop
**Dispatcher-verified.** Source: pkg-testing depth NF-007. Breadth's "loop step is always +1" was **REFUTED as stated and REFINED** — the distinction matters.

The **exec-mode** generator `arbLoopBounds` does draw `step: 1` and `step: -1` with `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`. But that generator is **TypeScript-only** (tri-modal). The **IR-mode** generator that feeds the cross-tier `--ir` parity fuzzer hardcodes `op: '<'` and `step: 1` at **both** its loop sites (`generator.ts:1358-1372`, verified). So the seven-tier parity gate has never compiled a countdown loop or a closed-bound loop in any tier. And no generator anywhere can produce `|step| >= 2` — the IR type is `step: 1 | -1`, making it unrepresentable.

Same pass established what the IR fuzzer can *never* emit: no `ByteString` property or param (only `bigint`/`boolean`), **no builtin call of any kind**, no `~`/`OP_INVERT` (absent from the `UnaryExpr.op` union — conspicuous given the repo's shift/bitwise divergence history), no `private` visibility (so `method_call` is unreachable), no ternary, and no `add_raw_output`/`add_data_output`/`get_state_script`/`raw_script`/`array_literal`/`deserialize_state`. It **confirmed** that `add_output` is constructed at one site and spliced as the last top-level statement, never inside a branch or loop.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-testing/src/fuzzer/generator.ts:1394-1404, function arbIrLoopBlock (used by arbMethodIR at lines 1456 and 1530, which feeds the IR-mode/--ir cross-tier fuzzer generator): both the inner and outer 'for' Stmt nodes are constructed with `op: '<', step: 1` hardcoded, with the comment 'Bounds: ascending, unit step, half-open — the cross-tier subset.' No countdown (step:-1) or non-'<' bound is ever produced by this generator. `arbLoopBounds` (line ~2186) does support step:1|-1 with all 4 ops but is a separate function used only by the TS-only tri-modal generator, not by the IR-mode contract generator.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate; cited generator.ts:1358-1372 now lives at 1394-1404 (an ~36-line shift from unrelated intervening edits) but is the same function and same hardcoded values.

items.testable_assertion_verified: A vitest test that samples arbMethodIR/arbIrLoopBlock via fc.sample (e.g. 200 runs) and inspects the generated 'for' Stmt nodes, asserting at least one has step === -1 and at least one has op !== '<'. This fails 200/200 today because both loop sites in arbIrLoopBlock hardcode op:'<', step:1.

sweep1.evidence: packages/runar-testing/src/fuzzer/generator.ts arbIrLoopBlock (~1389-1405): both innerLoop and loop still hardcode `op: '<', step: 1`. Only the exec-mode arbLoopBounds (~2181-2211) produces step -1 or other ops, and its type is still `step: 1 | -1`.
