items.title: The advertised standalone EliminateDeadCode pass is not wired into any compiler entrypoint's pipeline; only OptimizeEC's conditional (EC-rewrite-triggered) DCE call actually runs, so ordinary non-EC programs get no ANF dead-code elimination at all
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [CX-GAP-001] `EliminateDeadCode` exists as a standalone public pass, but compiler entrypoints call only `FoldConstants` followed by `OptimizeEC`. `OptimizeEC` runs DCE only when an EC rewrite occurred, while `FoldConstants` claims to run DCE but returns `foldConstantsOnly`. Ordinary non-EC programs therefore receive no ANF DCE.

evidence.CX-GAP-001: The only production call within the scoped pipeline is conditional `EliminateDeadBindings` at `anf_optimize.go:89-94`. Tests manually call DCE and describe that composition as mirroring the pipeline at `constant_fold_test.go:825-832`, masking the missing wiring.

remediation.CX-GAP-001: Invoke `EliminateDeadCode` as its own pipeline pass after folding/EC optimization and correct the stale function comment.

testable_assertion.CX-GAP-001: A non-EC source program containing a transitively dead constant chain produces ANF with that chain removed through every public compile entrypoint.

verification.evidence: compilers/go/compiler/compiler.go's `CompileFromProgram` (the shared body every public entrypoint funnels through) calls `frontend.FoldConstants` then `frontend.OptimizeEC` only — no direct call to `frontend.EliminateDeadCode` anywhere in compiler.go (confirmed via `rg -n 'EliminateDeadCode\(|EliminateDeadBindings\(' compilers/go/compiler/compiler.go`, zero matches outside a throwaway probe in options.go unrelated to codegen). `OptimizeEC` -> `optimizeMethodEC` (anf_optimize.go:88-92) only calls `EliminateDeadBindings(method)` `if anyChanged` (i.e. only when an EC rewrite actually fired). `FoldConstants` (constant_fold.go:588) contains no reference to EliminateDead anything. So a non-EC source program with a transitively dead constant chain still receives no ANF DCE through any public compile entrypoint, exactly as CX-GAP-001 describes. A new file (embed_always_dce.go) exists but implements an unrelated feature (issue #109's `@embedAlways` unused-readonly-field warning), not unconditional DCE wiring.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate; the standalone `EliminateDeadCode` pass exists (extracted from anf_optimize.go per commit 56b6e401, 'gap-003: extract standalone DCE pass module in 6 non-Zig tiers') but that extraction did not change the wiring — no entrypoint calls it unconditionally, exactly as described. This is a missed-optimization gap (larger/costlier scripts), not a correctness/security defect, so not adversary-reachable in the fund-safety sense.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile a non-EC-touching source program containing a transitively dead constant chain (e.g. a `const` binding computed from other constants but never referenced by any live binding) through any public entrypoint (CompileFromSource*, CompileFromIR*) with default options (fold ON, no EC rewrite anywhere in the method). Correct behavior: the dead chain is absent from the emitted Stack IR / hex. Today: FoldConstants folds arithmetic but performs no dead-binding elimination by design, and OptimizeEC's conditional DCE never triggers absent an EC rewrite, so the dead bindings survive to stack lowering and are emitted.

sweep1.evidence: Probe with a dead chain (`const a=7n; const b=a*3n+1000n; const c=b*b;` unused, then assert(x===this.t)): `runar-go --source Dead.runar.ts --asm` -> `<fd03> OP_DUP OP_DUP OP_MUL OP_ROT OP_0 OP_NUMEQUAL OP_NIP OP_NIP`. The live-only equivalent gives `OP_0 OP_NUMEQUAL`. compiler.go CompileFromProgram (~276-284) still calls only FoldConstants and OptimizeEC. constant_fold.go FoldConstants still returns foldConstantsOnly even though its doc says it 'Also runs dead binding elimination'. frontend.EliminateDeadCode is never called from compiler/.

items.title: EC algebraic optimization (optimizeMethodEC) only examines each method's top-level bindings and does not recurse into `if`/`loop` bodies, so EC-optimizable expressions nested inside control flow are never rewritten
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [CX-GAP-002] The EC optimizer builds its lookup exclusively from each method’s top-level body and examines only top-level bindings. `if` and `loop` nodes are rejected by the call-only optimizer dispatch, so eligible EC expressions nested inside control flow never receive algebraic optimization.

evidence.CX-GAP-002: There is no recursive walk in `optimizeMethodEC`; scoped EC optimizer tests contain no nested control-flow case.

remediation.CX-GAP-002: Recursively optimize nested binding lists with lexical lookup environments and then run a correctly effect-aware standalone DCE.

testable_assertion.CX-GAP-002: `ecMulGen(0)` inside both an `if` arm and a loop body rewrites to the infinity constant.

verification.evidence: compilers/go/frontend/anf_optimize.go:41-95 optimizeMethodEC loops only `for i := range method.Body` (top-level bindings); optimizeBindingECWithInserts (anf_optimize.go:100-104) returns immediately unless `v.Kind == "call"`, so an 'if'/'loop' binding is never even inspected, and — critically — its nested Then/Else/Body bindings are never visited by this loop at all (no recursion). An ecMulGen(0) etc. nested inside an if-arm or loop body is therefore never rewritten. Cross-checked the TS reference (packages/runar-compiler/src/optimizer/anf-ec.ts:296-320 optimizeMethodEC): it has the IDENTICAL top-level-only `for (const binding of method.body)` iteration with no recursion into if/loop arms, confirming this is a genuine, matching cross-tier limitation rather than Go-specific drift (informational, not a tier_correction since the vid's tier claim about Go is itself accurate).
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate — cited line range and mechanism match exactly.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Place `ecMulGen(0n)` inside an if-branch and inside a loop body in a .runar.ts contract; OptimizeEC(program) must rewrite both call sites to the infinity-point constant, matching what happens for an equivalent top-level ecMulGen(0n) binding (currently only the top-level case is rewritten).

sweep1.evidence: Probe: ecMulGen(0n) used at top level (EcTop) -> `--hex` length 615 chars, folded to the infinity constant. The same ecMulGen(0n) inside `if (x > 5n) {...}` (EcNest) -> 851,399 hex chars, so the full scalar multiplication is emitted. anf_optimize.go OptimizeEC still builds its lookup from method.Body top-level bindings only and does not recurse into if/loop bodies.

items.title: The Go CLI exposes no flag to set Groth16WAVKey, so witness-assisted Groth16 mode is unreachable from the compiler executable
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [CX-GAP-004] The CLI constructs `CompileOptions` using only constant-folding and source-map flags and exposes no verifying-key flag. Consequently the documented compiler mode is accessible through the library but cannot be invoked through the Go compiler executable.

remediation.CX-GAP-004: Add an explicit VK option and forward it to `CompileOptions.Groth16WAVKey`.

testable_assertion.CX-GAP-004: Invoke the CLI on a witness-assisted contract with a VK flag and assert compilation succeeds.

verification.evidence: compilers/go/main.go:95-116: the main flag set (ir, source, output, hex, asm, emit-ir, emit-ir-to, parse-only, disable-constant-folding, emit-source-map, acknowledge-unsound-sp1-fri) has no VK/Groth16 flag, and the `opts := compiler.CompileOptions{...}` literal at line 110 never sets Groth16WAVKey. There IS a separate `runar-compiler-go groth16-wa --vk ... --pub ...` subcommand (main.go:301-336, CompileGroth16WA) but it is a DIFFERENT, narrower mechanism: it synthesizes a bare fixed-VK verifier contract with pinned public inputs and takes NO `.runar.ts --source` file at all. [CL-GAP-117] # impl-python-frontend — ADVERSARIAL ADDENDUM (the repaired seed's payoff) — CL-BUG-214, CL-BUG-215, CL-GAP-117

**This is what the seed repair bought.** The worker re-ran the adversarial mandate against all 28
now-legible breadth findings and adjudicated **26 of 28**, listing the two it did not reach. Two
findings escalated to CRITICAL, and — the part that matters most — **it corrected two of its own
earlier claims against its own interest.** Report re-persisted (95,048 chars).

**Verified.** 3 spot-checks, all exact: `anf_lower.py:2378-2395`, `ir/loader.py:28` + `:206-209`,
`validator.py:690-703`.

...
## CL-GAP-117 — MEDIUM / P2 — The loop-iteration cap guards only the IR entry path; the source path has none
**Dispatcher-verified.** `ir/loader.py:28` defines `MAX_LOOP_COUNT = 10_000`, enforced at `:206-209`.
`validator.py:690-703` — the source path — checks only that the bound is a compile-time constant and
imposes **no cap at all**. Measured: N=2000 and N=20000 fail fast on the downstream 800-deep stack
guard; **N=200000 did not complete within 120 s.**
The asymmetry is the finding: the same program is rejected through one entry point and hangs the
compiler through the other.

---

...
CL-GAP-117 (Python) reaching a network-exposed surface.


[CL-GAP-159] ## CL-GAP-159 — MEDIUM / P1 — The source path has **no loop cap at all**; the IR cap is per-binding, not per-product
```
source path:  N=2,000,000  →  OK, 127.6 s, 21,967,089-byte script, no diagnostic
IR path:      N=20,000     →  ValueError ... maximum 10000   (0.0 s)
IR path:      nested 10000 × 10000 = 100,000,000 iterations  →  ACCEPTED, 604-byte payload
```
`grep -rn "MAX_LOOP_COUNT" runar_compiler/frontend/*.py` → nothing.
**The worker NARROWED its own seed here, and was right to.** The breadth claim was "N=200000 did not complete within 120 s". That is body-shape-dependent and does not reproduce for a stack-neutral accumulator: N=200,000 finishes in 9.5 s. *"The honest statement is not 'it hangs' but 'it silently succeeds and emits a 22 MB script with no diagnostic'"* — which is a different, and worse, defect. A per-binding cap on one of two entry points is **neither necessary nor sufficient**; the budget belongs on the unrolled product.
conflicts: CL-GAP-117 originally characterized the failure as the compiler hanging at N=200,000. CL-GAP-159 found a stack-neutral accumulator instead completes in 9.5s and silently emits a 22MB script with no diagnostic. Both agree the root cause (no source-path loop cap) is real; CL-GAP-159's symptom description supersedes CL-GAP-117's.

CL-GAP-117 reported that N=200000 'did not complete within 120s' (implying a hang). CL-GAP-159 re-measured with a stack-neutral accumulator and found N=200,000 finishes in 9.5s and N=2,000,000 finishes in 127.6s, producing a 22MB script with no diagnostic — i.e. it does not hang, it silently succeeds. This is CL-GAP-159 correcting its own earlier (CL-GAP-117) measurement, not a disagreement between two different reviewers, and CL-GAP-159's text says so directly, so the later (159) measurement is the one to act on.
items.tier_reason: reviewer conflict recorded (§5 floor: mid min)

verification.evidence: compilers/python/runar_compiler/frontend/anf_lower.py:2578-2585 now DOES enforce MAX_LOOP_COUNT=10_000 on the source path, per individual ForStmt (fixed CL-BUG-088/CL-GAP-117's 'no cap at all' claim -- reproduced: a single loop with count=20000 now fails fast with 'For loop unrolls to 20000 iterations, exceeding the maximum loop count of 10000', elapsed 0.03s). BUT the cap is still applied per-loop, not to the product of nested trip counts, exactly as CL-GAP-159 described. Reproduced live: two nested for-loops, 9000 outer x 9000 inner (each individually under the 10000 cap, product = 81,000,000), passed to compile_from_source and given a 90-second timeout: no output, no exception, process still running at timeout (exit 124). validator.py:740-779 (_validate_for_statement) likewise checks only that bounds are compile-time constants, with no cross-loop or product-level budget.
verification.conflict_resolution: CL-GAP-159's re-measurement is the accurate description of the SINGLE-loop case only for the pre-fix code the reviewers saw. At HEAD, R-009 (commit aebb8c19) has since capped every individual source-path loop at MAX_LOOP_COUNT=10000, so a single loop of N=200,000 or N=2,000,000 (CL-GAP-159's numbers) is now REJECTED in <0.1s with a diagnostic -- it neither hangs (CL-GAP-117's claim) nor silently succeeds with a 22MB script (CL-GAP-159's claim); both single-loop measurements are stale. What survives from CL-GAP-159 and remains true at HEAD is its structural point: 'the budget belongs on the unrolled product, not the per-binding count' -- nested loops each individually under the cap still multiply past it with no diagnostic and (reproduced) hang the compiler.
verification.reachable_by_adversary: true -- if the Python compiler is exposed as a compile-as-a-service surface, a caller supplying ordinary-looking, individually-capped nested loops can hang/exhaust the compiler with no diagnostic; this is a compile-time resource-exhaustion / DoS surface, not a consensus bug.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: CL-GAP-159's own text already flagged that CL-GAP-117's 'hangs' framing was measurement-dependent and offered the more precise 'budget belongs on the product' framing, which is the part that remains true and reproduces (as a genuine hang) for nested loops at HEAD.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile a SmartContract containing two nested for-loops, each individually under MAX_LOOP_COUNT (e.g. 9000 outer x 9000 inner = 81,000,000 total unrolled iterations). This must either be rejected with a located diagnostic before unrolling begins, or must complete compilation within a bounded time budget (e.g. 30s). Currently (reproduced) compile_from_source neither raises nor returns within 90 seconds.

sweep1.evidence: R-009 (aebb8c19) added a per-loop MAX_LOOP_COUNT check on the source path (anf_lower.py ~2807), but nothing budgets the unrolled product. items.description: [CX-GAP-020] `_eliminate_dead_code` is defined as an explicit safety-net pass, but both program compilation and source-to-IR flows go from constant folding/EC optimization directly to subsequent lowering or serialization. Correctness therefore depends entirely on the EC optimizer’s internal behavior despite the compiler documenting an independent pass.

evidence.CX-GAP-020: The helper has no call site in either visible pipeline sequence.

remediation.CX-GAP-020: Invoke it at the documented point for all applicable entrypoints, or remove/document the intentional delegation and prove equivalent coverage.

(1) Single-field site (stack.rb:4593): caught, by test_sig_state_varlen.rb and test_n078_single_method_definition.rb. This is the only shape the claimant's evidence covers. (2) Middle-field site (stack.rb:4604): Sig falls into the fixed OP_SPLIT branch with prop_sizes = -1, and the whole suite stays green. (3) Last-field site (stack.rb:4620): same result, suite green. Both mutations are live code: a two-field stateful contract (Sig, bigint) or (bigint, Sig), compiled with the mutated lib, gives a different script hash (mid a3874f19 -> d12557bb, last 582c8246 -> 9b72db79). items.title: TS EC optimizer (anf-ec.ts): rewritten bindings and freshly generated helper-scalar bindings carry no `sourceLoc`, so any EC rewrite strips source-map attribution from the affected binding and its helpers

items.description: [CX-GAP-023] Rewritten bindings are reconstructed with only `name` and `value`, while generated scalar helpers also have no source location. Any EC optimization therefore removes debugger/source-map attribution from changed operations.

evidence.CX-GAP-023: Helper bindings are created without metadata at lines 179-180, 221-222, and 238-239; the replacement binding is `{ name, value }` at lines 287-288. A grep for `sourceLoc|source.?map` across all nine scoped test files returned zero matches.

remediation.CX-GAP-023: Preserve the original binding location on rewrites and assign a deterministic originating location to helper bindings.

testable_assertion.CX-GAP-023: Optimizing a located EC binding must leave a nonempty source location on every emitted replacement StackOp.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-compiler/src/optimizer/anf-ec.ts:296-322 (`optimizeMethodEC`), line 314: `const newBinding = { name: binding.name, value: rewritten };` — constructs a new ANFBinding with only `name`/`value`, dropping whatever `sourceLoc` the original binding carried. The freshly generated helper-scalar bindings inside `tryRewrite` (e.g. the `ecMul` fusion rule's `newBindings.push({ name: newScalarName, value: makeLoadConst(product) })`) likewise carry no `sourceLoc`. `ANFBinding.sourceLoc` is an optional field (ir/anf-ir.ts:73), so this compiles without error but silently discards source-map attribution for every binding an EC rewrite touches.

items.title: TS EC optimizer (`optimizeMethodEC`) only walks a method's top-level binding list — it never recurses into `if.then`/`if.else`/`loop.body`, so EC calls nested inside a conditional or loop are never simplified despite the pass being documented as always-on
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [CX-GAP-022] `optimizeMethodEC` visits only top-level method bindings and invokes `tryRewrite` only on each outer value. EC calls inside `if.then`, `if.else`, and `loop.body` are never optimized, despite the pass being documented as always-on method optimization.

evidence.CX-GAP-022: The only traversal is `for (const binding of method.body)` at `anf-ec.ts:274`; there is no recursive branch for `if` or `loop`. Every EC rewrite fixture in `anf-ec-optimizer.test.ts` places calls at method top level.

remediation.CX-GAP-022: Recursively optimize nested binding lists while maintaining scope-local value maps.

testable_assertion.CX-GAP-022: `ecMulGen(0)` nested inside both an `if` arm and loop body must become the infinity constant.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-compiler/src/optimizer/anf-ec.ts:296-322 (`optimizeMethodEC`) iterates only the flat `method.body` list and calls `tryRewrite(binding, valueMap, extraBindings)` on each top-level binding's value. `tryRewrite` (line 116) only pattern-matches `value.kind === 'call'` against the binding's own value — there is no case that descends into an `if` binding's `.then`/`.else` arrays or a `loop` binding's `.body`. So `ecMulGen(0)` written inside an `if` arm or a loop body is never rewritten, even though the file's own header (lines 1-8) documents the pass as 'Always-on' method-level optimization.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: CX-GAP-022's description (optimizeMethodEC visits only top-level bindings; tryRewrite only touches the outer value) matches the code exactly. This is a missed-optimization gap, not a correctness defect — the un-simplified script is still correct, just larger.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile a method with `ecMulGen(0)` nested inside both an `if` arm and a loop body; both call sites must fold to the INFINITY constant after optimizeEC. At HEAD only a top-level `ecMulGen(0)` folds; the nested ones do not.

sweep1.evidence: anf-ec.ts optimizeMethodEC still does `for (const binding of method.body)` with no recursion into if.then/else or loop.body. items.title: `@sighash` directive has zero conformance coverage; independently confirmed dropped on multiple tier paths
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-GAP-080] - **CL-GAP-080 — `@sighash` has ZERO conformance coverage.** The directive carries eight
  documented soundness rules (ANYONECANPAY/hashPrevouts, hashSequence-under-non-ALL, NONE with a
  state continuation, SINGLE value-skim, SINGLE multi-output, …), each enforced by a per-tier
  validator, and not one fixture exercises any of them. Three independent workers separately
  found that the flag is DROPPED on some path — Go's constant folder drops `ANFMethod.SigHashType`
  (fold is ON by default), Rust marks it `#[serde(skip)]`, Java's `ExpandFixedArrays` rebuilds
  `MethodNode` without it, Ruby's `--emit-ir` omits it. Every one of those would have been caught
  by a single fixture. v1-blocker.
- **CL-GAP-081 — `FixedArray` has ZERO conformance coverage** despite owning a dedicated pipeline
  pass (03b `expand_fixed_arrays`) in all seven tiers and shipping nine-format examples. Workers
  found the pass drops `sighashType` (Java), drops `asmReturnType` (Rust, Python, Ruby), and that
  runtime-index READS are unbounded in every tier examined. v1-blocker.
- **CL-GAP-082 — `reverseBytes` has zero fixtures AND zero example uses AND does not compile at
  all in the Ruby tier** (reproduced: `stack underflow on swap`). A declared 7-tier builtin that
  is simultaneously broken and untested. v1-blocker.
- **CL-GAP-083 — `sha1`, `checkSigVerify`, `checkMultiSigVerify`, `byteLen`, `toByteString`,
  `int2str` have zero conformance coverage.** Several workers additionally report `sha1` is not
  implemented in some tiers at all, so the declared builtin surface and the implemented surface
  disagree with nothing to detect it.
- **CLEAN: fixture source wiring.** All 648 declared sources across all 72 fixtures resolve to
  existing files. No fixture silently lost its source, which is the fai

verification.evidence: Core claim ('zero conformance coverage for @sighash') still holds: `grep -rl '@sighash' conformance/tests` returns no results at HEAD — no fixture across any of the 82 conformance fixture directories exercises the directive. docs/contract-patterns.md:301-308 and docs/formats/move.md:52-58 confirm the directive's documented, non-trivial semantics remain undertested. HOWEVER, the specific 'independently confirmed dropped on multiple tier paths' sub-claims cited as corroboration are now STALE (fixed): Go — compilers/go/frontend/constant_fold.go:605-615 `foldMethod` now does `m := *method` (full struct copy) before overwriting only `.Body`, with an explicit comment citing N-093 and this exact prior bug; a full regression suite exists at compilers/go/compiler/n093_sighash_fold_test.go. Rust — compilers/rust/src/ir/mod.rs:89-96 documents the `#[serde(skip)]` as an intentional in-memory-only carrier (mirroring Go's `json:"-"`), and compilers/rust/src/frontend/constant_fold.rs:526 `fold_method` explicitly forwards `sighash_type: method.sighash_type`. Java — compilers/java/.../ExpandFixedArrays.java:448-453 explicitly preserves `method.sighashType()` with a comment citing R-025. Ruby — compilers/ruby/lib/runar_compiler/cli.rb:58-61 documents `sighash_type` as a deliberate `IR_EXCLUDED_FIELDS` entry (N-094/#123) because the wire-carried flag lives on the check_preimage node's `sighashFlag` instead, not a silent drop.
verification.fixed_by: Go: N-093 (compilers/go/frontend/constant_fold.go, compilers/go/compiler/n093_sighash_fold_test.go). Java: R-025. Ruby: N-094 (compilers/ruby/lib/runar_compiler/cli.rb). Rust: already correct (no bug found).
verification.tier_correction: This is a cross-tier conformance gap (the missing fixture affects all 7 tiers equally), not a TS-specific defect; filing it under compiler:ts is reasonable only insofar as TS is the reference tier for authoring the missing fixture.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: the 'zero coverage' headline claim is accurate and still true at HEAD; the corroborating per-tier 'dropped' bugs it cites (which read as evidence the coverage gap is not merely theoretical) have all since been fixed with dedicated regression tests, so citing them as still-live corroboration would be stale.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Add a conformance fixture (source.json + all 9 format variants) whose public method declares a non-default `@sighash` directive (e.g. SINGLE|FORKID); assert byte-identical ANF + hex across all 7 tiers in both fold-ON and fold-OFF modes, and cross-check against a real-crypto oracle spend signed under that flag. Today zero fixtures exercise `@sighash` at all, so this class of regression (already found and fixed 3 times under different IDs: N-093/R-025/N-094) has no standing guard against recurrence.

items.title: Zig IR loader performs no referential-integrity check; six fields (result_type, sighashFlag, loop start/step, isAutoInjectedStateCheck, add_output.preimage) silently take a default on a missing or wrong-typed JSON value
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-GAP-102] ## CL-GAP-102 — MEDIUM / P2 — The Zig IR loader performs no referential-integrity check, and six fields silently take a default on a wrong-typed value
**Source:** impl-zig-rest depth NEW-Z6. **Dispatcher-verified for the security-relevant field.**
Nothing validates that a `left`/`right`/`cond`/`operand`/`value`/`satoshis` reference names an
existing binding, that binding names are unique, that a `load_prop` names a declared property, or
that a `method_call` names a declared method; no cycle detection beyond the structural depth pre-walk
(`json.zig:43-74`). Six fields default silently rather than erroring: `result_type` → `null`
(`:419-425`), **`sighashFlag` → `0` i.e. ALL|FORKID (`:617-621`)**, loop `start` → `0` (`:517`/`:519`),
loop `step` → `1` (`:524`), `isAutoInjectedStateCheck` → `false` (`:541-544`), `add_output.preimage`
→ `""` (`:567-573`). The `sighashFlag` default is the one with teeth: `"sighashFlag": "0x43"` as a
**string** silently becomes ALL|FORKID, so a covenant author who mistypes the IR gets a different
script with no diagnostic. Compounds CL-BUG-118.
**Refutation recorded, do not carry forward:** the worker initially flagged the loop-`step` collapse
to ±1 (`"step": 5` → `1`) as lossy. It is **not** a defect — `types.zig:457-462` documents
`ANFLoop.step` as a *direction* only, and the unroll computes `start + i * step` over that domain.
dedup_uncertain: yes: shares a code site with CL-BUG-118 — both discuss `ir/json.zig`'s handling of `check_preimage.sighashFlag` defaulting to 0 (ALL|FORKID), and I verified `getOptionalI32` (json.zig:625-629, the function backing the call site CL-BUG-118 cites at :309) is the shared root. But the two findings target different failure mechanisms with different fixes: CL-BUG-118 is 'no semantic/FORKID validation pass runs at all on the compile-ir path' (fix: wire up sighash_validate or equivalent); CL-GAP-102 is 'the JSON loader silently coerces a missing/wrong-typed field to a default instead of erroring, across six unrelated fields' (fix: make the loader fail closed on bad input). Fixing one would not close the other, so kept separate, but flagging the overlap for the dispatcher's judgment.

verification.evidence: Of the six named fields, loop `start` is now fixed (json.zig:~869-883, N-133: an unreadable/out-of-range start returns `ParseError.InvalidLoopStart` instead of defaulting to 0). The other five remain silent-default on a missing OR wrong-typed value: `sighashFlag` via `getOptionalI32` (json.zig:986-992, any non-integer -> silently 0 = ALL|FORKID — the security-relevant one, compounds V089); `result_type` (json.zig:721-726, non-string -> null); `isAutoInjectedStateCheck` (json.zig:909-913, non-bool -> false); `add_output.preimage` (json.zig:938-943, non-string -> ""); loop `step` (json.zig:892-895, wrong type -> silently coerced to 1). No referential-integrity check (undefined binding names, duplicate binding names, unknown property/method references) exists anywhere in json.zig.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: accurate for 5 of 6 fields; `start` has since been fixed (N-133), narrowing but not closing the finding.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Feed `compile --ir` an ANF IR JSON where a check_preimage node's `"sighashFlag"` is a STRING (e.g. `"0x43"`) instead of an integer; assert the loader rejects it with a type error rather than silently defaulting to 0 (ALL|FORKID) and compiling a script with a different sighash byte than the author intended.

sweep1.evidence: compilers/zig/src/ir/json.zig:1109 getOptionalI32 returns 0 for any non-integer value (`else => 0`), used for sighashFlag at :689. Probe: add-raw-output expected-ir.json with check_preimage sighashFlag="0x43" (string) -> `runar-zig compile-ir --hex` md5 86b4d5cc... identical to the no-sighashFlag compile (no error); with integer 0x43 -> ddf24a94... (different). The string is silently treated as ALL|FORKID.

items.title: TypeScript SDK's envelope implementation has no injectable clock, so it is the one tier that cannot replay the shared frozen-time interop accept fixture

items.description:
[CL-GAP-111] ## CL-GAP-111 — MEDIUM / P2 — The TypeScript SDK is the only tier without an injectable clock, so the envelope reference implementation never replays its own frozen accept fixture
**Dispatcher-verified, and downgraded from the worker's HIGH after I read the project's own
documentation of the gap.**

Code facts, all confirmed by me. `packages/runar-sdk/src/envelope.ts:61` is `const nonce = Date.now()`
and `:154` is `if (env.expiresAt < Date.now() - clockSkewMs)`. A grep for `now_ms|nowMs|NowMs` across
all seven envelope modules returns **TS: 0**, Go: 5, Rust: 21, Python: 4, Ruby: 4, Zig: 28, Java: 4.
The fixture's `valid_envelope.expiresAt` is `1700000030000` (2023) and `verify_now_ms` is
`1700000000500`, so under a wall clock the TS expiry check short-circuits every vector to `'expired'`
before reaching steps 3-6. `.github/workflows/ci.yml:270-295` enumerates exactly six interop files
and prints *"All 6 non-TS SDK envelope interop tests present and wired to the fixture."*

**Why MEDIUM and not HIGH — the part the worker's framing missed.** The exclusion is deliberate and
written down in two places I read:
- `conformance/sdk-envelope/validate-fixtures.ts:20-23`: *"The lone-surrogate rejection vectors and
  the verifyEnvelope rejection vectors are intentionally NOT checked here: they depend on per-tier
  rejection semantics / an injectable clock and are owned by each tier's interop test."*
- `conformance/wire-primitives.json` carries a `residual` field for this exact row: *"The
  lone-surrogate and clock-dependent rejection vectors are owned per-tier rather than by the shared
  fixture (documented in validate-fixtures.ts)."*

And the canonicalJson half **is** covered: `validate-fixtures.ts:33-38` imports
`canonicalJsonStringify` from the schema source with the stated reas

verification.evidence: packages/runar-sdk/src/envelope.ts:62 `const nonce = Date.now();` and :219 `if (env.expiresAt < Date.now() - clockSkewMs)` — no injectable clock parameter anywhere in the file (grepped `now_ms|nowMs|NowMs`: TS 0 hits vs Go 8, Rust 21, Python 4, Ruby 4, Zig 28, Java 5). conformance/sdk-envelope/validate-fixtures.ts:20-23 still contains the verbatim cited comment excluding clock-dependent rejection vectors from the shared fixture check, 'owned by each tier's interop test.' .github/workflows/ci.yml:304 still prints 'All 6 non-TS SDK envelope interop tests present and wired to the fixture.' Matches the finding exactly; nothing has changed.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Fully accurate, including the deliberate-scope-limit framing (MEDIUM not HIGH) the reviewer itself argued for and cited textual evidence for.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Add an injectable-clock option to packages/runar-sdk/src/envelope.ts's signEnvelope/verifyEnvelope (mirroring the six peer tiers' nowMs param) and replay conformance/wire-primitives.json's valid_envelope fixture at verify_now_ms=1700000000500. Today envelope.ts:62/219 hardcode Date.now(), so the fixture (expiresAt=1700000030000, a 2023 timestamp) always evaluates 'expired' under a real wall clock and TS cannot replay its own interop fixture.

sweep1.evidence: packages/runar-sdk/src/envelope.ts:62 `const nonce = Date.now();` and :219 `if (env.expiresAt < Date.now() - clockSkewMs)`; grep for nowMs in packages/runar-sdk/src returns 0 hits — no injectable clock, so the frozen-time accept fixture still evaluates 'expired'.

dry-run rejects, so the described disagreement is not ex

verification.evidence: packages/runar-sdk/src/contract.ts:44-51 still justifies dryRun default-OFF by claiming dryRunContractInput rejects Auction.bid() while 'the independent real-crypto oracle ... items.title: Go: push-data encode/decode silently misencode ByteString state fields >= 64 KiB (no OP_PUSHDATA4 arm)
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-GAP-058] | worker | CL ID | sev | prio | title |
| F12 | CL-GAP-058 | LOW | v1-should-have | Go: push-data encode/decode silently misencode ByteString state fields >= 64 KiB (no OP_PUSHDATA4 arm) |

verification.evidence: compilers/go/codegen/stack.go:874-1003 emitPushDataEncode (the ON-CHAIN runtime push-header encoder used for ByteString state serialization) has exactly 3 arms: <76 direct push, 76-255 OP_PUSHDATA1 (0x4c), and >=256 OP_PUSHDATA2 (0x4d) via NUM2BIN(4)+SPLIT(2)+DROP — which keeps only the LOW 2 bytes of the length. No OP_PUSHDATA4/0x4e arm exists, so a ByteString state field >=65536 bytes gets a push header of 0x4d||(len mod 65536), silently wrong. By contrast the COMPILE-TIME encoder compilers/go/codegen/emit.go:440-475 (encodePushData) and the SDK's packages/runar-go/sdk_state.go:475-599 (encodePushDataState/EncodePushData) both correctly handle OP_PUSHDATA4 for len>0xffff — so off-chain SDK serialization and on-chain runtime re-encoding would disagree for very large ByteString state. `git log --oneline -S'emitPushDataEncode' -- compilers/go/codegen/stack.go` shows only the original creation commit (6ad3ac8e); the function has never been touched since.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate and precisely cited (matches the CL depth-worker's own citation of stack.go's three-arm structure almost line for line).

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile a stateful contract with a mutable ByteString property, drive it through ScriptVM with a >=65536-byte state value that round-trips through emitPushDataEncode, and assert the emitted push header is 0x4e + 4-byte LE length; at HEAD it emits 0x4d + a length truncated mod 65536.

needle '76':  len  40 → P(pass)=0.140     len 200 → 0.544     len 400 → 0.790

items.title: Five `roll` emissions carry `depth = d + 1` while their paired push carries `d`, defeating the depth-aware peephole optimizer's matching key (runtime output unaffected)
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-GAP-114] # PASS C BATCH 2R WAVE 1 — impl-python-codegen (CL-BUG-142 … CL-GAP-114)

**Verified.** 4 citation spot-checks plus one full independent numeric re-derivation, all resolved
exactly. Report persisted at `workers-depth/impl-python-codegen-depth.md`.

**The re-derivation is worth stating because it settles CL-BUG-051 by a second, independent route.**
The worker proved the SLH-DSA `a` typo from *signature lengths* rather than digest lengths. I loaded
the parameter table myself and computed `n + k·(1+a)·n + d·(len+hp)·n` for all six sets against the
FIPS 205 published sizes:

```
SHA2_128s  7856 == 7856 OK      SHA2_192s 16224 == 16224 OK    SHA2_256s 29792 == 29792 OK
SHA2_128f 17088 == 17088 OK     SHA2_192f 35664 == 35664 OK
SHA2_256f 48736 vs  49856  MISMATCH, delta 1120        with a=9 -> 49856  MATCHES FIPS
```

Five of six reproduce the published sizes exactly; the sixth is short by exactly
1120 = k·n = 35·32 — one missing FORS authentication-path node per tree, which is precisely what
`a = 8` instead of `a = 9` produces. **Definitive: a typo, not a design choice.**

**New consequence to append to CL-BUG-051.** The BUG-011 exact-length gate at
`compilers/python/runar_compiler/codegen/slh_dsa.py:1013-1026` emits
`OP_SIZE <48736> OP_EQUALVERIFY`. So a genuine 49,856-byte FIPS-205 SLH-DSA-SHA2-256f signature
**aborts the script**. `verifySLHDSA_SHA2_256f` cannot verify any conformant signature at all — the
hardening added for BUG-011 turned an interoperability defect into a total failure for that
parameter set. Zig's tuple was not checked by this worker; add it to the sweep.

This report also independently re-derived **CL-BUG-114** (`sqrt`) from the Python emitter and
**sharpened it**: the breadth framing was "wrong above ~2^32". The worker simulated the emitted
opcode s

verification.evidence: compilers/python/runar_compiler/codegen/stack.py has exactly 5 sites (lines 2349, 2408, 2433, 2455, 2681) emitting `StackOp(op='push', value=big_int_push(d))` immediately followed by `StackOp(op='roll', depth=d+1)` -- matching Go's identical 5-site pattern at compilers/go/codegen/stack.go:2694,2760,2796,2820,3050 (push d + roll Depth: d+1). Go's emit.go:624 (`case "roll": return ctx.emitOpcode("OP_ROLL")`) confirms the Depth field is never used to produce bytes -- OP_ROLL reads its depth from the value pushed on the runtime stack, not from StackOp.Depth -- so the mismatch is pure metadata and runtime output is unaffected, exactly as the title states. optimizer.py:176-190 requires an EXACT match between the pushed constant and b.depth (b.depth == 0/1/2) to fold PUSH+ROLL into no-op/swap/rot, so all 5 sites' off-by-one depth defeats that fold. Note: the item's cited python file:line (stack.py:1237-1247) is NOT where this defect lives -- that range is the unrelated silent-OP_0-placeholder guard; the real sites are 2349/2408/2433/2455/2681.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: The title's mechanism and count (5 roll sites, d+1 vs d) are exact; the batch report's pasted description text and python file citation (stack.py:1237-1247) are noise from an adjacent finding and do not describe this defect -- the real python sites are 2349/2408/2433/2455/2681.

items.testable_assertion_verified: A test compiling a contract that hits one of the 5 multi-result-branch-reconciliation sites and asserting the emitted roll StackOp's depth equals the immediately preceding push literal (enabling the PUSH(d)+ROLL(d) peephole fold) fails today because depth is recorded as d+1.

sweep1.evidence: compilers/python/runar_compiler/codegen/stack.py:2516-2518 (and :2577, :2602, :2624, :2859) emit push(big_int_push(d)) followed by StackOp(op="roll", depth=d + 1); optimizer.py:170-185 PUSH(k)+Roll(k) folds require b.depth == k, so these pairs never match. (Go mirrors it at stack.go:2871/2937/2973/2997/3241 for parity.)

items.title: Rabin script never range-checks `sig < n`, so `sig + k·n` (and `-sig mod n`) is a mempool-observable unlocking-script malleability vector
items.confidence_note: raised by GK; silent-but-inspected: ['CL']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description: [GK-GAP-015] (sig + k·n)² ≡ sig² (mod n). The script never range-checks sig against pubKey. A mempool observer can replace the sig push with sig+n and rebroadcast a functionally identical spend with a different txid. Inherent Rabin also accepts −sig mod n (documented). This is grief/malleability, not theft, provided n is the committed modulus (see GK-GAP-014).

evidence.GK-GAP-015: Opened rabin-codegen.ts:84-89 (ROT DUP MUL ADD SWAP MOD — sig is only squared). No OP_LESSTHAN of sig vs n.

remediation.GK-GAP-015: Emit 0 ≤ sig < n (and document −sig as accepted or reject it). Construct sig+n as a must-abort after the gate.

items.title: The conformance fuzzer's `--anf --fold-on` mode is a no-op: every tier's --ir path forces constant folding off, so the 'fold-on' gate is a byte-for-byte duplicate of fold-off, and its help text claims otherwise
items.origin: surfaced by the F-002 remediation subagent
items.description: conformance/fuzzer/index.ts (help text ~L400, call ~L716) runs `--anf --fold-on` by sending every tier through its --ir entry point, and all 7 tiers force folding off on IR input (TS compileFromANF, Go disableFoldForIRInput, Rust ir_input_options, Python compile_from_ir, Ruby, Java, Zig). The mode therefore re-runs fold-off and its help text ('Run every tier with constant-folding ENABLED ... must produce byte-identical hex') is false. The source-level fold-ON gate in ci.yml is real; this fuzzer mode is the vacuous one. Either compile from source with folding on, or delete the mode and fix the help text and fuzzer-nightly.yml:183.

sweep1.evidence: The fuzzer --fold-on mode still sends every tier through `--ir`; it only drops `--disable-constant-folding` (anf-differential.ts:808-842). The help text at index.ts:400-403 still claims it runs 'with constant-folding ENABLED', and fuzzer-nightly.yml still has the 'Fuzz (PR gate — fold-ON, fixed seed)' step. Probe with `assert(x + 3n * 4n === this.k)`: Go --ir with fold on gives 'OP_12 OP_ADD OP_0 OP_NUMEQUAL', identical to fold off, and Rust --ir with fold on is the same. Go --source with fold on is different: 'OP_3 OP_4 OP_12 OP_3 OP_ROLL OP_SWAP OP_ADD OP_0 OP_NUMEQUAL OP_NIP OP_NIP'. So the --ir fold-on gate is a byte duplicate of fold off. [CL-GAP-108] ## CL-GAP-108 — HIGH / P1 — Seven of the ten supported state-field types have ZERO coverage anywhere in the repository

**Dispatcher-derived, and it is the root cause of CL-BUG-132 and CL-BUG-133 going undetected.**

I parsed **every tracked JSON file in the repository** (excluding `node_modules/` and
`runar-verification/`), walked each one recursively, and collected every `stateFields[].type` value
that appears. The complete census:

| type | occurrences | distinct files |
|---|---|---|
| `bigint` | 60 | 32 |
| `ByteString` | 12 | 12 |
| `PubKey` | 5 | 5 |

**That is the whole list.** The compiler's on-chain state codec supports ten types
(`packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/05-stack-lower.ts:3506-3525`): `bigint`, `RabinSig`,
`RabinPubKey`, `boolean`, `PubKey`, `Addr`, `Ripemd160`, `Sha256`, `Point`, `P256Point`,
`P384Point`, `ByteString`. **Seven of them — `boolean`, `Addr`, `Ripemd160`, `Sha256`, `Point`,
`P256Point`, `P384Point`, plus `RabinSig`/`RabinPubKey` — never appear as a state field in a single
fixture, artifact, golden or test input anywhere in the repo.**

The one `"type": "boolean"` hit under `conformance/` is at
`conformance/tests/conditional-data-output-stateful/expected-ir.json:381` and is **not** a state
field — it is a value type inside the IR body, which exercises no codec path.

**What this means for the two-invariant model.** The stated gate is that all seven compilers produce
byte-identical Stack IR and hex, and that all seven SDKs produce identical deployed locking scripts
(`conformance/sdk-output/`). Both invariants are enforced only over the inputs the corpus contains.
For seven of the ten state types the corpus contains **nothing**, so for those types the gate makes
no claim at all — while the SDK codecs, the schema table and the compiler ea

**Dispatcher-verified.** Source: conformance-corpus depth F-17. **This is the most consequential architectural finding of the review.**

Both witness oracles drive the in-process TS compiler. And the one job that looks like the exception is not: the "Script Execution Oracle" (`ci.yml:1246-1281`) runs `conformance/script_execution_test.go`, whose `compileRúnar` calls `resolveTSSource(contractName)` and then `import('./packages/runar-compiler/dist/index.js')` — verified verbatim. So across the entire conformance suite: every byte any engine has ever executed was produced by the TypeScript tier from the `.runar.ts` format. The other six tiers and the other eight formats are gated by **byte-equality with a TS-produced golden, and nothing else.**

Nothing anywhere executes a Go-, Rust-, Python-, Zig-, Ruby- or Java-emitted script. items.title: The flagship end2end PriceBet webapp's settle path is provably unspendable and never exercised on-chain
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-074] ## CL-BUG-074 — HIGH — The flagship end2end webapp deploys `PriceBet` and never executes its settlement logic
**Dispatcher-verified.** Source: examples:end2end F4. Every element checked directly.

- `examples/end2end-example/ts/PriceBet.runar.ts:28` declares `settle(...)`, `:45` declares `cancel(...)` → method indices **settle=0, cancel=1**.
- `examples/end2end-example/webapp/bitcoin.go:281-284` builds the unlocking script as `[aliceSig] [bobSig] OP_1` — **selector 1 = `cancel`**, signed with *both* keys. No price, no Rabin signature, no padding is ever pushed.
- `examples/end2end-example/webapp/compiler.go:111` bakes the Rabin modulus as `float64(12345)` — a five-digit "public key", trivially solvable by hand.
- `examples/end2end-example/webapp/main.go:229,386` draw both the strike threshold and the "oracle price" from `math/rand`, server-side. Neither is ever signed; neither reaches the script.

[CL-BUG-105] ## CL-BUG-105 — P1 — 81 of 129 builtins are unimplemented in the Zig ANF interpreter and fail OPEN
**Dispatcher-verified.** Source: sdk-zig depth NEW-05. `evalCall` is a linear `eql` chain with **no default-error arm** — the terminal statement is `return anf_none`. `toInt(.none) = 0`, `isTruthy(.none) = false`. In the lenient mode `RunarContract.call()` uses, a state field derived from any unimplemented builtin silently becomes 0 or `""` and the continuation commits to it. Unimplemented set includes every EC op, every NIST-P op, every PQ verifier, the partial-hash builtins, and six preimage accessors the covenant flows use.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-zig/src/sdk_anf_interpreter.zig: `evalCall` (starts line 1424) is a long linear `if (std.mem.eql(u8, func, "..."))` chain with only 48 distinct recognized function names, terminating at line ~1725 with an unconditional `return anf_none;` and no error/panic arm for unrecognized names. Sampled unimplemented builtins that ARE present in the canonical typecheck registry (packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/03-typecheck.ts BUILTIN_FUNCTIONS, ~125 entries) but absent from evalCall: every EC op (ecAdd, ecMul, ecMulGen, ecNegate, ecOnCurve, ecModReduce, ecEncodeCompressed, ecMakePoint, ecPointX, ecPointY), PQ verifiers (verifyWOTS, verifySLHDSA_SHA2_128s/128f), NIST-P ops (p256Add, p256Mul, p256Verify, p384Add), partial-hash builtins (sha256Compress, sha256Finalize), and preimage accessors (extractScriptCode, extractOutpoint) — all confirmed 0 occurrences inside the evalCall body via grep. `toInt`/`isTruthy` (lines 1973, 1992) both map `.none` to `0`/`false` respectively, and the interpreter's own comments (toInt: "Arrays and none have no numeric coercion — fall through to 0 to mirror how... the rest of the lenient interpreter degrades gracefully on type mismatches") confirm the silent-degradation behavior described. This is not a test-only path: packages/runar-zig/src/sdk_contract.zig:3007,3128 call `anf_interp.computeNewStateAndDataOutputs` from `RunarContract.call()`'s real transaction-building code to compute the state-continuation output that gets broadcast, so a mutable-state field whose new value depends on any of the ~77-81 unimplemented builtins is silently computed wrong (0/"") in the live deployment SDK, not just in test mocks.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate — the "no default-error arm, terminal `return anf_none`" structure and the 81-unimplemented claim (125 canonical builtins minus 48 implemented = 77, in the same ballpark as the reported 81/129 depending on exact builtin-count denominator) both check out against current code; spot-checked EC/NIST-P/PQ/preimage-accessor names are indeed all missing.

[CL-GAP-091] ## CL-GAP-091 — CRITICAL (v1 claim) — "On-chain verified across 7 tiers" is materially weaker than stated
**Dispatcher-verified.** Source: integration:all INT-003. Verified verbatim in both tiers.

- `integration/ruby/spec/spec_helper.rb:234-249` — for any non-Ruby source the suite shells out to **node** and calls `packages/runar-compiler/dist/index.js`. Its own comment: *"The Ruby compiler's TS parser has known codegen divergences for complex contracts (e.g. TicTacToe), so the TS compiler remains the gold standard for .runar.ts sources until full cross-format conformance is verified."*
- `integration/java/.../helpers/ContractCompiler.java:135-143` — spawns `node --import <tsx> packages/runar-cli/src/bin.ts compile`. That is the **TypeScript CLI**.
- `integration/python/conftest.py:219-251` — a `compile_contract_ts` fallback used by all 7 TicTacToe tests, for the same stated reason.

So what the integration suite actually establishes is: **five** compilers (TS, Go, Rust, Python-minus-TicTacToe, Zig) emit bytes a node accepts; **two** (Ruby, Java) deploy bytes *TypeScript* emitted. The Java suite's 25 `assertEquals(ts.scriptHex(), java.scriptHex())` sites compare a `.runar.java` source against a `.runar.ts` source **both compiled by the TypeScript compiler** — a frontend-parity check, not a Java-codegen check.

Two in-repo statements directly contradict the seven-tier byte-identical invariant in `CLAUDE.md`, and are worth more than the integration gap itself: Ruby and Python both record *known codegen divergences* from TypeScript. Either `tic-tac-toe` carries a `compilers` allowlist opt-out, or conformance is not catching a real divergence. → Pass E, conformance partition.

verification.evidence: integration/ruby/spec/spec_helper.rb#compile_contract (lines 220-253): dispatches to the real Ruby compiler binary only for .runar.rb paths, else shells to `node -e` running packages/runar-compiler/dist/index.js (the TS compiler), with an explicit comment admitting the Ruby parser has 'known codegen divergences.' Across all 35 spec files, every one of the 130 compile_contract(...) call sites passes a .runar.ts path — zero pass .runar.rb — so the Ruby-compiler branch is dead in practice; the entire Ruby on-chain suite deploys TS-compiled bytes. integration/java/src/test/java/runar/integration/helpers/ContractCompiler.java:16-30 (self-documented): shells to the TS CLI unconditionally for ALL sources including .runar.java, because 'the native-Java compiler ... currently emits only ANF IR and Script hex ... full artifact emission is not yet wired'; 0 of 33 dependent Java test files use the native compilers/java compiler or CompileCheck. 25 assertEquals(...scriptHex()...) call sites confirmed via grep. By contrast, integration/python/conftest.py#compile_contract genuinely dispatches through the real Python compiler (runar_compiler.compiler.compile_from_source, which has its own multi-format frontend + codegen) for all 134 non-TicTacToe calls; only the 7 TicTacToe calls narrowly fall back to compile_contract_ts, matching the review's characterization exactly.
verification.tier_correction: Ruby and Java are the two materially-affected tiers; Python's TS fallback is narrow and legitimate (only TicTacToe, 7 of 141 calls) and should not be read as equally implicated.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate and, on inspection, understated: the review frames this around 'known divergences' as the stated rationale, but in practice 100% of Ruby integration tests (130/130) and 100% of Java integration tests (33/33 files) go through the TS compiler — not just the divergent contracts. The Java gap is structural (artifact emission not yet wired into the native compiler), not case-by-case.

items.title: 18 of 22 settle tests (81.8%) cannot fail if the winner-selection branch is inverted
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-252] ## CL-BUG-252 — HIGH / P1 — 18 of 22 settle tests (81.8%) cannot fail if the winner-selection branch is inverted
**The sharpest vacuity result in the review, and it is not a tooling limitation.**

The contract's entire purpose is choosing who gets paid:
`if (price > this.strikePrice) assert(checkSig(aliceSig,…)) else assert(checkSig(bobSig,…))`.
**18 of 22 settle-positive tests across the nine formats supply a *valid* signature for BOTH
parties**, so both arms reduce to `assert(true)`. Only Python and Ruby pass an invalid signature for
the non-winner. **Seven of nine formats have no test that can detect winner-selection inversion** —
while their test names all claim the behaviour they do not check (`settles to Alice when price
exceeds strike`, `TestPriceBet_Settle_AliceWins`, …).

**Six of seven runtimes do real ECDSA, so the machinery to discriminate already exists and two tiers
already use it.** Census: 15 of 54 tests non-REAL (27.8%); **2 of 12 negatives (16.7%) assert why** —
and Ruby's three that look reason-asserting are not, because `builtins.rb:26` raises the identical
string for every failed assert.

...
makes CL-BUG-252's branch-blind tests look unavoidable when they are not. **A project instruction
file that understates its own test infrastructure causes tests to be written weaker than the
infrastructure supports.**

*Recorded against myself too: I have treated `CLAUDE.md` as authoritative on intent throughout this
review. It is authoritative on policy and stale on at least one fact.*

Cross-format spot check of PriceBet settle-positive tests at HEAD: TS/sol/move (PriceBet.test.ts x3), Go (PriceBet_test.go) and Rust (PriceBet_test.rs) and Java (PriceBetTest.java) settle-positive tests all still pass BOTH aliceSig and bobSig as genuinely valid signatures regardless of which branch should win — these 6 formats remain unable to detect an inverted winner-selection branch. Python (test_price_bet.py:43-52) and Ruby (price_bet_spec.rb:182-200, dedicated dummy_sig tests) discriminate. IMPORTANT DRIFT: Zig's examples/end2end-example/zig/price_bet_test.zig was fixed for exactly this vacuity class under commit 70bacfe9 ('R-215: the Zig end2end example never tested settle()') — each settle case now deliberately puts a WRONG-KEY (checkSig-rejected) signature in the losing party's slot, with a comment explicitly citing the same failure mode this finding describes. So the numeric tally in the title (18 of 22, 81.8%, 'seven of nine formats') is now STALE: Zig moved from vacuous to discriminating, making it 3 of 9 formats (Python/Ruby/Zig) discriminating and 6 of 9 (TS/sol/move/go/rust/java) still vacuous — a fresh recount of the exact test tally is needed before the same numbers are cited again.

items.title: No generator in the partition can emit an EC expression, so the DCE defect class is unreachable by construction
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-GAP-122] ## CL-GAP-122 — HIGH / P0 — No generator in the partition can emit an EC expression, so the DCE defect class is unreachable by construction
`grep -rn "ecAdd|ecMul|ecMulGen|ecOnCurve|Point\b"` over the three generator modules every mode
delegates to returns **zero** matches. The built-in call vocabulary is `abs`, `min`, `max`.
Since `optimizeEC` delegates to DCE and only runs DCE when a rewrite fires, **CL-BUG-166 (Rust/TS DCE
deleting guarded `assert`s) is outside the reachable space at every seed and every run count.**

**And the oracle that would catch it already exists and is already wired.** `metamorphic.ts:298-306`
`insertDeadCode` injects `if (false) { assert(1n === 2n); }`, compiles both versions and asserts the
verdicts match — *precisely* "a guarded branch was deleted" detection. It runs on every PR. It
misses the defect for one reason: its corpus is bigint arithmetic. **Adding an EC arm puts a working
oracle onto a live fund-safety defect class.** The worker calls this the highest-leverage change in
its report and I agree.

verification.evidence: conformance/fuzzer/metamorphic.ts:298-306 `insertDeadCode` matches the description exactly (injects `const __mm_dead...` + `if (false) { assert(1n === 2n); }` after a public method's opening brace). packages/runar-testing/src/fuzzer/generator.ts (the sole generator module; contract-ir.ts and renderers.ts are its IR-type/rendering peers, not independent expression generators) has zero matches for ecAdd/ecMul/ecMulGen/ecOnCurve/ecNegate/ecPointX/ecPointY/ecMakePoint/ecEncodeCompressed or `Point` anywhere in the expression-generation code; the built-in call vocabulary at generator.ts:766-786 is `abs`, `min`, `max`, `pow`, plus bitwise/shift binary ops — all bigint-typed. Since EC calls can never be synthesized, a guarded-assert-around-an-EC-expression cannot be generated, so `insertDeadCode`'s dead-branch detection can never exercise that code shape.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Mostly accurate; "three generator modules every mode delegates to" overstates the module count (generator.ts is one file exporting several generator families) but the substantive claim — zero EC vocabulary anywhere in the fuzzer — is correct.

items.title: TS DCE's hasSideEffect classifies `if` and `loop` as pure; an unreferenced top-level if/loop binding is deleted whole, taking every assert/update_prop/add_output inside it
items.confidence_note: raised by CL+CX+GK; silent-but-inspected: none; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.severity_note: reviewers disagreed ['CRITICAL', 'HIGH']; highest taken per §6.2 (no downgrade justified at combination time)
items.description:
[CL-BUG-001] | worker | CL ID | sev | prio | title |
| F-001 | CL-BUG-001 | CRITICAL | v1-blocker | TS DCE classifies `if`/`loop` as pure, deleting asserts inside an unreferenced branch |

[CL-BUG-108] ## CL-BUG-108 — CRITICAL / P1 — TS DCE classifies `if` and `loop` as side-effect-free and deletes them whole
**Dispatcher-verified verbatim.** Source: impl-ts-pipeline depth NEW-4.

`packages/runar-compiler/src/optimizer/dce.ts:151-156` — `hasSideEffect` returns `false` for `'if'`, `'loop'` and `'array_literal'`. `filterLiveBindings` then drops any top-level binding that is neither referenced nor side-effecting. An `if`/`loop` binding's own name is never a ref (loops are statements, not expressions), so **a top-level `for` loop or a result-less `if` is deleted whole — taking its `update_prop`s, `assert`s and `add_output`s with it.**

Reachability: `optimizeEC`'s tail calls DCE across the whole program as soon as *any* method triggers *any* EC rewrite. Independently, `collectReferencedProps` calls `eliminateDeadBindings` on **every** compile — which is why a readonly field read only inside a top-level loop produces the spurious warning *"not referenced in any method body and was eliminated by DCE"* for a field that is referenced. That symptom is present today for every contract.

Seven DCE tests exist; all use flat bodies. None constructs an unreferenced `if`/`loop` containing a side effect.


[CX-BUG-096] Reference collection descends into `if` and `loop`, but `hasSideEffect` classifies both container kinds as pure. An unreferenced statement-level conditional or loop is therefore removed even when its body contains `assert`, `update_prop`, output construction, raw script, or `check_preimage`. `optimizeEC` invokes this DCE whenever any EC rewrite changes the program.

[GK-GAP-003] hasSideEffect returns false for kind if and loop, so an unreferenced statement-if whose then-arm is assert can be deleted when DCE runs. compile() does not call eliminateDeadBindings as its own pass; optimizeEC calls it on EVERY method if ANY method's EC rewrite changed (anf-ec.ts:310-326). Java Dce.run has no Cli call sites. TS depth: merged-local if drops the if and keeps the stale pre-if binding; for-loops with only asserts vanish.

evidence.CX-BUG-096: `if` and `loop` return false at `dce.ts:146-156`; the top-level filter retains a binding only if its name is referenced or its own value reports a side effect at `dce.ts:164-180`. The DCE tests cover only flat effect nodes and contain no nested-effect case (`optimizer.test.ts:599-695`).
evidence.GK-GAP-003: Opened dce.ts:153-154 (if/loop return false). Opened anf-ec.ts:310-326 (DCE only if anyChanged). Opened Cli.java optimizeAnf via worker quote matching ConstantFold then AnfOptimize.run.

remediation.CX-BUG-096: Make container side-effect classification recursive and perform recursive liveness within their bodies. Add direct tests for effects nested in both branches and loops.
remediation.GK-GAP-003: Mark if/loop as having side effects unless a nested walk proves purity. Invoke standalone DCE on every compile (or document that DCE is EC-only) and stamp goldens under that policy.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-096: DCE must retain an otherwise-unreferenced `if` whose arm asserts false and a loop whose body updates state.
testable_assertion.GK-GAP-003: An EC-containing method with a dead `if (false) { assert(false); }` currently has the assert DCE'd; after the fix the assert remains or DCE refuses to delete if-nodes with nested asserts.

Per instructions, findings in different groups are not merged here; flagging so the dispatcher can note GK-GAP-003 partially overlaps a finding outside this group.

items.title: Java: ExpandFixedArrays rebuilds every method through the 5-arg MethodNode constructor, silently resetting sighashType to null (default ALL|FORKID) whenever a contract has a FixedArray property
items.confidence_note: raised by CL+CX; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-243] ## CL-BUG-243 — MEDIUM-HIGH / P1 — Java's `ExpandFixedArrays` drops `sighashType` AFTER the security-core validator has already approved the method
Source: impl-java-main NEW-02. **Ninth `@sighash` defect, and the sharpest ordering yet.**
`Cli.java:126` runs `Validate.run` — which folds in `SighashValidate`, the pass its own javadoc calls
*"SECURITY CORE"* — and only then, at `Cli.java:142`, runs `ExpandFixedArrays`, whose
`rewriteMethod` uses the 5-arg `MethodNode` constructor that defaults `sighashType` to `null`.
`AnfLower` then finds `null`, emits the default ALL|FORKID, and **skips the sighash pin entirely.**
**The author's declared mode is validated, then discarded, then replaced with a different one, with
no diagnostic.**
The worker also **corrected breadth's `embedAlways` half**: non-`FixedArrayType` properties pass
through unchanged, so `embedAlways` is lost only on the synthetic scalar siblings of a FixedArray
property that itself carried the directive — narrower than reported.


[CX-BUG-036] When any fixed-array property exists, every method is reconstructed through the five-argument compatibility constructor, which sets `sighashType` to null. Validation runs before expansion, but ANF lowering runs afterward, so a valid non-default `@sighash` method is silently compiled using default `ALL|FORKID` semantics.

evidence.CX-BUG-036: `rewriteMethod` passes only name, params, body, visibility, and location; `MethodNode` documents that this overload supplies null. ANF lowering selects its preimage-binding flag directly from the now-lost field. `rg -n "sighashType\(\)" ExpandFixedArrays.java` returned zero matches.

remediation.CX-BUG-036: Preserve `method.sighashType()` when rebuilding methods and add full-pipeline tests combining fixed arrays with every supported non-default sighash mode.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-036: A TS contract containing a fixed array and `@sighash SINGLE|FORKID` must emit `CheckPreimage` and sighash-type assertion constants for `0x43`, not `0x41`.

verification.evidence: compilers/java/src/main/java/runar/compiler/passes/ExpandFixedArrays.java:439-454 (rewriteMethod) now calls `new MethodNode(method.name(), method.params(), newBody, method.visibility(), method.sourceLocation(), method.sighashType())` — the full 6-arg constructor, explicitly threading `method.sighashType()` through, with an inline comment citing R-025 explaining exactly why the 5-arg constructor must not be used here.

items.title: Java Emit unconditionally writes hex `00` for PushCodeSepIndexOp instead of the actual byte offset of the most recently executed OP_CODESEPARATOR
items.confidence_note: raised by CX+GK; silent-but-inspected: ['CL']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.severity_note: reviewers disagreed ['CRITICAL', 'HIGH']; highest taken per §6.2 (no downgrade justified at combination time)
items.description:
[CX-BUG-028] The marker explicitly promises that emission will substitute the final most-recent `OP_CODESEPARATOR` index, but the emitter writes `00` unconditionally. Variable-length state deserialization subtracts this value from `_codePart` length before `OP_SPLIT`; any separator not at byte index zero therefore selects the wrong state suffix.

[CX-BUG-039] Variable-length state extraction emits a symbolic code-separator index and explicitly expects final layout to resolve it. `Emit` instead appends literal `00` and performs no patching or layout calculation, so scripts whose last executed `OP_CODESEPARATOR` is not byte zero calculate the wrong scriptCode/state offset.

[GK-BUG-004] PlaceholderOp's javadoc says the SDK splices constructor args at offsets in artifact.constructorSlots. Emit.java handles PlaceholderOp and PushCodeSepIndexOp by appending hex 00 and does not record slot offsets. grep of compilers/java for constructorSlots finds only that javadoc. Java-compiled artifacts cannot have constructor args spliced or codeSeparatorIndex consumed by the Java SDK.

evidence.CX-BUG-028: `PushCodeSepIndexOp` documents deferred resolution at lines 4-5; lowering consumes the value as `codeSepIdx` at lines 3201-3217; the sole emitter branch appends `"00"` at lines 287-288.
evidence.CX-BUG-039: Whole-implementation search found the op only in its IR class, StackLower creation/stamping, Peephole stamping, tests of serialization, and `Emit`'s unconditional `ctx.appendHex("00")`; no resolver exists. The IR class comment states it is “filled in by the emitter after final script layout.”
evidence.GK-BUG-004: Opened Emit.java:285-288 (appendHex 00 for PlaceholderOp and PushCodeSepIndexOp). grep constructorSlots under compilers/java returned only PlaceholderOp.java comment.

remediation.CX-BUG-028: Track final byte layout and most-recent separator position per emitted method/branch, then encode the actual index at each marker.
remediation.CX-BUG-039: Make emission layout-aware and encode the actual most-recent code-separator byte index, including method-dispatch and constructor-prefix bytes.
remediation.GK-BUG-004: Record byte offsets when emitting placeholders and OP_CODESEPARATOR, matching TS assembler constructorSlots / codeSeparatorIndex. Fail closed if a placeholder is emitted without a slot table.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-028: Emitting a stateful method with a nonzero-position `OP_CODESEPARATOR` must push that byte position, not `OP_0`, and deserialize a variable-length field correctly.
testable_assertion.CX-BUG-039: A stateful multi-method contract with variable-length state must encode a nonzero separator offset equal to the emitted script's actual last-executed `OP_CODESEPARATOR` position.
testable_assertion.GK-BUG-004: A Java-compiled stateful contract artifact has empty or missing constructorSlots/codeSeparatorIndex today; after the fix they match TS for the same source.

verification.evidence: compilers/java/src/main/java/runar/compiler/passes/Emit.java:525 (`constructorSlots.add(new ConstructorSlot(paramIndex, byteLength))`) and :542-545 (`codeSepIndexSlots.add(new CodeSepIndexSlot(byteLength, codeSeparatorIndex < 0 ? 0 : codeSeparatorIndex))`) — both offset tables are now recorded during emission, and Cli.java:513-536 writes constructorSlots, codeSepIndexSlots and codeSeparatorIndex into the artifact JSON via `--emit-artifact`. packages/runar-java/src/main/java/runar/lang/sdk/ContractScript.java:232,355 and RunarContract.java:1588-1599 consume codeSepIndexSlots/codeSeparatorIndex to splice the real value at deploy time — the emitted '00' in the compiler's template hex is an intentional placeholder byte (Emit.java:610-620 comment: 'a 1-byte OP_0 in the template that the SDK replaces with a push of the adjusted separator index'), not a bug; post-R-010 the codesep is architecturally pinned to offset 1 and Emit.java:614-621 (codeSepIndexGrowth) throws loudly if that invariant is ever violated.

items.title: Java loop lowering has no maximum iteration/unroll ceiling anywhere in the pipeline (Validate, AnfLower, or StackLower), so a small source or IR loop count can exhaust CPU/memory before unrolling
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CX-BUG-035] The IR CLI accepts parsed ANF and can proceed directly to emission, while stack lowering unrolls `count` iterations without an upper bound. A very large but valid integer count can consume extreme CPU and memory before the later stack-depth check, affecting CLI and persistent-daemon availability.

[CX-BUG-043] Validation requires a compile-time bound but imposes no magnitude limit. ANF converts any positive count fitting `int`, and stack lowering materializes the body once per iteration, allowing a tiny source file to consume extreme CPU and memory.

items.description:
[CL-BUG-242] ## CL-BUG-242 — HIGH / P1 — `addOutput` arity and type checking exists in ONE tier; four-plus tiers accept an under-supplied call and silently truncate the state section
**Dispatcher-verified in Java.** `Typecheck.java:1004-1021`, which I read, does `inferExpr` on the
args and `return "void"` — **no base-class check, no arity check, no satoshis-is-bigint check, no
per-state-value type check.** `Validate.java` has no `addOutput` handling at all.
Then `StackLower.java:3599`, which I also read, is
`int cnt = Math.min(stateValues.size(), stateProps.size());`

So a `StatefulSmartContract` with two mutable properties compiles `this.addOutput(sats, v1)` clean
and **emits a continuation output whose state section carries one value instead of two.**

**The `Math.min` is cross-tier-consistent and safe in TS *only because* the TS typechecker rejects
the input upstream** (`03-typecheck.ts:1278-1320` enforces all four checks). Remove the upstream gate
and the shared truncation becomes a reachable miscompile. Go, Python and Rust share the gap
(`typecheck.go:1163-1167`, `typecheck.py:772-782`, `typecheck.rs:1028-1033`) — **so the conformance
suite's majority comparison cannot surface it.**

...
- **CL-BUG-242 extended — wrong-TYPE `addOutput` operands compile all the way to hex.** Missing
  operands fail closed in the backend with a location-free message; **swapped types produce real
  hex silently.** *"That half is the real defect and F6 did not call it out."*

[CL-BUG-203] ## CL-BUG-203 — HIGH / P1 — The Python EC optimizer emits a reference to a binding it never adds to the body
`anf_optimize.py:298-302` inserts the fresh constant into the local value map only; nothing writes
it back into `method.body`. TS pushes a real `ANFBinding` (`anf-ec.ts:179-181`, inserted at
`:283-285`) and Rust does the same. Proved: `ecMul(ecMul(ecMulGen(s), 3n), 5n)` →
`*** DANGLING ARG __ec_opt_1` → `Compilation error: value '__ec_opt_1' not found on stack`.
**A contract that TS and Rust compile fails in the Python tier.** Two further defects on the same
lines: `_fresh_counter` is a module-level global never reset, so binding names differ between two
compilations in one process; and the folded scalar is written as a raw int with no
`bigint_json_value` boundary, so a 256-bit product would lose precision in every JS/Go/Rust consumer.

## CL-BUG-166 — CRITICAL / P0 — Rust DCE deletes an entire `if`/`loop` binding, `assert`s and all; the Go tier gets this right, so it is a live cross-tier divergence the gate does not catch
**Dispatcher-verified on every static citation, and the worker proved it by execution.**

I read all three tiers:
- **Rust** `compilers/rust/src/frontend/dce.rs:171-186` — `has_side_effect` is a flat `matches!` over
  `Assert | UpdateProp | CheckPreimage | DeserializeState | AddOutput | AddRawOutput |
  AddDataOutput | MethodCall | Call | RawScript`. **`If` and `Loop` are absent**, so both are
  effect-free, and `body.retain(...)` at `:44-58` drops them when unreferenced.
- **TypeScript** `packages/runar-compiler/src/optimizer/dce.ts:153-156` — `case 'if': case 'loop':
  case 'array_literal': return false;`. **Same bug.**
- **Go** `compilers/go/frontend/dce.go:171-192` — `case "if":` recurses into `Then` and `Else`,
  `case "loop":` recurses into `Body`, each returning true if any nested binding is effectful.
  **Go is correct.**

So this is not a shared blind spot: it is a **divergence**, and the byte-parity g

## CL-BUG-259 — CRITICAL / P0 — **One EC operation anywhere in a program silently deletes every `if`-guarded `assert` from the emitted script.** Fail-OPEN.

**Dispatcher-verified, structurally, at both ends.** `dce.rs:171-186`:
```rust
pub fn has_side_effect(value: &ANFValue) -> bool {
    matches!(value, Assert | UpdateProp | CheckPreimage | DeserializeState
        | AddOutput | AddRawOutput | AddDataOutput | MethodCall | Call | RawScript)
}
```
**`ANFValue::If` and `ANFValue::Loop` are not in the list**, so the `matches!` default classifies them effect-free. `dce.rs:53` is `body.retain(|b| refs.contains(&b.name) || has_side_effect(&b.value))` — **top level only, never recursing into an arm.** A statement-`if` binds a name nothing references, so the whole `If` binding is dropped, **taking its nested `Assert` with it**. And `anf_optimize.rs:431-453` — which I read — sets `any_changed` across **every method** and then re-runs `eliminate_dead_bindings_method` over **all** of them. So the blast radius is the whole program, not the method.

The worker executed it through the shipped CLI. Two contracts differing only by the presence of an EC expression:
```
NoEc.runar.ts    ops=   15  OP_IF=1  OP_ENDIF=1  OP_VERIFY=1
EcDce.runar.ts   ops= 7722  OP_IF=0  OP_ENDIF=0  OP_VERIFY=0
```
Both contain `public check(...) { if (x > 0n) { assert(x < this.limit); } … }`. **Both compile clean, exit 0, no di

[CL-BUG-260] ## CL-BUG-260 — HIGH / P1 — The constructor-args fund-safety guard and the issue-#109 diagnostic are both corrupted by the same DCE probe
`collect_referenced_props` (`lib.rs:132`) runs DCE on a clone and walks the *result* for `load_prop` names, so **any property referenced only inside an `if`/`loop` arm is invisible to it.** Executed:
```
POC-A   readonly `limit` used only inside `if (x>0n){assert(x<this.limit);}`, left unbaked
        → COMPILED OK, guard did NOT fire.
POC-A-CONTROL  same ref moved to top level
        → guard fired: "…would carry an OP_0 placeholder that fails at runtime."
POC-B   → #109 warning says `limit` "is not referenced in any method body and was eliminated
          by DCE" — while the emitted script plainly contains the if and the load.
```
So the guard that exists to stop an `OP_0` reaching a deploy misses every `if`-guarded reference, and the warning tells the author to annotate a field that is neither unreferenced nor eliminated.
**The worker refuted the lead it was given while confirming the defect:** the lead said `lib.rs:132` "runs DCE on EVERY compile"; it does not — `apply_constructor_args` returns early on empty args and the #109 block lives only in `_with_result`, which the CLI never calls. *"The scope is narrower, the consequence is not."*

items.title: Rust tier's Java frontend clamps integer literals to i128 and silently substitutes 0 on overflow
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-168] ## CL-BUG-168 — HIGH / P1 — The Rust tier's Java frontend clamps integer literals to `i128` and silently substitutes `0` on overflow
Source: impl-rust-frontend NEW-03, proved by execution. `parser_java.rs:359-375` ends in
`let n: i128 = val.parse().unwrap_or(0);`. Every other Rust-tier tokenizer uses arbitrary precision
(`parser_sol.rs:330`, `parser_move.rs:415`, `parser_python.rs:688-693`, `parser_ruby.rs:662-667`,
`parser_zig.rs:321-326`, `parser_gocontract.rs:454`, `parser_rustmacro.rs:1062` — all
`from_str_radix`). And `ast.rs:319-327` states the requirement it breaks: `BigIntLiteral.value` was
*"Widened from `i128` so 256-bit constants (e.g. the secp256k1 group order used in schnorr-zkp's
s-bound assert) round-trip losslessly."*
**Executed:** `Bigint.of(<secp256k1 n>)` compiles to **`OP_NOT`** — the literal became `0` and the
folder collapsed `a == 0`. The exact constant class `ast.rs` names is the one that breaks.

verification.evidence: The exact scenario CL-BUG-168 executes — `Bigint.of(<secp256k1 group order>)` — is now fixed: examples/java/src/main/java/runar/examples/schnorr-zkp/SchnorrZKP.runar.java:66-72 writes the constant via `new BigInteger("115792089237316195423570985008687907852837564279074904382605163141518161494337")`, and compilers/rust/src/frontend/parser_java.rs:1863-1909 has a dedicated `new BigInteger("decimal"[, radix])` branch that calls `parse_radix_to_bigint` (arbitrary-precision, :2042-2054) rather than the tokenizer's i128 path, producing a lossless `BigInt`. ast.rs:317-327 documents `BigIntLiteral.value` was widened from i128 to arbitrary-precision BigInt for exactly this constant class. Residual gap: the plain digit-literal tokenizer at parser_java.rs:373 (`let n: i128 = val.parse().unwrap_or(0);`) is unchanged and would still silently clamp a BARE (unquoted, un-wrapped) oversized decimal literal to 0 — but that shape is not valid real Java syntax to begin with (Java's own int/long literals cap at 64 bits; `.runar.java` files must also compile as real Java per CLAUDE.md's native-test pattern), so it is not the reachable path the finding demonstrated, which is now closed.
verification.fixed_by: 86e6777c "BUG-001: parser support for new BigInteger() + oversize literals across 7 tiers" (plus 97c885ff "rust(ir): widen BigIntLiteral / ConstValue::Int to num_bigint::BigInt")
