items.title: exprCallsSP1Fri's AST switch (CallExpr/BinaryExpr/UnaryExpr only) misses TernaryExpr (and, per GK, ForStmt init/update and non-Identifier callees), letting `verifySP1FRI` evade the mandatory unsound-verifier refusal
items.confidence_note: raised by CL+GK; silent-but-inspected: ['CX']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-103] ## CL-BUG-103 — HIGH / P1 — The SP1-FRI unsoundness gate is bypassable by a ternary, and absent entirely on `--ir`
**Dispatcher-verified.** Source: impl-go-codegen depth N1. Extends CL-BUG-084/085.

`exprCallsSP1Fri` (`frontend/sp1_fri_soundness_warning.go:107-127`) switches on three expression kinds — `CallExpr`, `BinaryExpr`, `UnaryExpr`. The AST defines seven more that can contain a call (`TernaryExpr`, `MemberExpr`, `PropertyAccessExpr`, `IndexAccessExpr`, `IncrementExpr`, `DecrementExpr`, `ArrayLiteralExpr`). So `assert(x > 0n ? verifySP1FRI(a,b,c) : false)` evades the gate entirely and emits the known-unsound verifier with no error and no warning.

Independently, `CompileFromProgram` never runs the validator — confirming CL-BUG-084 from a second direction.


[CL-BUG-191] ## CL-BUG-191 — HIGH / P1 — The SP1-FRI unsoundness refusal is bypassed by a ternary, and the acknowledgement directive is ignored on `.runar.sol` and `.runar.rs`
Runtime-proved. The gate refuses to emit a verifier the project itself documents as accepting forged
Merkle openings. `exprCallsSP1Fri` (`sp1_fri_soundness_warning.go:105-124`) handles only `CallExpr`,
`BinaryExpr`, `UnaryExpr` — not `TernaryExpr`, `IndexAccessExpr`, `MemberExpr`, `ArrayLiteralExpr`,
`IncrementExpr`, `DecrementExpr`. `assert(verifySP1FRI(...))` → refused ✓;
**`assert(flag ? verifySP1FRI(...) : false)` → `parser ok`, the unsound verifier is emitted.**
Separately, `parser.go:89` and `:109` return the `.runar.sol` / `.runar.rs` parse results **without**
`stampSP1FriAck`, unlike the seven peers — so a valid acknowledgement on those two surfaces is
ignored and compilation is refused.


[GK-BUG-031] The validator's hard error that blocks the known-unsound SP1 FRI verifier is gated on contractCallsSP1FriVerifier. exprCallsSP1Fri handles only CallExpr / BinaryExpr / UnaryExpr — no TernaryExpr. ForStmt walks condition+body, not Init/Update. callExprIsSP1Fri matches only an Identifier callee named verifySP1FRI. Typecheck registers verifySP1FRI (typecheck.go:74) and inferExprType walks TernaryExpr consequent/alternate (940-946), so `const x = cond ? verifySP1FRI(a,b,c) : false` typechecks, skips the refuse, and stack-lowers. The comment on the error string is explicit that the default is REFUSE because the verifier accepts forged Merkle openings.

[CL-BUG-101] ## CL-BUG-101 — CRITICAL / P0 — Go constant folding silently drops loop `Start`/`Step`, miscompiling every non-zero-start and countdown loop
**Dispatcher-verified verbatim.** Source: impl-go-codegen depth N2. Named depth target; confirmed against current source.

`compilers/go/frontend/constant_fold.go:521-530`:
```go
case "loop":
    return &ir.ANFValue{ Kind: "loop", Count: value.Count, IterVar: value.IterVar, Body: foldedBody }
```
`Start`, `StartRaw` and `Step` are dropped. They are real fields with documented semantics — `ir/types.go:162-167`: *"Countdown loops carry Step=-1."* `lowerLoop` then applies legacy defaults (`start=0, step=1`), so `for (let i = 3n; i > 0n; i--)` binds `0,1,2` instead of `3,2,1` — **the semantics invert**.

**Constant folding is ON by default** (`compiler.go:714-716`). The emitted hex therefore differs between fold-ON and fold-OFF for the same source.


[CL-BUG-182] # PASS C BATCH 2R WAVE 1 — impl-go-frontend (CL-BUG-182 … CL-BUG-199) and impl-python-frontend (CL-BUG-200 … CL-GAP-116)

executed them, so most findings are runtime-proved rather than read. The Go worker states its
baseline plainly: *"`go test ./frontend/` is green — every defect below is invisible to the existing
suite."* The Python worker compiled **all 648 (fixture, format) pairs** and got 648/648
byte-identical against the goldens in both fold modes — so every finding it reports lives outside
the corpus, which is exactly why they survived.

**Verified.** 4 spot-checks on go-frontend and 4 on python-frontend, all exact.

`compilers/go/codegen/stack.go:2636-2641` then applies its "older ANF payload" defaults of

`packages/runar-compiler/src/optimizer/constant-fold.ts:376` is `return { ...value, body: foldedBody };`,

pushes `OP_3 OP_2 OP_1`, fold-ON pushes `OP_0 OP_1 OP_2`.

[CX-BUG-002] Folding reconstructs loop values with only `Kind`, `Count`, `IterVar`, and `Body`, dropping `Start` and `Step`. Stack lowering consumes those fields and substitutes zero and one when absent, so a source loop with a different start or increment is compiled with different iteration values whenever folding is enabled.

[CX-BUG-016] ANF lowering records `Start`, `StartRaw`, and `Step`, but folding reconstructs loop values without any of those fields. Stack lowering interprets missing metadata as start zero and step +1, silently changing every supported non-zero-start or countdown loop under the default pipeline. The folding test covers only an old-style zero-based loop.

[GK-BUG-017] Issue #121 added Start/Step so for (let i = 3n; i > 0; i--) binds 3,2,1. ANF lower sets those fields. Go fold rebuilds the loop node with only Kind/Count/IterVar/Body. Stack lower documents nil Start as 0 and step 0 as 1, then emits start+i*step. Fold is on by default. Zero-start count-up goldens still match. TS fold spreads the value and keeps start/step. The Go #123/#121 tests compile fold-OFF. Cross-tier fold-ON would diverge if a countdown fixture existed; none does.

[CL-BUG-102] ## CL-BUG-102 — CRITICAL / P0 — Go constant folding drops `SigHashType`, shipping an ABI that contradicts its own script
**Dispatcher-verified verbatim.** Source: impl-go-codegen depth N3.

`constant_fold.go:577-584` reconstructs `ANFMethod{Name, Params, Body, IsPublic}` — dropping `SigHashType`, documented at `ir/types.go:63-70` as existing precisely *"so the SDK builds a matching preimage"* and carrying `json:"-"` (in-memory only, unrecoverable from serialisation).

The script side is unaffected — the flag also rides on each `check_preimage` node, which folding passes through untouched. So with folding **on (the default)**, a `@sighash SINGLE|FORKID` method ships a locking script demanding a SINGLE preimage plus an ABI omitting `sigHashType`, telling the SDK to build ALL|FORKID. The signature never matches; the UTXO is unspendable.

**Invisible to the existing gate by construction:** the fold-ON conformance step compares cross-tier script *hex*, and `sigHashType` is ABI-only.


[CL-BUG-183] | ID | tier | defect |
| CL-BUG-183 | Go | the default-ON constant folder strips `SigHashType` from the ABI while leaving the runtime pin in the script → **guaranteed-unspendable deploy** |

[CX-BUG-001] `foldMethod` constructs a new `ANFMethod` with only `Name`, `Params`, `Body`, and `IsPublic`; it does not copy `SigHashType`. Constant folding is enabled by default, and artifact assembly relies on the optimized method’s `SigHashType` to expose non-default modes to the SDK. The locking script and ABI can consequently disagree about the sighash mode.

[CX-BUG-015] ANF lowering attaches the non-default sighash type to `ANFMethod`, but the default-enabled folding pass reconstructs each method without copying `SigHashType`. The `check_preimage` node itself is retained, so the locking script still verifies the requested flag while the artifact ABI omits it and causes clients to use the default. Existing codegen tests disable folding and therefore mask the normal-pipeline failure.

[GK-BUG-014] foldMethod rebuilds ANFMethod with Name/Params/Body/IsPublic only, omitting SigHashType. Fold is on by default. Assembler copies method.SigHashType onto ABI only when non-nil. Python/TS/Rust/Zig/Ruby fold copies sighash_type. Go sighash_codegen_test.go compiles with DisableConstantFolding:true, so it cannot catch the default path. Result: a @sighash SINGLE|FORKID Go compile under default options emits the on-chain flag via check_preimage.sighashFlag (if that node is preserved) but ABI sigHashType is missing, so the SDK builds ALL|FORKID preimages.

evidence.CX-BUG-001: The reconstruction at `constant_fold.go:579-584` has no `SigHashType`, while `compiler.go:337-340` reads that field after optimization. No scoped constant-fold test sets or asserts method sighash metadata.
evidence.CX-BUG-015: `foldMethod` copies only `Name`, `Params`, `Body`, and `IsPublic`; ABI assembly emits `sigHashType` only from the omitted field. `compileOK` unconditionally supplies `DisableConstantFolding: true`.
evidence.GK-BUG-014: Opened constant_fold.go:576-584 (struct literal has no SigHashType). Opened compiler.go:337-339 (ABI copy). Opened sighash_codegen_test.go:33 (DisableConstantFolding: true). Opened Python constant_fold.py:536-537 which preserves sighash_type with an Issue #123 comment.

remediation.CX-BUG-001: Preserve every `ANFMethod` field when folding, preferably by copying the original method and replacing only `Body`. Add an end-to-end non-default-sighash test with constant folding enabled.
remediation.CX-BUG-015: Preserve all method metadata in `foldMethod` and add a default-options end-to-end test. Prefer cloning the method before replacing its body to avoid future metadata loss.
remediation.GK-BUG-014: Copy method.SigHashType in foldMethod (and any other ANFMethod rebuild). Add a fold-ON test that ABI sigHashType stays 0x43 for SINGLE|FORKID.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-001: Folding a public method with `SigHashType=0x43` preserves `0x43`, and the compiled ABI contains `sigHashType: 67`.
testable_assertion.CX-BUG-015: Compile a `@sighash(SINGLE|FORKID)` method with default options and assert its artifact ABI contains `sigHashType: 0x43`.
testable_assertion.GK-BUG-014: CompileFromSourceStrWithResult(singleForkIdSrc, file, CompileOptions{}) Artifact.ABI.Methods[bump].SigHashType is 0x43; today it is nil.

[CL-BUG-090] ## CL-BUG-090 — MEDIUM / P2 — The CI missing-binary guard protects 2 of 4 entry points; a zero-fixture run exits 0
**Dispatcher-verified.** Source: conformance-harness depth NEW-03. This answers a question I had queued for Pass E.

`assertAllCompilersAvailableInCi` is called at **function entry** for `--parser-only` (`:1598`) and `--ir-parity` (`:1842`), but for the two source-driven modes it lives **inside the per-fixture function** (`:2384`, `:2801`). So if `testDirs` is empty — an empty `--tests-dir`, or a `--filter` matching nothing — the guard never executes, `results` is `[]`, `report.failed` is 0, and the process **exits 0** having printed `Completed 0 test runs`.

Nothing asserts a floor. The worker grepped `MIN_FIXTURES`, `expectedFixtureCount`, `toBe(72)`, `72 fixtures`, `Completed` — **zero hits repo-wide**. The runner prints how much work it did and no gate reads that number.

verification.evidence: conformance/runner/runner.ts still has assertAllCompilersAvailableInCi() called only inside the per-fixture functions runConformanceTest (line 2453) and runConformanceTestForFormat (line 2953), not at the top of runAllConformanceTests/runAllMultiFormatConformanceTests -- so the structural pattern the reviewer describes is unchanged. But conformance/runner/runner.ts:2040-2053 now defines emptyFixtureSetError(count, ctx), and conformance/runner/index.ts calls it for ALL FOUR entry points: parser-only (line 269), ir-parity (line 304), and both source-driven modes -- multi-format and default golden -- which share one code path at index.ts:353-429 and are both floored at line 418 (`emptyFixtureSetError(report.totalTests, {...})`). Any zero-fixture run now prints the error and calls process.exit(EXIT_HARNESS_FAILURE=2) instead of exiting 0. The specific defect ("a zero-fixture run exits 0 with no floor") is fixed.

items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-120] ## CL-BUG-120 — HIGH / P1 — Zig multi-method dispatch computes the `_codePart` prelude with a different predicate than the ABI advertises and the single-method path uses
**Source:** impl-zig-rest depth NEW-Z3. **Dispatcher-verified — I read all three predicate sites.**
- ABI: `emit.zig:636` → `methodUsesCodePartFull(...)`
- Single-method stack setup: `stack_lower.zig:5327` → `methodUsesCodePartFull(...)` — agrees
- Multi-method dispatch prelude: `stack_lower.zig:5580` → `methodUsesCodePart(inner_bindings)` alone

The dispatch predicate drops both the `usesCheckPreimage` conjunct and the `readsVarLenState`
disjunct. For any contract with ≥2 public methods this splits two ways: (a) output-intrinsic without
`check_preimage` — the prelude pushes `_codePart` onto the stack model while the ABI omits it, so the
SDK does not prefix it and every `roll`/`pick` depth is off by one; (b) var-len state read plus
`check_preimage` but no output intrinsic — the ABI says `usesCodePart:true` so the SDK *does* prefix
it, the prelude does not push it, and `stack_lower.zig:2909-2913` silently takes the
*"Variable-length state but `_codePart` not available (terminal method). Skip deserialization"*
branch, emitting a method that never reads its own state.
**Confidence as recorded by the worker and preserved:** HIGH on the predicate mismatch (three lines,
read directly); MEDIUM on reachability of each class, which needs the compiler run. `stack_lower.zig`
is another partition — the ABI half (`emit.zig:636`) is this worker's.

All three sites now agree. The bare-predicate helper `usesOutputBuiltins` (stack_lower.zig:6359, using `methodUsesCodePart` alone) still exists in the file but is called from nowhere — dead code, not on any live path.

items.title: Zig `@intFromFloat` roundtrip guards sit after the cast that panics, so they never catch the out-of-range values they were written for
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-122] ## CL-BUG-122 — MEDIUM / P2 — Zig `@intFromFloat` roundtrip guards sit after the cast that panics, so they are inert for exactly the inputs they target
**Source:** impl-zig-rest depth NEW-Z5. **Dispatcher-verified at `json.zig:163-167`.**
Four sites share the idiom `const int_val: i128 = @intFromFloat(f); const roundtrip: f64 =
@floatFromInt(int_val); if (roundtrip != f) return ParseError.InvalidConstValue;`
(`ir/json.zig:163-167`, `:337-342`, `:350-355`, `:372-377`). `@intFromFloat` on an out-of-range value
is safety-checked illegal behaviour in Zig, so `"initialValue": 1e300` **panics at the cast** before
the guard can return the error. The guard catches `1.5` and nothing wider. `json.zig:502`
(`.float => |f| @intFromFloat(f)` into `u32`) has no guard at all.

verification.evidence: compilers/zig/src/ir/json.zig:96-107 introduced a dedicated `floatToInt(comptime T, f)` helper that computes an exact power-of-two bound and does `if (!(f >= -limit and f < limit)) return ParseError.InvalidConstValue;` BEFORE calling `@intFromFloat`. All four float-narrowing call sites (json.zig:~394, ~610, ~623, ~646) now call `floatToInt` first and only then perform the roundtrip-exactness check on the already-safe integer — so `"initialValue": 1e300` now returns a typed parse error instead of panicking at the illegal-behavior cast.

items.confidence_note: raised by CX+GK; silent-but-inspected: ['CL']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none

items.description:
[CX-BUG-120] The CLI runs `expand_fixed_arrays` between type checking and ANF lowering, but `compileSourceWithOptions` neither imports nor invokes that pass and lowers the original contract directly. Any SDK/tool using the documented library API therefore compiles fixed-array contracts through a materially different pipeline and can fail or emit wrong property/index handling.

[GK-BUG-005] compiler_api.zig does not import expand_fixed_arrays. compileSourceWithOptions runs parse, validate, typecheck, ANF lower, optional fold, EC optimizer, stack lower, peephole. CLI main.zig:420 does call expand. SDK compile_check and any library caller therefore compile FixedArray contracts without the scalar-split pass the CLI uses, so library vs CLI hex diverge and nested FixedArray lowering is wrong on the library path.

evidence.CX-BUG-120: The API import list has no `expand_fixed_arrays`; its pass sequence jumps from typecheck at lines 174-176 directly to ANF lower at 178-186. The CLI explicitly expands at lines 418-425 and lowers `expanded_contract`.
evidence.GK-BUG-005: Opened compiler_api.zig imports (lines 1-20): no expand_fixed_arrays. compileSourceWithOptions at 147-194 has no expand call. CLI main.zig:420 does expand.

remediation.CX-BUG-120: Centralize the source pipeline and invoke the exact same expansion/error handling from CLI and library entry points.
remediation.GK-BUG-005: Call expand_fixed_arrays.expand in compileSourceWithOptions in the same position as main.zig, before ANF lower.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-120: Compiling the same fixed-array source through the CLI and `compileSourceWithOptions` must succeed and produce byte-identical script/artifact semantics.
testable_assertion.GK-BUG-005: compileSource on a .runar.zig contract with a FixedArray property produces different (or failing) ANF than the CLI for the same file.

items.description: [CX-BUG-126] Validation checks only that the bound was literal. Lowering subtracts and adds signed 64-bit endpoints without checked arithmetic and casts the positive result to `u32`; stack lowering then unrolls it. **Dispatcher-verified in both tiers I could check.** This is the most consequential finding in the
review's gate analysis.

`--anf --fold-on` drives every tier through its `--ir` entry point, and **every `--ir` entry point
force-disables ANF constant folding regardless of the CLI flag.** So the gate is a byte-for-byte
duplicate of the fold-OFF gate sitting immediately above it in the same workflow — same mode, same
`--num 40`, same `--seed 424242`, same tier list.

I read both sides myself:
- `packages/runar-compiler/src/index.ts:611-619`, verbatim: *"Constant folding … is intentionally NOT
  run here on already-lowered ANF IR … **(opts.disableConstantFolding is accepted for CLI symmetry
  but is a no-op here.)**"*
- `compilers/go/compiler/compiler.go:188-192` — `disableFoldForIRInput` sets
  `o.DisableConstantFolding = true`, applied unconditionally at `CompileFromIR` and
  `CompileFromIRBytes`.

And the mode's own contract, which it does not keep
(`conformance/fuzzer/index.ts:395-398`): *"Run every tier with constant-folding **ENABLED** …
**Either mode must produce byte-identical hex across all tiers.**"*

**CL-BUG-182 is the defect this gate exists to catch, and cannot.**

...
job turns it on. Combined with CL-BUG-224:

| mode | tiers | ANF folder |
|---|---|---|
| `--anf`, incl. `--fold-on` | 7 | **never runs** |
| `--ir`, `--ir --stateful` | 7 |

[CL-BUG-078] ## CL-BUG-078 — CRITICAL / P0 — The stateful continuation does not bind the next contract's code; `_codePart` is attacker-supplied
**Dispatcher-verified by independent disassembly of the cross-tier golden.** Source: crypto:sighash SH-01 (adversarial). The worker attacked its own finding from six angles and it survived all six; I then re-derived the decisive evidence myself.

For every `StatefulSmartContract` public method that builds a continuation, the compiler **prepends an implicit witness parameter `_codePart`** to the method's parameters — verified in source, e.g. `compilers/go/codegen/stack.go:5077`:
```go
paramNames = append([]string{"_codePart"}, paramNames...)
```
That spender-supplied value is `OP_CAT`-ed with `0x6a` and the new state to form **the entire locking script of the continuation output**, which is then hashed and compared to the preimage's `hashOutputs`.

**My independent disassembly of `conformance/tests/stateful-counter/expected-script.hex`** — the checked-in artefact all seven tiers emit byte-identically, so this settles all seven at once:

- `OP_EQUAL` (0x87) at exactly **two** offsets: **934** and **1872** (one per method)
- **`OP_EQUALVERIFY` (0x88): ZERO occurrences in the entire script**
- offsets 847-853: `847:53` `OP_3` · `848:79` `OP_PICK` · `849:01 850:6a` push `0x6a` · `851:7e` `OP_CAT` · `852:7c` `OP_SWAP` · `853:7e` `OP_CAT`

items.description:
[CL-BUG-219] ## CL-BUG-219 — MEDIUM-HIGH / P1 — An unknown `call.func` silently lowers to `OP_0`, violating the codebase's own tested invariant
**Dispatcher-verified.** `compilers/go/codegen/stack.go:1840-1846`, which I read:
```go
opcodes, ok := builtinOpcodes[funcName]
if !ok {
    // Unknown function — push a placeholder. …
    ctx.emitOp(StackOp{Op: "push", Value: bigIntPush(0)})
```
**The project has an explicit, tested invariant against exactly this**: `loop_outer_refs_test.go:278-302`
compiles a hand-written ANF with a `load_param` naming a nonexistent parameter and **requires the
error text `"Refusing to emit a silent OP_0"`.** The `load_prop` path honours it too. The `call`
dispatch does not.
Three `--ir` probes, all exit 0: `Math.floor` contributes **no opcodes at all**; `sha256()` with
**zero** arguments emits `OP_SHA256` and hashes whatever was on top of the stack; `sha256(a,b,c)`
likewise. On the source path all three are rejected. The typechecker knows 133 builtins;
`builtinOpcodes` has 19 entries — the silent-`OP_0` surface is every name outside the dispatch chain.


[GK-BUG-010] After typecheck, unknown callees should not exist. The --ir path skips typecheck. Python stack.py:1586-1591, Ruby stack.rb:1902-1908, Go stack.go:1790-1796, and Rust stack.rs:1826-1834 all push integer 0 on a builtin-opcode miss. TS throws (05-stack-lower.ts:1850-1852). Java throws (StackLower.java:1537-1542). Zig comments that the old OP_0 fallback was removed. A well-formed locking script then treats the unknown call as 0 (if-then-else takes the else/allow arm). Go's comment claims this is for private method calls in non-public methods that are never emitted; --ir of an unknown `call` still takes the same arm.

evidence.GK-BUG-010: Opened stack.py:1586-1591, stack.rb:1902-1908, stack.go:1792-1794 (Unknown function — push a placeholder / bigIntPush(0)), stack.rs:1830-1834 (PushValue::Int(0)), 05-stack-lower.ts:1850-1852 (TS throws), StackLower.java:1531-1543 (unknown builtin throws).

remediation.GK-BUG-010: Unknown kind/builtin must throw, matching TS/Java/Zig. One shared fail-closed policy on every --ir path.

testable_assertion.GK-BUG-010: python/ruby/go/rust --ir on ANF with kind call name not_a_builtin currently emits OP_0; after the fix each exits non-zero with the unknown name in the message.

Two incompatible `raw_value` encodings: the `--source` path writes `json.dumps(...)`, the `--ir`

unconditionally. Quantified by sweep: **OK 42, CRASH 30**, with all 30 fixture names listed in the

[CL-BUG-267] ## CL-BUG-267 — HIGH / P0 — `artifact_to_json` crashes on 30 of 72 fixtures, and the "fix" turns it into silent corruption
**Dispatcher-verified.** `compiler.py:942-944`:
```python
if v.raw_value is not None:

    d["value"] = json.loads(v.raw_value) if isinstance(v.raw_value, str) else v.raw_value
```

OK: 42    CRASH: 30    (all 30 stateful; 100% JSONDecodeError; identical in both fold modes)

items.description:
[CX-BUG-064] All source compilation APIs call a private dispatcher that invokes format parsers directly. The 4 MiB pre-tokenization guard exists only in `frontend.parser_dispatch.parse_source`, so CLI/library compilation accepts and tokenizes arbitrarily large source after first reading it fully into memory.

[GK-BUG-026] compiler.py defines a second nine-extension dispatcher _parse_source with zero size check and zero directive check. compile_from_source, compile_source_to_ir, and CLI --parse-only all go through it. parser_dispatch.parse_source is the function tests pin (test_source_size_guard.py, test_directive_guard.py) and the function whose docstring claims fail-closed mirrors Go/Rust/Zig/Ruby/Java. evidence.CX-BUG-064: `rg -n "parser_dispatch|parse_source\\(" compilers/python --glob '*.py'` shows compiler entry points using `_parse_source`; `compiler.py:122-159` contains no call to `assert_source_bytes_under_limit`, while the guarded dispatcher does at `parser_dispatch.py:73-80`.

items.confidence_note: raised by CL+CX; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-271] **both ways** — see CL-BUG-271.

**Pass F should quote this.** A worker that corrects its own delivered report without being asked is

## CL-BUG-271 — HIGH / P1 — Two divergent Ruby ANF serializers produce two different sighash failures
The worker adjudicated a delegate's blanket "REFUTED" and found **both measurements correct, for
different serializers** — a distinction neither party had alone:
```
CLI path   (bin/runar-compiler-ruby --emit-ir → --ir)   <- what users and conformance invoke
   sighashFlag in --emit-ir: 0 occurrences (dropped);  sighash_type: a key the loader never reads
   SCRIPT differing byte: [[725, "43", "41"]]           ABI sigHashType: 67 -> nil
Library path (compiler.rb::_serialize_anf_program)
   sighashFlag present: true    SCRIPT EQUAL: true      ABI sigHashType still lost
```
**Library path = deploy-to-brick:** the script demands SIGHASH_SINGLE while the ABI tells the SDK to
build ALL|FORKID, so the signature can never verify. **CLI path additionally downgrades the on-chain
binding flag** from `0x43` to `0x41`. The eleventh `@sighash` defect, and the second tier in which the
flag silently changes value.


[CX-BUG-079] The CLI’s ANF serializer hard-codes the serialized fields and omits `sighash_flag`, while the compiler’s artifact serializer includes `sighashFlag`. Consequently `--emit-ir`/`--emit-ir-to` loses a non-default signature mode and recompiling the emitted IR changes semantics to the default flag.

evidence.CX-BUG-079: `serialize_anf_value` omits the field present in the ANF type; `serialize_anf_value_for_artifact` explicitly emits `"sighashFlag"`.

remediation.CX-BUG-079: Use one canonical serializer for artifact and CLI IR or add `sighashFlag` to the CLI representation.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-079: CLI IR emitted from a `SINGLE|FORKID` signature check contains `"sighashFlag":67` and recompiles to the same script as direct source compilation.

conflicts: none between the two reports. Current HEAD (compilers/ruby/lib/runar_compiler/cli.rb `_snake_key`, comment 'N-094: the old table ... dropped +sighash_flag+ entirely') shows this was fixed by deriving field names generically instead of a hand-maintained table — confirms the bug both findings describe rather than contradicting either.

verification.evidence: compilers/ruby/lib/runar_compiler/cli.rb:305-333 -- _snake_key now derives the wire key generically from the field name (split on '_', capitalize each following part) instead of a hand-maintained allowlist table, so 'sighash_flag' -> 'sighashFlag' is emitted correctly; the comment at :312-316 documents the exact old N-094 bug.
verification.fixed_by: 11fa3200 N-094: derive the ANF wire format from the type; Ruby and Python were downgrading @sighash (further generalized by 6b8ca1d9 R-113)

items.title: Go: source loops bypass the IR path's `MaxLoopCount` bound entirely, and the `big.Int`→`Int64()`→`int` count conversion can overflow/wrap before any check
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [CX-BUG-019] Hand-authored IR is capped at 10,000 loop iterations, but source validation only requires a literal bound. ANF lowering converts an arbitrary-size `big.Int` count through `Int64()` and `int`, then stack lowering unrolls that count. Large values can cause resource exhaustion, while values outside signed 64-bit range can wrap and silently change iteration count.

(CL-BUG-118); Python's does too. Two of six tiers confirmed; four unchecked.

items.description: [CX-BUG-056] Each `if` arm receives a new context whose `private_methods` remains empty. A private helper call inside the arm therefore falls through to general builtin lowering; unknown functions are silently represented by `PUSH 0`, producing wrong Script instead of inlining or rejecting the call.

conflicts: none between reports. items.title: Ruby: FixedArray expansion rebuilds CallExpr without asm_return_type, turning asm<ByteString> byte ops into numeric ops (e.g. OP_CAT -> OP_ADD)

items.description:
[CL-BUG-272] ## CL-BUG-272 — HIGH / P1 — A rebuilt `CallExpr` drops `asm_return_type`, turning `OP_CAT` into `OP_ADD`
`expand_fixed_arrays.rb` rebuilds `CallExpr.new(callee:, args:)` without `asm_return_type:`. Two
contracts identical **except for one unrelated FixedArray property**: `OP_CAT` silently becomes
`OP_ADD` — **ByteString concatenation becomes numeric addition in the deployed script.** CLASS 1.


[CX-BUG-078] Reconstructed and cloned `CallExpr` nodes preserve the callee, arguments, sighash, and location but omit `asm_return_type`. Since this transformation runs after type checking, an `asm<ByteString>` expression in any contract requiring FixedArray expansion loses the type information that later lowering uses to distinguish byte-string from numeric operations.

evidence.CX-BUG-078: Both `CallExpr.new` sites omit `asm_return_type`; ANF lowering explicitly consults that field when deciding whether an expression is byte-typed.

remediation.CX-BUG-078: Preserve every semantic field when cloning/rebuilding calls and add a transformation-level metadata test.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-078: After FixedArray expansion, an `asm<ByteString>` call retains `asm_return_type == "ByteString"` and byte equality lowers to the byte opcode.

verification.evidence: compilers/ruby/lib/runar_compiler/frontend/expand_fixed_arrays.rb:661-671 (`rewrite_expression`'s `CallExpr` branch) and :1028-1029 (`clone_expr`'s `CallExpr` branch) both now pass `asm_return_type: expr.asm_return_type` explicitly when rebuilding a `CallExpr`. The R-026 comment at :663-667 documents this exact bug: 'Dropping it here turned a byte concat into a numeric add for any contract that also declares a FixedArray property.'

[CL-BUG-146] ## CL-BUG-146 — MEDIUM / P2 — WOTS+ emits no signature-length gate, so `sig || junk` verifies identically to `sig`
**Dispatcher-verified by absence proof.** I counted `OP_SIZE` per file across the whole partition:
`stack.py` 19, `p256_p384.py` 4, `blake3.py`/`ec.py`/`emit.py`/`sha256.py`/`slh_dsa.py` 1 each, and
**`wots.py` 0**. WOTS+ consumes 67 chains × 32 bytes = 2144 signature bytes and discards the
remainder (`wots.py:224-225` `swap; drop`).

The project already treats this exact class as a real bug in two sibling modules, in its own words:
`slh_dsa.py:1014-1016` (*"Without this guard the d xmss-layer split loop silently dropped trailing
bytes"*) and `p256_p384.py:1235-1238` (*"Without it `sig || junk` verified identically to `sig`
(fatal for any contract using signature bytes as a nullifier)"*). **WOTS+ is the outlier that never
got the same treatment.** Project-wide, not Python-specific: `compilers/go/codegen/wots.go` and
`packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/wots-codegen.ts` also contain zero `OP_SIZE`. Short signatures
fail closed (`OP_SPLIT` past end aborts); only over-long ones are malleable.

items.description:
[CL-GAP-104] ## CL-GAP-104 — LOW / P3 — Python SDK `canonical_json` has none of the reference implementation's DoS guards
**Source:** sdk-python depth NEW-07.
Missing depth cap, circular-reference detection, per-string byte cap and output byte cap — all four
present in `packages/runar-ir-schema/src/canonical-json.ts`. `_canonical_append` recurses with no
depth accounting and no `seen` set, so a self-referential dict is unbounded recursion. Mitigated in
practice: reached only on the **signing** side over caller-owned data; `verify_envelope` never calls
it and has its own size guards. Relevant to the wire-protocol-parity rule in CLAUDE.md, which names
`canonicalJson` as a must-be-byte-identical primitive across all seven SDKs.

...
- **CL-GAP-104 (`canonicalJson` missing DoS guards) — Ruby confirmed.** NEW-08: no depth limit, no
  circular-reference guard, no output-size cap — plus a Ruby-specific wrinkle, that a malformed Hash
  *key* raises an untyped `Encoding` error while the same bytes in a *value* raise the typed one.
- **CL-BUG-137 (`TokenWallet` signs a discarded transaction) — Ruby confirmed.** NEW-05 finds the
  identical defect in `packages/runar-rb`, with the Ruby-specific mechanism spelled out:
  `resolve_method_args` only auto-signs `nil` Sig slots, so the stale signature is embedded verbatim.
  Two tiers, same bug, neither with a consumer. Strengthens the "delete it in all seven" remediation.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-py/runar/sdk/envelope.py now has all four guards: depth cap (MAX_WIRE_NESTING=100, enforced at :101,112 in _canonical_append before descending into children), per-string byte cap (MAX_ENVELOPE_FIELD_BYTES, :198-200), and output byte cap (MAX_ENVELOPE_PAYLOAD_BYTES, :60-62). No explicit 'seen' set for circular-reference detection exists, but a live python3 probe (`d={}; d['self']=d; canonical_json(d)`) confirms a self-referential dict raises `ValueError: canonical JSON: nesting exceeds 100` via the depth guard rather than looping/overflowing the stack — the practical circular-reference protection the finding asked for is present, just implemented via the depth cap rather than a dedicated seen-set.

items.title: TS `BYTE_RETURNING_FUNCTIONS` hand-maintained heuristic misclassifies the numeric preimage extractors (extractVersion/extractLocktime/extractSigHashType) as byte-returning, breaking both arithmetic (OP_CAT instead of OP_ADD) and equality (OP_EQUAL instead of OP_NUMEQUAL) lowering
items.confidence_note: raised by CL+CX; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-109] ## CL-BUG-109 — HIGH / P1 — Three numeric preimage extractors are registered as byte-returning, so `extractLocktime(pre) + k` compiles to `OP_CAT`
**Dispatcher-verified.** Source: impl-ts-pipeline depth NEW-5.

`BYTE_RETURNING_FUNCTIONS` (`04-anf-lower.ts:2487-2496`) lists `extractVersion`, `extractLocktime`, `extractSigHashType` — all three declared `returnType: 'bigint'` in the typechecker and terminated with `OP_BIN2NUM` in lowering. `lowerBinaryExpr` sets `result_type: 'bytes'` when either operand is byte-typed, and `lowerBinOp` then emits **`OP_CAT` instead of `OP_ADD`**.

So `assert(extractLocktime(this.txPreimage) + 100n > this.deadline)` — an idiomatic timelock-offset guard — concatenates the locktime bytes with `0x64` and compares the blob numerically. The ANF interpreter behind `TestContract` performs a numeric add, so source and script disagree **silently**. The mirror error is also present: genuine byte-returners (`extractScriptCode`, `extractOutputs`, `extractPrevOutputScript`, both Merkle roots, `buildChangeOutput`) are *missing* from the list. Root cause is a hand-maintained duplicate of the return-type table.


[CX-BUG-100] `extractVersion`, `extractLocktime`, and `extractSigHashType` are listed as byte-returning, causing `===`/`!==` to use byte equality. Stack lowering explicitly converts all three results with `OP_BIN2NUM`, so their language-level result is numeric and comparison must use numeric equality. Byte equality can disagree for equivalent numeric encodings.

[CX-BUG-108] Pass 4 chooses byte equality using an independent, incomplete builtin-name heuristic rather than the typechecker’s result. It wrongly classifies numeric `extractVersion`, `extractLocktime`, and `extractSigHashType` as bytes and omits byte-returning builtins including `buildChangeOutput` and several typed crypto helpers. This selects `OP_EQUAL` for numeric values or `OP_NUMEQUAL` for arbitrary byte strings, yielding incorrect or failing script behavior.

evidence.CX-BUG-100: The three names appear in `BYTE_RETURNING_FUNCTIONS` at `04-anf-lower.ts:2347-2349`; equality annotates `result_type: 'bytes'` from that heuristic at lines 1788-1795. Stack lowering uses `OP_BIN2NUM` for version and sighash type at `05-stack-lower.ts:3825-3838` and `3912-3933`, with locktime documented and lowered as numeric at lines 3936 onward.
evidence.CX-BUG-108: Type signatures at lines 198-211 mark the three extractors as `bigint` and `buildChangeOutput` as `ByteString`; the byte-returning list at lines 2341-2350 says the opposite. Stack lowering defaults equality to `OP_NUMEQUAL` and only overrides annotated byte comparisons, as documented at lines 121-133.

remediation.CX-BUG-100: Remove numeric extractors from the byte-return set and define return types from the builtin signature table rather than a hand-maintained heuristic.
remediation.CX-BUG-108: Preserve resolved expression types from Pass 3 into the AST/ANF and select equality opcodes from those types. Remove the independent builtin-name heuristic.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-100: Equality involving each numeric extractor must lower to `OP_NUMEQUAL`, never `OP_EQUAL`.
testable_assertion.CX-BUG-108: `extractVersion(preimage) === 2n` must emit `OP_NUMEQUAL`, while `buildChangeOutput(...) === expectedBytes` must emit `OP_EQUAL`.

Fixed by N-054 (be3eefdb), whose commit message confirms the exact miscompile: 'assert(extractLocktime(p)+1n===65281n) emitted OP_1 OP_CAT instead of OP_1ADD ... Only Rust got this one right.' Residual note (not the batch's headline defect): buildChangeOutput and merkleRootSha256/merkleRootHash256 (ByteString-returning per 03-typecheck.ts:196-197,212) are still absent from BYTE_RETURNING_FUNCTIONS, so CX-BUG-108's narrower 'missing byte-returner' sub-claim may retain partial truth, but that is a distinct, smaller residual, not the confirmed defect.

therefore has **36** encodings that pass. Go has the identical gap (`bn254.go:1296-1318`), so this
is project-wide — but it is an inconsistency with the project's own stated GAP-301 remediation.

[CL-BUG-107] ## CL-BUG-107 — HIGH / P1 — TS `sqrt` emits wrong results for ordinary inputs; fold-ON and fold-OFF disagree
**Dispatcher-verified by independent execution.** Source: impl-ts-pipeline depth NEW-1.

`05-stack-lower.ts:4548` runs a fixed `SQRT_ITERATIONS = 16` Newton steps from `guess = n` with **no convergence guard**. The constant folder's version of the same function *has* the guard (`if (next >= guess) break`).

I re-executed both algorithms myself rather than trusting the report:
- `sqrt(8)`: emitted → **3**, correct → **2**
- **64 values below 10 000** where the emitted algorithm disagrees with `floor(sqrt)` — first: 8, 15, 48, 63, 80, 99
- `sqrt(10^9)`: emitted → **32640**, correct → **31622** (16 iterations cannot converge for `n ≥ 2^28`)

**Fold-mode divergence:** `sqrt(8n)` folds to a push of `2` with folding ON (the default) and compiles to the 16-iteration loop yielding `3` with `--disable-constant-folding` — the mode the checked-in goldens were stamped under. Per CLAUDE.md the fold-ON CI step *"enforces cross-tier parity … and skips the golden comparison"*, so a divergence identical in all seven tiers is invisible to the entire matrix. `docs/language-reference.md:460` states flatly: *"Returns the integer (floor) square root."*

Same shape, lower severity: `pow` clamps to `base^min(exp,32)` while the folder computes the true power for `exp ≤ 256` — so a constant exponent in 33..256 also disagrees between modes.

## CL-BUG-114 — HIGH / P0 — The constant folder and the stack emitter compute `pow`, `sqrt` and `clamp` to different values; `--disable-constant-folding` flips contract semantics
**Source:** impl-ts-optimizers depth NEW-01. **Dispatcher-verified and independently re-derived.**

Two evaluators for the same builtins disagree. The folder is correct in all three cases; the emitted
script is wrong, and the checked-in fold-OFF goldens enshrine the wrong value.

| builtin | folder | emitter | worked divergence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pow` | exact `base^exp` for `exp ∈ [0,256]`, declines above (`constant-fold.ts:156-163`, decline at `:159`) | 32 guarded multiplies, `MAX_POW_ITERATIONS = 32` (`05-stack-lower.ts:4421-4436`) | `pow(2n,40n)` → **2^40** vs **2^32** |

items.title: Python's fixed-array expansion drops MethodNode.sighash_type, letting @sighash validation and codegen see different contracts
items.confidence_note: raised by CL+GK; silent-but-inspected: ['CX']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-204] | ID | tier | defect |
| CL-BUG-204 | Python | fixed-array expansion rebuilds `MethodNode` without `sighash_type`; validation runs under the declared mode and codegen under the default — **the two passes see different contracts** |

[GK-BUG-025] When any FixedArray property exists, every method is rebuilt as a new MethodNode(name, params, body, visibility, source_location). sighash_type defaults to None. Validate + validate_sighash_usage already ran on the original flag. ANF lower then treats the method as default ALL|FORKID, omits sighashFlag on check_preimage, and the ABI loses sigHashType. A .runar.ts board contract with @sighash SINGLE|FORKID and a FixedArray field silently ships ALL|FORKID through the Python compiler. TS copies via { ...method, body }. Go copies the struct and overwrites Body. Python uniquely reconstructs.

evidence.GK-BUG-025: Opened expand_fixed_arrays.py:341-349 (no sighash_type=method.sighash_type). Opened ast_nodes.py:324-330 (sighash_type field, default None). TS spread at 03b-expand-fixed-arrays.ts:439-441.

remediation.GK-BUG-025: return MethodNode(..., sighash_type=method.sighash_type). Test: FixedArray + @sighash SINGLE|FORKID keeps 0x43 through expand, ANF check_preimage.sighash_flag, and ABI sigHashType.

testable_assertion.GK-BUG-025: A StatefulSmartContract with board: FixedArray<bigint, 9> and @sighash SINGLE|FORKID on a public method compiles with method.sighash_type == 0x43 after expand and sighashFlag == 0x43 on the injected check_preimage node. Today both are missing.

verification.evidence: expand_fixed_arrays.py:413-414 (rewrite_method) now does `return replace(method, body=new_body)` using dataclasses.replace, which preserves every field of the source MethodNode (sighash_type included) instead of reconstructing the node positionally. items.title: Python's typechecker accepts an undeclared identifier in a boolean position (`<unknown>` is compatible with everything)
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-206] ## CL-BUG-206 — HIGH / P2 — Python's typechecker accepts an undeclared identifier in a boolean position
`typecheck.py:535` returns `"<unknown>"` for an unresolved identifier and `:253-255` makes
`"<unknown>"` compatible with everything, so `assert(zzzUndeclared)` type-checks clean and ANF
lowering emits a `load_param` for a name that is not a parameter. Proved: parse `[]`, validate `[]`,
**typecheck `[]`**, ANF carries the phantom, and only stack lowering fails closed. The control
`assert(a + zzzUndeclared > 0n)` **is** caught, so the hole is specifically where `<unknown>` meets a
non-arithmetic expected type. **The phantom node reaches `--emit-ir` output** even though script
emission refuses.
dedup_uncertain: yes: verified by reading typecheck.py:514-601 that CL-BUG-206 (undeclared Identifier) and CX-BUG-069 (missing ArrayLiteral case) are two different branches of the SAME `_infer_expr_type` function, both falling through to the same permissive `<unknown>` sentinel that downstream checks treat as compatible with everything. They share a root mechanism but are triggered by different expression kinds and each needs its own specific fix (reject unresolved identifiers vs. add ArrayLiteral inference), so 'same fix closes both' does not hold cleanly — kept separate but flagged as a plausible single-root-cause candidate for the dispatcher to reconsider.

verification.evidence: typecheck.py:685-699 (_infer_expr_type, Identifier arm) now calls self._add_error(f"Undefined variable '{expr.name}'") before returning "<unknown>" for any identifier that resolves to no local/builtin/property/KNOWN_GLOBALS -- unconditionally, independent of the surrounding expression's expected type. [CL-BUG-050] 1. **CL-BUG-050 (Python `--ir` cannot emit an artifact for ANY stateful contract).** I ran
   `compile_from_ir_bytes` + `artifact_to_json` over the checked-in goldens under
   PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE, worktree verified clean after:
       basic-p2pkh       artifact_to_json OK   (stateless -> anf is None)
       stateful          artifact_to_json FAILED JSONDecodeError
       stateful-counter  artifact_to_json FAILED JSONDecodeError
       auction           artifact_to_json FAILED JSONDecodeError
   Root cause confirmed at two lines: `ir/types.py:354` stores the DECODED json value in
   `raw_value`; `compiler.py:943` then does `json.loads(v.raw_value)` on it. A bare binding
   name like "t3" is not valid JSON. CRITICAL, reproduced, not inferred.
2. **CL-BUG-051 (SLH-DSA SHA2_256f uses a=8; FIPS 205 requires a=9) — SEVEN-TIER.**
   Found independently by the impl:python:codegen and impl:ts:pipeline workers, who share no
   context. I verified the parameter in four tiers directly:
       packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/slh-dsa-codegen.ts:46  slhMk(32, 68, 17, 8, 35)
       compilers/go/codegen/slh_dsa.go:54                        slhMk(32, 68, 17, 8, 35)
       compilers/python/.../codegen/slh_dsa.py:86                _slh_mk(32, 68, 17, 8, 35)
       compilers/rust/src/codegen/slh_dsa.rs:102                 slh_mk(32, 68, 17, 8, 35)
   and re-derived the FIPS digest length myself:
       256f a=8 -> 44   256f a=9 -> 49 (= FIPS m)   128s -> 30 OK   192s -> 39 OK
   Only 256f is wrong. Consequence: the on-chain length gate rejects every genuine FIPS-205
   SHA2-256f signature, and FORS security drops 315->280 bits. Because all seven tiers carry
   the same value, cross-tier conformance CANNOT detect it. This is the "agreement is not
   correctness" failure mode in its pu

items.description: [CX-BUG-098] `subContext()` constructs a child without forwarding `sideEffects`. Consequently, `shouldInlinePrivate()` always returns false inside an `if`, ternary, or loop. remediation.CX-BUG-098: Forward the same immutable side-effect summary to subcontexts. Add branch, ternary, and loop tests where a private helper emits each output kind.

[CL-BUG-140] ## CL-BUG-140 — LOW / P3 — `WalletProvider.getTransaction` returns a 0-output shell, turning `fromTxId` into a misleading "index out of range"
Source: sdk-ts NEW-10. `wallet-provider.ts:275-276` returns
`{ txid, version: 1, inputs: [], outputs: [], locktime: 0 }` on a cache miss instead of throwing.
`contract.ts:2379` then reports *"output index 0 out of range (tx has 0 outputs)"* — which reads as
a fact about the transaction, not about the provider.
**Downgraded from the breadth framing by the worker, correctly:** the deploy/call post-broadcast
path is unaffected because `broadcastTx` caches the raw hex (`:167`, `:189`) before `getTransaction`
is called. Only `fromTxId`/`fromUtxo` on an uncached historical txid reaches the shell, and it fails
closed there.

The deploy catch now uses txToTransactionData, but only if getTransaction throws. WalletProvider.getTransaction on cache miss succeeds with that same empty shell (wallet-provider.ts:275-276). Because it does not throw, deploy's .catch never runs and the caller receives a 'confirmed' transaction with zero outputs. fromTxId then throws output index N out of range — or, if outputIndex===0 were tolerated, would restore from an empty script.

evidence.GK-BUG-032: Opened wallet-provider.ts:256-276 (return { txid, version: 1, inputs: [], outputs: [], locktime: 0 }). Opened contract.ts:562-569 (catch only on throw; comment names C4).

remediation.GK-BUG-032: Throw on cache miss (and overlay miss), matching MockProvider. Let deploy/finalizeCall hit the txToTransactionData fallback.

items.title: `subContext()` drops `sideEffects`, so a private output-helper called inside an `if` is not inlined and its output escapes the continuation hash
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-184] ## CL-BUG-184 — CRITICAL / P0 — `subContext()` drops `sideEffects`, so a private output-helper called inside an `if` is not inlined and its output escapes the continuation hash
**Runtime-proved with a same-source control.** `anf_lower.go:934-969` copies nine fields and not
`sideEffects`; `shouldInlinePrivate` bails at `:772` when `ctx.sideEffects == nil`. So inside any
nested block the helper stays a `method_call` and its `add_raw_output` never registers on the
parent's `addOutputRefs`.
Identical helper, identical call, only the nesting differs: at top level the hash is
`cat(cat(t12, t15), change)` — the helper's output **is** committed; inside `if (amount > 10n)` the
hash is `cat(t12, change)` — it is **not**. `rc=0`, no diagnostic. **Funds leave the covenant
uncommitted.**
A second failure mode falls out of the same root: `ContinuationShapeFor` *does* walk the call graph
(`side_effect_summary.go:173-187`), so it omits `_newAmount` from the ABI while the lowering emits
`load_param _newAmount` anyway — *"the param-injection decision and the continuation-path decision
use two different, disagreeing notions of 'has an output'."*

...
**Runtime-proved.** Same root as CL-BUG-184. When the caller's arg has a *different* name the
failure is loud (`method parameter 'amount' is not on the stack`). When the caller's own parameter
happens to share the helper's parameter name, `this.payOut(amount * 1000n, true)` resolves correctly
*outside* the `if` (to `t15 = amount*1000`) and **inside the arms emits `load_param amount` — the
un-multiplied witness**. `rc=0`, script emitted, semantics silently wrong.

verification.evidence: compilers/go/frontend/anf_lower.go:1030-1047 (`subContext`) now explicitly copies `sideEffects: ctx.sideEffects` (line 1040, comment: 'read-only summary — a nested call site must make the same inlining decision as a top-level one'), so `shouldInlinePrivate` no longer sees a nil sideEffects map inside nested if/loop blocks.

items.title: The only CLI-reachable Groth16 backend emits the verifier that does not bind public inputs
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-081] ## CL-BUG-081 — HIGH / P1 — The only CLI-reachable Groth16 backend emits the verifier that does not bind public inputs
**Dispatcher-verified.** Source: crypto:bn254-groth16 F1 (adversarial). Go tier only — the other six ship no Groth16 codegen (worker proved by grep, not assumed from policy).

Two verifier variants exist. `EmitGroth16VerifierWitnessAssistedWithMSM` recomputes `IC[0] + Σ pub_i·IC[i+1]` on-chain and `OP_EQUALVERIFY`s it. `EmitGroth16VerifierWitnessAssisted` takes the spender's `prepared_inputs` G1 point on trust. **The `runarc groth16-wa` subcommand — the only CLI path, and the one the shipped SP1 example drives — hard-codes the raw variant** (`compilers/go/compiler/groth16_wa.go:163`), and its flag set has no `--msm`.

The raw variant's own comment is the defect (`bn254_groth16.go:1456-1462`), verified verbatim:
> *"The on-chain verifier does not bind to specific public input values — **the pairing check already discriminates between valid and invalid prepared_inputs values.** This matches SP1's Solidity verifier…"*

That reasoning does not hold. The pairing proves the spender knows *a* valid proof for *some* statement under this VK; it says nothing about *which* statement. The SP1 analogy fails because SP1's Solidity verifier receives public inputs as calldata into a contract whose surrounding semantics bind them — here they are simply absent from the script.

A spender holding any proof they generated themselves (trivially obtainable for an SP1 program) spends the UTXO. The worker looked for an unconditional forgery and did **not** find one: with `A, B, L, C` all free, an attacker still faces fixed-target pairing inversion. So this is a statement-binding break, not a total break — reported at that strength, not inflated.

Compounding (F2): the one ship

verification.evidence: At HEAD, compilers/go/codegen/bn254_groth16.go (~1403-1418) carries an explicit 'SOUNDNESS WARNING -- this variant does NOT bind public inputs' comment on EmitGroth16VerifierWitnessAssisted (the raw variant); the misleading SP1-analogy text the finding quoted is gone (grep for 'does not bind to specific public input values' -> zero matches). compilers/go/compiler/groth16_wa.go:266 hardcodes codegen.EmitGroth16VerifierWitnessAssistedWithMSM (the safe, public-input-binding variant) for the `runarc groth16-wa` CLI backend, with Groth16WAOpts.PublicInputs documented as REQUIRED and checked against numPubInputs. The shipped example integration/go/contracts/RollupGroth16WAMSM.runar.go:34-38 calls runar.AssertGroth16WitnessAssistedWithMSM(), not the raw marker. The unsafe raw path (codegen/stack.go:5807) still exists but is reachable only via the differently-named intrinsic AssertGroth16WitnessAssisted(), whose own doc comment now flags it as opt-in/unsafe-by-design ('Use this variant only where something outside the script fixes the statement') -- not the silent CLI default the finding described.

items.title: EC optimizer Rule 9 truncates the folded scalar through `i64`, turning `ecMul(ecMul(p, 2³²), 2³²)` into `ecMul(p, 0)`
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-170] ## CL-BUG-170 — HIGH / P1 — EC optimizer Rule 9 truncates the folded scalar through `i64`, turning `ecMul(ecMul(p, 2³²), 2³²)` into `ecMul(p, 0)`
**Dispatcher-verified.** `compilers/rust/src/frontend/anf_optimize.rs:137-141`, which I read, is
`fn make_load_const_int(n: i128) -> ANFValue { ANFValue::LoadConst { value: serde_json::json!(n as i64) } }`.
Rule 9 computes `k1.checked_mul(k2)` in `i128` — guarding `i128` overflow — and then hands the
product to a function that silently wraps it to `i64`. Each factor is bounded by 2⁵³ (the JSON
number path), so the product reaches ≈8·10³¹, far past `i64::MAX`.
**Executed:** `ecMul(ecMul(p, 4294967296n), 4294967296n)` emits `t4_k = {"kind":"load_const",
"value": 0}` — the correct scalar is 2⁶⁴; the emitted one is the point at infinity. Control with
`3n`/`5n` correctly gives 15.

...
Source: impl-rust-frontend NEW-06, same root as CL-BUG-170. `anf_lower.rs:256-267`'s
`bigint_to_json` emits a JSON number only when `|i| ≤ 9007199254740991` and otherwise the quoted
`"<n>n"` form; `constant_fold.rs:318-326` routes through it precisely so *"the JS-safe-integer
boundary is defined exactly once"*. The EC optimizer bypasses it. **Executed:** a rewritten scalar
emitted as the bare JSON number `18014398509481982` where the crate's own contract requires the
string `"18014398509481982n"`. **A cross-tier IR-parity risk**, since the IR JSON is compared
byte-for-byte across tiers. One-line fix, shared with CL-BUG-170.

...
byte-for-byte across tiers. One-line fix, shared with CL-BUG-170.

verification.evidence: compilers/rust/src/frontend/anf_optimize.rs:172-175 make_load_const_int now takes &BigInt and routes through anf_lower::bigint_to_json (the shared JS-safe-integer-boundary encoder), with a comment explicitly stating 'n as i64 used to be the encoder, which silently wrapped any product past i64::MAX'. Rule 9 (232-266) computes k1/k2 via get_const_int (returns Option<BigInt>) and reduce_mod_n(k1*k2) using BigInt arithmetic throughout -- no i64/i128 narrowing anywhere in the path -- before calling make_load_const_int(&product).
verification.fixed_by: 41b77f1c (R-033: decode oversize load_const scalars in Rust's EC optimizer)
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate at review time (the described i64 truncation matches the fix commit's own description); the fix goes further than the minimal one-line remediation, using BigInt through the whole computation, not just at the final encode.

[CL-BUG-194] ## CL-BUG-194 — HIGH / P1 — Unguarded `big.Int → int` on the loop count: a bound ≥ 2⁶³ silently runs the loop zero times, and a larger one hangs the compiler
Runtime-proved. `anf_lower.go:1722-1725`. Bound `9223372036854775808n` → `OP_0 OP_0 OP_NUMEQUAL`,
the loop body emitted **zero** times, silently. Bound `9999999999999999999999n` → compiler exceeds
25 s with no output. Bound `100000n` → unrolls 100,000 iterations; **there is no upper bound at
all.** `input_limits.go:15` caps only source bytes.

...
**Not webapp-local: the same missing cap exists in `runar compile`.** This is CL-BUG-194 (Go) and
CL-GAP-117 (Python) reaching a network-exposed surface.

items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description:
[CL-BUG-231] ## CL-BUG-231 — HIGH / P1 — A full-sweep frontend run finds 6 Python and 3 Ruby failures across all 667 example contracts
The worker ran the Python frontend over **all 667** `.runar.*` files and the Ruby compiler's full
pipeline over the same 667. Failures: the Python tier cannot parse Rust `[T; N]` array syntax
(`[[Bigint; 2]; 2]`, `[Bigint; 9]`); neither Python nor Ruby can parse single-argument
`FixedArray<T>` in `.runar.java`; the Python tier's Solidity parser emits an auto-generated
constructor **without `super()`** for `BoundedCounter.runar.sol`, which Ruby and TS both accept.
**All four parse failures are `*.v2` FixedArray contracts — exactly the family with zero conformance
fixtures.** The `*.v1` peers in the same directories parse in both tiers.
**664 of 667 pass Ruby's full pipeline and 661 of 667 pass Python's frontend** — a strong clean
result that makes the six failures precise rather than diffuse.

...
   *cross-tier* coverage.** CL-GAP-115 is corrected accordingly — and CL-BUG-231 shows the gap is
   load-bearing rather than academic.
3. **F16 sharpened, one part refuted.** `MultiSig2of3` *does* have meaningful tests — real Bitcoin
   Script through `ScriptVM` with real secp256k1 in ts, and three each in sol/move. What is vacuous
   is only the ANF-interpreter test. **The real gap is worse and different**: no test at all in five
   tiers.
4. **F17 confirmed with exact per-surface figures**, and the worker's independently computed Zig
   figure of 18 untested directories **matches the prior sub-report's 18** — a useful cross-check
   that the detection rule is right.

---

verification.evidence: Full-pipeline sweep (parse → validate → typecheck → expand_fixed_arrays → anf_lower) over all 767 current .runar.* files under examples/ via the Ruby compiler finds only 1 failure (examples/zig/tic-tac-toe/TicTacToe.runar.zig — an unrelated 'property initializer must be a literal value' validate error), none of the three originally-reported Ruby failure modes. The specific fixtures behind the java/FixedArray failures — TicTacToe.v2.runar.java and Grid2x2.v2.runar.java — no longer exist: commit b6e63ec9 ('N-122 java: FixedArray is unsupported on the Java surface — withdraw it') removed them, noting they 'were rejected by all seven compilers from the day they landed' (not just Python/Ruby) and that FixedArray-on-Java is permanently unsupported (docs/formats/java.md:157-189), not a parser bug.
verification.fixed_by: b6e63ec9 N-122: withdrew the two invalid *.v2.runar.java FixedArray fixtures that produced the java-related failures.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Was accurate for the Ruby portion at the reviewed commit; the underlying invalid fixtures were subsequently withdrawn as out-of-scope rather than the parsers being fixed. items.title: `/api/compile` is a one-request process kill, and the missing cap is in the compiler
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-254] ## CL-BUG-254 — MEDIUM-HIGH / P1 — `/api/compile` is a one-request process kill, and the missing cap is in the compiler
`webapp/main.go:523` decodes with a bare `json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req)` — no
`http.MaxBytesReader`, no `io.LimitReader`, and the zero-value `ListenAndServe` with no timeouts.
Loop bodies are **unrolled** at ANF lowering, and `compilers/go/frontend/validator.go:914-918`
requires only that the bound be a *literal* — **no cap on the count**. A ~60-byte body
`for (let i = 0n; i < 99999999999n; i++) {}` passes validate and typecheck, then unrolls ~10¹¹ times.
**Not webapp-local: the same missing cap exists in `runar compile`.** This is CL-BUG-194 (Go) and
CL-GAP-117 (Python) reaching a network-exposed surface.

verification.evidence: examples/end2end-example/webapp/main.go now bounds all three vectors the finding named: maxCompileBodyBytes = 1<<20 enforced via `r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, maxCompileBodyBytes)` (:583) before json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req) in handleCompile; server-level ReadTimeout/ReadHeaderTimeout/WriteTimeout/IdleTimeout are all set (~:38-40, :134-136) instead of a zero-value http.ListenAndServe; and the compile call is wrapped in context.WithTimeout(r.Context(), compileTimeout) (compileTimeout = 10s, :623, with an error path at :640) so a pathological compile cannot hold the handler goroutine forever. Separately, the underlying loop-unroll-count root cause is the same one fixed for V453/CL-BUG-194 (ir.MaxLoopCount = 10000, R-013), so the ~10^11-iteration input this finding constructs now fails fast inside the compiler itself.

items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']

[CL-GAP-094] ## CL-GAP-094 — HIGH — The release path publishes with zero tests run
**Dispatcher-verified.** Source: ci-scripts-tools SCRIPT-2. `scripts/release.sh` read in full.

The documented release command (`pnpm run release`) runs, in order: `bump-version.sh` → `pnpm run build` + `cargo build --release` (`:29-30`) → `git add -A`/`commit` (`:36-37`) → `git tag` ×3 (`:42-44`) → `git push` (`:50-51`) → `scripts/publish-all.sh` (`:56`).

It never runs `pnpm test`, `test:all`, `test:ci`, the conformance suite, or `bump-version.sh --check`. `publish-all.sh`'s pre-flight checks are authentication and tool presence only — it does not consult CI status for the tag. So nothing between `pnpm run release 1.0.0` and packages reaching npm/crates.io/PyPI asserts that a single test passes.

For a compiler whose output controls funds, this is the least-guarded path in the repository.

The same worker reports (not independently verified by me) that the path is also *broken*: `bump-version.sh:414-419` already commits and tags, so `release.sh:36-37`'s commit against a clean tree exits 1 under `set -euo pipefail`. Both claims point the same way — the release path is not exercised.

verification.evidence: scripts/release.sh at HEAD (412 lines) is a full rewrite from what the finding describes: Step 1 (toolchains), Step 2 (build), and Step 3 (Verify: `pnpm run lint:silent-skips`, `pnpm run typecheck`, `gate_conformance_golden` — the 7-tier golden suite with count-asserted summary parsing, `gate_script_size`, and `pnpm run test:all`) all run and are asserted (via `assert_conformance_summary`/`assert_script_size_summary`, which reject a missing Summary line or a short passed-count) BEFORE Step 4 (`bump-version.sh`, which owns commit+tag) even runs. The file's own header explicitly documents and fixes the exact double-commit/double-tag bug the finding describes ('bump-version.sh OWNS git add -A, git commit and git tag ... This script must NOT repeat them. It used to, and under set -euo pipefail the duplicate git commit exits 1 ...').

Only after both checks pass does the loop do `proof.subarray(i*32, (i+1)*32)`. items.description:
[CL-BUG-052] 3. **CL-BUG-052 (Java compiler emits no deployable artifact).**
   `grep -rn "constructorSlots" compilers/java/src/main/` returns exactly ONE line, and it is a
   javadoc comment in PlaceholderOp.java:8. No abi, no codeSeparatorIndex, no slot table.
   Emit.java:285/287 hard-code `00` for PlaceholderOp and PushCodeSepIndexOp with no back-patch.
4. **CL-GAP-070 (Java Zig/Ruby parsers emit an EMPTY else-list where TS/Go emit null).**
   ZigParser.java:1053 `elseBranch == null ? List.of() : elseBranch` vs the consumer
   AnfLower.java:791 `is.elseBody() == null`. The early-return-nesting rewrite therefore never
   fires for .runar.zig / .runar.rb, so those surfaces lower to different ANF than .runar.ts.
5. **CL-BUG-053 (six parsers silently turn a leading-zero decimal into 0).**
   I ran Python's own semantics: int('0123', 0) raises ValueError; five call sites swallow it
   and return 0, one (Zig) has no try at all. Rust and Java use base 10 and return 123.
   The same literal means two different numbers depending on the surface format.
6. **CL-GAP-071 (Go-DSL `x += 1` compiles to `x = 1`) is REAL but currently LATENT.**
   parser_gocontract.go:432-457 confirmed: only token.DEFINE is special-cased, every compound
   assignment falls to the plain-assignment arm. I then checked blast radius myself:
       grep for compound assignment in **/*.runar.go across examples/ + conformance/  -> 0 files
       grep for bitwise compound assignment in **/*.runar.ts                          -> 0 files
   So no shipped contract exercises it and conformance is legitimately green. It is a live trap
   for the next contributor, not an active miscompile. Severity stays HIGH; priority annotated
   "latent — zero current blast radius".

items.title: extractSequence/extractLocktime BIN2NUM without sign-pad; recommended sequence guard is a tautology
items.confidence_note: raised by GK; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'CX']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [GK-BUG-012] extractSequence splits 4 LE bytes then OP_BIN2NUM with no unsigned sign-pad. BIP-143 nSequence 0xffffffff is ff ff ff ff; Bitcoin script numbers treat the last-byte high bit as sign, so BIN2NUM yields a large negative. The compiler-recommended guard assert(extractSequence(this.txPreimage) < 0xffffffffn) therefore compares a negative to 4294967295 and is always true. nLockTime is not consensus-enforced when all inputs are final. OP_PUSH_TX itself pads a 0x00 sign byte before BIN2NUM for z; extractors do not. Interpreter mocks return unsigned values, so TestContract cannot see the tautology.

evidence.GK-BUG-012: Opened 05-stack-lower.ts:4066-4097 (extractSequence ends OP_BIN2NUM, no CAT of 0x00). Opened 02-validate.ts:1122-1127 (warning text recommends extractSequence < 0xffffffffn). Opened oppushtx-codegen.ts:117-120 (HASH256 path does pad 0x00 then BIN2NUM).

remediation.GK-BUG-012: Pad 4-byte unsigned extractor fields with 0x00 before BIN2NUM (same as z), or compare raw 4 bytes to ffffffff. Change the H2 recommended assertion so it is actually false for 0xffffffff on-chain. Add a ScriptVM test with nSequence=0xffffffff that asserts the numeric TOS.

testable_assertion.GK-BUG-012: Compiled extractSequence of a preimage with nSequence=0xffffffff must not satisfy < 0xffffffffn on ScriptVM; today it does (negative < 2^32-1). After the pad, TOS is 4294967295 and the comparison is false.

items.title: Oversize Point (G‖extra) is on-curve as G and ecEncodeCompressed of it is −G
items.confidence_note: raised by GK; silent-but-inspected: ['CL']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description: [GK-BUG-027] Point is a branded ByteString with no on-chain length gate. decomposePoint OP_SPLITs at 32 then emitReverse32 peels 32 bytes and drops the rest, so a 65-byte push G‖0x01 is accepted by ecOnCurve as canonical G. emitEcEncodeCompressed does not use that decoder: it SPLITs at 32, then SIZE/1 SUB/SPLIT to take the last byte of the y slice as parity. For G‖0x01 that last byte is 0x01 (odd) → prefix 0x03 concatenated with Gx, which is compressed −G. Honest G compresses to 02‖Gx (Gy last byte 0xB8, even). A contract that assert(ecOnCurve(pt)); assert(ecEncodeCompressed(pt) == committedMinusG) then adds pt has accepted a point that encodes as −G and adds as G. Interpreter ecDecodePoint throws on length!==64, so the differential oracle never sees this. Undersize aborts (OP_SPLIT), so ecOnCurve is not a boolean for malformed length.

evidence.GK-BUG-027: Opened decomposePoint 299-317 + emitReverse32 373-396 (32 peels, drop rest). Opened emitEcEncodeCompressed 1045-1068 (last byte of y slice for parity).

remediation.GK-BUG-027: Emit a branch-free OP_SIZE==64 flag and BOOLAND it into ecOnCurve; make encode and add/mul abort or clamp consistently to 64 bytes. Pin ScriptVM: G‖0x01 must not compress as −G while remaining on-curve.

testable_assertion.GK-BUG-027: ScriptVM of ecOnCurve(G‖0x01) is true and ecEncodeCompressed(G‖0x01) equals compressed −G today. After the fix either both reject or both treat it as G.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/ec-codegen.ts:334-395 (`emitPointLenVerify` / `emitPointLengthGate`, both explicitly labelled "CL-BUG-095") now gate every Point consumer's width; `decomposePoint` (line 452-458) calls `emitPointLenVerify(e, 64)` before splitting, so a 65-byte `G 65` blob now ABORTS rather than silently dropping the surplus byte. `emitEcOnCurve` (1347-1410) uses the clamping form so the predicate stays total and ANDs the length flag into the boolean result; `emitEcEncodeCompressed` (1433-1442) calls `emitPointLenVerify(emit, 64)` first and reads the parity byte from a fixed offset (comment explicitly describes the exact −G-forgery bug this closes). A second gate, `emitCoordCanonVerify` (398-446, R-117), additionally rejects non-canonical coordinates ≥ p.

items.title: Fixed-array rewriting drops expression-form asm return types
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [CX-BUG-038] Both call rewriting and expression cloning rebuild `CallExpr` through the two-argument constructor, resetting `asmReturnType` to null. Because fixed-array expansion precedes type checking, an unrelated fixed-array property can turn `asm<ByteString>` into a void-valued call or make later byte-oriented lowering choose the wrong path.

evidence.CX-BUG-038: Neither reconstruction passes `ce.asmReturnType()`; type checking and byte-expression classification explicitly rely on that field. `rg -n "asmReturnType\(\)" ExpandFixedArrays.java` returned zero matches.

remediation.CX-BUG-038: Preserve the third `CallExpr` component in both rewrite and clone paths.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-038: A contract combining an unrelated fixed array with `const b: ByteString = asm<ByteString>(...)` must type-check and emit the same asm bytes as the equivalent contract without the array.

The only 2-arg `new CallExpr(...)` site in ExpandFixedArrays.java (line ~987, inside `buildWriteDispatchIf`) constructs a synthetic `assert(false)` call from scratch, not a clone/rewrite of an existing asm call, so there is no asmReturnType to preserve there.

items.description:
CL-BUG-239 … CL-GAP-133
- **`scripts/release.sh` cannot complete.** `set -euo pipefail`, then Step 1 calls `bump-version.sh`
  which **already** commits and tags; Steps 3–4 repeat both. Executed: `git commit` on a clean tree
  exits 1; `git tag` on an existing tag exits 128. It aborts **after the local commit and tag exist
  but before push and publish** — a half-released state. And it runs **no test of any kind** between
  bumping and publishing.

items.title: Java compiler CLI exposes no annotated-script/debug output mode of its own (may be intentionally delegated to the repo-level CLI)
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [CX-GAP-013] The Java CLI can emit raw IR, raw hex, and a standalone source-map file, but it exposes no source-line-annotated script or debug command. This may be intentionally provided by the repository-level CLI, but the Java implementation alone does not expose it.

evidence.CX-GAP-013: Exhaustive `rg -n -i "debug|annotat(ed|ion)|source[-_ ]?map|sourcemap" compilers/java` found only source-map plumbing plus incidental “debug” wording; the CLI option list contains no debugger or annotated-script mode.

remediation.CX-GAP-013: Either document the repository-level debugger as the sole supported consumer or add an implementation-level annotated output mode if parity requires one.

testable_assertion.CX-GAP-013: If implementation-level parity is required, invoking the documented Java debug/annotated-output flag must produce source-annotated script output.

dedup_uncertain: yes: the finding's own text says this may be intentional (repo-level CLI provides the debugger); real defect status is uncertain and there is nothing else in this batch to corroborate or refute it.

verification.evidence: Cli.java's flag dispatch (~936-960) confirms the factual claim — there is no --debug/--annotated flag, only --hex/--emit-ir/--emit-ir-to/--emit-source-map/--emit-artifact/--parse-only. But this is not a Java-specific gap: the Go CLI (compilers/go/main.go) and the Rust CLI (compilers/rust/src/main.rs), checked directly, ALSO expose no source-annotated/debug flag — both only support --parse-only/--emit-ir/--emit-ir-to-style flags, the same shape as Java. The repository-level `runar debug` command (packages/runar-cli/src/bin.ts:90, wired to commands/debug.ts) is the sole place this capability lives across the whole project, and it works directly against the TS compiler/ScriptVM rather than shelling out per-tier. So Java's CLI is at parity with its peer NATIVE-tier CLIs (Go, Rust), and the finding's own text already flagged this as possibly intentional.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Factually correct about what Java's CLI exposes, but the implied cross-tier gap does not hold: Go and Rust — checked directly — have the identical shape, so this is consistent, by-design project architecture rather than a Java-specific defect.

items.title: Conformance gate builds the Zig compiler `-Doptimize=ReleaseFast`; CI builds `ReleaseSafe` — the byte-parity-graded binary is not the CI-tested binary
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-GAP-098] ## CL-GAP-098 — HIGH / P1 — The conformance gate builds the Zig compiler `ReleaseFast`; CI builds it `ReleaseSafe`
**Dispatcher-verified.** Source: impl-zig-passes depth N-5. `conformance/runner/index.ts:435-441` passes `-Doptimize=ReleaseFast`; every CI step uses `-Doptimize=ReleaseSafe`, with `ci.yml:533-536` explicitly noting ReleaseSafe *"keeps overflow + bounds"* checks. Both write to the same `zig-out`, **so the binary the parity suite grades is not the binary CI built.**

This changes the failure mode of every unchecked narrowing cast in the tier: `stack_lower.zig:1250` (i128→i64) and `ec_optimizer.zig:369/376` (u256→i128) **panic** under the CI binary and **silently emit a truncated constant** under the conformance binary. The gate that decides byte-parity is the one configuration where overflow produces wrong bytes instead of aborting.

verification.evidence: conformance/runner/index.ts:466 `zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast` does exist inside `prebuildAllCompilers()`, but that function only runs `if (opts.prebuild)` (index.ts:~250), gated by the CLI flag `--prebuild` or `RUNAR_PREBUILD=1`. Neither appears anywhere in .github/workflows/ci.yml (grep: zero hits) — confirmed identical at the reviewed commit 2b3af765 (also zero hits). CI's actual conformance job (ci.yml:839 job `conformance:`) never calls `prebuildAllCompilers` — it downloads the `runar-zig` artifact built by the separate `zig-compiler` job (ci.yml:593-641), whose 'Build release binary' step runs `zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe -Dtarget=x86_64-linux-gnu -Dcpu=baseline`, with an explicit comment: 'ReleaseFast was SIGILL-ing on heavier conformance fixtures on the conformance runner ... ReleaseSafe keeps overflow + bounds checks.' So the binary CI's parity gate actually grades IS the ReleaseSafe binary that CI built; the ReleaseFast code path is a documented local-dev convenience ('dev loops should pass --prebuild') never exercised by CI, then or now. The reviewer conflated the opt-in dev path with the CI-run gate.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: inaccurate — the --prebuild ReleaseFast path is opt-in and never invoked by CI; the CI conformance job downloads a separately-built ReleaseSafe artifact. Same was true at the reviewed commit.
