items.title: Ruby: FixedArray runtime reads have no bounds check; out-of-range/negative index silently aliases the last element instead of failing
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [CX-BUG-076] Both statement and expression rewrites initialize the result from the last slot and conditionally replace it only for indices `0..length-2`. Negative, equal-to-length, and arbitrarily large indices therefore alias the last element instead of failing closed; writes have an explicit terminal assertion, so read/write behavior is inconsistent.

evidence.CX-BUG-076: The read chains at lines 631-685 and 688-710 have no bounds assertion; the direct test at `compilers/ruby/test/test_expand_fixed_arrays.rb:211-246` explicitly expects the fallback-to-last behavior.

remediation.CX-BUG-076: Add explicit `0 <= index < length` enforcement before selecting a slot, consistently for expression and statement contexts.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-076: Executing a runtime FixedArray read with `index == length` fails rather than returning the final element.

verification.evidence: compilers/ruby/lib/runar_compiler/frontend/expand_fixed_arrays.rb:812-832 build_read_dispatch_ternary seeds the ternary chain from meta.slot_names.last and only conditionally replaces it for indices 0..length-2 (comment at :809-811 states 'runtime reads do NOT bounds-check in this form'); try_rewrite_read_as_statements (:755-807) does the same for statement-position reads. Contrast build_write_dispatch_if (:881-914), whose terminal else is an explicit assert(false).
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Cited range 631-710 is off (actual mechanism is at :749-832 / :755-807); the described read/write asymmetry is accurate.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Executing a runtime FixedArray read with `index == length` fails rather than returning the final element.
items.status_reason: BY DESIGN — user gate decision 2026-09-22 (D1: keep documented v1 semantics; spec/grammar.md:325-334).

items.title: TS: isSubtype's 'both in the ByteString family -> compatible' rule makes every nominal byte-domain type (PubKey, Sig, Sha256, Addr, Point, ...) mutually interchangeable, defeating nominal crypto typing
items.confidence_note: raised by CX+GK; silent-but-inspected: ['CL']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.severity_note: reviewers disagreed ['HIGH', 'MEDIUM']; highest taken per §6.2 (no downgrade justified at combination time)
items.description:
[CX-BUG-103] `isSubtype` is symmetric between `ByteString` and every nominal byte subtype and also declares any two byte-family subtypes compatible. Consequently a `ByteString`, `Sha256`, or `Addr` is accepted where `checkSig` requires `Sig` or `PubKey`, defeating the source language’s nominal crypto types. Runtime opcodes may later reject some malformed encodings, but the compiler’s advertised type boundary is absent.

[GK-GAP-002] isSubtype returns true whenever both sides are in BYTESTRING_SUBTYPES, which includes PubKey, Sig, Point, P256Point, P384Point, Addr, etc. A Sig is assignable to a PubKey parameter. Zig pipeline worker reported the same bidirectional family rule.

evidence.CX-BUG-103: Lines 262-266 permit both directions and every cross-family pairing; builtin declarations at lines 72-73 require nominal `Sig`/`PubKey` types; argument checking delegates to `isSubtype` at lines 1924-1935.
evidence.GK-GAP-002: Opened 03-typecheck.ts:265-266 (Both in the ByteString family -> compatible).

remediation.CX-BUG-103: Make nominal types covariant only toward `ByteString`; do not accept generic or unrelated byte types where a specific crypto domain type is required. Add explicit casts/construction APIs if intentional reinterpretation is needed.
remediation.GK-GAP-002: Allow subtype → ByteString and documented aliases (Addr/Ripemd160), not sibling-to-sibling Sig ↔ PubKey.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-103: `checkSig(rawBytes: ByteString, digest: Sha256)` must produce type errors for both arguments.
testable_assertion.GK-GAP-002: checkSig(pk, sig) with swapped argument types currently typechecks; it should error.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/03-typecheck.ts:243-246 (`BYTESTRING_SUBTYPES = {ByteString, PubKey, Sig, Sha256, Ripemd160, Addr, SigHashPreimage, Point, P256Point, P384Point}`) and :298 inside `isSubtype`: `if (BYTESTRING_SUBTYPES.has(actual) && BYTESTRING_SUBTYPES.has(expected)) return true;` (comment: 'Both in the ByteString family -> compatible (e.g. Addr and Ripemd160)'). `checkSig`'s declared signature is `params: ['Sig', 'PubKey']` (line 73) and argument checking goes through `isSubtype`, so a `Sig` typechecks where `PubKey` is expected and vice versa, and a bare `ByteString`, `Sha256`, or `Addr` typechecks anywhere `Sig`/`PubKey` is expected.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Both CX-BUG-103 and GK-GAP-002 accurately describe the code; unchanged since the reviewed commit.

items.testable_assertion_verified: `checkSig(rawBytes: ByteString, digest: Sha256)` — a call with both arguments of the wrong nominal type but the right byte-family — must produce type errors for both arguments; at HEAD it typechecks cleanly.
items.status_reason: Prior user decision (previous remediation run, "USER DECISIONS #2 — Length discipline → KEEP PERMISSIVE"): ByteString-family mutual assignability is a documented language property, not a defect.

items.title: Every stateful contract's auto-injected checkPreimage binding emits OP_2MUL, a pre-Chronicle-disabled opcode; unspendable on BSV mainnet below Chronicle activation height 943,816
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-112] ## CL-BUG-112 — CRITICAL / P0 — **Every Rúnar stateful contract is unspendable on BSV mainnet below block height 943,816**
**Dispatcher-verified end to end.** Source: integration-all depth INT-001/U2. **This is the headline finding of the review.**

The chain, each link verified by me directly:

1. **Every `StatefulSmartContract` auto-injects `checkPreimage` at method entry** (project design, stated in CLAUDE.md).
2. **`lowerCheckPreimage` emits the OP_PUSH_TX binding block** — `packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/05-stack-lower.ts:3888` calls `emitCheckPreimageBindingRaw`.
3. **That block contains `OP_2MUL`** — `packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/oppushtx-codegen.ts:141`: `e({ op: 'opcode', code: 'OP_2MUL' });`
4. **The byte is in the pinned cross-tier constant** — `compilers/go/codegen/oppushtx.go` contains `…ffffff007c8d7c949594…`, where `8d` = `OP_2MUL`. All seven tiers share it.
5. **`OP_2MUL` is disabled pre-Chronicle** — `go-sdk` `interpreter/thread.go:163` returns `ErrDisabledOpcode` unless `afterChronicle`.
6. **Chronicle activates on BSV mainnet at height 943,816** — verified in the pinned dependency `go-chaincfg/params.go:277` (`ChronicleActivationHeight: 943816`), in the MainNet block. Unlike the test-network entries at `:395`, `:476`, `:653`, `:733`, the mainnet value carries **no** *"temporary and subject to change"* caveat.

**Therefore: deploys succeed and every spend fails.** Funds sent to any Rúnar stateful contract on mainnet below that height are locked until activation.

Also affected, via the same disabled-opcode mechanism: the EC family (`ec-codegen.ts:236,901,907` — `SchnorrZKP`, `ConvergenceProof`, `ECDemo`, every `ec_isolation` test), Merkle (`merkle-codegen.ts:106,109`), NIST P-256/P-384 (`p256-p384-codegen.ts:181,911,916` — `P256Wallet`, `P384

verification.evidence: The finding's own premise is stale/wrong even at CL's review time (8937c1ad, 2026-09-07) and doubly so at HEAD. docs/audit/upstream-bsv-sdk-op2mul-chronicle.md states 'Status: STILL PRESENT — and it is NOT an upstream defect' and explains OP_2MUL/OP_2DIV in OP_PUSH_TX are a DELIBERATE Chronicle-profile target, not a bug — 'Upstream is not wrong; it is targeting a different node.' docs/language-reference.md:390 states OP_RSHIFTNUM 'arrived with the BSV Chronicle upgrade, live on mainnet since block 943,816 (7 April 2026)' — mainnet passed the cited activation height five months before HEAD. Most decisively: CL's OWN ledger (runar-audit/claude-main-8937c1ad/findings/ID-LEDGER.md:1292) contains a self-correction dated 2026-09-21: 'CL-BUG-112 — WITHDRAWN (owner decision, 2026-09-21). Not a defect. The project owner states that Chronicle-dependence is by design... Severity → none. Remove from the P0 list.'
verification.fixed_by: Not a code fix (nothing to fix — by-design). The adjacent disclosure gap (undocumented Chronicle dependence, tracked as CL-BUG-137) was addressed by commit 6321feb4 ('R-014: disclose the Chronicle opcode-policy requirement'), which added the Chronicle-live-since-7-April-2026 language to docs/language-reference.md and other user-facing docs, plus tests/chronicle-opcode-disclosure.test.ts.
verification.tier_correction: Tagged compiler:go but the actual substance is cross-cutting (compiler codegen for all 7 tiers + docs) — Go isn't specifically implicated over the others.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: The technical chain (OP_2MUL present, disabled pre-Chronicle, mainnet activation height 943,816) was independently verified as accurate by both CL's own dispatcher and by this worker — but the severity/defect classification was wrong: it ignored that the project deliberately targets a post-Chronicle profile and that mainnet has already passed that height. CL itself flagged this as its single biggest 'evidence right, severity mine to get wrong' lesson and withdrew it.

items.status_reason: R1: Chronicle activated on BSV mainnet at 943,816 on 2026-04-07 (docs/chronicle-opcode-policy.md:10, spec/opcodes.md:500); the dependency is the declared target profile and its disclosure was closed by R-014 (6321feb4).

items.title: SHA2-256f tree-index mask computed as 1<<(h-hp) with h-hp=64: Java's `1L << 64` (JLS shift-mod-64) zeros idx_tree; Rust release builds mask identically via LLVM shift-count masking; Go's unsigned conversion instead yields all-ones
items.confidence_note: raised by GK; silent-but-inspected: ['CL']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description: [GK-BUG-016] SHA2-256f has h=68, hp=4, so h-hp=64. Java `1L << 64` is `1L << 0` (JLS shift mod 64), mask 0, treeIdx always 0 (SlhDsa.java:575). Rust `1u64 << 64`: debug panics; release LLVM masks count so result is 1, then -1 = 0 — same always-zero as Java (slh_dsa.rs:831). Go `1 << uint(64)` on int is 0, then -1, converted to uint64 all-ones (no clip) (slh_dsa.go:688). Java-SDK 256f signatures therefore use tree 0; on-chain verify uses the digest's real 64-bit idx_tree. Combined with GK-BUG-013 (a=8 vs FIPS a=9).

evidence.GK-BUG-016: Opened SlhDsa.java:54-55 and :575. Opened slh_dsa.rs:91-94 and :831. Opened slh_dsa.go:684-688. SLH-DSA depth: Rust release is zero-mask not MAX (LLVM shift-count mask), matching Java.

remediation.GK-BUG-016: Mask with a 64-bit-safe construct (if bits>=64, mask is all ones / skip). Add a 256f test that idx_tree is not identically 0 after Hmsg.

testable_assertion.GK-BUG-016: Java SlhDsa sign of SHA2-256f produces treeIdx==0 always today; after the fix it matches Go's unmasked 64-bit value, and both match FIPS once a=9 is fixed.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-java/src/main/java/runar/lang/runtime/SlhDsa.java:594,665: `treeIdx &= (1L << (params.h - hp)) - 1`. For SHA2-256f, h-hp=64; JLS 15.19 defines long shift counts mod 64, so `1L<<64` == `1L<<0` == 1L, mask=0, treeIdx forced to 0 always. packages/runar-rs/src/slh_dsa.rs:874,971: `tree_idx &= (1u64 << (params.h - hp)) - 1` — a release build's LLVM lowering masks the out-of-range shift count the same way, giving the same mask=0 result (debug builds panic instead, per Rust's overflow checks). packages/runar-go/slh_dsa.go:688,705 computes `(1 << uint(params.H-hp)) - 1` where the untyped constant 1 is promoted to uint64 by context: `uint64(1)<<64` is well-defined-zero in Go (no panic), then `0-1` wraps to all-ones (also well-defined, unsigned wraparound), so `treeIdx &= all-ones` is a no-op — Go's SHA2-256f treeIdx is unmasked and correct, not broken.
verification.tier_correction: The batch's tier ('sdk:go') is wrong for the actual defect. packages/runar-go/slh_dsa.go is NOT affected — its wraparound arithmetic coincidentally produces the correct all-ones mask. The real bug lives in sdk:java (always) and sdk:rust (release builds only); Rust debug builds panic instead, a separate and milder defect.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate on mechanism and on the Java/Rust code, and the description text itself correctly characterizes Go's divergent (correct) behavior — but the batch's tier assignment and Go file citation put Go alongside the two actually-broken tiers, which misleads at a glance.

Same assertion against a Rust *release* build (`cargo test --release`) of packages/runar-rs.
items.status_reason: Tier wrong and Go is correct: Go shift wraparound yields the right all-ones mask; the Java and Rust instances have their own items (V264/V265).

items.title: Runtime FixedArray element reads silently alias any out-of-range index to the final array slot
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [CX-BUG-101] Both statement-form and expression-form runtime reads initialize or terminate their dispatch with the final legal slot. Negative indices and indices greater than or equal to the array length therefore read the last element instead of failing. An attacker-controlled selector can make authorization or state logic operate on a different element from the one named by the input.

evidence.CX-BUG-101: Lines 567-570 explicitly state that out-of-range indices fall through to the final slot. Lines 934-951 admit the ternary path also returns the last slot, is wrong, has no emitted bounds assertion, and currently has no test relying on runtime reads.

remediation.CX-BUG-101: Emit a mandatory `0 <= index < length` assertion before every runtime read, including reads nested inside larger expressions. Do not place a legal array element in the invalid-index fallback.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-101: A two-element FixedArray contract invoked with indices `-1` and `2` must fail instead of returning element `1`.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/03b-expand-fixed-arrays.ts:970-974, verbatim: "Deliberately matches the ternary-form behaviour: runtime reads do NOT bounds-check, callers must assert(i < N) if they care. This is Deviation 2 from the original plan and stands by design so v1 TicTacToe semantics are preserved." The statement-form dispatch builder (:1015-1021, :1020-1057) sets `fallbackInit`/the final `else` fallthrough to the LAST slot (`board__{N-1}`) and only overrides it for in-range indices 0..N-2, so any index that fails every `===` check (negative, or >= N) silently keeps the last-slot value. The same fallback pattern governs the ternary expression-form reader referenced in the same comment block.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: accurate; the code contains an explicit in-repo comment acknowledging this exact behavior as an intentional, documented v1 design decision (not an unnoticed bug) — worth noting for triage/severity discussion, but the security-relevant consequence for un-asserted callers is real as described.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile a StatefulSmartContract with a 2-element FixedArray property whose public method does `return this.board[i]` for a caller-supplied index `i` with NO explicit `assert(i < N)`; call it with `i = -1n` and `i = 2n`; assert both invocations FAIL rather than returning `board[1]` (today's actual last-slot fallback behavior).
items.status_reason: BY DESIGN — user gate decision 2026-09-22 (D1: keep documented v1 semantics; spec/grammar.md:325-334).

items.description: [CX-BUG-066] Both statement and expression rewrites initialize their dispatch with the last valid slot and compare only indexes `0..N-2`. Negative and over-range attacker-controlled indexes therefore read a valid but incorrect element instead of failing.

evidence.CX-BUG-066: The code and docstring explicitly say runtime reads do not bounds-check; `fallback_init` is `slot_names[n - 1]` and the ternary alternate is `slot_names[-1]`.

remediation.CX-BUG-066: Emit a lower- and upper-bound assertion before runtime read dispatch, matching the fail-closed runtime write path.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-066: A method reading `self.board[idx]` must fail for `idx=-1` and `idx=len(board)` rather than return `board[-1]`.

verification.evidence: compilers/python/runar_compiler/frontend/expand_fixed_arrays.py:780 (statement-form fallback_init = meta.slot_names[n-1]) and :818-820 (_build_read_dispatch_ternary terminal branch = meta.slot_names[-1]); dispatch only compares indexes 0..N-2 (range(n-2,-1,-1) at :779 / range(len-2,-1,-1) at :821). A runtime index that matches none of those (negative or >= N-1) falls through to the last-slot value in both the statement and ternary read paths, with no bounds assertion. NOTE: this is not accidental — the module docstring (:21-24) and the function docstring (:753-756) both state 'runtime reads do NOT bounds-check ... matches the TS spike semantics by design', and the TS reference (packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/03b-expand-fixed-arrays.ts:971-974) carries the identical rule with an explicit 'Do not fix this without also updating the ternary fallback path and the grammar spec.' So the behavior is real and reachable exactly as described, but it is a deliberate, documented, cross-tier language-semantics decision, not a Python-only slip — closing it (if desired) is a spec-level change affecting all 7 tiers, not a Python bugfix.

items.description: [CX-BUG-085] Literal out-of-range indexes are rejected, and runtime writes fail closed, but runtime reads use the last array slot as their unconditional fallback. items.description: [CX-BUG-032] `PUSH 0; OP_ADD`, `PUSH 0; OP_SUB`, and double `OP_NEGATE` are removed without constraining the producer or later consumer. Bitcoin numeric opcodes parse and validate ScriptNum encodings and normalize their result; deleting them can allow an oversized/noncanonical byte vector to bypass the original failure or preserve a distinct byte encoding.

evidence.CX-BUG-032: The three unconditional removal rules are at lines 192-199. Tests only assert their structural removal at `PeepholeTest.java:59-89`; unlike double-NOT, no producer-safety guard exists.

remediation.CX-BUG-032: Remove these rules unless numeric provenance and value-only downstream use are proven, or retain a normalization/validation opcode sequence.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-032: A noncanonical or oversized ScriptNum followed by `PUSH 0; OP_ADD` must have identical failure behavior with peephole enabled and disabled.

verification.evidence: compilers/java/src/main/java/runar/compiler/passes/Peephole.java:195,197,201: `PUSH 0, OP_ADD -> identity` (return List.of()), `PUSH 0, OP_SUB -> identity`, `OP_NEGATE, OP_NEGATE -> remove both` — all three fire unconditionally with no check on the producer's ScriptNum canonicality, unlike the neighboring `OP_NOT, OP_NOT` rule (:246-255) which is explicitly gated on 'only fires when that producer provably yields a canonical 0/1' with `isCanonicalBoolProducer`. CROSS-TIER: identical unconditional rule exists in Go (compilers/go/codegen/optimizer.go:129-130, comment 'PUSH 0, OP_ADD -> remove both (x + 0 = x)'), so this is not Java-specific.
verification.tier_correction: Cross-tier (at minimum Go shares the identical unconditional rule) — not a Java-only gap, though verified only for Java + Go here.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Accurate mechanism; the practical exploitability depends on whether any codegen path can ever produce a non-canonical operand ahead of these opcodes, which was not established either way.

items.testable_assertion_verified: A stack producer that pushes a non-canonical/oversized ScriptNum byte vector (e.g. a 5+ byte, non-minimally-encoded number) followed by `PUSH 0; OP_ADD` must exhibit identical execution behavior (success/failure and resulting stack) whether the peephole optimizer is enabled or disabled; today OP_ADD's ScriptNum decode/validate is silently skipped when the rule fires.

[CL-BUG-116] ## CL-BUG-116 — MEDIUM / P1 — `push0-add-elim` / `push0-sub-elim` / `negate-negate-elim` delete a runtime operand-validity check, widening the accept set
**Source:** impl-ts-optimizers depth NEW-04. **Dispatcher-verified.**
All three matchers (`peephole.ts:157-165`, `:170-178`, `:216-224`) `return []` with **no producer
check**, in contrast to the documented C17 producer-provenance guard at `:181-211` that exists for
exactly this hazard. `OP_ADD`/`OP_SUB`/`OP_NEGATE` do not merely normalise an operand — they *reject*
one that is not a valid script number (over the numeric length limit, or non-minimal under
`SCRIPT_VERIFY_MINIMALDATA`, a standard relay flag). Deleting the pair removes the rejection.
The exhaustive sweep cannot see it: `__tests__/peephole-exhaustive.test.ts` builds witnesses only as
`{op:'push', value: bigint}`, always canonically encoded.
**Severity is bounded deliberately:** this *widens* the accept set. The worker states, and I agree on
the evidence presented, that no path was found where the widened set is itself a spend. Record at
MEDIUM with the mechanism HIGH-confidence and the exploitability MEDIUM.

...
- `OP_NEGATE` appears in no golden, so the `negate-negate-elim` peephole rule of **CL-BUG-116** can
  never fire on any corpus fixture. Its "the exhaustive sweep cannot see it" claim is now joined by
  "and neither can the golden corpus."
- `OP_SHA1` and `OP_RIPEMD160` appearing in no golden matches **CL-GAP-083**'s independent finding
  that `sha1` has zero conformance coverage and is not implemented in some tiers at all.

**Characterisation, not a finding, recorded so a later reader does not re-raise it:** the smallest
golden is `conformance/tests/asm-raw-script/expected-script.hex`, one byte, `51` = `OP_1` — a script
any unlocking script spends

[CX-BUG-095] `x PUSH_0 OP_ADD`, `x PUSH_0 OP_SUB`, and `x OP_NEGATE OP_NEGATE` are deleted as algebraic identities. The original opcodes decode and canonicalize ScriptNums and can reject malformed or oversized numeric encodings; the replacement leaves attacker-supplied witness bytes untouched. Double negation also canonicalizes negative zero/non-minimal numeric representations, so deletion can change downstream byte equality or state serialization even where decoding does not abort.

evidence.CX-BUG-095: Runtime rules return `[]` at `peephole.ts:160-161`, `173-174`, and `219-220`. The equivalence domain contains only canonically emitted `bigint` pushes, not malformed, negative-zero, non-minimal, or over-limit byte encodings (`peephole-exhaustive.test.ts:33-41`).

remediation.CX-BUG-095: Retain a numeric-normalization operation, or prove the operand was produced by a validating/canonical numeric opcode before applying the rewrite. Extend equivalence tests to raw byte encodings.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-095: For each rule, executing original and optimized scripts with negative-zero, non-minimal, malformed, and over-limit witness encodings must produce identical success and final-stack results.

conflicts: Severity disagreement, not a factual contradiction: CL rates MEDIUM ("widens the accept set" but "no path found where the widened set is itself a spend"), CX rates CRITICAL (frames it as erasing validation with possible byte/state-serialization divergence). Verified current code at packages/runar-compiler/src/optimizer/peephole.ts:154-224 (runar-review-claude-main, 8937c1ad): all three rules do return `[]` unconditionally with no operand check, confirming the shared factual basis; the severity gap is a judgment call for the dispatcher, not a code disagreement.

verification.evidence: packages/runar-compiler/src/optimizer/peephole.ts:154-161 (push0-add-elim: `isPushZero(ops[0]) && isOpcode(ops[1],'OP_ADD') → []`), :167-174 (push0-sub-elim, OP_SUB), and :212-221 (negate-negate-elim: `OP_NEGATE, OP_NEGATE → []`) all delete the opcode pair outright with no producer-provenance check. This is in direct visual contrast with the very next rule in the same file (:180-206, `<canonical-bool producer>, OP_NOT, OP_NOT`), which explicitly gates on `producesCanonicalBool(ops[0])` (the 'C17' guard) for exactly this class of hazard — OP_ADD/OP_SUB/OP_NEGATE reject non-minimal or over-limit ScriptNum encodings, so deleting them widens the accept set for attacker-supplied witness bytes that reach that shape.
verification.conflict_resolution: CL rated this MEDIUM ('widens the accept set... no path found where the widened set is itself a spend') and CX's framing was folded into this CRITICAL-severity cluster. Both cite the same code correctly; the factual basis is identical, so this is a judgment-call severity dispute, not a code disagreement, per the item's own conflicts note. My read leans toward CL's more conservative framing — the removed validation is real and the mechanism is HIGH-confidence, but no concrete forgery/fund-loss path is demonstrated in the evidence gathered here, only a widened accept set. I have not disproven CX's broader byte/state-serialization-divergence claim either; it would need its own differential test (original vs optimized script on adversarial encodings) to settle.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Both CL and CX accurately quoted the code (verified again at HEAD, unchanged since the reviewed commit).

items.testable_assertion_verified: For each of the three rules, execute the pre- and post-peephole scripts (via ScriptVM) against negative-zero, non-minimal, malformed, and over-numeric-limit witness encodings feeding the eliminated opcode; the original script must reject some of these while the optimized script accepts all of them — the two must be required to produce identical success/failure and final-stack results.

[CL-BUG-051] 2. **CL-BUG-051 (SLH-DSA SHA2_256f uses a=8; FIPS 205 requires a=9) — SEVEN-TIER.**
   Found independently by the impl:python:codegen and impl:ts:pipeline workers, who share no
   context. I verified the parameter in four tiers directly:
       packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/slh-dsa-codegen.ts:46  slhMk(32, 68, 17, 8, 35)
       compilers/go/codegen/slh_dsa.go:54                        slhMk(32, 68, 17, 8, 35)
       compilers/python/.../codegen/slh_dsa.py:86                _slh_mk(32, 68, 17, 8, 35)
       compilers/rust/src/codegen/slh_dsa.rs:102                 slh_mk(32, 68, 17, 8, 35)
   and re-derived the FIPS digest length myself:
       256f a=8 -> 44   256f a=9 -> 49 (= FIPS m)   128s -> 30 OK   192s -> 39 OK
   Only 256f is wrong. Consequence: the on-chain length gate rejects every genuine FIPS-205
   SHA2-256f signature, and FORS security drops 315->280 bits. Because all seven tiers carry
   the same value, cross-tier conformance CANNOT detect it. This is the "agreement is not
   correctness" failure mode in its purest form.
3. **CL-BUG-052 (Java compiler emits no deployable artifact).**
   `grep -rn "constructorSlots" compilers/java/src/main/` returns exactly ONE line, and it is a
   javadoc comment in PlaceholderOp.java:8. No abi, no codeSeparatorIndex, no slot table.
   Emit.java:285/287 hard-code `00` for PlaceholderOp and PushCodeSepIndexOp with no back-patch.
4. **CL-GAP-070 (Java Zig/Ruby parsers emit an EMPTY else-list where TS/Go emit null).**
   ZigParser.java:1053 `elseBranch == null ? List.of() : elseBranch` vs the consumer
   AnfLower.java:791 `is.elseBody() == null`. The early-return-nesting rewrite therefore never
   fires for .runar.zig / .runar.rb, so those surfaces lower to different ANF than .runar.ts.
5. **CL-BUG-053 (six parsers silen

[CL-BUG-077] ## CL-BUG-077 — P0 — SLH-DSA-SHA2-256f is built with FIPS 205's `a` parameter wrong in every tier
**Dispatcher-verified, arithmetic independently reproduced.** Source: docs-spec DOC-03; convergent with two earlier workers and four tiers I had already checked.

FIPS 205 Table 2 specifies SLH-DSA-SHA2-256f with FORS tree height **a = 9**. Every tier ships **a = 8**:

```
packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/slh-dsa-codegen.ts:46   'SHA2_256f': slhMk(32, 68, 17, 8, 35)
compilers/go/codegen/slh_dsa.go:54                          "SHA2_256f": slhMk(32, 68, 17, 8, 35)
compilers/rust/src/codegen/slh_dsa.rs:102                   "SHA2_256f" => slh_mk(32, 68, 17, 8, 35)
compilers/python/runar_compiler/codegen/slh_dsa.py:86       "SHA2_256f": _slh_mk(32, 68, 17, 8, 35)
compilers/ruby/.../codegen/slh_dsa.rb:86                    "SHA2_256f" => _slh_mk(32, 68, 17, 8, 35)
compilers/java/.../codegen/SlhDsa.java:138                  "SHA2_256f", slhMk(32, 68, 17, 8, 35)
```

items.description:
[CL-BUG-070] # CL-BUG-070 — CRITICAL, DISPATCHER-VERIFIED, CROSS-TIER
...
## Correction — CL-BUG-070 fixture-coverage wording SUBSTANTIATED
The ledger sentence "zero conformance fixtures declare a state field of any of the four types" appeared to conflict with a probe reporting "9 fixture sources mentioning it". Resolved by re-probing for **mutable state-field declarations** specifically, over all 648 resolved fixture sources: `RabinSig` 0, `RabinPubKey` 0, `P256Point` 0, `P384Point` 0 mutable-state-field declarations. The 9 hits are `readonly` properties, method parameters and type references — not mutable state. **Claim stands as written.**
Scope limit, stated rather than hidden: the probe covered `.runar.ts` sources only. Since every fixture ships the same contract in all nine formats, the contract set is covered; a format-specific state declaration would not be. → Pass E.

...
## CL-BUG-070 (REFRAMED by Pass C — the SHARED TABLE is the outlier, not the SDKs)
**Dispatcher-verified.** Source: sdk-zig depth U2. This corrects my earlier framing.

`packages/runar-ir-schema/src/state-layout.ts` — the single shared width table every SDK derives from — **omits `RabinSig`, `RabinPubKey`, `P256Point`, `P384Point`** (verified: absent). So `annotateStateFieldLayout` stamps all four `'pushdata'`.

The compiler disagrees: `05-stack-lower.ts:3026` treats `RabinSig`/`RabinPubKey` as **8-byte bigint aliases** (`OP_NUM2BIN 8`), and `:3509-3521` fixes `P256Point` = 64 and **`P384Point` = 96** (I had recorded 64 — the depth pass corrected this).

So the SDKs faithfully implement a table that is wrong versus the script. Fix belongs in the schema, not in seven SDKs. **`boolean` goes the other way** — the table *does* list it, so tiers matching only `"bool"` are genuine per-tier outliers.


[GK-GAP-001] Validator accepts P256Point/P384Point as property types. STATE_FIELD_WIDTHS keys are int/bigint/bool/boolean/PubKey/Addr/Ripemd160/Sha256/Point only. Missing types fall through to pushdata. A mutable P256Point continuation is then described as variable-length while stack lowering treats the point as raw bytes.

remediation.GK-GAP-001: Add raw widths matching the EC codec, or reject those types as mutable properties in validate.

testable_assertion.GK-GAP-001: A StatefulSmartContract with p: P256Point produces stateFields[0].encoding === 'pushdata' today; it should be raw with fixed byteLength, or a compile error.

conflicts: CL-BUG-070's own text self-corrects an earlier claim that P384Point is 64 bytes to the correct 96 bytes, matching CL-BUG-133's stated 96 — an internal self-correction by the same reviewer, not a cross-reviewer dispute.

verification.evidence: Narrowed since review: `packages/runar-ir-schema/src/state-layout.ts`'s `STATE_FIELD_WIDTHS` table (lines 39-49) NOW includes `P256Point: {size:64,...}` and `P384Point: {size:96,...}` (added by commit a7b646a2 'N-066: add the curve-point widths to all seven SDK state codecs', confirmed via `git log -S P384Point`), matching the compiler's own layout (05-stack-lower.ts case P256Point=64/P384Point=96). But `RabinSig` and `RabinPubKey` are STILL entirely absent from that table (`grep -n Rabin packages/runar-ir-schema/src/state-layout.ts` returns nothing) even though the compiler treats them as fixed 8-byte raw state fields identical to bigint: `packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/05-stack-lower.ts:3373-3374/3726-3727/3868-3869/4294-4295` all special-case `prop.type === 'RabinSig' || prop.type === 'RabinPubKey'` as 8-byte layout. `annotateStateFieldLayout` therefore still stamps a mutable RabinSig/RabinPubKey field `'pushdata'` (variable-length framed) instead of the fixed 8-byte raw layout the script actually reads. The same gap is mirrored in the SDK-local tables: `packages/runar-rb/lib/runar/sdk/state.rb`'s `TYPE_WIDTHS` (lines 19-30) lists PubKey/Addr/Ripemd160/Sha256/Point/P256Point/P384Point but no Rabin* entries; TypeScript's `packages/runar-sdk/src/state.ts` reads off the same shared `STATE_FIELD_WIDTHS` table so it inherits the same omission.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: CL-BUG-070's REFRAMED framing (the shared table, not the SDKs, is the outlier; P256Point/P384Point width corrected to 64/96) was accurate and has since been acted on for P256Point/P384Point (N-066). GK-GAP-001's specific P256Point testable_assertion is now STALE on its own (P256Point today correctly serializes 'raw', not 'pushdata'), but the RabinSig/RabinPubKey half of the same finding remains open exactly as described — the fix was partial.

items.title: On-chain Rabin verification compares the unreduced SHA-256 digest while every off-chain verifier reduces it mod n
items.confidence_note: raised by GK; silent-but-inspected: ['CL']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description: [GK-BUG-021] The 18-op sequence OP_MODs (sig²+pad) by n, then SHA256, CAT 0x00, BIN2NUM, NUMEQUAL. There is no OP_MOD of the digest. LHS ∈ [0,n). RHS is num(SHA256(msg)) ∈ [0, 2^256). Those are equal iff SHA256(msg) < n. Off-chain every verifier computes rhs = hash % n (rabin.go:71-75, builtins.ts:365). The two worlds coincide only while n > 2^256. Nothing in typecheck, validate, or the script enforces that. A user who bakes a 251-bit (or smaller) RabinPubKey gets SDK/TestContract green, chain rejects, funds locked. Ruby/Zig/Rust off-chain suites use exactly those small moduli and assert accept. Production comments say 1024+ bit keys; the compiler does not require it.

evidence.GK-BUG-021: Opened rabin-codegen.ts:88-101 (OP_MOD of sig²+pad, then SHA256…NUMEQUAL, no second MOD). Opened rabin.go:71-75 (rhs := hashBN.Mod(pkInt)).

remediation.GK-BUG-021: Either OP_MOD the digest by n on-chain (and keep NUMEQUAL) or reject n ≤ 2^256 in typecheck/validate. Pin a ScriptVM test with n=251, sig=0, padding=SHA256%251: off-chain true, on-chain false today.

testable_assertion.GK-BUG-021: EmitVerifyRabinSig with n=251, sig=0, padding = SHA256(msg)%251: off-chain rabinVerify returns true; ScriptVM rejects. After a digest OP_MOD (or an n>2^256 gate) the two agree.

verification.evidence: compilers/go/codegen/rabin.go:51-59 (matches cited range exactly): OP_MOD reduces only the LHS (sig^2+padding) mod pubKey (line 51); the RHS is the RAW OP_SHA256 digest (line 53), padded with a 0x00 sign byte and passed through OP_BIN2NUM/OP_NUMEQUAL (lines 56-59) — never reduced mod pubKey. Identical logic in packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/rabin-codegen.ts:67-101. Both off-chain verifiers explicitly reduce the digest: packages/runar-lang/src/runtime/builtins.ts:370 `const rhs = (hashBN % pubkey + pubkey) % pubkey;` and packages/runar-go/rabin.go:72 `rhs := new(big.Int).Mod(hashBN, pkInt)`. So off-chain computes SHA256(msg) mod n, on-chain compares against the unreduced SHA256(msg) — they agree only when n > 2^256. No such check exists in 02-validate.ts, 03-typecheck.ts, or any RabinPubKey construction path. Checked whether the most recent Rabin fix on main (2b3af765, 'fix/rabin-digest-encoding-bug011', the exact commit GK/CX reviewed at) touches this — it does not: that PR is entirely about BYTE-vs-NUMERIC digest encoding for the honest-signature acceptance path (a different, real bug fixing ~50% honest-sig rejection). None of its 4 new tests touch small-modulus / digest-not-reduced behavior.
verification.tier_correction: Tagged compiler:go but the on-chain emitter bug is duplicated identically in the TS compiler (rabin-codegen.ts) and the off-chain/on-chain divergence equally implicates the Go SDK (runar-go/rabin.go) and the TS runtime (builtins.ts) — this is a cross-tier codegen+SDK design gap, not Go-specific.
verification.reachable_by_adversary: true, but the exploit direction is fund-lock/footgun, not forgery: a deployer who uses a Rabin modulus that isn't > 2^256 gets green off-chain tests for a script the real on-chain interpreter will reject. It does not let an attacker force an on-chain ACCEPT of a forged signature; it silently locks funds for legitimate small-n deployments.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: High — the mechanism, the n>2^256 requirement, and the specific line citations are all correct at HEAD (line numbers drifted by a handful of lines but point at the identical statements).

items.testable_assertion_verified: Construct RabinPubKey n=251, sig=0, padding = SHA256(msg) % 251. Off-chain verifyRabinSig/rabinVerifyImpl returns true. Feed the equivalent unlocking script through ScriptVM against the compiled verifyVerifyRabinSig script — it must reject, because the on-chain check compares the small padding value against the full unreduced ~256-bit SHA-256 digest via OP_NUMEQUAL. Passes once the emitter also reduces the digest via OP_MOD before comparison (or once RabinPubKey construction/typecheck enforces n > 2^256).

items.title: Go numeric-identity peephole rules (x+0, x-0, --x) erase ScriptNum validation/canonicalization performed by the removed opcode
items.confidence_note: raised by CX; silent-but-inspected: ['CL', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description: [CX-BUG-011] Rewriting `x 0 OP_ADD`, `x 0 OP_SUB`, or `x OP_NEGATE OP_NEGATE` to raw `x` is algebraically valid only after `x` has been decoded as a legal Script number. Removing the arithmetic removes runtime numeric decoding and result normalization, so malformed or non-canonical witness bytes can behave differently in optimized and unoptimized scripts.

evidence.CX-BUG-011: The optimizer performs these rewrites without inspecting the producer of `x`. Tests assert only resulting opcode shape and do not execute malformed ScriptNum inputs, despite the adjacent double-`OP_NOT` rule having already been hardened for the analogous provenance problem.

remediation.CX-BUG-011: Require a producer proven to yield a canonical Script number, or retain operations whose validation/normalization is observable.

testable_assertion.CX-BUG-011: Optimized and unoptimized scripts reject the same oversized/non-canonical numeric witness for `x + 0`, `x - 0`, and `-(-x)`.

verification.evidence: compilers/go/codegen/optimizer.go matchWindow2 (~118-149) unconditionally deletes PUSH(0)+OP_ADD, PUSH(0)+OP_SUB, and OP_NEGATE+OP_NEGATE pairs with no check on the operand's provenance. compilers/go/codegen/stack.go:1443-1466 (lowerLoadParam) confirms a witness-supplied bigint method parameter is placed on the stack with ZERO normalization — no OP_BIN2NUM, no size/canonical check is ever inserted at parameter entry. So for a value whose ONLY numeric touch is exactly x+0/x-0/-(-x), that arithmetic opcode is the sole ScriptNum-decode gate on it, and deleting it lets a malformed/oversized/non-canonical witness value flow through unvalidated. Verified via go-sdk (v1.2.21, pinned) that OP_ADD/OP_SUB/OP_NEGATE enforce an unconditional length cap (len(bb) > scriptNumLen -> ErrNumberTooBig) independent of any policy flag, so oversized-operand rejection genuinely differs between optimized/unoptimized scripts. The codebase's own authors already guard the adjacent OP_NOT,OP_NOT rule against exactly this class of issue (producesCanonicalBool + c17_not_not_guard_test.go) — yet no equivalent guard exists for the three arithmetic-identity rules this item targets.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Files/line ranges correct in spirit (optimizer.go:129-146 is the matchWindow2 identity-rule block); optimizer_test.go does NOT already guard this — it only guards the unrelated C17 OP_NOT,OP_NOT case (a value-changing bug, not a validation-skipping bug). Real-world severity is somewhat bounded vs. a naive reading of the finding — BSV's post-Genesis max-script-number-length is large and MINIMALDATA is policy/standardness-only, not universally enforced consensus, and this project's ScriptVM doesn't appear to enable verifyMinimalData by default — so the cleanest, always-reachable divergence is specifically the unconditional length-cap check, not every 'non-canonical encoding' framing in the original finding.

items.testable_assertion_verified: Compile a StatefulSmartContract method containing `this.count = x + 0;` (x a witness bigint parameter, count a mutable property serialized via addOutput with no other arithmetic on x). Feed a deliberately oversized (or non-minimally-encoded) byte string as the witness value for x. With the peephole optimizer disabled, the spend fails (OP_ADD's MakeScriptNumber rejects the oversized/non-canonical operand); with the optimizer enabled (default), the same spend succeeds and the raw unvalidated bytes are written into the new UTXO's serialized state — an optimizer-dependent accept/reject divergence on identical source and identical witness.

So the SDKs faithfully implement a table that is wrong versus the script. Fix belongs in the schema, not in seven SDKs. **`boolean` goes the other way** — the table *does* list it, so tiers matching only `"bool"` are genuine per-tier outliers.


`packages/runar-sdk/src/state.ts:338-342` · `packages/runar-rb/lib/runar/sdk/state.rb:20-24` ·

via `state-layout.ts`). **Seven of seven.**

verification.evidence: packages/runar-ir-schema/src/state-layout.ts's STATE_FIELD_WIDTHS table (lines ~40-51) now DOES list P256Point (64, raw) and P384Point (96, raw) — that part of CL-BUG-070/133 is fixed. But RabinSig and RabinPubKey are still absent from the table, so annotateStateFieldLayout still stamps them 'pushdata'. The compiler disagrees: packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/05-stack-lower.ts:3373-3374, :3726-3727, :3868-3869, :4021, :4295 and the isVariableLengthStateType comment at :6591 all confirm RabinSig/RabinPubKey are treated as 8-byte NUM2BIN-le bigint aliases, on-chain RAW, not push-data-framed. packages/runar-sdk/src/state.ts:338-351's encodeStateValue is table-driven off the SAME state-layout.ts table (`const rawWidth = STATE_FIELD_WIDTHS[type]`), so a RabinSig/RabinPubKey state field falls through to the push-data default branch there too. packages/runar-go/sdk_state.go:427's raw-type switch (`case "PubKey", "Addr", "Ripemd160", "Sha256", "Point", "P256Point", "P384Point":`) likewise omits RabinSig/RabinPubKey, confirming the mismatch is cross-tier, not TS-only. grep across all 7 SDK state files for 'RabinSig'/'RabinPubKey' returns zero hits — no SDK special-cases them outside the shared (still-incomplete) table.

via `state-layout.ts`). **Seven of seven.**

items.title: On-chain treeAddr8 packs idx_tree with OP_NUM2BIN 8; 256f indices in [2^63, 2^64) cannot fit
items.confidence_note: raised by GK; silent-but-inspected: ['CL']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): ['CX']
items.description: [GK-BUG-018] Inbound 256f tree index is reversed, CAT 0x00, BIN2NUM, MOD 2^64, producing an unsigned 64-bit script number. Values in [2^63, 2^64) encode as 9 bytes (sign-pad). Then treeAddr8 does OP_NUM2BIN 8, which fails if the number does not fit in 8 bytes. Zig already special-cases the 2^64 modulus because 1<<64 does not fit i64, but still packs width 8. Half of 256f hypertree indices abort on-chain. All 7 emitters share this pack.

evidence.GK-BUG-018: Opened slh-dsa-codegen.ts:1187-1197 (CAT 0x00 BIN2NUM MOD 2^{h-hp}) and :1216-1219 (NUM2BIN 8). Opened pq_emitters.zig:467-476 (comment on exponent 64, still NUM2BIN width).

remediation.GK-BUG-018: Pack treeAddr as 8-byte unsigned (explicit byte split, not script-num NUM2BIN), or use NUM2BIN 9 and drop the sign byte. Add a ScriptVM test with idx_tree = 2^63.

testable_assertion.GK-BUG-018: Compiled SHA2-256f verify with a preimage whose tree-index bytes decode to 2^63 currently fails at NUM2BIN 8; after the fix it continues and uses ADRS tree address 0x8000000000000000.

verification.evidence: compilers/go/codegen/slh_dsa.go:1362-1370 computes treeAddr8 via copyToTop('treeIdx','_ti8'); rawBlock(push 8; OP_NUM2BIN; reverse8) — byte-for-byte the same shape as packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/slh-dsa-codegen.ts:1232-1239 and compilers/zig/src/passes/helpers/pq_emitters.zig's appendNumToBigEndianToBuilder (width=8, ~471-474). For SHA2_256f (N=32,H=68,D=17,HP=4 -> H-HP=64), treeIdx = digest bytes mod 2^64 (slh_dsa.go:1330-1342, mirrored in TS at slh-dsa-codegen.ts:1204-1216), so treeIdx ranges over the full unsigned 64-bit space. A Bitcoin Script number needs 9 bytes to minimally encode any value in [2^63,2^64) (sign-pad byte, since bit 63 would otherwise be read as the sign bit), and OP_NUM2BIN fails when the requested width can't hold the minimal encoding. push 8; OP_NUM2BIN with no special-casing for that range therefore aborts script execution for roughly half of all valid 256f tree indices. Zig's appendPowerOfTwoModulusToBuilder (pq_emitters.zig:458-470) even has a comment acknowledging '1<<64 does not fit in i64' for exactly this 256f case, proving the codebase already knows H-HP=64 is reachable, yet the downstream NUM2BIN-8 pack was never adjusted.
verification.tier_correction: The finding's cited file list (pq_emitters.zig, slh-dsa-codegen.ts) omits the Go tier entirely, but tier=compiler:go is nonetheless CORRECT: compilers/go/codegen/slh_dsa.go:1362-1370 carries the identical unguarded treeAddr8 packing logic, and slh_dsa.go:1337 even independently comments on the H-HP=64 overflow risk for big.Int shifts, confirming Go's authors were aware of the 256f edge case for the modulus computation but did not carry that awareness through to the NUM2BIN(8) pack immediately below. Recommend adding compilers/go/codegen/slh_dsa.go:1362-1370 (and likely the equivalent in Rust/Python/Ruby/Java, unverified) to the evidence file list.
verification.reviewer_accuracy: Cited Zig/TS paths and line ranges were accurate; the claim 'all 7 emitters share this pack' is directionally correct for Go (verified) though the original evidence omitted the Go file.

items.tier_reason: ANF/stack/emit/EC-optimizer boundary and emitted bytes change (§5 floor: mid min, top if bytes move)

verification.evidence: compilers/go/codegen/optimizer.go: 'PUSH 0, OP_ADD -> remove both' (:129-132), 'PUSH 0, OP_SUB -> remove both' (:134-137) and 'OP_NEGATE, OP_NEGATE -> remove both' (:144-146) all unconditionally delete the opcode pair as a numeric no-op. items.title: Rust peephole: the C17 unsoundness fix was applied to one rule and not its three adjacent siblings
items.confidence_note: raised by CL; silent-but-inspected: ['CX', 'GK']; never-opened (silence, not disagreement): none
items.description:
[CL-BUG-096] ## CL-BUG-096 — MEDIUM / P2 — Rust peephole: the C17 unsoundness fix was applied to one rule and not its three adjacent siblings
**Dispatcher-verified, and sharper than the worker's framing.** Source: impl-rust-codegen depth NEW-07.

`compilers/rust/src/codegen/optimizer.rs:340-357` contains, verbatim, a note recording that the author *understood this exact unsoundness class*:
```rust
// NOTE: `OP_NOT, OP_NOT -> []` used to live here as an unguarded 2-op rule.
// It is unsound (C17) and now lives in `match_window_3`, which takes the
// PRODUCER of the negated value into the window.
```
Immediately above and below that note sit three rules with the same normalising property, still unguarded 2-op windows:
- `PUSH 0, OP_ADD -> []` (`:340-343`)
- `PUSH 0, OP_SUB -> []` (`:345-348`)
- `OP_NEGATE, OP_NEGATE -> []` (`:354-356`)

`OP_ADD`/`OP_SUB`/`OP_NEGATE` re-encode their result as a minimal `CScriptNum`. Deleting them preserves truthiness but **not the bytes**, leaving whatever encoding the spender pushed — which is precisely the C17 argument. A value reaching a byte-wise consumer (`OP_EQUAL`, `OP_CAT`, state serialisation) then compares differently with the peephole on and off.

This is the review's recurring shape in miniature: a defect class correctly diagnosed, fixed at one instance, and left standing at its immediate neighbours in the same file.

...
- (a) The clearing rested on the genuine `OP_NOT OP_NOT` guard — but three sibling rules in the same file are unguarded (CL-BUG-096).
- (b) The branch sub-context drops **seven of ten** lowering fields, producing CL-BUG-094 (P0 miscompile), CL-BUG-095, and two compiler panics.

Methodological consequence for Pass F: a breadth "CLEARED" verdict is a *hypothesis that one worker failed to confirm*, not a negative result. Only

items.title: affineAdd doubling branch with y=0 computes lambda=0 instead of returning O: ecAdd(q,q) for an off-curve q=(x,0) returns (p-2x mod p, 0); EC optimizer R8/R8r (ecAdd(x,ecNegate(x))->O) therefore disagrees with the unoptimized script on such points; contradicts the R-157 comment in ec-codegen.ts
items.description: DESIGN (DECIDED, see below): (a) fix the adder's y=0 doubling to return O in all 7 tiers (moves every ecAdd golden), or (b) restrict/gate R8/R8r. Note: on-curve secp256k1 has no y=0 point, so only off-curve operands reach this. USER DECISION (dispatcher-resolutions line 349, 2026-10): 'Fail on y=0 in all 7 tiers' — the ecAdd doubling branch must make the script FAIL (assert y != 0, i.e. OP_VERIFY-style abort) when the doubling branch is taken with y = 0, in all 7 compiler tiers' EC codegen, byte-identical across tiers. Do NOT return O. Restamp every moved conformance golden through the golden-provenance gate (route A witness preferred: an independent real-crypto/EC check that honest on-curve inputs still verify and that a y=0 doubling now aborts), regenerate derived artifacts (check-derived-artifacts.ts), and keep Lean pipelineGolden green per R19a (counts/buckets only; if a fingerprint/model row would need to move, STOP and report). Cross-tier parity: conformance golden STRICT, multi-format fold off AND fold on, ir-parity.
items.testable_assertion_verified: Executing the compiled ecAdd doubling branch with an operand whose y = 0 aborts the script (real script execution, all 7 tiers byte-identical); honest on-curve ecAdd/ecMul vectors still verify.

items.title: TokenWallet's assumed ABI (merge(sig, otherSupply, otherHolder), transfer(sig, Addr)) is inherently unsound: merge cannot authenticate its companion input (supply inflation); transfer cannot re-key the PubKey holder
items.description: Needs an ABI redesign (e.g. token-ft's allPrevouts/otherParentTx walk, PubKey recipient) or TokenWallet deprecation. Design decision for the user. USER DECISION R92 (2026-10-13): DEPRECATE. In every SDK that ships TokenWallet (find them all: TS packages/runar-sdk/src/tokens.ts, and any Go/Rust/Python/Zig/Ruby/Java TokenWallet ports), mark merge and transfer deprecated and unsafe: language-native deprecation marker (@deprecated JSDoc, // Deprecated: Go doc, #[deprecated], warnings.warn DeprecationWarning, Java @Deprecated, Ruby warn, Zig doc comment + runtime std.log.warn), a one-time runtime warning that names the supply-inflation (merge) and holder re-key (transfer) problems and points to token-ft (FungibleTokenExample) as the sound alternative, and docs (SDK README/docs token section) saying the same. Do NOT redesign the ABI or remove the methods. Keep examples/*/token-wallet-naive-INSECURE as the documented counter-example. No golden or script bytes change.
items.testable_assertion_verified: In every SDK tier that ships TokenWallet, calling merge or transfer emits the deprecation warning naming the unsoundness and token-ft (one test per tier); the methods still work otherwise; the deprecation marker is present.

items.description: USER DECISION R96 (2026-10-13): gate R8 on y != 0. The rewritten form must keep the y != 0 abort (assert y != 0, then push O), so optimized and unoptimized agree, byte-identical across all 7 tiers. Golden-moving only where R8/R8r fires: restamp via the provenance gate (route A preferred). N-104's test docstring records the divergence. Context: N-110 (landed) added the y=0 guard to the unoptimized adder in all 7 tiers' EC codegen. items.title: Security review of N-316: matchesArtifact accepts ANY script element at a codeSepIndex slot, though the SDK bakes a deterministic value there, so a lookalike script with a forged codeSep index matches as genuine (fail-open, now reachable for codeSep-only artifacts)
items.description: buildCodeScript/_resolvedCodeSepSlotValues write a value fully determined by slot.codeSepIndex plus the expansion of earlier constructor and codeSep slots. matchesArtifact (all 7 SDKs) skips whatever element sits at a codeSepIndex slot (readScriptElement), so any push there matches. Before N-316 a codeSep-only artifact fell through to a literal compare (fail-closed); N-316 routes it through the slot-aware path, making the fail-open reachable for TokenWallet.getUtxos and fromUtxo. Fix: at each codeSepIndex slot require the element to equal encodeScriptNumber(expected adjusted index), where the shift from constructor slots is computed from the ACTUAL element lengths read at those slots in the candidate script. Fix in all 7 tiers; extend the shared vector conformance/sdk-matches-artifact/ with forged-codeSep-index cases.
items.testable_assertion_verified: A script identical to an honest deployment except for a different number pushed at a codeSepIndex slot does not match in any of the 7 SDKs, while honest deployments (with and without constructor args before the codeSep slot) still match.

items.title: Hostile-script parsing outside getUtxos: Java Integer.parseInt accepts '+'/'-' opcodes (SIOOBE via fromTxId state parsing), Rust find_last_op_return slices &str by byte index (panic in from_utxo/from_txid on non-ASCII), Python find_last_op_return raises ValueError on non-hex via contract.from_utxo

(a) Java decodePushDataState/decodePushData use Integer.parseInt, which accepts a leading '+'/'-': opcode string '-1' takes the <=75 branch with dataLen=-2 and throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, reachable from fromTxId state parsing. (b) Rust find_last_op_return slices &str by byte index: contract from_utxo/from_txid panic on non-ASCII. (c) Python find_last_op_return raises ValueError on non-hex via contract.from_utxo. items.title: Go SDK NewRunarContract accepts a non-hex ByteString constructor arg and splices raw bytes into the locking script; examples pass raw runar.Alice.PubKeyHash and build corrupt scripts
items.description: checkpoint-24 ex-go: TestBSV20Token_InscriptionFromUtxoRoundTrip, TestBSV21Token_DeployMintFromUtxoRoundTrip, TestBSV21Token_TransferFromUtxoRoundTrip and TestOrdinalNFT_InscriptionRoundTripFromUtxo fail with "FromUtxo: script is not an even-length hex string". Probe the other 6 SDKs for the same fail-open (non-hex ByteString constructor arg) and fix any that splice it unchecked. Other examples using Alice.PubKeyHash (post-quantum-wallet, sphincs-wallet, p256-wallet, p384-wallet) must be checked too.

MethodNode has no return-type field: TS infers private return types; 01-parse-python.ts:995 discards it; 01-parse-java.ts:665 drops _returnType; Rust/Move keep only a hasReturnType flag; on Zig/Go surfaces the slot doubles as the runar.Sighash(...) directive. Fix needs either a new AST field (both TS AST files, ir-schema, 6 tier ASTs) or a parse-time check in each surface parser x 7 tiers; refuse an unknown name with a diagnostic naming it, plus rejection-parity negatives from N291.
items.testable_assertion_verified: All 7 tiers refuse a return type TTT on every surface with return annotations and accept the same contract with the real type.

items.title: A public method with a declared return type (.runar.rs `-> T`) is accepted by go/rust/zig but refused by ts/python/ruby/java

items.title: Native Go type names on .runar.go (int64, int, bool, []byte, string, uint64) are mapped inconsistently across tiers as param and return types; docs/formats/go.md lists int64 and bool as valid

As params (since N-325): `x int64` refused by Go and Ruby; Go tier refuses native bool params. Decide the documented mapping (docs/formats/go.md) and make all 7 tiers agree for params and return types, with rejection-parity negatives / acceptance fixtures.
items.testable_assertion_verified: All 7 tiers give the same verdict for each native Go type name as param and return type, matching docs/formats/go.md.

items.title: runar-py native sha256_compress guards operand sizes with `assert`, which python -O strips, so wrong-size state/block is accepted there
items.description: Found by N-161 probe. Python sha256_compress uses assert for its 32-byte state / 64-byte block check; under python -O the check disappears and a wrong-size operand is silently accepted, unlike the on-chain F-114 guard. Replace with an explicit raise (ValueError, as blake3_compress does) and grep runar-py for other assert-based input validation in runtime (non-test) code.
items.testable_assertion_verified: Under python -O, sha256_compress refuses a 31-byte state / 63-byte block.

items.title: runar-py RPCProvider narrows JSON-RPC node responses with `assert isinstance(...)` (rpc_provider.py:87,112,119,146); under python -O a malformed node response is not refused there
items.description: Found by N-336 sweep. Replace the four assert-based type checks on node responses with explicit raises (a provider error naming the RPC method and the unexpected type) so a malformed / hostile node response fails closed under python -O too.
items.testable_assertion_verified: Under python -O, RPCProvider refuses a node response of the wrong JSON type with an explicit error.

items.title: Native Go type names the docs do not list (int, uint, uint64, []byte, string) are accepted by some tiers and refused by others on .runar.go
items.description: From the N-333 probe (remediation-logs/N-333/probe.txt): int accepted by ts/rust/py/zig/ruby/java, refused by go; uint, uint64 and string accepted by rust only; []byte accepted by rust and zig as params (zig also as a return). docs/formats/go.md Type Mapping lists only int64, bool and the runar.* types. Needs a user decision: (a) refuse the unlisted names in every tier, or (b) document a mapping (e.g. int/uint/uint64 -> bigint, []byte/string -> ByteString) and accept them everywhere. Then make all 7 tiers agree, with a parity test and over-rejection sweep. USER DECISION (2026-10-18, AskUserQuestion): refuse the unlisted names — all 7 tiers refuse int, uint, uint64, []byte and string on .runar.go with the N-325/N-331 'not a Rúnar type' wording; docs/formats/go.md stays the spec (int64, bool, runar.* only).
items.testable_assertion_verified: All 7 tiers refuse int, uint, uint64, []byte and string as param, private return and field types on .runar.go; int64/bool/runar.* stay accepted.

items.title: Move `while` loop rejections quote a different synthetic iterator name per tier (Rust MOVE_WHILE_STUB_ITER vs the TS placeholder)
items.description: Found while fixing N-026: the Move surface lowers `while` to a for-loop with a synthetic iterator. Rust names it MOVE_WHILE_STUB_ITER while TS uses its own placeholder, so a refused Move `while` (e.g. a non-constant condition) quotes a different variable name per tier in the 'For loop condition must compare the loop variable ...' diagnostic. Other tiers unprobed.
items.testable_assertion_verified: A refused Move `while` program yields the same quoted iterator name in the diagnostic across all 7 tiers (TS reference).

items.title: Java TS-surface parser drops let/const mutability in its AST: is `const` reassignment on .runar.ts refused by all 7 tiers?
items.description: Found while fixing N-054: the Java TsParser's AST records no mutability for `let` or `const`. Unless a later Java pass recovers it, a `.runar.ts` program that reassigns a `const` local may be accepted by Java while TS refuses it (fail-open). Probe const reassignment (statement, compound assignment, ++/--, for-loop body) on every surface with const locals, across all 7 tiers; fix any tier that accepts.
items.testable_assertion_verified: A conformance/negatives parity test: reassigning a const local is refused by all 7 tiers on every surface that has const locals; the let twin is accepted.

items.title: Zig compile time is quadratic in nested-if depth: each level re-runs the peephole over its whole subtree and copies it (D=127 x 120: 50 s vs Go 2.7 s)
items.description: Found while fixing N-280 (memory): after the fix, peak RSS is linear-ish but compile time is not. Each nested if-arm is peephole-optimized and then spliced into the parent, which is optimized again, so the work is quadratic in depth. D=127 x 120 compiles in ~50 s in ReleaseSafe against Go's 2.7 s.
items.testable_assertion_verified: runar-zig compiles the D=127 x 120 composite chain within a small constant factor of Go's time, byte-identical to Go.

items.title: Immutable locals on the .runar.rs (let without mut) and .runar.zig (const) surfaces can be reassigned: all 7 tiers accept
items.description: Found while fixing N-342 (.runar.ts const reassignment): the probe matrix (remediation-logs/N-342/probe.txt) shows a Rust-DSL `let x = ...` (no mut) and a Zig `const x = ...` reassigned later are accepted by all 7 tiers. Go `const` / Java `final` probes were inconclusive (non-Rúnar spellings). Sol, Move, Python and Ruby have no immutable-local spelling. Whether those surfaces must enforce immutability is a design question (docs/formats/rust.md, zig docs); default per fail-closed is to refuse, matching N-342.
items.testable_assertion_verified: All 7 tiers refuse reassigning an immutable local on .runar.rs and .runar.zig with the N-342 sentence; the mutable twin (let mut / var) compiles identically.

items.title: `toByteString(a) === toByteString(b)` lowers to OP_NUMEQUAL in TS and Rust but OP_EQUAL in Go, Python, Zig, Ruby and Java
items.description: Found while fixing F-160 (probe in remediation-logs/F-160/probe.txt): with folding off, equality between two toByteString(...) results emits 9c (OP_NUMEQUAL) in TS and Rust and 87 (OP_EQUAL) in the other five tiers. Numeric equality is the wrong semantics for ByteStrings (it compares as script numbers, fails on operands over 4 bytes, and equates non-minimal encodings), and the cross-tier hex diverges. Check whether any conformance fixture exercises it (none should, or parity would have failed) and whether the typechecker mis-types the call result.
items.testable_assertion_verified: All 7 tiers lower ByteString equality on toByteString results to OP_EQUAL; a cross-tier parity test pins the hex and a ScriptVM run shows two different >4-byte ByteStrings compare unequal.

items.tier_reason: possible EC miscompile in all 7 tiers
items.title: EC rule R8 matches operand names that were rebound, folding ecAdd(q, ecNegate(p)) to INFINITY
items.description: Per the F-269 agent: `a=p; nx=ecNegate(a); a=q; ecAdd(a, nx)` via --ir still fires R8 by raw name in every tier, since ANF reuses a local name on reassignment (top level and if/loop arms). Result is O instead of q-p: a wrong-value miscompile. First determine whether pass 04 can emit this from SOURCE in each tier (let a = p; const nx = ecNegate(a); a = q; assert(ecAdd(a, nx) == ...)); execute on @bsv/sdk Spend with EC optimizer on vs disableEcOptimizer. Fix: name-equality and value lookups in every EC rule must refuse names in collectReboundNames (F-269 helper). F-269 review: reachable from source after F-269 (R8, R8r, R7, R9, R11 all miscompile with a rebound name); F-269 attempt 2 must fix the from-source form; the --ir form shares the root cause.
items.status_note: expected STALE once F-269 lands (attempt 2 refuses rebound names in identity and lift-and-emit in all 7 tiers; --ir de-aliased forms tested)

items.title: Go EC rule engine treats two const bindings with equal payloads as the same $x; other tiers use name equality
items.description: Go sameResolvedValue: for --ir input c1=G; c2=G; ecAdd(c1, ecNegate(c2)) only Go folds to O. Pick one rule across 7 tiers (value-equality is sound for consts) and add an --ir parity case. REGRADED (F-269 review 2026-10-19): reachable from SOURCE in Go: `let t = p; const a = t; t = q; const b = t; assert(ecAdd(a, ecNegate(b)) === e)` folds to O (both a and b hold "@ref:t"); wrong-value miscompile. Evidence remediation-logs/F-269/review/. UPDATE (F-269 attempt 2): the wrong-value @ref: equal-payload fold is fixed by F-269. Remaining: Go still equates distinct const bindings with equal payloads (value-sound) -> from-source byte-parity break: `const g1 = ecMulGen(1n); const g2 = ecMulGen(1n); assert(ecAdd(ecAdd(g1, ecNegate(g2)), p) === e)` Go 2244 bytes vs 50457 in the other 6 tiers (review2/).

items.title: Reassigning a method parameter is silently dropped in Python, Ruby, Zig and Java ANF lowering

items.title: runar-zig native package gaps keep 17 example contracts compile-check only (missing re-exports, intrinsics, builtins; hex-literal semantics)
items.description: From remediation-logs/N-371/bugs.txt and compile-only.txt. (1) currentBlockHeight and requireOutputP2PKH are not re-exported from packages/runar-zig/src/root.zig. (2) No native addOutput/addDataOutput on contract structs. (3) No native p256*/p384*, split, int2str, reverseBytes. (4) The extractPrevOutputScript stub returns empty, and the intent-output-p2pkh stub is a no-op, so neither can reject. (5) A ByteString literal "006a" in the GoDsl contract is hex to the compiler but 4 ASCII bytes natively: a native-vs-compiled semantic divergence. Each fix should turn the corresponding examples/zig test from compile-only into a native positive+negative test.

items.title: Zig tier refuses a stateful .runar.zig contract with no init while the other six tiers accept it
items.description: Accept/reject split: Zig reports "property must be assigned in the constructor" for a .runar.zig StatefulSmartContract without init; TS and the other five accept. Pinned in conformance/negatives/n490-synthesized-constructor-loc-parity.test.ts last it(). Decide reference per TS and align.
items.testable_assertion_verified: All 7 tiers give the same accept/reject verdict (and identical bytes if accepted) for a stateful .runar.zig contract with no init.

items.title: Rust .runar.zig parser adds no implicit param-to-property assignments for an init without struct-return
items.description: TS synthesizes param->property assignments for a .runar.zig init that does not return .{...}; Rust parser_zig.rs does not. Check the other tiers too.
items.testable_assertion_verified: For a .runar.zig init without struct-return, all 7 tiers produce the same ANF/hex as TS.

items.title: Several tiers Rust-DSL parsers accept only attributed structs; TS also accepts a bare struct
items.description: TS 01-parse-rust.ts accepts a bare `struct` as the contract; several non-TS .runar.rs parsers require a #[runar::...] attribute. Measure all 7 tiers and align to TS.
items.testable_assertion_verified: For a .runar.rs contract with a bare struct, all 7 tiers give the same verdict and, if accepted, identical bytes.

items.title: Rust tier accepts an if-expression operand in .runar.rs that TS and most tiers refuse to parse
items.description: (if flag { x } else { x }) + 1 in a .runar.rs contract is accepted by the Rust compiler but TS and most other tiers do not parse an if-expression there: a parse-acceptance split. Measure all 7 tiers and align to TS (or STOP if TS rejecting it contradicts docs/formats/rust.md).
items.testable_assertion_verified: All 7 tiers give the same verdict for a .runar.rs if-expression operand; if accepted, identical hex.

items.title: Comparison/equality operands (==, !=, <, <=, >, >=) are outside the N-491 anchor matrix; Rust Java-surface comparisons are unlocated
items.description: Rust parser_java.rs parse_equality / parse_relational (fold_compare_to_zero path) build Binary nodes with no location, so a Java-surface == or < operand error anchors at the statement. The N-491 matrix covers only !, unary -, &&, || and arithmetic composites, so comparison operands are unmeasured on every surface and tier. Extend the matrix with comparison shapes, measure, then align every tier (TS reference per R194).
items.testable_assertion_verified: The N-491 matrix includes comparison-operand shapes on all 9 surfaces and its DIVERGENT allowlist is empty for them.

items.title: Stale doc comments: AST sourceLocation "only the .runar.ts parser sets it" after N-491..N-497
items.description: Java BinaryExpr.java, UnaryExpr.java, Identifier.java Javadoc (and any equivalent comments in the other 6 tiers incl. TS runar-ast.ts and Zig ir/types.zig) still say only the .runar.ts parser sets the operand location; since N-491..N-497 every surface parser does.
items.testable_assertion_verified: No comment in any tier claims operand sourceLocation is set only by the .runar.ts parser.

items.title: Other Rust surface parsers may locate methods/constructors after the body
items.description: By inspection (unverified): parser_sol.rs ~1009, parser_move.rs ~1178, parser_ruby.rs ~1538 (constructor branch after expect(End)), parser_python.rs ~1533 (__init__ branch) build MethodNode with self.loc() after parsing the body, the defect N-500 fixed in parser_zig.rs. Verify each, then fix those that are wrong.
items.testable_assertion_verified: For each Rust surface parser, every MethodNode/constructor location equals the TS location of the method start.

items.title: Zig prints no location for method-anchored validation errors
items.description: The Zig tier prints e.g. "recursion detected" and "must end with an assert" without a file:line:col while Go, Rust and TS print one. Align with TS.
items.testable_assertion_verified: For method-anchored validation errors, all 7 tiers print the same file:line:col as TS (cross-tier row in conformance/negatives/n233-diagnostic-anchor-parity.test.ts or similar).

items.title: conformance/n498-python-ruby-anf-sourceloc.test.ts is not executed by any CI workflow
items.description: checkpoint-62 vitest: tests/conformance-tests-reachable-from-ci.test.ts fails — conformance/n498-python-ruby-anf-sourceloc.test.ts (landed by N-498, 303215f1f) sits at the conformance/ root, which turbo does not descend into, and no .github/workflows step names it. Every other new conformance test lives under conformance/negatives/ (covered by `npx vitest run negatives/` at ci.yml:1112).
items.testable_assertion_verified: tests/conformance-tests-reachable-from-ci.test.ts passes: the n498 test file is reachable from a CI workflow step.

items.title: Rust compiler is ~40x slower than Go on the N-264 D=32x120 composite-nesting input; n264 parity test times out under load
items.description: checkpoint-62 vitest: conformance/negatives/n264-composite-nesting-parity.test.ts 'D=32 x 120 (fold-off)' failed with rust spawnSync ETIMEDOUT (NATIVE_TIMEOUT 120s). Idle timing on comp32k120.runar.ts --hex --disable-constant-folding: Rust 29.9s/31.2s, Go 0.70s; identical 29.7s at checkpoint-61 commit d358f75f9, so not a regression — a pre-existing super-linear pass in the Rust tier that turns the parity test into a load-dependent flake (case durations 57s @cp60, 91s @cp61, >120s @cp62). Fix the Rust hot spot; do not raise the harness timeout.
items.testable_assertion_verified: A test proves the Rust tier compiles the D=32x120 composite input within a bound comparable to the other native tiers (profile-identified pass fixed so the compile drops well under the harness timeout), with byte-identical output to Go's pinned digest.
